Called several times but they couldn't do anything and gave us explanations like may be some one else needed those seats and there are no other seats together available. When we boarded, the whole plane was empty and still they didn't allow us to seat together.

Note that BA actually charges for seat pre-selection in biz class -- 100 UK pounds in this case! Does any other airline in the world dare do that? I saved the money and waited until checkin to choose my seat for free. The seats were BA's universally derided, cramped 6-across back-to-front configuration, where you stare into the face of your seat mate an arm's length away. No other airline ever came up with this awkward arrangement --- I wonder why? No preflight drink was offered. At meal time I selected one of the three main offerings, only to be told it wasn't available -- even though there were only 3 people in my 16 seat biz section. The seat area has practically no storage except a tiny drawer at ankle level that is inaccessible when the seat is in lie flat position. The "bed" is the narrowest I have experienced in biz class, and is also very hard. The cabin was very cold and the blanket very thin; I had to raid blankets from two other seats just to stay warm. The amenity kit is the smallest I've ever seen in biz class -- it fits in the palm of the hand. All in all, this uncomfortable, miserly experience is hardly worth the £5,727 that BA charges for this route. I used miles to pay for my ticket -- but of course got whacked with BA's unique and notorious "fuel surcharge" fee of $636 for using miles.

It was good to see that check-in carefully scrutinised lateral flow certificates and passenger locator forms. Thanks to just 30 passengers on board, with more than half in Club Europe, the flight took off ahead of time. Service was a little perfunctory and the food was more reminiscent of economy than business class, with too much pre-packaging - the COVID effect, presumably. Arrival into T5 was also comfortably ahead of schedule, and although we were dreading many hours of queuing at border control, we were through the e-gates and collecting our luggage just 20 minutes after landing.
After frustratingly missing my flight due to M25 road closures, she helped me secure and book the next day flight without additional charges. I am really grateful.

review_header: "a thoroughly reassuring, coming out of COVID, experience"
review_text: T5 was blissfully quiet, with no queues at check-in or security, and even the Galleries South lounge was less frenetic than usual, despite families with kids similarly desperate to escape Boris Johnson’s bully boy attitude. Ordering food and beverages from one’s table seems something worth continuing, avoiding all the wastage of endlessly replenished buffets. The flights was very quiet, with just 30 pax on board, 9 of whom were in Club Europe. Boarding by row also seemed a welcome improvement on the previous ‘groups’. Service on the flight was good and the food was of the usual Do&Co quality. Landing was ahead of schedule and we were through passport control in just a few minutes after a quick check of vaccination certificates and the passenger locator form. Overall, a thoroughly reassuring, coming out of COVID, experience.

review_header: "going in circles to avoid issuing any voucher"
review_text: Refund was promised in voucher form by call center. We are now 6 months down the line, 13 calls of which each is 40 min waiting time, and 16 email reminders. Conclusion is that they are just going in circles to avoid issuing any voucher. Head of call center is keeping to her empty promises.
Crew doing their best to keep everyone happy in challenging times. Nice to see they have introduced a free snack and water. It’s a start.

Same at disembarking: passengers were asked to remain seated, then row per row was called. crew members were supporting the process. What could be improved: distribute hand-sanitizer during boarding. When snack was distributed my row (#8 business) was overlooked for some reason; after a while my seat neighbour highlighted that we did not get food - staff was surprised and fixed it, This was my first flight since one year, and I appreciated the COVID measures taken by BA - still it left some strange experience.

review_header: "COVID protocols are not as robust as they should be"
review_text: I was happy with the fast baggage check-in. This was a bus gate which is not my favourite thing but not a blemish on the airline. The COVID protocols are not as robust as they should be, particularly attendants need to be armed with sanitizer at the cabin entrance. There was a big mix up which I find inexcusable - I and another passenger were allocated the same seat on the same plane, causing a few anxious moments and the friendly attendant had to get me another seat but I don't expect such at this level. Bottles of water were offered to every passenger which was welcome. The plane arrived 10 minutes late.

review_header: "I would need to call up to rebook"
review_text: After having my return cancelled 3 times I opted for a voucher so I could rebook a new route. I had not been informed before requesting the “E-voucher” and I would need to call up to rebook (I’m in a different country and the phone tariffs are extortion). So not only was my flight cancelled 3 times I wasn’t offered an option to rebook a new flight online I was inconvenienced every step of the way.

British Airways, unfortunately, has lowered it's standards and to my dismay, I've been recently having a much better flying experience with budget airlines rather than BA. Customer service representatives are completely clueless, unprofessional and not bothered.  I recently had my flight cancelled on 3 occasions and the staff weren't interested in helping me return home.

But the travel restrictions changed a week before the travel dates. The airline didn’t notify me until I learned that I could not fly with the airlines only at the airport when I went for check-in. It was a single ticket with the company and they said they didn't realise I was flying from Canada to India via London. The restrictions didn't allow any via flights but were ok with direct ones. When I booked a single ticket from Canada to India, how come they didn't realise I couldn't fly? No refund at all. Gave me a credit for me to travel anytime in the next two years, but I don't have any travel plans for the next two years. That means my money is gone? When talking to representatives, they ridiculously put everything on the website agents which was 'Onetravel'. The worst experience ever with an airline. Am a frequent flyer, was trying BA for the first time but now I guess I am never going to fly with you. On my return journey, the other flight gave me a full refund when the new travel restrictions didn't allow them to take me. A poor show with BA.

When I call to BA several times their computer system didn’t work and they couldn’t issue new ticket, as the result I had to pay airport price for baggage, as I couldn’t pay online without ticket. They promised to give me compensation of hotel stay, food and travel if complete online form. When I done it, I was asked to submit expenses, but link provided was to lost baggage expenses, not what I claimed. I replied that link is wrong and asked for correct link. They replied that they wouldn’t compensate anything.

review_header: "Do not recommend to anyone in Covid restrictions"
review_text: Do not recommend to anyone in Covid restrictions.

She was an amazing person as she made sure I was feeling okay as I had come back from my surgery and was traveling by myself. She was more then a nurse and took care of my needs like a mom. She also made sure I had eaten my food and stood by next to me as I was feeling awful because I was in lot of pain

review_header: "not what you'd expect from a premium product"
review_text: Fully aware of the covid safety restrictions at the moment, which the staff do an admirable job with - but nevertheless a lot to say on the state of BA First at the moment. Firstly - no lounge at all at Mexico City Terminal 2. There's a paid lounge, but the check in staff wouldn't help with the details. Mexico City Terminal 1 has functional lounges for AeroMexico working. Not good enough for an expensive ticket. Finally got to board and the staff are incredible - but throughout they were super apologetic as to what was to come. The food was literally inedible in First and staff offered commented as much every time. So for an 11 hour trip in First the option really was chocolate or crisps. The first suite on the flight had visible signs of wear and tear and needs some attention. The seat would not easily convert to a bed. It had scuff marks around it and generally looked a bit shabby. Again, not what you'd expect from a premium product. I left my watch on the flight in error and contacted BA immediately about this. Despite assurances that they have a comprehensive cleaning process during Covid my watch was never found. BA has outsourced their lost and found service to a separate company and in the process they have completely washed their hands on helping out customers. Given that I told them specifically where I'd left the watch I can only assume that one of the cleaning staff decided to keep it. All in all, you pay premium on a flight for additional service. BA isn't offering it at the moment. If it is essential that you have to fly really don't bother with first unless you have to - or go to another airline. The company just don't care.

review_header: "43 euros each to check our carry-on"
review_text: Rude, unprofessional staff. Unreliable flights. Uncomfortable seats. Food is expensive and lousy. You need to pay to sit next to your spouse. We were charged 43 euros each to check our carry-on which they claimed was above their limit. We’d checked it for free many times on many airlines because it’s only a small carry on. Uncaring and rude staff. We arrived at counter 3 hours before flight and were told checkin starts at 2 hours. Wasted an hour and returned to a huge lineup. Checkin clerk got in a big fight with customer in front of us. Perhaps took it out on us. Arrived at gate and saw flight delayed by 90 minutes when we had a 100 minute connection. In the end flight was 2.5 hours kate. Next flight was waiting for us and many other connecting passengers. Passengers had boarded on time and waited on plane for 90 minutes for us. Crew refused them water with excuse of limited supply. Crew made an announcement blaming connecting passengers for delay.

On 26-02-24 it was a particularly ugly day in Paris and the loading crew didn't bother to cover the luggage carts carrying luggage to the plane with a tarp or plastic covering as is usually done everywhere in the world across all airports, instead leaving it to get soaked senseless before loading it, causing water to get through into the luggage and cause many items to get wet, among them books, comic books and carton boxes with toys such as Lego or carton boxes with food items. Upon sending a claim to CSA l was told that it is MY problem and that no visible damage has been recognized despite me sending in not only photos of the damage (the CSA claim site allows only two photos in total) but also of the event happening, of which l have both photos and videos. Absolutely disgusting treatment of a frequent flyer customer of the CSA Plus program, if not of all customers in general.

review_header: "I'm being had and that's how it is"
review_text: To flee at all costs. Tickets ordered in 2019 for a flight in 2020. Tickets canceled due to COVID but refusal of reimbursement by the company which sends (without any explanation and without my agreement) vouchers directly following the cancellation emails. A year later, at my request, these vouchers (which are only valid for 1 year) are extended a second time because the company refuses reimbursement (although promised at the end of the validity date) on the pretext that they are in a statute of protection of the firms in bankruptcy and that to obtain a refunding I would have to introduce a procedure near a Czech court! Anyway it's too late because I'm out of time. All this happens via email and with incredible response times (when they dare answer because you have to systematically relaunch them). You don't have to be in a hurry with them. We are now at the end of validity of these second vouchers and I realize that Brussels is no longer even offered as a possible airport (nor any other in Belgium). I contact them directly by phone (in English, which they don't speak very well by the way) and they explain to me that the vouchers will expire in Oct 2022, that I just have to board at another airport that they serve, that they will not reimburse the vouchers and that they will not extend them either. Despite my request, my contact explains to me that no one else within the company can't give me more info. In summary, I'm being had and that's how it is. Two words come to mind: thieves and scampers!

On my requests they answer, that I need to wait. When I ask - how long to wait? - no answer! On top of that, my two previous flights were delayed for more than 24 hours with no reasons. Do not book flights with them.

Unfortunately, my mother suffered an unexpected stroke just before the flight. Due to this medical emergency, I needed to cancel or reschedule only my ticket so I could stay home and support my family, while my wife and children still flew. I contacted Finnair immediately and explained the situation, hoping for some flexibility or a goodwill gesture given the seriousness of the emergency. However, I was told repeatedly that the ticket was non-refundable and non-changeable due to the fare conditions. Finnair refused to offer any refund, rebooking, or voucher — only a cancellation with no reimbursement. Despite providing all relevant information and asking for an exception, the customer service was inflexible and unsympathetic during a very difficult time. I understand fare rules, but I expected some compassion or accommodation for a genuine crisis. This experience has been very disappointing, and I would caution others to carefully consider the risks of purchasing non-flexible “Superlite” fares, especially when travel plans might need to change unexpectedly.

You can change it for free by speaking with customer care. I called the customer care number in Germany and waited for 2 hours before hanging up. I started chatting with their customer care Sisu bot online, waited for 14 hours online for the customer care agent to be connected to, even despite giving the ticket number, names and other details, the customer care agent would not make any changes till we provide the bank details from which the payment was made, since the payment was made three months ago. I asked for few minutes to lookup the details, the agent said that he does not have the time. They later changed the message on the site, saying you can change your ticket using Manage Booking, and if you're charged extra, the money will be refunded as compensation. Still, the Manage Booking is an error even after giving all the details.

Less than three hours before my scheduled 19:30 flight to London, I received an SMS informing me the flight was cancelled. No explanation. No guidance. After frantically trying to reach anyone—from Finnair, another SMS 30 minutes later telling me I’ve been rebooked onto a 21:10 flight. No apology. Just a new time casually thrown at me. At the airport, the Finnair agent confirms the new flight and hands me my boarding pass. I ask about compensation and am told there’s a €17 meal voucher linked to my ticket. A complete fabrication. I go through security, reach the restaurant, and am told no voucher is defined. Back to Finnair customer service—because apparently my evening now belongs to chasing their mistakes. This time, I’m told there’s no voucher because the delay was only 1 hour and 40 minutes, not the two-hour threshold. The cancellation reason: “We didn’t have enough planes today.” Not enough planes? At your own hub? And you find this out only hours before departure? Finnair’s customer service is chaotic, contradictory, and dismissive. The communication is abysmal, and the way they treat paying passengers is borderline contemptuous. Avoid them at all costs—unless you enjoy confusion, misinformation, and utter disregard for your time.

Several weeks before departure, we were informed that our original flight schedule had changed. This new itinerary included a significantly shorter layover in Helsinki. While the notice was given in advance, the reduced transfer time proved to be problematic. Although we just barely managed to catch our connecting flight to Los Angeles, our luggage did not. Upon arrival in LA, we discovered there was no Finnair office at the airport. A local airport representative advised us not to travel far from the city, as this could complicate the delivery of our luggage. Following that advice, we booked a hotel and waited for our luggage, which arrived three days later. In the meantime, we purchased only essential clothing, keeping our spending to a minimum. The airport staff assured us we would be reimbursed for these costs. All our equipment for a West Coast camping trip—an experience we had planned and saved for over several years—was in our checked baggage. The delay forced us to abandon our original plans. While we did our best to salvage the trip by staying in LA, it was far from what we had envisioned. After returning home, I submitted a detailed compensation request to Finnair, including all receipts and a written explanation. The response was automated and offered €150 in cash, or €225 in the form of a Finnair voucher. This falls well short of covering the hotel and essential items we had to purchase. When I followed up with a detailed explanation, I received a reply stating that the money spent on clothing wasn’t truly lost, since we could still wear the clothes. This argument is unhelpful—we neither needed nor wanted those items beyond the emergency, and I would gladly return them if it meant receiving a fair reimbursement. This entire experience suggests a deliberate strategy of delay and denial to avoid fully compensating affected customers. Rather than providing practical assistance, Finnair offered minimal gestures and rigid justifications. Considering the poor communication, mishandling of baggage, disruption of our holiday, and the lack of fair compensation, I would strongly advise against flying with Finnair if you have any other choice.

Our flight was canceled over two months ago, and it’s been a complete nightmare trying to get proper compensation. After the cancellation, we were stranded for 24 hours with no belongings because they also lost our luggage. To make matters worse, there was no information provided at the airport — just a brief email and text. Luckily, we were able to access our email, but this would have been impossible for someone without access to technology or the ability to use it. No ground staff came to speak to us, and there were no staff around to offer any help or guidance. We were left completely on our own to figure out what to do next. Despite repeated follow-ups and providing all the necessary documents, they’ve consistently ignored key points in our claim, delayed responses, and then issued an incorrect compensation amount. They have also ignored our claim for additional costs we incurred due to the cancellation and mishandling of our luggage. What’s worse is that this isn’t even the first time. In the last two years, we’ve had another Finnair flight canceled, and they separately lost our luggage for an entire week on a different trip. This level of incompetence and disregard for customers is completely unacceptable — we expected far better from a major airline.

I bought seats with returns and a day after I received and email from Finnair that they changed my place. I was travelling with my daughter and I wanted to be with her, but they changed it. That's a shame on Finnair - that was my first and last time when this airline.
The cabin looked very clean and the seat was comfortable enough for this quick hop. Early departure and early arrival. Really nice and efficient male purser, Fredrik was just perfect.
Good breakfast. Feel safe. Flight attendants were very professional They take care of you. All was perfect

Premium economy still a good value on Finnair. The cabin chief was competent as I got a problem with only one choice of meal. Im platinum and I was upset to see the poorest service during the dinner on board .. he went to apologize so its good but when you pay 1800 euros you expect a better service concerning the food. The flight attendants have to be more smiley.

I flew back and forth from Tokyo to Stockholm with my 8-month-old baby and my wife. We booked the flight around half a year before the scheduled date and I was trying to use their website to book the type of meals and seats we would need such as a bassinet for our baby. I checked several times after reserving the seats on the website and it seemed to remember the seats I had chosen. Since it was around 20 hours per trip I needed to make sure that we could have a bassinet seat for our baby. Come the day of the flight and we were seated in the middle of the plane with little space and not being able to sleep as I had to hold my child end make sure that people walking by didn't bump into her. It was an excruciating experience and after pleading to the cabin attendant even though said that she would try to get us a seat and come back to me later she never came. Other cabin attendants could not help either as I tried several times. Scared that the same experience would befall upon us on our trip back I had to pay extra to use their wifi and book a front row seat for the next flight when I noticed that the website could not conclude the booking of seats even though it seemed like it would. I had to download their application and book the seat from there due to supposedly faulty software. I was scarred by this experience and knew better than to think my seat would be fine by just booking it this time around so I called their support to double check (which I had to do through my Japanese SIM card which cost even more money). Low and behold the seat I had managed to book in the front row would not be able to have a baby bassinet and there was no indication during the booking that that would be the case. So I asked her to fix it (mind you about a month before said flight) and she said that it could not be arranged and that we had to change flights. The change of flight would cost us a substantial amount extra compared to what we had paid for our ticket and nothing would be covered by them until I created a feedback ticket. We had to lengthen our trip by several days costing us even more money outside of our planned expenses. When she had booked my seat, I asked her if my wife would be sitting beside me or not as she had not said any such thing. No, then we had to pay extra for that seat as well. She didn’t suggest placing my wife in the seat next to me. During the flight back they handled our baggage in such a violent fashion that a wheel was ripped out of its socket and the suitcases were battered and bruised. Also they had made a mistake and the diet selection on our meal had not gone through (thank god I don’t select my meals due to allergies!). I have an open support ticket with them still but they have yet to compensate me and their replies take weeks to arrive.

Finnair kept the gate open 10min longer than scheduled making me to run like mad from one end of the airport to another just to close the gate 30 seconds before I managed to run to it! The lady at the gate: "sorry, try another flight". This was the second time in 10 months the lady does the same! They are late with the first flight, wait 10min with the second and make you run like crazy just to close the gate in front of your nose! When my luggage was delayed they made me pay for the transport of it so that I could get it the same day. Very poor service!!

Such a bad selection of food and drinks. Cramped seats. Will never fly with them again. My flight got delayed almost 4 hours and they lie and refuse to pay compensation which they are required by European law.

Do not fall for that. The service is really bad. When visiting US for just 10 days, I didn’t receive my baggage when I arrived. They sent the bag to a totally different state. From there the bag never made it to my destination. There I was stranded in a foreign land with no luggage. Their customer service is so bad. They do not even bother to update the status or trace your bag

The line stretched through the half length of the terminal hall. Passenger and the poor checkin guy were equally frustrated and stressed. Contract airport lounge decent and not too crowded. Flight to Helsinki uneventful and on time. Helsinki Finnair Platinum lounge as always great in terms of design, F&B, and service. Unfortunately, its opening hours spoiled that good impression. The lounge closes at 5.30 pm, just before all the long haul flights depart and everyone was herded into the next door business class lounge which by then was so crowded that I left. What’s the point of having a wonderful lounge for their most loyal customer and it’s closed at peak hour? The long haul flight had a different configuration with no premium economy washroom, which made the trip to the economy cabin a very long journey with long lines waiting to be greeted by a messy toilet. Service was ok, but catering (or rather the lack of it) was simply insufficient for such a 12hours flight. Finnair does a lot of things right, but the unacceptable opening hours of their premium lounge and their inadequate catering on long haul flights cannot convince me (yet) to make my switch from my usual one world carrier.
Very friendly FA who recognised my OWE status. An acceptable snack with a drink offered on this flight. The cabin looked very clean and in good condition.
Delays, cancellations, compensation almost never paid, always find some excuses to not provide it, also practically no assistance, customer service is impolite and provides irrelevant information

review_header: "okay in the air, on the ground a disaster"
review_text: We were kicked off a fully boarded flight from Osaka to Helsinki for a technical Problem at 2am and advised to make our own hotel arrangements, with no time as to when our flight might leave. There was no Finnair representative at the airport, and we were left stranded in the middle of the night. Communication was awful, with no clear indication as to when our flight would leave. We had to stay at a fairly pricey airport hotel for two nights. When we reached Helsinki a day and a half after out initial arrival time, we were left stranded again, with huge queues, and no hotel rooms again, due to weather - there were maybe 10cm of snow on the ground from what you could see. Only putting a foot down, quite heavily, secured us a hotel room for the night. I arrived home over 50 hours later than planned. My request for compensation and reimbursement of extra cost was batted off. Eventually I was sent a "gift card" which would cover perhaps 50% of my extra expense, not to mention the two full days delay where I was unable to work. Before this massive delay, I had flown with them and they were okay - I picked them for their safety record and modern A350 which is sometimes half empty so you get to sleep. They are okay once they are in the air, everything on the ground is a disaster.

For a national carrier they should be ashamed. Here’s why A) they charged me to use my Amex card. I understand for small retailers the extra service fee is a lot, not for a national airline B) I wanted to change my flight and the chat function could not find my booking reference despite entering it many times. To speak with customer service they were going to charge me 1.70/min including wait time C) only free drink option on board is water & blueberry juice. Give me a break: you can offer coffee or tea. D) I changed my ticket. The price to change showed $143. But the checkout price was $168. No explanation why. And no way to find out since you have to pay to speak to customer service. To the best of my knowledge this isn’t a discount airline. So don’t treat your passengers as though they are lower class citizens. Who charges for customer service? Absurd! Not to mention the flight attendants threw my coat on my lap when I said I didn’t want to getting wet from a dripping wet suitcase. Disgusting behaviour.

No choice of Food, you get what you are given and I wasn't asked if I wanted it. A lentil lasagne, shortly after a chicken sandwich was served. A pack with a wooden knife and fork and off they went. Soon after I was offered a drink. To say the crew were in a rush was an understatement, little to no interaction, just get the job done. Very impersonal. Wifi was $20 for the whole flight for the streaming package, but was very intermittent. For the extra for premium you are just getting a slightly bigger seat.

review_header: "big letdown was the lack of food"
review_text: Contract Miracle lounge among the worst lounges at Bangkok airport. Premium economy seats comfortable, good IFE and service. The big letdown was the lack of food. After takeoff a meager breakfast of a tiny omelet and three potatoes wedges was served, and then nothing for the next 10 hours. Another meal was served just before arrived on this 13h flight This was in premium economy and keeping the guests without food for 10h is simply unacceptable; especially on a day flight. When I told the flight attendant that I was hungry, I was given a 25g pack of pretzel.
And still such uncomfortable seats! Not my choice. And go-to-gate and boarding means totally different things here. Boarding is NOT boarding. It means go-to-gate!

..awful. This is really a review of two tales. First before the flight. Finnair changed the departure time about 5 times. When I subsequently said I wanted to fly the return leg a day later they said I could, for a fee of about £1,300. I pointed out they had changed flight times numerous times and surely this should allow me to change for free? They said the last time was within 20 minutes of the scheduled time so I was not entitled. I then pointed out the change time was much longer once you factored the others changes in but they replied saying as I had accepted these changes they would not budge. Awful customer service. The return flight time was moot anyway as a couple of weeks before travel they cancelled it due to a pilots strike, with no alternatives offered, forcing me to book another return with another airline costing me £400 more. Total shambles. I did get my money back for this cancelled flight quite quickly. So pre-flight, absolutely terrible. As for the flight itself, it was brilliant. The non-reclinable business class seat for Helsinki - Bangkok is a game changer, far more comfortable than the traditional sets offered by other airlines. The food was great, the service attentive and overall it was a brilliant experience. The price of the flight was very competitive, the lounge at Heathrow great, Helsinki airport is terrific. I would have no hesitation making them my airline of choice... if only the strength of the flight was matched by the pre-flight experience.

We had to spend the night at the airport with no one to help us, with 2 small children. Flight rescheduled 1 day and a half later! In all this, they rejected the request for a refund that we were legally entitled to! Worst airline ever, avoid them like the plague!

120€ I supposed to receive later. Today Finnair return my money and took it back. So they just didn’t return my money. And impossible to contact them in any way to fix it. On the website no contact email of help centre, live chat doesn’t work properly. To connect to operator is impossible because the queue is +99 people 24 hours, I tried at 5 am, at 10 am, at 4 pm at 6pm- it’s just literally impossible to contact them. The crew are rude and unfriendly, they don’t like people and don’t have any empathy. In general the worst impression about service I’ve had for all my 200+ flights. And the last but not the least- I recieved my payed twice luggage without 2 wheels. It the worst and the most bitter experience I’ve ever had with airlines. I feel robbed. Give them one star for reaching the point of destination but I will never recommend this airline.

The Asian cabin crew on the flight to Hong Kong was amazing. Unfortunately Platinum Wing is closed for the late departures. The food was good but I still wish they would quit the one-tray service, it feels a little cheap.

I never asked to cancel my flight. It was a nightmare getting a refund for my late traveling partner's flight and rebooking my flight as I was bounced back and forth between my travel agent and Finnair. Ultimately, Finnair, in spite of repeatedly telling me to work with my travel agent, was the only one able to process the refund. Next I my business class flight from DOH to LAX was cancelled about a month before my trip. Finnair would only rebook me on a flight that was 8 hours longer and had an extra layover in spite of the fact that a better flight was available. They refused to book me on the better flight. Overall a terrible experience working with Finnair.

We both also had difficulties connecting to WiFi. Now, the not so good: At LAX, the check-in crew never applied our Global Entry, so we were stuck in the long lines. The Business Class lounge at LAX was just so so, nothing extraordinary and disappointing. (On the other hand, the lounge in Helsinki was good -- food and drinks and enviornment quite comforting.) The flight crew seemed needlessly rushed. For instance, on both legs, the dinner cart rolled up barely an hour after takeoff. We were given salted nuts and a cocktail, but before we had time to finish either one, dinner was served. The menu described two starters and then dinner; both arrived at the same time and on the same crammed tray. My wife had a glass of wine with dinner, and was never offered a second glass. After dinner, the attendants offered dessert, and then were nowhere to be seen. The morning meal was confusing: It was certainly wasn't breakfast, but instead an unidentifiable meat stew. Overall, for a Business-class price, the meals didn't stand out. Finally, compared to other airlines, the seating was narrow and poorly designed. For instance, I'm two meters tall and I felt cramped. Moreover, the 3-point seat belt was very uncomfortable and difficult to manage, even for the attendants. Wi-Fi took a crew member to figure out how to connect; on the LAX leg, Wi-Fi didn't work. (I applied for a refund and got it within a week.) Will we fly Finnair Business again? That, and pardon the pun, is up in the air.

It was my first flight but I know I will not be back. The ground service in the USA was fast, but not very high level. The employee could not handle the reservation system very well, he talked on the phone during the passenger check-in, I have rather unpleasant memories. The crew on the plane was very nice and helpful, here they deserve applause. Unfortunately, what surprised me was the budget cuts in Finnair, because during the 8-hour intercontinental flight, only one meal was served. Before landing, only drinks were served, which was surprising, because usually other airlines serve a meal or at least a cookie. The meal itself was tasty, although there was no possibility of choice, because everyone got a vegetarian meal (which was fine for me), however, it is the first time I have encountered that there was no possibility of choosing a meal. I am already surprised that there was no pillow on a night flight and only a small blanket. This is not a low-budget airline but I felt as if I was flying with such an airline. Unfortunately, I am very disappointed. I will probably never have a choice again, my leg will not stand on a Finnair plane.

The food is pathetic, small and tasteless. The service is only just service. I had a comfort seat which was good but from what I could see of Business class there wasnt a lot of difference. Their seats are bigger but they got the same food and from I could nothing more. It was really good to have Qantas on at least one leg on my trip and there was a very noticeable difference in everything. So much better than Finnair!

Plane was an old aircraft but was very well kept and clean. Crew were very friendly and engaging. Seat was comfortable and enough space with big windows as well Washroom was very small and there was no water apparently as they locked the sink but kept a lot of wipes. It was a very short flight. But it makes me want to fly again with Finnair maybe on a longer route someday.

Flight to HEL uneventful and on time. Transfer at HEL airport as always a breeze, Finnair Platinum lounge delightful with good a la carte restaurant, friendly service and sauna. Flight delayed by 2 hours due to technical issue and missed slot. Delay well communicated at lounge. Flight itself uneventful with decent food and service onboard anweist and comfortable A350. Flight arrived at BKK airport with a 125 min delay. Wifi did not work throughout the flight.

Miracle contact lounge very average. Boarding well organised. The newish gorgeous A350 clean, bright and comfortable. IFE good, service friendly. The only downside of this 13h flight was the breakfast, which was poor in quality and quantity. There was simply too much time till the next meal 11 hours later, which was surprisingly good. WIFI did not work throughout the flight Transfer in Helsinki was fast. Finnair platinum lounge very crowded with no available seat. Short flight uneventful with punctual arrival.

This was a codeshare flight with ticket booked via Qatar Airways. The new Business Class seat on Finnair has a peculiar feature in that it does not recline and achieves its flatbed position through sliding mechanism. It is not the most comfortable seat around. Finnair's onboard service was outstanding and the WiFi worked.

Additionally, she provided inaccurate information about the status of our flight, which added to our frustration. The flight itself was disappointing. The legroom was extremely limited, making an 8-hour journey uncomfortable. Moreover, only one complimentary meal was provided, which is unusual for such a flight. We frequently travel this route with various airlines, all of which provide two meals on long-haul flights. This was our first experience with only one complimentary meal. I would not recommend this airline to anyone

Due to my back pain, I decided to put a backpack in a small trolley. I used 2 trolleys which were both small. I flew business class via Helsinki to Asia. Given the initial flight was announced to be delayed and the connection time was short, I decided to not to check in the trolleys. At the gate the agent told me it was policy that I could not have 2 trolleys. I begged and told him about the delay and chance of missing the flight. He would not have it so I took out the backpack and had to abandon the trolley. He laughed and told me I should have just carried the backpack in the first place. When I asked for his name, he threatened to weigh my items. From a policy point of view, he was not wrong but 1. The flight was quite delayed. 2. I'm begging him 3. I'm flying business which was empty. He enjoyed abusing power, I'm sure me saying I'm traveling business gave him a power trip. Especially threatening to weigh my items and laughing at me why I did not just use my sore back to carry my backpack was very bad experience. Never Finnair again, never expected this from non low cost business class

But seat was really hard after only 3 hours from Helsinki. The leg from Madrid was a shared code on an Iberia plane. Late 50 minutes and only had 50 minutes lay over in HEL so i thought for sure that i would miss my connection to KEF. Luckily Finnair was waiting. But Finnair only gives you water and blueberry juice for free. Not even a tiny snack or a soda. And the offerings in the menu were not even barely appealing. Power food: oatmeal with some yogurt? Tiny cup of pasta. Mix of cheeses? Tiny sandwiches? They also made me weigh my carry on luggage even though i paid full fare. Not a cheap flight so i didn’t expect a cost cutting airline. Free Wifi for what? No movies. Only some audio books and magazines? Travel brochures they were. You had to pay to read a real magazine. No music options either. Never again unless i have to go to HEL.
Finnair food could be better but the cabin crew is amazing most of the times.
Friendly staff. They love to feed you complimentary blueberry juice, which the whole family loved. They did great with a transfer that was running a little late - kept our stress levels to a minimum.

They don't want to see us at any stage of the journey, really. Flew LIN-HEL-SIN in J class on 29 June 2024 and found the Finnair experience quite strange: the check-in at LIN was a zoo and the person at the counter clearly had no clue who printed us wrong boarding passes; ran through to check-in again to get new boarding passes; finally got through security and found ourselves in the strangest lounge on earth that gave us a beautiful tarmac view, as well as room-temperature prosecco. In Italy, can this really happen? Yep, it is true! Had the cheapest possible pasta dish on board worth maybe 3-4€/4-4.50 USD (no dessert included!) during the 2½ hour flight, and touched down at HEL on time. Off to the lounge after a quick automated border control - so sorry but the Premium Lounge is closed at 5:30PM already and you should be happy what we have on offer during the peak travel season: the usual lounge at gate 52 where the seats/sofas are not suitable for a proper nap, not to mention foods that are heavily downgraded from our last visit in 2023 - were extremely lucky to visit the Premium Lounge on our way to BOM and DEL several times over the past 12 months where the lounge came with proper food and areas for work and relax between flights. Not on the late night flights after Covid-19 any longer (HKG and SIN) - we're cutting costs at Finnair, sorry! Off to the flight: they check us in to the strange cow shed 50 min before boarding at gate 52, and everybody is wondering what happens next since half of the premium passengers are left out there as they cannot possibly fit in to the small cow shed ("Boarding" is displayed, however). Finally we board and the rest turns out to be equally amusing: the champagne is the same lowest-end brand on the market served lukewarm from HEL (opted for the sparkling water!), and the meals are heavily downgraded since "we do our best to reduce food waste". Why don't you put it all to food waste in the first place - the meals ex-Helsinki are mediocre at best and the best idea would be to include food packs from the Premium Lounge to save the cabin crew the stress to serve meals at night to weary travellers - the meals on board Finnair seem to be some utterly cheap compositions that nobody likes, really. Who designs them in the first place? Should be fired, really. In conclusion, Finnair brands itself as a high-end brand with a number of benefits for J class - however, the reality is this: it's primarily cheap, cheap and cheap. Flights are usually on time, but the rest is hopelessly cheap.

First leg operated by Norra. Nice crew. Food ok. Last leg by Finnair. Crew very friendly and attentive. Food also good. Overall good experience. Only minus is Finnair Schengen lounge in Helsinki. The level of food there is below all standards. Wines ok.

We only got given water once during the 3 hours and I am surprised I did not pass out, once we got off we were told to go to immigration and collect our bags to stay the night. N Finnair representative was present and we were left to find our own hotel and way to a hotel at 2:30 am in Hong Kong as a family of 5 with 2 15 year olds. We then have a rescheduled flight for the next day at 1pm and when we get there they tell us it is cancelled and we must get a rebooked flight which we do through turkey however the next day (we actually got a hotel booked by Finnair this time). We line up and turkish Airlines tell us Finnair put us on an overbooked flight and for the third day we cannot leave Hong Kong, we then go back to Finnair check in and they find us a flight in 30 mins and we end up having to sprint to make the flight. We get to Helsinki and they booked our flight to our final destination 13 hours after we arrive in Helsinki, we change it to 4 pm arrival instead of 10pm however there was a 9 am flight available but Finnair refused to pay for a 1 hour business class upgrade for this flight to Riga. We arrive in Riga going through Talinn and 2 out of our 5 checked in bags are not with us and I am still waiting for my bag. Terrible handling of the situation, it couldnt have been any worse, delayed our family visit by 4 days. Do not fly Finnair, you pay for good problem solving, when it goes smoothly it doesn't matter, you need good service for when things go wrong.

Despite having a business class ticket, the service provided was abysmal. I have a medical condition that severely limits my mobility, making it difficult for me to walk or sit without assistance. When I arrived at the service desk at Delhi Airport, the staff were rude and unhelpful, I was left waiting for an unacceptably long time for wheelchair assistance. I had a luggage allowance of 32kg x 32kg. I requested to distribute my allocated weight into three pieces of luggage for easier handling. However, the staff refused. I had requested a Jain meal due to my dietary restrictions, but no such meal was provided on the flight. I will never recommend Finnair to anyone.

I have a disability and needed my hand luggage on my flight for a specific purpose, went to the check-in counter to see if I’ll be allowed. The guy was so fixated in charging for a small suitcase I was bringing on that he totally missed what I was saying and kept talking about costs. He said they will figure it out at the gates. At the gate the lady said I can’t bring it on (could have paid for it at the check in counter) and I have to check it in which cost 60 euros more. Doesn’t seem like they support people with disabilities or even take the time to hear out the passengers request. They were so fixated and focused on getting the 60 euros from me!

When they served in-flight purchased meals and drinks, I read on the on board menu that I can pay with Avio points and I reconfirmed that with the flight attendant. He put hot water to our cup noodles and served us drinks. After that he said there is a difficulty to get our profile because of they didn’t get full name list for travellers and we cannot pay with Avio points, implying we should pay by credit card now. After some hustle, I was able to pay all my and my partner’s food and drink from my points. If I would have needed to pay by my pocket, I wouldn’t even order the cup noodles that were never cooked with their lukewarm water. In addition to previous episode of avio point purchase, no one collected my paper cup and noodle cup filled with water for long time until I returned them all the way to the back of the plane. There was a crew member just chatting with her passenger friend while I walked past her holding my garbage. All in all, not so professional service despite expensive ticket price and cutting all in-flight services and luggage allowance. They still have customers just because there isn’t much competition in flying direct from Helsinki.

Transfer in Helsinki was seamless and quick. When you fly economy you are assigned seats even on long-haul flights without possibility to change it at checkin, at a counter or even onboard if there are seats. There was a passenger, very tall man 190-200cm that asked politely if he could change to a seat that was free that would then give him better space for the legs. He was taken back to his original seat 2 rows back and that better seat was free for the 13,5 hour flight. I tried to change my seat to a window seat instead of isle at checkin, impossible. PAY PAY PAY, and my ticket was not cheap at all as I booked very late. The meals was below substandard on the longhaul, a small paperbox with food that had dried, no bread, nothing. It was tiny. You receive soft drinks and 1 wine or beer. After that nothing. So conclusion is, if you fly long-haul with Finnair - bring your own food, like a cup of noodle. Otherwise you will be starving. It was the same on the return flight. The entertainment was limited and very old. Boring. Never again with Finnair.
Yet I had to pay 150 eur for baggage They only served me one meal on a 14 hour flight.  On a two hour flight they only served water. Coffee was chargeable

The super mini portions both for late dinner and breakfast were plain horrible. Not only bland but really bad. I did not order special meals but will be doing so on the return in September just to check if, by some kind of magic, that could improve the experience though my expectations are now super super low. Should I add that, believe it or not, there was NO sparking water. None at all apparently or the crew was too lazy to get some from the business class. I am not drinking alcohol but was kindly offered to drink some instead of sparkling water. Also facing high sugar issues due to pancreas surgery I avoid sugary or artificially sweetened drink. I asked for a large bottle of water. The crew said they would get some but never did. Very little interaction with the crew members who, most of the time, were busy at the back of the plain, with themselves. Having visibly a great time. Should I mention that I am one of those top tier frequent flyers. For those with no status rest reassured that it made absolutely no difference at all for the crew. Anyway very poor Finnair service. Absolutely not enjoyable at all on that flight. I am writing this review as I just discovered that apparently I boarded the first flight to Singapore enjoying the "summer menus". Marketingwise Finnair is doing a fantastic job describing them on their website but in the air that is a complete different story. Awful. Shameful. Was that an error? I asked the crew but they said no. Not an error. Same incredibly poor food offering in Economy AND Premiums Economy. So basically you only pay double or more in Premium compared to Economy for the privilege of enjoying a much better seat (yes very comfortable indeed) as well as a better headset and blanket. First airline in the Oneworld alliance making that step to my knowledge. I am NOT positively impressed at all. Plus the service in general on board that flight was really poor. Shame on you Finnair! Last comment: the only item from the food offering I enjoyed was the large yoghurt served with the tiny omlet before landing in Singapore. Creamy, tasty and not much sugar (total).

Just horrible. We were dealt in a rude, cold, inhumane manner from start to end. The airport personnel was just disgusting in a way we never encountered, anywhere in the world. The plane was dirty, crowded and unpleasant. The staff was rude and disgusting. We will surely never fly with Finnair. Such a disgrace!

Seats are in a 1-2-1 configuration. Very comfortable with nice storage compartments. Amenity kit pretty modest. Entertainment system offers enough movies for 10 hours flight. Good selection of music and games. Champagne for welcome drink, quite tasty starter and main meal with 3 options to choose - everything on one single tray. The service provided by the crew was just ok. Professional but no extra smile. All in all that was comfortable flight with some room for improvement. I really like the modern cabin, fully flat seats/beds, selection of movies. And a price - that was much cheaper than similar service of competitors. Amenity kit, meals, selection of alcohol, service onboard could be better and more friendly.

Before boarding we noticed the cabin crew had no company logo on their uniform as they were local outside contractors. The seating situation onboard was abysmal, I cannot comprehend how this carrier has made this enormous plane so squished - there were several additional rows of seating than what was in our QANTAS plane on the way to BKK, which in turn meant far less legroom (nearly 3 inches less) smaller seats and nowhere to stand and stretch - which was a godsend on the QANTAS flight on the way there. The food was poor and so was the service with myself and my daughter skipped twice during food service. My Wife's chair had a broken armrest and the chair would in turn not recline. The entertainment was average at best. Pilot was great with a very smooth landing. Overall a very poor experience - definitely would not recommend.

This was a codeshare with Qatar Airways which is where my ticket was booked. While Finnair's product does not approach the level of comfort and sophistication of Qatar Airways, it is nevertheless a respectable experience. The peculiar seat design - the Business Class seat does not recline but it still a flatbed - is not the most optimal but I survived. Service was warm and presented with a smile.

Staff was mainly very unfriendly and had poor service mentality. For example, they made me forcibly take out the tray table while serving food instead of doing it themselves, and made me uncomfortable in several other ways too. Food was tasteless and simply bad with small portion sizes. It very much resembled the typical economy class food and was served in the same way from a trolley at certain times. The main course had two cardboard-like dry pieces of bread that I left untouched. Food options were limited. It was not possible to order a dessert at the same time as the starter and main; instead, I received a rude comment saying "you'll get dessert when it's the time for it." The seat without a reclining or adjustable backrest is just horrible unless your physique happens to fit the shape. The space for your feet not being concentric to the seat is such a bad design decision that it's unbelievable. I had feet and backpain as a result of spending nearly seven hours in the p.o.s. space that is supposed to be business class comfort. The entertainment system had a malfunction mid-flight and despite the attempt from the crew never recovered. Most of the content remained unaccessible for the second half of the flight. TL;DR: avoid Finnair business class. Fly with almost any other option available from the otherwise excellent Helsinki airport.

The TV screen was all greasy from the previous passengers. It looked like it was not cleaned at all. The wifi was not working on the flight at all. When you see how much Finnair charges for this flight you'll understand that things like this are a problem.

They upgraded me only so I had to contact their somewhat rude and not very competent customer service who then, after some back and forth and some heated discussion somehow miraculously managed to upgrade us both. Ten hours before the flight we got a notification the aircraft had to be changed, the new one doesn't have premium economy so I was moved to business and my partner to economy. Had to contact them again and be like 'hey, again, we're traveling together' please put us both in business class or economy. 'Sorry no availability' and they just close the customer service chat. Then contact them again, and same story again 'please put us then both in economy'. They eventually did, no effort made to put us eg in the first row or exit row, to mediate the whole thing. We flew back on this 13 hour and 45 minute flight, during which my partner didn't get the meal he ordered. I wrote a complaint about it when I came back and got a copy/pasted 'thank you for your input, we take it seriously to improve our services'. And that's all. I'm a platinum flyer and my partner is gold. That's the treatment. I've been flying with Finnair for about 15 years as my primary airline and half of that time as gold/platinum and I can say that their service has completely deteriorated. It was never amazing to begin with but in the past 5 years or so it's become a joke. The prices are premium, the service is a bad joke.

After relutancly rebooked my connection flight to the next day, they said they do not issue voucher in Paris. How can they sell connections through Paris and don't have such Service for cases like this? Expected more from a company from finland.
The aircraft was very comfortable, clean spaceous and the crew was spot on. We will defenitly travel with them in the future and recomend Finnair to any friends and family.
The food and drink offering sits somewhere at the middle of the pack of legacy airlines but given the economy superlight ticket price this is fair. The product is excellent.

Check-in at Dubai was quite chaotic with a long priority queue (and even longer economy queue). Maharba lounge in Dubai is acceptable - nothing to write home about. An old A330-302 is used on the Dubai route and the business class is the old version. The plane is showing it's age but the seats are in fairly good condition nevertheless. There was a slight delay in take-off due to a suspected brake issue that turned out to be a false alarm. The crew were pleasant enough and service was perfunctory. Pre-takeoff drinks were served and the meal service was fairly quick after takeoff. The meal itself was OK but not memorable. As this was a late night flight all passengers soon prepared the seat for sleeping. It was not the most comfortable as there was no bed pad provided - only a duvet/pillow. About an hour before landing the cabin lights were put on and a rather dry cheese roll was distributed along with drinks. Connecting passengers have to pass through a security check in Helsinki so need to have separated liquids in hand luggage. The lounge in Helsinki was quiet at the early hour we visited (7am) but spotlessly clean with self service food and drink selections available (oddly, there were no tea bags). The flight from Helsinki to London was on a new A350. The new business class seats were installed and are very comfortable. No amenity kit or blankets/duvets are provided due to the relatively short duration of this leg. There is a single food service which is breakfast and was all good quality and tasty. We landed early but ended up on a remote stand at Terminal 3. Overall our experience was great but I do hope Finnair update or replace the old A330 (OH-LTN) soon.

We used the express security lane, but this ended up taking as long as the regular line due to some disorganised passengers. Once through Security, we made use of the lounge until our flight. On board the aircraft was spotlessly clean. The pilots were Finnish and the Cabin Crew were Indian. Cabin crew members were all friendly and welcoming and did a great job looking after the passengers. The flight was slightly late leaving, but time was made up on the way and we actually arrived in Delhi slightly early. The food was nicely presented. The salmon caviar and onion / beetroot puree did not appeal to my personal taste, but I enjoyed the chicken curry and both desserts. The seat was comfortable enough to sit in, but lying on it was a bit cramped and uncomfortable. I suffer from claustrophobia when I am in a confined space and lying my back with my legs in the small space felt like lying in a coffin, so when lying, I lay on my sides. I would have preferred the old style seats commonly used by airlines to these seats. They were easy to maneuver into the sleeping position though. There was a reasonable selection of entertainment for the length of the flight, but I was disappointed that the map did not track the aircraft's path and flight. The rest of my family were well looked after and our children got a few hours sleep and we woke them just before the descent. The captain made a nice firm landing into Delhi and all 6 of our bags were safely waiting for us at the baggage carousel when we arrived at it 30 minutes later. A common complaint with reviewers in Skytrax is luggage going missing. I recommend to everyone that you remove the tags and barcode stickers from your luggage either when you collect it, or before you next check it in as machinery in the luggage system may misread and spit luggage with old barcodes out leading to baggage handling mistakes.

Boarding was slow due to a large group of disorganised passengers who were blocking the middle of the aircraft, but we pushed back pretty much on time. On board, the crew were very smartly dressed and genuinely friendly, welcoming and helpful. The aircraft (OH-LZS) was clean and tidy - actually I'd say spotless. I was disappointed that for a 3 hour flight, there were no films available on screens and the WIFI had to be paid for, so accessing films via a tablet was not an option. I think Finnair can improve here and also put in some seats with a bit more padding when they refresh the aircraft's interiors. We did purchase some food, which was medicre - my son was not impressed with the pizza, but last night, we did have the most amazing pizzas in Rome which will be hard to beat. The blueberry juice is nice and although I was disappointed that the food I ordered was covered in mayonnaise - it was a generous portion. Disembarking was delayed by about 10 mins due to an issue with the Jetbridge, but this was out of Finnair's control and it meant that our 5 bags were waiting for us on the belt when we arrived to collect them.
All our jackets were in the luggage’s and gods knows when they are gonna come to us. The whole journey was fills delays and technical errors

Free Hand luggage is restricted to 1 bag 40x30x15cm. You have absolutely no choice to choose your seat without a fee. You get assigned one and if you want to change to another one, even if it is in for example the middle seat on the other side of the isle, you still have to pay 9 EUR. in addition, the way they communicate the new baggage rules is like policing. The check in desk monitor threatens with "Your carry on luggage will be controlled by the crew" or something like that. I do understand that there might be issues with large amount of carry on luggage but why punish everyone for a few people not being able to follow simple rules? I feel so sorry for the crew that has to endure such awful tactics from a airline that was once the greatest amongst the nordic carries. Sad and stupid. Now I will try to fly Norwegian or BRA on my weekly trips between Stockholm and Helsinki.

We were delayed 1+ hours do to a faulty machine part that needed to be replaced. The staff told us repeatedly during the wait and flight that due to expected tail wind we would easily make the expected arrival time. Turns out we were 1 hour late, which was not announced until we landed. The business class seats are the most uncomfortable I have ever experienced. They do not adjust, and if you're tall as I am (192cm) you simply can not get comfortable lying down or sitting up.  I had to return earlier, but the business class ticket was non-refund/non-changeable. I do not remember signing up for non-changeable Business class ticket? The food was really good.
Apologies from the captain and cabin crew received. Really friendly service on this short hop. The sandwich was good and a small bottle of wine was fine too.

review_header: "no room left for our cabin bags"
review_text: My children and I were therefore in different groups. I asked if we can all board in group 3, and they said no, we all need to board with the last group. This is the first time I was denied this request, which seemed weird since usually airlines board families with young children first. Anyway, we boarded last, and when we got on the plane people were boarding from both the front and the back. Apparently for some reason the airline boarded half the passengers from the back, even those with seats in the front. People were struggling to get to their seats since there were coming both ways. When we managed to reach our seats, there was no room left for our cabin bags, because the other passengers put pretty much anything but cabin bags in the overhead lockers. Coats, jackets, handbags, backpacks, toys, you name it. I would have expected the cabin crew to ask people on a full flight at least hold their jackets on their lap and put their handbags under their seats. We had to reshuffle items in the overhead lockers to find some space for the cabin bags, without any assistance from the cabin crew.

But they are clearly a budget airline masquerading as premium. Firstly, they charge an extortionate fee (over £300) for selecting a business class seat. Then, they secretly changed their business class baggage allowance from 2 32kg suitcases to 1 23kg suitcase for flights between Asia and Europe. By the time of the flight they had changed the luggage allowance back to 2 32kg suitcases, but the officious, arrogant, rude and aggressive check in manager in Hong Kong refused to allow more than one suitcase, despite the alliance having changed back. He was demanding an extra £200 to check in another suitcase. It was an awful experience and I will never book a ticket with them again.
The plane was too cold and beverages were not that good or worth the cost. Cabin crew could have been more helpful. An ok level flight but not worth the price.

Priority security pretty efficient. Used CX lounge which was quiet. Late boarding via bus gate, not to blame Finnair. Friendly welcome from the purser who came around for a chat before departure. Mostly Thai crew was also friendly and accommodating. The food was surprisingly tasty and the crew went through the cabin often with fruit, chocolate, snacks etc. I’m one of those who like the new seat which gives a lot of privacy.

Got to check in, issued boarding passes and when I (thankfully) looked at them noticed some high looking seat numbers for business class, turned out I had been downgraded with no mention of this from the check-in agent at all. Told aircraft change to blame but no effort otherwise to put things right, rhetoric was to call the customer services in Finland. Calling them was a total waste of time as they refused to acknowledge I had even been downgraded. Was treated so badly and was basically given ultimatum of sit in economy or don't go. Return flight was horrendous, check in was utter chaos, no priority at all. Plane was ancient and tatty and crew were cold. The main meal was of meagre portions, mostly peasant fare of boiled beetroot with a blob of cream cheese. For breakfast a cheese roll in plastic was served, no plate just a paper napkin and this was business class. Avoid them at all costs, don't take a chance as its highly likely you won't end up travelling the class you booked and if even if you do its on a par with other carriers economy anyway.
My refund was approved in March 2022 and I still not get the money, despite extensive e-mail correspondence. They only find excuses not to pay.
Seats are horrible without any adjustments. Either you sit straight up or lie down. Nothing in between. Cabin crew is mostly out of sight and the menu is poor.

I'll still never flying Finnair again but will note these improvements: the Singaporean staff were gracious and helpful and the extremely long flight was broken by having the lights dulled so we were able to sleep. What hasn't changed is the barely edible food and the 10-hour wait between the first and second meal. This time we were prepared by bringing on our own sandwiches and snacks.

We boarded at 07:30 and were fed breakfast of scrambled eggs, tomato, potatoes and spinach, all overcooked, 2 hours later. Dinner arrived at 18:00 - 8.5 hours later! Once again, there was no choice of meal and, although we'd waited so long, the couscous was inedible and we left it. Both meals were served in unappealing brown boxes. During this time the flight attendants weren't to be seen, except to very occasionally walk through and offer water. Cordial, water, coffee and biscuit were available self-serve at the back of the aircraft. A small blanket of inadequate size was provided but no pillows. None of this is acceptable on a flight of this length and we're dreading the return flight which will take 12h 35m overnight.
Very cold and unwelcoming cabin crew and not a personalised service. Unfriendly. Avoid this airline if you want to enjoy your flight with friendly cabin crew.

review_header: "Dreading the return with those terrible seats"
review_text: Platinum section in the Finnair lounge in Helsinki staffed by friendly enthusiastic team, good selection of drinks and al la carte dining. Boarded flight to Bangkok on time, unfortunately the IFE screen was faulty, moved to another seat without a problem. Food was the worst that I have had on a long haul business class trip, greasy and unappealing. The new seat design is one of the most uncomfortable that I have ever sat in...made the 12 hour flight very long! Crew visible in the cabin frequently, always friendly and helpful. Dreading the return with those terrible seats, made a note to eat at the airport before I board.

Local Chinese crew, very friendly and polite, maybe except a somewhat grumpy male FA.. Two starters were once again served together with the main course. Tasted good. The dessert was rather boring. Early arrival to Helsinki. Then a short flight to Stockholm. Once again a lovely purser who served the usual sandwich with a big smile.

Flying from Singapore to London. After checking-in and going through the boarding gates, I received an email that said that I had been rebooked on British Airways (direct flight). My happiness was short-lived as the transfer counter shared that the flight did not exist. The email was erroneously sent with no explanation. We were wrongly sent to the transfer counter and we queued in vain. There was confusion and a lack of staff to assist and guide. Another staff tried to send us back to the boarding gate, moving us around like sheep with no explanation. Eventually, the flight to Helsinki retimed by 11 hours. We had to go back home, only to check in again in the wee morning. We arrived to find a long queue as they did not have enough staff to check in. We only boarded another 2 hours later. Upon reaching Helsinki, the staff shared that they had no idea about my connecting flight from Helsinki to London. They were making things up as they went. Eventually they rebooked us on an afternoon flight to London the next day. Our family had to spend the night in Helsinki instead of the original 2 hour layover. We essentially lost 2 days of our vacation in London. No words can fully express my disappointment in the airline's planning and staff. It was my dream to bring my elderly parents to London for their retirement trip but this experience thoroughly ruined the start of it. Please think twice before flying with Finnair.

Nightmare. Flying from Singapore to Bruxelles. Flight to Helsinki retimed by 11 hours. I received an email that said that I had been rebooked on British Airways flight. Rush to the transfer counter just to find out that the flight did not exist. Went back home to check in again the morning after to find a queue of hours because they do not have enough staff to check in. And they have no idea about my onward flight from Helsinki- just say to get to Helsinki and they will figure it out. I will likely need to spend the night in Helsinki for what was supposed to be a 2-hour connection. Worse airline experience ever

Our then 6 year old daughter was afraid of flying. So we had written confirmation we could sit together on the airplane. When entering the plane, both our daughters were placed alone, next to a stranger. We asked the air host to seat us together (it was a small plane, 2 seats each side, first leg of the trip to Helsinki). She refused, daughter crying. Luckily two passengers stepped in and let our daughter sit together. We got the names of these passengers and afterwards complained to Finnair. First they refuse to admit this ever happened. Then we asked them to contact the witness, they never did. We showed our written correspondence with Finnair from before the flight - they ignored it. Later we found out that we should be sitting together - then they offered us 50 USD discount on future tickets.
I missed my connecting flight in Helsinki, and she professionally handled all the things.

Crew was outstanding, very attentive and seemed to be genuinely happy to have us aboard. The new style seats work great! Sleep was some of the best I have had on long hauls. Food was excellent. As we flew out of LAX I was surprised the food seemed to be authentic Finnish and not from the kitchens in Los Angeles. We had a very tight connection in HEL going on to OSO and had no trouble getting through the airport on onward to Oslo. Cost of flight was very competitive. We will certainty fly them again and next time we will stay a few days in HEL to see the city!
Food was good but the presentation could be somewhat better. Don’t like the post-covid “one-tray-service “ The crew was attentive and friendly.

review_header: "saying we are out of time to make a claim"
review_text: Upon our return (same route), Finnair checked in one of our carry on baggage and when we retrieved the baggage in Hong Kong, the handle was broken and we have been unable to use the bag since. We immediately filed a damage baggage report (the day after we landed) and Finnair decided to not do anything about it until I recently messaged their customer service team on why there was no update on our report. Finnair has denied responsibility in: 1. Accepting that they broke our luggage 2. Acknowledging that they made us wait over 6 months to get a response. That too, only because we started to contact their customer service!! Finnair are now saying we are out of time to make a claim for damaged baggage. This is incredibly shocking customer service for an airline that has factually broken our luggage and now refusing to take any responsibility for it. My advice is to avoid Finn Air at all costs necessary, particularly if you value your luggage and the money you spend on buying luggage. If I could give 0 stars, I absolutely would.

This is a low cost carrier with premium prices. Expect to pay for absolutely everything starting from luggage on long haul flights, food, beverages and seat selection. Portions of meals they’re serving are minimal, will not sustain you on an 11 hour flight. The IFE crashes a lot. The seats are narrow and cramped.

We upgraded to premium economy on the way back. Unfortunately 1 of the hand luggage items was 2kg too heavy. Finnair forced us to check it in at an extra cost of 120 euro. A 2.5% upsell by a very uncooperative desk lady has now cost you a customer. Never again. We flew business class on the way in. Food is the worst business class food. In premium economy the equipment Was not working.

Paid $260USD several months ago for "exit row" extra legroom" seat both directions (booked directly with Finnair). I have receipts and actually had confirmed assigned seats (that I paid for) up until just minutes before the flight. Then all of a sudden they changed my seating to a regular seat (not even extra legroom) as I was boarding and didn't provide an explanation. They just said to apply for a refund on their website and that they could no longer accommodate my seating request as the "system" automatically adjusts and reassigns seats prior to boarding. Well, I filled out all the refund forms on their website, waited a few days, and received a one-sentence reply telling me "seat extras are not refundable" (which is ridiculous because they charged me for something and didn't deliver the product they sold). On top of that my exit row seat on the return flight in two weeks has "disappeared" without reason as well. I will have to resort to a chargeback on my credit card and fly this horrible airline back home to Dallas in a regular seat (to be assigned at check-in). They simply do not care, and I hope other experienced travelers heed my advice. I'm also a OneWorld Ruby member, which means absolutely nothing to this airline but puts this review in perspective that I fly a lot. Please FLY A DIFFERENT AIRLINE IF YOU CAN.
A bit dirty and worn planes and not very friendly service. Would choose something else if they did not have a monopoly on flights to Finland.

Good legroom in the first row of European style Biz class with empty middle seat. Very friendly purser who also acknowledged my frequent flyer status. The catering was okay considering that it’s only a 45 minutes flight, love especially the Iittala glassware. Wifi didn’t work but not a big deal.
The experience made me sad: visibly dirty plane, (obviously) the same seating as in couch, food like from school cafeteria. The flight attendant was friendly.

The person at checking counter was rude, she was literally saying "I see no added bag, now pay or leave yours behind". Even though my mother had been showing her the booking confirmation with clear text extra baggage with it. My senior mother, that time frustrated and tired, lacking the language capacity to explain herself, decided to just leave the luggage behind. Contacted customer service afterward, they wrote "As it was not associated with the flights, it seems it has caused the airport to not be able to see it upon checking the reservation." How could a bag even be "not associated with the flight"? I even booked it together with the flight. They offered a refund for the purchase fee of the extra bag, but just tell us to "contact the airport" for the 20kg bag that we were forced to leave behind.

I no longer could check-in in advance. So I had to arrive to the airport earlier, even though I didn't have a bag to check in. When I got to the check in, they said they can't find my booking, they only see the economy but they see that has been cancelled but they don't see the business one. Ten minutes of angry conversation with the person at check in and at the end I had to go to Finnair's website, queue in the chat feature, while everybody is waiting behind, and the person in the chat did something and suddenly my reservation popped up and they could check me in. So much drama and hassle and waste of everyone's time just because their system broke down from a simple business class upgrade. And then the meal in business class. Since I had marked 'vegetarian', I got few slices of raw tofu on a salad leaf (breakfast meal). Raw tofu slices! Just plain old unseasoned, but oh so vegetarian tofu. Like, who eats raw tofu and for breakfast. Anyway, I've been flying Finnair a long long time, and if I'd write about every bad experience I'd be contributing a lot here. The service has deteriorated catastrophically. In recent years I refer to Finnair as 'premium priced for no apparent reason' or 'low cost airline with premium pricing'. I see others have started to refer to it in similar ways too. Very sad.

..with only water and blueberry juice and coffee. Breakfast? Whatever you buy if you like cheese. Because that's the breakfast option, that is not included in your ticket. Flight crew numbers have been reduced, so restrooms will sure become pretty interesting after the fifth hour. Even crew itself feels it (8-hr flight, you have a chance to talk with them).
