The FA’s were very attentive, polite and had smiles. The on-board WIFI was OK but slow. The IFE had a wide selection and easy to navigate. The flight left on time and arrived early. In summary, the experience on both flights was great onboard but seriously subpar on the ground (except for Lounge Istanbul) entirely due to TK’s rude, indifferent and inefficient ground staff.

For the meal, the salad with tomatoes and mozzarella cheese was ok and this came with an olive and lemon dressing. The turkey sandwich was also amazing. For dessert, the little chocolate vanilla cake was not bad. We arrived on time but we had to taxi 20 minutes. The WiFi wasn’t available, but the inflight entertainment made up for it. Overall, great flight and definitely flying with Turkish Airlines again!

Instead of providing proper assistance or taking responsibility for the disruption, Turkish Airlines rebooked us for a flight the following day — without any explanation or apology. What made the situation even worse was the treatment we received at Istanbul Airport. Since we were forced to stay overnight, we had to go through immigration. The immigration officers were unprofessional and dismissive. Despite traveling with a 4-year-old child, we were denied entry because his passport was due to expire in three months. We were charged a visa fee of nearly $300 USD — an unreasonable amount considering the circumstances. The entire process lacked basic empathy, transparency, and customer care. Unfortunately, both Turkish Airlines and Istanbul Airport failed to meet the most basic standards of service.

The seats have so much recline that meal trays were difficult to use. Food served was above average in taste and portions were generous. Soft beverages, beer and wine were complimentary. After meal service, the flight attendants basically disappeared until the last two hours of the flight. No mid-flight snack or beverage service was offered. Service call button requests were ignored and turned-off. No effort was made to pickup trash during the flight, so the cabin was trashed when deplaning. A large cleaning crew with vacs and face masks was waiting to board. Onboard experience leaves much to be desired. Will not fly Turkish again.

The transfer desk rescheduled us for the next morning at 6:45 and told us that while we are entitled to a hotel, they did not have any contracts with hotels near Istanbul airport and that for a downtown hotel the time is too short (as we would need to literally get back on a shuttle at 2 or 3am) - hence we should go to the business class lounge. We did and they had some 'suites' with beds to relax - but these are only available when your layover is between 4 and 9h - not the 12h we had (counting our non-delayed scheduled arrival and the newly scheduled departure). Hence, we could not get those suites - a rule that quite apparently should not be applied to cases where due to TA's failure we had to be rescheduled on such inconvenient terms. Yet, 2 lounge employees and their supervisor stood by that rule. I literally asked the supervisor why he was going to great lengths to make sure that we had a miserable experience if there was such a simple way to please a tired business class traveller. That's TA business class for me - will find other ways to travel to Asia in the future. In short, very clearly not the best business class airline.

I purchased a round-trip ticket  for an international flight on March 19, 2025, and completed online check-in well in advance. On the day of my flight, due to a delay in a connecting United Airlines flight, I arrived at the Turkish Airlines counter 58 minutes before departure. Upon noticing the delay, I had contacted Turkish Airlines, who assured me that a note had been added to my reservation to allow for a brief waiting period. When I arrived at the counter, I was told that my check-in had been canceled. When I followed up with Turkish Airlines  I was shocked to receive a template response that ignored every point I raised. They offered no compensation.  I had paid for additional services (exit row seat and business upgrade on return), and I was left to cover the cost of replacement tickets.

I asked for a glass of wine with my meal and it never arrived so I asked again during my meal but still nothing happened. The crew were not friendly and seemed disinterested.  I contacted their Customer services on 13th March 2025 to get my membership activated so I could use Shop and miles but it has not been activated despite several attempts to contact the customer services the reply remains exactly the same and they don't answer any questions but simply say the activation is being worked on but I feel they have no intention of activating my membership.

But for this itinerary, purchased in April 2025 for a flight in July, we paid the fare indicated on the web site ($1095) and were given a receipt and promised an eticket in email within 24 hours. No eticket! The first phone agent said that there were $365 in taxes added to the fare in between the time we clicked on it and paid for it, thus they would not issue the ticket until we paid that. After talking to a supervisor, he agreed to reduce the extra payment by $100. Then I spoke to the "floor supervisor" who explained that it was not taxes, it was a glitch in their computer system and we must pay the $265. Finally he agreed to forget it and promised an eticket in 24 hours. No eticket! Now they want me to pay $300 just to cancel the ticket. And the supervisor (the same guy) refused to recognize what he had said before.

Last year our return flight war a real adventure, but we wanted to give it the benefit of the doubt and booked again with the same company. This time I needed a more comfortable seat and booked a preferred seat, noticing that they advertised it as an extra legroom seat. I was wrong. The Facebook advertisement is misleading and I got it wrong, seating in a place with incredibly little legroom, less than in an ordinary seat on their A320s. I asked for a refund, given the fact that I felt misled into buying a product that does not exist, but they denied any responsibility and I threw away lots of mileage points for nothing.

First they canceled our seat reservation 2 weeks before our flight seperating our family with children. Then we called and they told us we couldnt do anything but wait for reimbursement (which takes 7 days and it was a full flight) and then pick our seats again. It was a full flight! I told them we didnt cancel it they did. He yeld at us saying we had to pay for seats. Finally they understood that i already Paid and they canceled us. We ended up with the same seats i reserved in the first place. Then i asked at the airport ticket stand to make sure our stroller got off with us when we arrived at Istanbul specifically said before we boarded that we need our stroller with a 6 hour layover, the lady put something on our stroller saying it will be taken off, they did not leave us the stroller for our baby and when we went to customer service they ran us around the Istanbul airport looking for their stupid strollers that are hard seats and dont lay back. We did not find anything. We were exhausted and they didnt help us at all. We walked in every direction they told us and we found no help. We had a lot to carry and a 1 year old who needed to nap. Now we missed our flight going home because our child became sick just before we left for the flight. Customer service couldnt even get us stand by and kept telling us they couldn't do anything. What's the point of customer service if they can't help their customers. The worst attitudes too. You pay all that money and they can't even help. They tried to sell us a one way ticket that was more than what we paid for our entire trip. We had a 2 week trip.

Boarding was unorganized and chaotic with just two gate agents being overwhelmed controlling the crowd. There were no boarding groups and at the end they gave up and it was free for all. As a result, the flight took off 50 minutes late. Seats on the A330 were comfortable with a responsible seat pitch. Service was good with ok food.

However, on Turkish Airlines' new aircraft, the windows no longer have manual blinds—instead, they use an electronic dimming system that can be centrally controlled by the crew. On both the outbound and return flights (Istanbul–Taipei–Istanbul), the crew kept the windows fully dimmed the entire flight, despite multiple requests to adjust them even slightly. Their response? “Company policy.” One of the most frustrating parts was flying over China, where the high mountains were covered in snow—an absolutely spectacular view. But the only way to see it was through the bottom camera on the entertainment system, which is available from any seat. This is no substitute for a real view through an actual window. If this is their policy, why do they charge extra for window seats? This is misleading and unfair. Keeping the cabin in total darkness for daytime flights forces passengers into an unnatural sleep cycle. Many people, including myself, arrived at our destinations in the evening, unable to sleep at night and severely jetlagged. It makes you wonder—is this about passenger comfort, or just making the crew’s job easier by keeping people asleep? I reached out to customer service, expecting an explanation or resolution, but all I received were generic, copy-paste responses that ignored my concerns. Their final message made it clear that they would not take my complaint further, essentially telling me to give up and stop writing. It’s obvious that Turkish Airlines does not care about passenger experience.

During our recent trip, they broke our baby stroller, which we only noticed after leaving the terminal and reaching the parking lot. When we reported the issue and sought compensation, they refused to assist, citing that we didn’t report it immediately at the airport. Even though we raised the concern the same day after arriving home, their response was dismissive. They claimed the report should have been made on the same day if we had already left the airport, and they denied any compensation. The lack of accountability and poor customer service is unacceptable, especially when it involves essential items like a baby stroller. Their support team showed no willingness to resolve the issue fairly.

If you plan to book a trip in which ones possible airline option is Turkish, please make sure you have adjusted expectations. I travel often from the US to middle east and tried different airlines. This time I chose Turkish because it has sightly shorter duration on the longer leg compared to other service providers in the region (Qatar, Emirates, etc). But unfortunately I didn't get what I wanted (shorter trip) and also missed some other standard benefits. With Turkish airlines, you can happily book a flight and make travel plans accordingly. But the airline doesn't feel obliged to commit to that booking. They very very often cancel some legs of your flight likely due to the fact that the leg is not being fully booked. This selfish cost saving approach won't stop there. In my case, it led to a major layover duration increase (1.5 hr to 7 hr). And as you may have guessed, they don't care for your time and won't even mention a penalty. Having a 7 hr layover, I decided to book a lounge at Istanbul airport. I won't bother readers with describing quality and variety of accommodations at the lounge. But it's good to change your expectation about a lounge if you think it's supposed to be a comfy area for resting and good food. If you could find a spot to rest (like taking a nap), you should be proud of yourself. And lastly, after all the misery, we arrived at the destination (Newark NJ) with two out of five checked luggages missing! Again, it might be surprising to a regular reader, but it's very usual for Turkish airline staff if you ask them. The airline had only seven hours to transfer our luggages and this is indeed error prone. You may be more lucky with >10 hr layovers next time. Why am I writing this? Just to vent a little. I'm sure the effect would be minimal. But I also hope this helps some future travelers to dodge the bullet if they have other options.

review_header: “I warn against traveling with this airline”
review_text: On December 27, 2024 we flew from Istanbul to Cotonou (Benin)- group of 11 people. The plane (if I'm not mistaken Boeing 747) was almost full - maybe 2-3 seats vacant. Upon arrival, it turned out that no luggage (for all passengers from the plane!) arrived with us. We received our luggage on January 2, 2025 after 6 days of “struggle” and daily questions when our luggage would arrive at the airport. When it turned out that the luggage finally arrived we had to make our own arrangements to pick it up. I understand that anything can happen, but from an airline boasting that it is among the top five airlines in the world I expected: - A modicum of interest in what happened, It is the airline that should keep us informed when the luggage will arrive and not us calling them every day - A simple word of apology, not to mention compensation for organizing the transport of luggage to the place of our stay at the time or for shopping for the most necessary personal hygiene products and underwear for a change of clothes. Immediately after returning to Poland, we complained to Turkish Airlines about the situation (each separately, on January 15-16), and after almost two months of waiting, the matter “is still under consideration”. Immediately after returning home, we complained to Turkish Airlines about the situation (each separately, on January 15-16), and after almost two months of waiting, the matter “is still under consideration.” Therefore, Turkish Airlines has lost at least some possible future passengers. Probably this is not a problem for them, but this is why I warn against traveling with this airline.

Ran through the airport as quickly as possible, arrived at the gate one minute after the gate closed and denied boarding. We then spent the next five hours in queue after queue after queue to eventually arrive at a hotel that was neither near the airport or central to Istanbul and couldn’t fly for almost 24 hours. The replacement flight also wasn’t direct, it was via Kilimanjaro. The airline staff were not sympathetic and the queues were huge. The airline is now refusing to provide compensation which we are entitled too. They say it was out of their control.

Little that I know that the IST is so vast that there’s no way that I can transfer from gate D to gate A within that time limit. My luggage never arrived to CDG when I arrived. I was asked to complete a form online indicating my address in France, telephone number and off course my information and the ticket number. At that point I was told that I should expect the luggage in 72 hours. That was Thursday 20/2/2025. My flight to Istanbul was booked on Sunday, by Saturday I was concerned that the luggage may not arrive before my flight, I decided to change my flight to Tuesday afternoon 3:50 pm. I was forced to pay for charging my flight even though it was not my fault that the airline didn’t deliver the luggage. It has been a week now since I left Detroit and I still don’t have my belongings.

The food on board was as usual very good indeed as was the superb service provided by cabin crew hostess Grulsah. She was extremely friendly and very professional for which I would like to thank her for. If I had one perhaps negative comment to make and that is regarding the dated seating layout on the airbus A330. Which with a layout of 2-2-2 doesn't provide much in the way of privacy and should, if possible be changed to a 1-2-1 layout. That aside the flight itself arrived into Bangkok exactly on time. Highly recommended.

The aircraft felt outdated, with uncomfortable seats. The cabin temperature was unbearably high, turning the entire 11-hour flight into a sauna. While the food was passable, I found it below the standard of other airlines’ business class offerings. My connecting New York to Rochester flight was canceled with no assistance from Turkish Airlines. No automatic rebooking. No refund or apology. I had to book a same-day ticket on a different airline at my own expense just to get home. Reaching customer service was a nightmare they were dismissive, unhelpful, and indifferent. Each call ended with them simply asking me to "leave feedback" on their website. Emails were ignored, and when I finally spoke to a ground agent, they were rude and uncooperative. Despite multiple attempts, I received no refund, no compensation, and no resolution. This level of service is unacceptable, especially for a business-class passenger. I will never fly Turkish Airlines again.

Women was not friendly at all and shouted. We had some valuables with us what we had to take out and keep in our hands. When i asked for bag she did not even answer. Most unpolite people. I never fly Turkish Airlines.

When they finally located it, the airport refused to cover the cost of shipping it to me, meaning I had to pay out of my own pocket to get my own belongings back. My Chicago to Istanbul flight was delayed by over 3 hours, causing me to miss my connection to Malta. Turkish Airlines rebooked me on another flight, but that flight also departed late, meaning I missed my connection again and was forced to wait another 9 hours in Istanbul for the next available flight. The only thing they provided during this 9-hour wait was one free mea l— completely inadequate for such a long delay and Turkish Airlines refused to compensate me. Despite all of these issues being caused by their delays, Turkish Airlines offered me nothing but a 15% discount on a future fligh which is insulting, considering how much time and money I lost. They closed my compensation request without even properly reviewing it, refusing to acknowledge their responsibility. Their customer service is dismissive, they do not take responsibility for their mistakes, and their so-called "compensation" is a joke. If you want a stress-free travel experience, choose another airline.

The aircraft used on each of the four legs was a narrowbody but seats felt more spacious than wide bodied competitors. Business class seats were proper business unlike BA (though not flat). Food was good. Flight crew were helpful and pleasant. But clearly Turkish have poor IT / policies - I paid for seat allocations well in advance as traveling with family and wanted forward row. Airline cancelled theses at the last minute without any notice. And then placed us in separate rows (ie split up the family and moved to the back). On all four legs. Was told all I could do was submit feedback form - which they ignored and gave a pro forma response about “operational reasonss”. There weee clearly no such reasons as the (pleasant) checkin staff at the airport reallocated us back (or nearby) on each of the legs. Just creates terrible impression of (a) IT systems and (b) ground customer service / feedback operations. Tried to register with loyalty club and that failed to start with. And when it did succeed it told me my name was incorrect so the flight couldnt be allocated to it. Online checkin a joke - you have to enter all your details separately each time (as if I would have changed passport in the few days between outbound and return). And was pointless anyway as no bag drop area in London so had to queue for nearly an hour to checkin anyway. Again - no thought applied to customer experience at policy level. When will airlines learn that how they mistreat customers on the ground really does matter. Won’t fly with them again as trust now eroded.

We were a group of six passengers, including elderly parents, traveling on a connecting flight that was delayed. Upon arriving at the Turkish airline desk, we requested assistance with checking in, the staff said she cannot checkin because we are late, our previous flight was delayed and my mom needed wheelchair assistance. (It was requested with Turkish airline as well). We asked for finding alternative flight options, unfortunately, the two staff members the lady and the man displayed unprofessional behavior, particularly the female staff member who was dismissive and unwilling to help. When we asked if there were any available flights, she simply stated, "we don't have any more today or tomorrow" without making any effort to check. When we requested to speak to a manager, she refused to call one and repeatedly stated " I can't help". We were left to search for solutions on our own, despite our urgent need especially with elderly parents. When we asked the two staff members for their names, they refused to "provide their names". This experience was extremely frustrating and disappointing, as we have previously had positive experience with Turkish Airlines. However, this level of customer service was unacceptable. The lack of assistance, professionalism, and willingness to help customers in distress does not align with the high standards from an huge airline company like this. I wanted to address this issue to ensure that other customers do not experience similar treatment.
Flight attendants and crew were okay. Seats we not comfortable, the timing were almost fine.  I won't fly with Turkish anymore.
There were still plenty of space to put us all together but they decided to behave like Ryanair and force us to spend extra 120 USD to 1k EUR ticket each. Really not fair.

But, thanks to the incredible TA staff I was able to make my flight. I would like to Thank Dimitra Kiritsi, Neofitos Amaxiopoulos, Melina Sykioti Thank You. Without your help, I would have lost my flight and a lot of money.

It was extremely difficult to book a reservation through this program. I was ultimately able to book my reservation for the hotel and receive my voucher roughly 6 weeks prior to my departure. I was scheduled to fly out of Marrakech on Monday afternoon. Late Sunday afternoon I received an e-mail from the airline stating my voucher was cancelled. No explanation. No option to e-mail back inquiring as to why. No way to appeal. I booked a hotel at my expense as I did not want to be stranded. Several hours later, I received a new voucher for a different hotel. This did me no good as I'd already incurred the expense for a hotel room with no way to cancel. I will never fly this airline again.

Our Dubai-Istanbul flight was 40 mins late, causing us to miss our connection to Malaga. Delays happen, but what followed was unacceptable. Onboard, we informed the crew that we still had a chance to make our connection. Their response? Blank stares and a complete refusal to assist. No priority disembarkation, no attempt to coordinate with the ground staff. From 6 AM at Dubai Airport until our arrival at the hotel in Istanbul at 6 PM, we had almost nothing to eat. Upon arrival in Istanbul, we were informed that our flight to Malaga had already left and that we would be rebooked the following morning. The compensation was a hotel stay and dinner. But our five checked bags, which were supposed to be in transit, were only returned to us after a 2.5-hour wait. The only positive note? The baggage service staff, who finally understood our situation after I had to go back and forth twice. In short, if you want a smooth and stress-free journey, avoid Turkish Airlines. With indifferent staff, poor management of connections, unaddressed delays, this airline is simply not worth it.

I began to fly with TK a couple of times before as early as the year of 2000 as I can remember. They even provide the comfort kit in economy class for any flights although less than 5 hours of flight time. Especially on the night flights. Very smart gesture. A big in flight screen in economy class and very easy to explore. Crew were very friendly and well groomed. I personally found the onboard service was more relax and comfortable compared to some major airlines.
The only issue was the counter was about to open 3 hours before departure but it opened with half a hour delay.
We were kept for about 15 minutes in the jetway, The food was good for a 2 hours flight and flight attendants were nice. The aircraft was clean and comfortable.

Staff member in Istanbul airport scammed me for undisclosed amount for an upgrade. He took my card, scanned it, did not tell me how much I was going to be charged and then just printed the ticket. When I complained, he rudely said "OK transaction was cancelled". He refused to provide the proof. I was inadvertently charged and I filed a complaint with the Feedback via airline and they refused to provide any explanation to what happened and said there is nothing they are going to do. Terrible customer service, very dodgy, not trustworthy.

I arrived on 1st January from Islamabad to Istanbul which was supposed to then go to Manchester after 1 hour transit at Istanbul airport. The flight got delayed 1 hour 15 min during departure from Islamabad to Istanbul. When I reached Istanbul, they told me that I have missed the flight, and another Turkish airline flight will leave after 2 days. Their ground staff is very rude, they don’t guide about anything and talk in a very bad manner. They told me that I cannot claim my luggage until I pass the security check/immigration and for that I need to buy e visa. I bought an e visa, which costed me all my savings. Then I went to claim my bag and I was informed that they have left 1 of my bag in Islamabad (which I was able to retrieve after few days by launching a complain with Turkish airline). I went to buy ticket from the shops on airport and I was told that there was only 1 flight operating that day from Istanbul to UK (Gatwick) which was very expensive but I had to buy that as I had no other option. I reached Gatwick Airport and found out there was no direct flight operating on that date from Gatwick to Manchester. So I had to take a coach from Gatwick to Heathrow. All economy flights had a very limited baggage allowance while I was carrying 1 large bag with an estimated 25 kg weight. So I had to buy a business flight from Heathrow airport to Manchester. I was able to sleep/rest after more than 48 hours of being in this constant trauma.

review_header: "I am glad I tried TK again"
review_text: I expected that the flight would be full. However, I did not expect the boarding to be disorderly. No one's listening to the ground staff despite their insistence on following the row numbers before boarding. I found the cabin comfortable and did not feel stuffed. The food they served was good, although they lacked the additional treats I usually get from flying Middle Eastern airlines. I hope they can match theirs with what the other top airlines are serving. The toilets were well-maintained and supplied with adequate hygiene supplies. I am not sure though about my experiences with the cabin crew - it was mixed. Some of them were pleasant and approachable, the others were not. I bought this ticket sometime around March 2024 when the price was still cheaper and I am glad I tried TK again after a few years.

Flight was cancelled and rebooked 4 times. The 5th happened midair and flight was cancelled in Istanbul. Terrible service at the airport and no one would speak to us and tell us what was happening. After lots of calls and attempts to stop anyone, we finally were told the flight was cancelled and rebooked for the next day. Accommodations were given but when asking about delaying the return flight an extra day since that time was lost in Istanbul, their response was wait till you reach your destination 1st. Once we did, calls were placed on a daily basis as well as more than 7 feedback petitions asking for a delayed return flights. None of these were successful. When asked to speak with a manager the answer was no manager was available. After lots of calls, we finally reached “Brian” the manager who promised to fix it and call us an hr later. Again none of that happened and no one could tell us who Brian was.

The flight was smooth and left generally on time. The cabin was clean and well-maintained. The food was palatable although I think not enough variety as one could get from some other Airlines. I was amazed by their individual travel care packs they gave to us during my earlier flight to Manila from London. So I was hoping to get another on this return flight. Unfortunately, they did not provide on Manila to Istanbul leg. Also, I can sense that some cabin crew do not like the work they are doing. I observe they don't empathise with the passengers needing assistance during the flight. I felt they simply just want to finish giving the food then that's it. I miss the crew in my previous TK travels years ago. They were more amiable and attentive than the cabin crew members this time. Also, Istanbul Airport has become the most expensive airport now. So while I appreciate flying with TK, I will probably not use this flight for a long time unless the Istabul Airport considers lowering their prices on food.

Good service on board. Cabin crew amazing, paying heed to passenger requirements, accommodating them as much as possible. Food is great and IFE is reasonably good. Ground staff, although accommodating customer requirements seem to be annoyed, giving the vibes of someone engaging in a fight. They can be more friendly. One particular issue was wanting economy class passengers to board the rear of the aircraft on foot at Edinburgh at a time when it was still drizzling and the ground had puddles without a bus being provided despite the aircraft being connected to the aerobridge. Could have an extra meal option in the economy class as flights in the morning have only one option. (Edinburgh - Istanbul had two options but all the morning flights (Istanbul - Cairo and Istanbul - Edinburgh had only one option) as did the evening flight from Cairo to Istanbul.  Could have more options in IFE. TK doesn't have the policy of fragile baggage handling. Although my bag reached in good condition, it doesn't guarantee that your bag will be intact and that is a point of concern. Despite these, Turkish Airlines is a good airline to fly with and would recommend them.

I reported this to the flight attendant. She took my food and reported it to the main flight attendant. After some time I was given a card that said the following: Dear Passenger, We are sorry for the unfavorable experience you have had. We will take record of the situation and inform our relevant departments. Our Customer Contact Center will evaluate the case and get in touch with you as soon as possible through the contact info you have provided. Thank you for your understanding. Well that sounded great but they say talk is cheap but what did they actually do to fix the situation. Many days passed without a response. After a week I reached out through chat and within a couple of days I got a response. We have reviewed your case and are giving you 3000 miles and we are closing this case as fully satisfied. I never spoke with anyone directly. The response seemed very impersonal and unprofessional.

The lack of customer service and general manner of the staff left a lot to be desired. Dublin Airport ground staff I would say were the best of a bad bunch. On the long haul part of our flight I received my food choice with no offer of a drink which I had to ask for which seemed to be an inconvenience. Once food was over the staff disappeared and dare you ask for water or anything for that matter and it was met with a bad attitude. The flight staff was mostly male and had no customer service whatsoever, I used the toilet while on board and a minute or so into been in the bathroom the door was banged on for me to leave. I came out to a very aggressive staff member with no reason for his actions.

Our flight from Heathrow was delayed by 2 hours no reason given. Went to airline desk said we would have to sort it at the other end. We had a connecting flight from Istanbul which gave us half an hour at the most to check in for it. The meals on the plane which we had pre-booked was all mixed up. On arriving at Istanbul we ran through the airport to the gate only to find the gate had closed no staff and we still had 10 minutes to spare and the aircraft was still waiting. This was at 2.30am. We found a Turkish help desk they were very dismissive and unhelpful and waved us elsewhere. On finding another desk they said the next flight to Vietnam was in 3 days. We declined and they found us a connecting flight a day later to Doha then Ho Chin Minh City. We had to find our bags which took another hour and then ask them to put us up in a hotel. The man at the Turkish airline desk booking the hotel was most unfriendly and yawning the whole time. We were taken in a mini bus to a hotel 40 minutes drive away. We had no idea where we were being taken too. No communication whatsoever. The taxi the following day was supposed to pick us up at 5pm it was nearer 6pm. I will never again fly with Turkish Airlines the staff are rude and unhelpful.

We booked tickets for three people—two adults and one child—from Sydney to Madrid, Spain, with a return in December 2024. At the time of booking, we had limited options, especially considering we were traveling with our 11-year-old daughter. We paid extra to ensure we could sit together, as our daughter has asthma, struggles with separation anxiety, and suffers from severe panic attacks. We thought we were making a responsible choice, but despite the additional payment, we received multiple emails shifting our seats around 2-3 times before our flight. This created unnecessary frustration and distress during what should have been a joyful holiday. This trip was particularly significant for us, as we’ve endured four gruelling years dealing with my husband’s Stage 4C melanoma. Finally, we received good news that allowed us to travel outside Australia for an extended period, as my husband no longer needed his regular treatments every three weeks. However, we were left with no control over the connections between our flights. The airline placed us on a journey with 15 hours of connection delays, despite their website promising free accommodation for customers facing 12-hour-plus waits. When we approached the Turkish care desk, there were only three staff members attending to a long line of customers. We stood in line for nearly 40 minutes, only to be met with unprofessional, rude, and dismissive attitudes. One staff member, with an insulting air of arrogance, told us it was "not his problem" and that we should change our tickets at our own expense, essentially forcing us to cut our holiday short by waking up at 3 AM to catch a flight at 7 AM. He stated it was our fault for choosing a different time and date last year, despite the fact that there were no alternative options available when we booked in September 2024. The lack of communication from the airline was appalling; they expected us to keep checking for available flights that might pop up after months of silence. It's outrageous that we should have to bear the burden of their poor planning. After spending 15 hours at the airport, waiting from midnight until 3 PM the next day, I will never recommend this airline.  When we expressed our intent to leave a negative review, the staff member simply scoffed and said, “Please, we don’t care. It won’t affect us; you won’t be the first or last.” I was left utterly disgusted and in disbelief at his blatant disregard for customer feedback.

It was one booking with two passengers. When we landed in Turkey our connecting flight were delayed. After getting back we put in a passenger claim as per the Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 since the delay were more than 3 hours at destination which gives passengers a right of EUR600 per passenger payout. First they delayed their replies so much that we are now in January second they insisted that Article 7(2) applies claiming that we are only entitled to EUR300 per passenger – this is wrong as the flight were delayed and not rerouted. Now they refuse to pay the second passenger because they claim the signatures does not match. Don’t ever book with them… they have no respect for their passengers.

The flight was ok in terms of comfort on service. I made it to Melbourne on January 6th however my bag did not. Apparently Turkish airlines works with Dnata Baggage Services in Australia and I was given a PIR number by dnata baggage services at the airport. As I am traveling through Australia on vacation I had to leave an address of my next stop in the Gold Coast as I was told that there is a Turkish Airlines flight only every 2 days to Melbourne. At no point I was offered any kind of "survival bag" or similar with essentials. The bag arrived in Melbourne on the 8th January. I have been in touch with Dnata baggage services every day from the 8th Jan onwards without any new information apart from that my bag is in Melbourne. Apparently dnata themselves were unable to reach their own office in Melbourne and didn't get even replies to their own emails. On the 10th January I continued my journey on to Sydney prior calling dnata and updating the delivery address to Sydney. The file, the online tracker everything displayed the address in Sydney at that point. On the 12th of January my bag was finally send out from Melbourne but not to Sydney, but to the Gold Coast. I am leaving today on January 14th without having my bag still (we are talking about flight distances of 1-1,5 hours here) after in total 9 days and with the bag being in Australia for 7 days. Because of this I was forced to travel through a different continent in the summer with my winter clothes. I have never witnessed this amount of incompetence by an airline or ground handling service and will never ever again set a foot into a Turkish Airlines flight or any airline that is being handled by dnata ground services again.

I asked for confirmation multiple times and they confirmed. On the day of the flight, at the check-in desk, she was told there was no wheelchair booked and more was there any available. Calling the airline customer service, they said we are sorry, we don't have any wheelchair available, you can write feedback. That's all the service I could get for someone who could not walk and needed assistance.

I had booked our business class flights directly with Turkish Airlines and reserved all seats four months before the trip. The first surprise came via email two days before the outbound flight when the airlines informed me that my wife’s seat had been changed. Luckily, I was able to adjust this quickly by changing my seat so that we could sit next to each other. The same thing happened on the return flight from Zanzibar. Just one day before departure, our seats were changed, and we could no longer sit together. I find this behavior by the airline outrageous. I don’t understand the point of seat reservations if the airline changes them at will anyway. Another absurdity was that the short two-hour flight from Istanbul to Zurich on the A350-900 had flat seats, but the long seven-hour flight with B737-8 from Istanbul to Zanzibar did not (you could only recline the seatbacks about 45 degrees). I am truly very disappointed with the business class service of Turkish Airlines.

Had to go back to the airport myself at my own cost to look for my luggage several days in a row. When I found the first suitcase, no one controled whether the suitcase I picked up really belonged to me. During the four days I was at the airport looking for suitcases, new suitcases kept arriving that the airline had "lost" - probably in Istanbul.  There was no help  when calling customer service to claim the luggage. They had different stories every time we called and blamed the previous customer service agent for lying. Some spoke such bad English that we couldn't understand what they were saying. One suitcase was broken when it arrived, but we got a new one. Satisfied with the solution. We had booked emergency exits on all four flights due to the fact that my traveling companion has very long legs. All our seat reservations were changed due to a change of flight type. After some discussion, he was given emergency exits on all flights. The staff at the airport in Istanbul were not very service minded and forced us to check in the one hand luggage we had with us (which we are allowed to have with us according to your own guidelines) despite the fact that it contained important possessions. The airport in Istanbul required a new security check, so the drink I had bought at the airport in Oslo had to be thrown away. Other airports do not run new security checks when we arrive from Norway or from airports that come under the EU's directives as these places already have strict guidelines for security checks. A large airport with long distances as well as time-consuming security check, makes me to avoid Istanbul on all subsequent flights. I will probably choose transfer through European airports such as Schipol. Positive sides: The airplane was okay. Flight attendants were polite and helpful. Totally ok food. I will not recommend Turkish Airlines to anyone. It is the worst flight experience I have ever had. This is the first time I have been really dissatisfied with the travel experience of an airline operator.

There was a delay of over four hours to one leg of the outbound flight. I found care of passengers was not great and the compensation offer was not great either. Food vouchers were provided for limited outlets at the airport in which we were delayed - none of which catered to specific health related dietary requirements I have. There was a general lack of awareness and care about dietary needs. Seeking to offer feedback and request any redress for this from the UK is proving to be one of the most difficult experiences I have had with a service provider.

I had two kids with me. One was 5 & one was 23 months old. I booked wheelchair service for both Dhaka airport & Istanbul airport. The staff at Dhaka Istanbul office booked my tickets & also the wheelchair service for me.  In my boarding pass it was also written ‘wheelchair’. I got the service at Dhaka but not at Istanbul airport. When I got off the airplane at Istanbul airport, I found no wheelchair waiting for me. A buggy car was waiting there after to carry the passengers who had wheelchair booking but when I approached it the driver said I couln't ride it with my babies as the buggy car was not safe for kids. I had a flight to catch in one & half hours so I started walking with my 23 months old kid. I couldn't find any stroller station in the airport.  I assume that they didn't have any wheelchair service at Istanbul airport. I mailed them about my complained by they replied me the same thing telling that because of the security of the passenger they didn't provide me the wheelchair. Then why did they provide me a wheelchair at the first airport?  Only a buggy car was present at the Istanbul airport to take the wheelchair needed passengers. They denied to give me any compensation.

The crew was polite and friendly. The onboard meals were tasty. The in-seat entertainment system worked flawlessly. Very limited legroom, which was uncomfortable during a 5-hour flight. Our original flight was canceled, and a replacement was provided only after a few hours of delay. The aircraft was later changed, and we lost our pre-assigned seats that we had paid for. In comparison, we flew with Qatar Airways a year ago, where the aircraft was also changed, but our seat assignments were honored. Turkish Airlines fell short of expectations, and such service is unacceptable for a top-tier airline.

Plane starts in Tblisi with 40 minutes delay. On my request to the ground service in Tblisi to receive assistance in Istanbul, answers were just saying wait to arrive there and somebody will help. Once on the plane, no one apologize for the delay. Once in Istanbul, we asked several staff members, no one was able to help. They just provided assistance for people with connection to India, but the others had simply to run. We run 20 minutes through the airport, and were able to catch our connection. Again no one able to help with a quick transport via electric trailer or even an excuse. Next time i will fly with low cost companies.

Our trip was in Dec 2024 and we booked well ahead in June 2024 so that we could guarantee our preferred seat selection. This strategy often doesn’t provide the best price, but we choose to book early to insure we had our choice of seats. Problems began in July; we received an email notice that our seats had changed. When we contacted Turkish customer service, they told us they changed equipment and rather than just moving us to comparable seats they made us completely rebook the trip. There were many communication issues as customer service representatives speak less then fluent English. We finally got the trip rebooked and had acceptable seat together for the trip. Three days before the trip we once again got a notice that they had moved our seats. Except this time, they split us up in business class so that my wife and I were in different rows. Calls to customer service were met with indifference and they refused to re-establish our seats together. On check-in we once again tried to fix our seats and were told that the seat next to me was occupied and they couldn’t move my wife back to her original seat without that person’s approval. Our argument that they moved my wife out of the seat without her approval met uncaring and disinterested ears. We tried again at the gate and then were forced to address the seat issue onboard with the passenger directly who declined out request to set together even though we offered the same seat one row back. It just ruined a 15-day trip of a life time cruise on the Nile. I can say categorically it was the worst customer service I have experienced in all my years of travel. Believe it or not this wasn’t the end. They changed our seats on all four legs with a 3 days’ notice. None of our seats were protected. So, buying seats ahead does no good with Turkish. Adding cramped waiting areas in Istanbul and Cairo, we got sick on the return trip, and seat maps provided on their website don’t match the actual seat configurations on the plane used, it will be my last booking on Turkish.

Appalling behaviour by Turkish Airlines cabin crew. On my first leg from Lahore to Istanbul we were completely ignored by stewards serving refreshments. Why? I don't know. The passenger sitting next to me was flying to USA. He and I are older people. We noticed a marked difference as stewards would park their refreshments trolly next to our seats - then noticing all passengers in front, back and other sides being served. We had to ask for water (umpteen occasions), food etc. We both felt never again would we fly Turkish airlines. I provided immediate survey feedback to Turkish Airlines that they need to train staff on basic customer service on inclusion, respect and care. On my second leg of the journey from Istanbul to Edinburgh I asked for a small bottle of water. Instead I was given water in a cup (I find myself thirsty due to my diabetes). Yet other passengers were given bottles when they asked. However, the alarming and distressing part was when using the wash room one steward knocked on the door thrice. Basically banging. I was washing my face. When I can she and her colleague were laughing. I asked is this normal practice for you to bang on the door. She replied I wanted to clean up and ensure their were enough paper towels!. I was shocked and lost for words. Again I felt disrespected and treated differently. I really feel Turkish Airlines cabin crew further training. I cannot believe I just happened to come across two sets of different cabin crew displaying similar poor unprofessional behaviour. I have never experienced such appalling bad behaviour by cabin crew of any airline on my regular travels. I think Turkish Airlines staff have a problem with older passengers. Yet they forget our money is paying for their salaries.

40 minutes flight. That makes over 6 hours waiting time. We were denied use of premium rooms as we don’t meet rules. All the ground staff at the lounge and anywhere else are truly sorry displaying computer says no attitude.  Very mediocre product and terrible, woody service. Will not fly with them ever again.

On the morning of the 7th we were due to board a cruise ship so they arranged for the luggage to arrive on a later flight on the 6th. They could not guarantee to deliver the luggage that evening so we travelled to the airport and returned to Istanbul by taxi (30 miles each way) to collect the luggage ourselves. They have refused to pay the £60 taxi cost. Not only that but my wife aged 78 was treated like a criminal by TA's staff being escorted by two men on the secure side of the airport over long distances and told to deal with moving the case herself. The experience took well over 2 hours and involved filling in multiple forms and photocopying her passport. It's clear that they didn't see themselves as doing something wrong. We had been to Istanbul before but will not be visiting again. We will never travel with TA again.

My luggage, was checked in, but as of December 9, 2024, I still have not received it. Despite multiple updates indicating the luggage was checked in and transferred in Istanbul (IST) for flight TK550, there has been no communication or resolution. This experience has caused significant inconvenience and frustration. I expected better service and more proactive handling from Turkish Airlines, especially regarding delayed or lost baggage. I hope they improve their customer service and luggage tracking process to avoid situations like this in the future.

Despite multiple complaints, they keep changing the departure time, bouncing between a reasonable 9:15 am and a completely inconvenient 10:22 pm. This isn't a minor adjustment; it throws any travel plans into complete disarray. Useless Customer Service: They refuse to acknowledge their responsibility to provide accommodation for the extended layover they created, instead telling me to figure it out myself at the airport. Unbelievable! Excessive Baggage Fees: To add insult to injury, their baggage fees are exorbitant ($200). They seem determined to nickel and dime passengers at every turn.

The destination airport claims they have sent it, home airport claims they have not received it and I am supposed to call, email and check myself for my baggage. Worst customer service. Expensive tickets. Pretty ordinary meal. No responsibility taken for missed connections even if it’s their fault.

Cabin crew was not very friendly to me. Food on all the legs were fairly awful.  They lost two of my check-in bags on the way back from Athens to SFO. One bag was delivered the next day, and then when the second bag didn't show up, I inquired. They said I didn't check in a second bag. Luckily, I still had my check-in bag ticket and emailed them a copy of it. They claimed that I didn't check in the bag properly and it wasn't on my bag retrieval form. I scanned the bag-retrieval form with both bags listed and emailed it to them. They then claimed that I didn't fill out the paperwork properly. I informed them that the Turkish Airlines agent at SFO filled out the form, I only signed it. It took them another 3 days to deliver my bag to me and then acted like they did me favor. I lost several hours on the phone and email, communicating to them what was happening, they didn't seem to care and just threw the blame on me for losing my bag. Weird airline, wouldn't go through them again, which is a shame since Turkey was on my bucket-list to visit.

The airport itself has below par facilities for such circumstances and at 12.30 AM it makes the whole journey a truly unforgivable experience. Spending the whole night at the airport with walls being drilled around past midnight is not the way any passenger deserves to pay for. A dry email notification from airlines customer support beginning with "To help you manage your time more efficiently..." without a word of apology is highly inappropriate and utterly useless in a case when all one can do is wrap in a coat and attempt to get some sleep on a chair, while suffering from abdominal pain.. Will select Finnair or Swiss Air for my next journey on the same route and just like Emirates and Dubai, will avoid this flight option in the future. The cabin experience and onboard service cannot make up for this time lapse that is not dictated by adverse weather. Clearly, the airline has Operational Issues they need to improve on managing better.

I was lucky as I had 2 good seatmates on both return legs and there were some privacy concerns, but once the lights were turned off and we all went to sleep, it was no bother. However, I can see an issue of a female passenger feeling uncomfortable with a male seat mate being a huge issue. The flights themselves were fantastic. The staff are super friendly and extremely polite in the business class cabin. Although the aircrafts may be the older type (B777-300 are my favourites) the seats were still comfortable and the washrooms very spacious. I personally didn't mind the way the seats were configured on this Turkish Airlines flight as i find some to the Herringbone and reverse Herringbone too claustrophobic. The other issue I had was the free wifi for business class customers. When the internet is practically your only source of entertainment, then the "free" wifi, which really is 1GB, can get used up pretty quickly on a 10/11 hr flight watching YouTube videos. The last time I flew Turkish was in 2018 and I don't believe there was any limit on usage. The only other issue I had was the Business class lounge in Istanbul. The Lounge itself is amazing. Great selection of freshly made foods, plenty of drinks, plenty of comfortable seats and clean, however the women that control the sleeping pods and showers seem to be miserable. Both traveling to India and back I wanted to keep fresh (10-11 hours from YYZ to/from IST) but every time I went to the counter they just seamed miserable and cold. That Turkish smile was just not there.

You sit right next to someone. it was a 2-3-2 configuration with for 14 hours is uncomfortable. They need to update that plane. The outbound flights and other Turkish flights I have taken are great. That is my only complaint. I love the chefs on board and the meals are fantastic.

The cabin only had a total of four passengers which meant it turned out to be very relaxing. The food was as usual on Turkish Airlines very good but I want make a special mention to the assistant cabin crew manager Nilifer. She was so friendly and very professional. I really hope she is promoted to cabin crew manager very soon. She deserves it.

This company is inhumane. I booked my tickets from Paris to Lebanon 4 months in advance, and then the war erupted. They did not cancel their tickets throughout the past 2 months of war. They only cancelled the tickets once negotiations of a ceasefire started taking place and all other airlines began flying back to Beirut. Turkish airlines has a partnership with MEA, yet they did not accept to transfer me to another flight going to Beirut. THEY are the ones who should bear the financial damage of such a war, not the everyday poor man who can barely afford a ticket back home. It would have cost them nothing to switch me to a MEA flight (they frequently fly their planes). Yet, all the time spent on the phone with customer service and filling out feedback forms was gone to waste. They keep giving you fake promises that they are going to fix it but they offered me 0 solution. They only accept to reimburse me the price that I paid 4 months ago - which is far cheaper than the current prices. This does not make sense in any way shape or form. If I bought a gold bar 4 months ago I cannot resell it at that day's price - especially if it appreciated in value. This is pure greed and inhumane behaviour. If I could give them negative ratings I would.

I have traveled many times through other airlines and have never experienced this level of underperformance. First and foremost, my pillow cover had STAINS and possibly drool on it, which was extremely shocking, I felt very uncomfortable and nauseous for the rest of my 12 hour flight. Then I opened the food tray to find it UNWIPED with FOOD ON IT from a previous flight…DISGUSTING!! The crew didn’t even bother to do a basic wipe down of the seats, this is extremely disgusting and potentially hazardous. To make matters worse, the spacing between the seat rows were extremely congested and uncomfortable compared to their counterparts, their TVs were glitching and freezing every 5 minutes, and their menu options were VERY limited with no snacks served beforehand. The service in general was very subpar. I am not one who usually goes out of their way to leave a review, and honestly I could have lived with the subpar services and seats, but I draw the line at hygiene. Avoid this airline if you can, I would highly recommend traveling either through Qatar, Emirates, or Ethihad.

We encountered unprecedented issues on October 24, 2024, while traveling from Istanbul to Vancouver on flight TK0075. Due to heightened security protocols following an explosion in Ankara, massive delays at passport control and security checks caused us and approximately 20 other passengers to miss our flight. Despite arriving early at the airport, we were delayed due to circumstances entirely out of our control. Some of our group even managed to reach the gate with security stickers on their boarding passes, yet Turkish Airlines staff had already abandoned the gate, denying them boarding. What made matters worse was the unprofessional behavior of both Turkish Airlines and the airport security staff. They shifted blame onto each other, refusing to take accountability, and were offensive and dismissive toward us and other passengers. This ordeal forced us to purchase new tickets for the next day at a significant cost. It also disrupted our professional schedule—our tour started late, and the lack of rest severely impacted our performance quality. As a loyal customer who has long admired Turkish Airlines, I’m appalled by how poorly this situation was handled. The lack of professionalism, customer care, and accountability is unacceptable. I cannot recommend Turkish Airlines based on this experience, and I hope they take steps to address these issues for future passengers.
They prices are expensive and they cannot fulfil their duty: take people from A to B on time. Unfortunately I booked return ticket with them but I will not use them again.

In those six hours one just gets all this not useful notifications. After five hours they brough some sandwiches to the passengers waiting at the gate (once you are at the gate and screened for USA you cannot go out again without undergoing the whole process again). Boarding for TK157 was chaotic and it dragged. We finally took of around almost 7:45 AM (instead of 1:45 AM). Once seated in the business class, we all were just tired and hungry and I had to beg for food. The flight attendants said that it is night flight and everybody is sleeping, so I have to request if I want something, and they have sandwiches and snacks in the galley. First of all, it was not anymore a night flight, and secondly I am not booking and paying for business class and then eating sandwiches.  After arriving in MIA, I have flied the complaint (they make it difficult to file a complaint) and six weeks later got the response; that they will credit 30.000 miles but one need to apply for their Mileage Program Miles & Smiles. When it comes to service, a lot of room for improvements, especially inside the cabin, where the crew quickly finishes their service in order to rest. When it comes to Customer Service, this is almost non-existing and to get an answer, is like winning the lottery.

20. I mistakenly misspelled my wife’s middle name on one of the tickets. Despite numerous attempts to resolve this with Turkish Airlines, I was informed at the O'Hare Airport (ORD) ticket counter that I had to buy a new ticket, costing $1,729.20. Turkish Airlines assured me that the base fare of the original ticket, $944.00, would be refunded via check within 14 business days. This was promised on September 10, 2024. However, as of November 13, 2024, I have not received the refund. While I acknowledge that the initial mistake was my responsibility, this does not give Turkish Airlines the right to make false promises just to secure another ticket sale. Their behavior is deceitful, and their refusal to escalate the matter for resolution is alarming. If they are willing to handle my case this way, they could just as easily show a lack of integrity in your situation. Despite multiple claims filed with Turkish Airlines, they insist that the refund was processed through Chase Travel Agency, yet they provide no proof or documentation to support this.  When I contacted Chase, they confirmed that no refund had been issued and clarified that Turkish Airlines, having sold the second ticket directly, is responsible for the refund. Chase reiterated that they cannot act further without evidence from the airline. Turkish Airlines has refused to offer proof of the check being issued and will not coordinate with Chase or escalate the case. They continue to claim, without documentation, that the refund was processed. This situation is unacceptable. I bought the second ticket only because a Turkish Airlines manager assured me of the refund. The airline has since denied that refund, provided no evidence and stonewalled all attempts to resolve the matter. Their practices are deceptive, and their customer service is completely unreliable.

They made us wait for 6,5 hours at the airport and they only gave soda and sandwiches to us while we waited without any information. At one point they made us board the airplane, wait there and then asked us to step down again to wait some more at the airport. At the airport they said we were entitled to some compensation and we can get it via applying in the website. But when we applied for it they said “they were delayed due to reasons they have no control of”. We missed 1 day of a very expensive vacation without any compensation. If we knew the conditions would be like that at least we would prefer a low cost airline.

The flight from Dubai was operated by a totally worn-out 330 with no leg recline and unfriendly staff. The flight was delayed almost 2 hours and not a word of apology from the captain or the crew. On arrival I expected TK would be proactive and speed up the connecting passengers in order to catch the flights due to the delay. Nothing of that sort. I was a wheelchair passenger and no wheelchair was available. I had to ask for a buggy to take me to the gate as I just could not run. With reluctance, a buggy was arranged. They told me it was free for me as I was above 65 years but my son had to pay. On the return sector, the buggy was free for both of us but the driver did not leave us until we tipped her. Our bags did not arrive in Seattle and the staff made us come the next day to collect the bags without giving us any compensation for the delay and inconveniences we incurred due to the loss of bags and most importantly my medications. This must be the worst airline and the worst level of customer service. They seem to have gotten accustomed to hearing negative comments and could not care less.

review_header: "cabin crew were mostly offhand to me"
review_text: Unfortunately the poor service was just that, cheap. I flew out of Melbourne on 2 October 2024 and when checking in I was told "no luggage would be loaded on to the flight due to a technical issue but would be delivered within 24 hours". When checking in my luggage I was given a tag to attach to it which included Istanbul hotel name, my contact number and email address. When arriving at Istanbul airport, I also completed a form with those same details at the airline's baggage services office. I then spent the next 36 hours close to the hotel waiting for the airline to contact me. In frustration on day 2 of the stopover the hotel contacted the airline on my behalf to find out where my luggage was. The hotel staff member was told that the airline had tried to contact me but with no success. Nonsense! There were no missed phone calls or an email. To add to my frustration the airline then said it couldn't deliver the bag for at least another 24 hours - after I was due to leave for Copenhagen. So what was the point of providing all the contact details to the airline in the first place. In desperation to (hopefully) avoid my luggage following me on my travels for the next 5 weeks, I went to the airport at 6am on my day of departure to try and find my luggage. Eventually, after filling out the same 'delayed luggage' form that I had previously completed twice more, my luggage was located and returned to me in time for me to check in for my flight to Copenhagen and without a word of apology for the awful customer service. To add insult to injury, for the entire flight from Melbourne to Istanbul, the in-flight entertainment system in parts of the Business Class cabin either didn't work or with a very limited selection, also due to a technical issue.  The cabin crew were mostly offhand to me at best for the flight. Poor in-flight service, limited announcements made (what passengers needed to do at the Singapore stopover etc) and although the airline prides itself on its Business Class food, it was no better than other airlines. It seems that Turkish has expanded too quickly without having appropriate levels of staff training including their non-Turkish language skills.

Pay that extra 50-100 for the other airline because it would be better than flying with this one. Turkish Airlines sucks. First are the delays. Fly with them and 9 out of 10 times you will have a delay. You can claim a refund if it is 5 hours or more delay, but good luck getting it. Boarding their planes is so unorganised. Everybody just stands up and rushes and the staff don’t care. Want a small snack while on the flight? Lol, what are you thinking? Snacking is unhealthy according to cabin crew, so you get nothing. When you get on the plane to get to your seat and you want to use the lavatory, you can’t. You tell them the plane isn’t moving yet, but no, you have to hold it until the plane takes off and is at cruising altitude. Oh man, you know your in-flight entertainment screen? Half the time it would be faulty, and when you sit in front of a faulty screen for a long flight the experience is miserable. I’ve had to endure this many times, it is just the worst. What’s that? You want to add an infant to your flight because you’re picking up your infant child so they could travel in your lap? They tell you over the phone it is possible but you cannot as the computer system blocks you from doing so. Repeated calls to then say yes it would be fixed in 20 minutes / 2 hours / 2 days but it never gets fixed. You have to buy a new ticket and cancel the existing ticket so you lose money and risk no getting a seat. Amazing, thanks Turkish Airlines. I really hated my time flying with Turkish Airlines as you can tell. I have flown with them multiple times but the recent one really was the last straw. Avoid them at all costs.

I purchased a ticket well in advance, but had to renew my passport due to a change in my last name. For over a month, I’ve been trying to get them to update my ticket with the new passport details. Despite numerous attempts to contact them, they only replied today, just days before my flight, saying they won’t update my information. They’re now forcing me to buy a new ticket at a much higher price, which is simply unacceptable. This lack of customer service and responsiveness is appalling. I’ll never be flying with them again and wouldn’t recommend anyone else does either.

My flight London - Heathrow was delayed and I missed all my connecting flights. As a seventy two year old solo traveller I was assured by senior Turkish ground staff at Heathrow that I would be met by ground staff at Istanbul Airport to arrange alternative travel to Sydney. Nothing could have been further from the truth. I informed the on board staff about my problem and they assured me it would all be taken care of by the ground staff in Istanbul. In short upon arrival I was totally ignored by all Turkish Airways staff -the flight attendants were busy sharing biscuits and a laugh. I had to basically corner a staff member who gave me vague directions to Turkish Airlines 'Help Desk'. After a number of hours - around 4 am I was told to make my way through customs to Turkish Airways hotels - a good half hour walk stopping many people along the way to refresh the directions having been sent the wrong way a number of times. Finally I made my way back to Sydney having endured the most traumatic travelling experience of my life. I have travelled a lot. It beggars belief that Turkish Airlines is no 7 in the world. No chef on board will make up for the way I was treated. Surely the essence of a good airline is how they treat their passengers when something goes wrong. I have contacted Turkish Airlines. Will I hear back from them ?

We booked our route tickets back to April from Athens to Oslo through Istanbul and the layover was 2 hours. After two months the layover in the returned flight changed from 2 hours to 17. This changed our plans and some bookings we had already made. After changing our returned flight for free but an inconvenient flight since the others were fully booked, the new email contained the old e-ticket numbers. Therefore, we could not do the online check in and we had to contact the support center once more. The app is a disappointment as it does not guide the user to do their job, but to charge them as much as possible (Seat selection part). One more incident in Oslo airport was that we were asked to weigh our personal item but the only instruction we got is that it should fit under the front seat. We did that and they told us that is should be 3 kilos, but the company's site states that it should be 4. Ridiculous things that we met first time in our lives. The result was to open suitcases in the airport. Last thing is how terrible the flights were in comparison with the weather conditions. Their pilots probably need a training in landing.

Rang up to request an aisle seat close to bathroom and in the bassinet row for easy access to toilet as a disabled passenger. Was told to go online and pay £95 for the seat as it's not free. Went on line all seats were taken. Rang back to be told this time that those seats are only for parents with babies. I asked her were they more important than their disabled passengers in which I was told 'sorry but you need to buy a seat I can't do anything. They advertise they do their best to accommodate disabled with front row seats when possible yet it is a lie. I ended up paying £65 for two seats at the back of the plane which I am now guaranteed when someone reclines a seat I will not be able to get easy access up out of my seat for the bathroom.

This is very frustrating and disappointing for us may be even resulting in us forced to cancel instead of changing, which would cost us up to 2000 euro. My experience with Turkish Airlines during flight always has been very pleasant. However, the customer care is the worst I have ever experienced. We had booked semi-flexible tickets and wanted to change the dates (which would cost 65$ per ticket, but should be no big deal otherwise). I tried to change the flight on the Turkish Airlines (TA) website, but I got an error: "Unable to process your request, please try again later." Which I did a few times, before calling the Customer Care (CC). They couldn't change it either. So we had to file a 'Feedback ticket'. Which we did. The first week after filing the ticket, I called every day, people promised to call me back in a few hours, which never happened. After a week I got an email from TA that they had tried to called me, but couldn't reach me on the number provided. It turned out that they entered the country code incorrect. They had closed the case right after this and I had to open a new case. Restarting the process. At the day of writing, TA still hasn't taken any responsibility for the fact that their website is not working and leaving us with the consequences of it.

My flight was cancelled two times and after contacting the Airline, they gave me nothing as compensation for the cancellation. I was absent on duty, due to these cancellations and they just ignored me when I asked for compensation and extra costs they caused me. Staff are very rude and unprofessional. It was the last time, I won't fly with Turkish Airlines again.

To begin with, I encountered severe misinformation regarding my flight, which ultimately forced me to change my plans. When I reached out to customer service for assistance, I was met with indifference and a lack of accountability. Despite my repeated calls, they refused to acknowledge the issues or provide any meaningful support. What struck me as completely absurd was their request for me to specify when I called them, so they could "listen to the call." This level of incompetence is astonishing. It feels like they are more interested in shifting blame than resolving problems. Turkish Airlines has the worst customer service of any airline I have flown with! The process for addressing issues seems endless, with representatives sending you from one department to another. Instead of resolving my concerns, they just added to my stress, ultimately causing me to miss my flight. The combination of ignorance, incompetence, and arrogance exhibited by their customer service is unbelievable. If Turkish Airlines truly wants to improve, they need to completely overhaul their customer service process and staff. However, given their current mindset, I doubt any real change will occur. In conclusion, I would caution anyone considering flying with Turkish Airlines to think twice. The hassle and frustration are simply not worth it.

review_header: “take a long time to clear your trays”
review_text: Overall, I don't think it's deserving of being ranked 7th best airline in the world. Yes, food was pretty good, especially the dessert. And inflight entertainment has a wide range of selections. But that's where it starts getting bad. Service is horrible, they take a long time to clear your trays (2 hours) and the only time I pressed the service button, took them a good half hour to even attend to me and a further significant amount of time to serve my wine. Not to mention the drink selections are limited with only beer or wine. I asked the guy for what beers they have, he gave me a heineken and walked off. They ram the service cart through the aisle like a bulldozer without giving verbal warnings or stopping. My wife was sleeping and extended into the aisle by a bit, they hit her with the cart a few times without any apology. Also baggage took 1 hour to unload on arriving in Melbourne, not sure if this has to do with the airline or just the airport but I think it's worth mentioning.

They gave me a hotel in Istanbul as I missed the plane to Malta. I had to purchase a visa to go out from the airport. Cost me 200 euro for 4 people. They told me you can claim me back with Turkish Airlines but they refused to pay me as I didn’t gave a receipt. When I purchased the visas I asked for a receipt but the man in the office told me the visa is the receipt just send them a copy of your passport visa but later Turkish airline refused it. They scammed me. I will never travel with Turkish airline anymore.

I had selected the seat months in advance, and it showed that seat 24 hours beforehand. Upon checking in they had moved me to a much inferior seat next to the bathroom. I was told the reason was to allow a couple to sit together, but they could have easily placed this couple in the seats they moved me to. So basically, it means nothing if you preselect your seat with Turkish. They can and will move you. Otherwise, the flight was just ok. I was also a bit disappointed in the food. I had high expectations of Turkish, especially with business class. They failed to deliver.

Arriving at Istanbul we checked our departure time to Cape Town, only to find out that the flight was delayed for 7 hours. No one could give us a reason why. We were offered food vouchers that were not suitable as we had few choices of food. The flight was announced and we were herded on without any structure. It was chaos. The flight back was delayed and we were told to board and sat on the plane for nearly two hours. No explanation given. The plane was full and the seats are so uncomfortable. If the passenger in front reclines their seat, you sit with no space to watch the TV or read a book. I could not put my belongings in the space in front of me as the pouch was broken. I informed a staff member of this and he said they are aware of this. I asked for a bag to make it easier for me, and was given a big plastic bag. Staff appeared to be under pressure. Not enough toilets for all the passengers. I will not be flying Turkish airlines again.

There is a minor mistake on the ticket - My wife's Name was Incorrectly Printed. Last 2 months I am contacting and email and raise a feedback to correct the ticket but Turkish Airlines is not fixing the problem. Turkish Airlines do not have any office on Sydney and every time I contact call goes to Turkey and their customer service is very Poor. I am still holding the problem. Hope Turkish airlines will resolve the problem and we will be able to fly smoothly.

review_header: "first and last use of Turkish Airlines"
review_text: Unfortunately, it turned out a horrible experience with Turkish Airlines. 1. When checked in at Houston airport, the Turkish Airlines ground staff first weighed my carry-on luggage (smaller than a regular carry-on) and said it's 1.5 pound overweighed and asked us to repack it. After re-packing and meeting the weight limit, the same staff told us that this suitcase must be checked in and cannot be carried on. So, if so, why did she not tell us to check it in at the beginning? How professional a "5-star" APEX airlines staff could be? disappointed! 2. There is not any regular power connection (either 110V or 230V) for long-distance flights over 12 hours. All passengers are forced to use their USB jacks that potentially put the passenger privacy at risk! Even though, many USB jacks on the monitor do not function at all. So, it's impossible for many passengers to charge their portable devices over the long flights, making the long trips very boring! 3. We had over 4 hours’ layovers in Istanbul. During the transit, the Istanbul airport staff asked us to leave the gate because they needed to close it. Then, we moved to another gate but, again, we were asked to leave the second gate due to gate closure. The same thing happened again on our return stop at Istanbul airport. I would guess such rude behavior is routine in Istanbul airport as they do so normally. I must say that Istanbul airport is huge and kind of new, but what does it mean for the passengers? 4. Horrible luggage management. Our 2 luggage was checked in Houston and to be picked up in Barcelona.
