All passengers from Istanbul to Barcelona on that flight had to wait for over 2 hours at the belt before getting a luggage announcement. Then, we were asked to go to the luggage office at Barcelona airport. The luggage staff told us that our two checked-in luggage were left in Istanbul after checking their luggage computer system and verifying by calling the Istanbul airport. So, we left our hotel information and expected to receive the 2 pieces the next day with great anxiousness and stress because lots of belongings for my daughter's wedding were delayed. Surprisingly, right before we left the airport, we found our luggage was actually on the belt by that moment. What trash management! 5. When checked-in at Istanbul airport, there were 3 times of passport check and 4 times of luggage scan. The departure gate staff refused to let passengers get in even after the airport announced that departure gate. As you can imagine, this trip by Turkish Airlines brought us lots of stress/unpleasantness. The "Turkish Airlines, a 5-star APEX Airline" on the large displays in Istanbul airport is simply a shame. It was our first and last use of Turkish Airlines. Finally, to be honest, Istanbul is a beautiful city. People on the street are nice and helpful to the tourists.

I encountered an issue with the spelling of my name on my ticket, and I was concerned about potential complications. However, the staff was incredibly responsive and took immediate action to correct the name to match my passport. Their professionalism and efficiency made what could have been a stressful situation remarkably smooth. I truly appreciate their commitment to customer satisfaction. Additionally, my overall travel experience was outstanding — comfortable seating, delicious food, and attentive service throughout the flight. I highly recommend Turkish Airlines to anyone looking for a reliable and customer-focused airline. I will definitely be flying with them again in the future!

I received a refund note with my booking reference. This was on 15 June. Till today no money was returned. No further information from their side. It is almost impossible for me to get in touch with them. I tried to call several times, but nobody felt to be in charge. I have written to them ([email protected]), no response.
Customer service responded with the airline has the ultimate right to change the seats at any point.
” They put us on another flight for Friday, August 30 at 18:20, which was delayed by 8 hours. We finally arrived in Madrid 43 hours after the scheduled time.

Upon confronting, we found out that TK’s ground staff round up all the weight of our luggage individually, eg, 23.4kg to 24kg. Hence, all our luggages was unreasonably round up to heavier. Eventually, we were forced to pay overweight charges. During our confrontation, the TK’s ground staff even replied that this is the practice for all airlines in Helsinki Airport which was an absurd explanation.

With the text letting us know this, they attached a flight that they have re-scheduled us on. They changed our R/T, business class, assigned seat flight to an unassigned economy seat, which leaves one day later without any mention of a refund or paying for a hotel for the extra night. As others have mentioned, there is no one at 'customer service' who can help. Apparently once we called to ask questions and assign to our already paid for business class, this was taken as agreeing to the flight and the downgrade (!!!) with no refund, which of course, we absolutely did not agree to. Even though they canceled the flight they will also not refund (cancel) the flight. We have to submit an on-line form and wait for a possible response. I went on-line and looked up the flight that they assigned us to. Business class is sold out. I found another Turkish flight that would work. Customer service says they can't 'upgrade me.' I said, well, I paid for business class, they admit to seeing that I paid for R/T business class but they are unable (unwilling) to change to the acceptable flight. They admit to seeing that Turkish canceled our flight but are, again, are unable (unwilling) to refund the flight. I have called ten times. It is an exercise in frustration and goes against their own rules of carriage. It's sad because we were definitely looking forward to flying business with this airline. I should have read the reviews before booking. They are a shameless mess.

Turkish airlines ground staff initially promised us that they would send the luggage to Oslo via the rescheduled flight. The day of the flight came, everything was great up to the check in, but after that, things started going downhill. We checked with the ground crew regarding our luggage and they told us it was in Istanbul and that we had to reclaim it there. Upon arrival to Istanbul, we were told the luggage has already been transported to Oslo. Then we reached Oslo, waited more than an hour by the conveyor belt to collect the luggage that never even showed up and when we went to inquire about it, we were told it was still in Kuwait. Their apology was two amenity bags from business class that was useless. It’s like the staff have no idea what they’re doing and have no regard whatsoever for the luggage of their passengers. I definitely would not recommend this airline if you want to keep your sanity and don’t wan’t to be treated like cattle.

review_header: “Passengers were left to sort things out”
review_text: We boarded at Vienna, with a three-flight leg to Australia. Turkish secured our luggage all the way through, but refused to provide boarding passes for the final flight. The incredible explanation was that "code shares are not our problem". Nobody could explain why they could manage our luggage but not the actual flights. We couldn't ask further questions at Vienna because both the lounge and help desk closed before 5pm. At Istanbul Airport, the "Turkish Care" did not care. The same excuse of "it may have a Turkish code, but it's not our problem...you can figure things out in Malaysia". When we asked again at the Business Class lounge, we were directed to the gate. the flight was delayed by an hour but the lunge staff insisted we go to the gate for the earlier time because...why was that? The plane itself was simply not business class. It was cramped and most people travelling in a couple were seated a long way from their partner. Passengers were left to sort things out for themselves. Many of the good options ran out (in business class?). The configuration of the plane meant most people in business class had to step over people - which is exactly the thing elderly people book business class to avoid. I shouldn't have been surprised by people having to step over others in business class because that lack of concern for passengers was signaled as we boarded. It was an old fashioned walk up the steps from the ground. A very elderly man in front of me was using a walking stick. The ground staff turned away as if he didn't exist. I could only say "I will be right behind...if you fall, it will be onto me and not further...try not to worry". More seriously, clearly unwell people having to walk up steep stairs while the bored ground staff turn away?

The airline’s promise of complimentary hotel accommodation for long layovers proved to be a hollow one, leaving me stranded and frustrated. At the airport The airport itself, a labyrinth of billboards and advertisements, was a far cry from the serene, efficient space one might expect from a major international hub. Navigating the airport at midnight was akin to stumbling through a maze, with the signage for gates, terminals, and lounges obscured by the overwhelming visual clutter. After finally locating the business lounge where I was supposed to receive overnight accommodations, I was met with a disheartening revelation: despite being a business class passenger with a lengthy layover (over 9 hours to be eligible for accommodation by airline policies), there were no rooms available. The situation was further complicated by the fact that I was traveling with my pet. The prospect of leaving the airport with my furry companion was daunting, as I had no idea what regulations or restrictions might apply outside the terminal. Reluctantly, I opted to pay out of pocket for a hotel room within the airport as an option proposed by the airline Concierge. Determined to hold Turkish Airlines accountable, I filed a complaint and requested reimbursement for my hotel expenses. However, my efforts were met with resistance. The airline repeatedly claimed that I had failed to apply to the hotel desk at the airport, a claim that I vehemently denied. I argued that the airline’s staff had directed me to speak with the concierge inside the busies lounge, and that I had never been informed of the need to submit a formal application for accommodation. The issues with the airline My experience highlights a number of issues with Turkish Airlines’ customer service. The airline’s lack of transparency regarding its hotel accommodation policy, coupled with the failure of its staff to provide clear guidance, led to a significant inconvenience and financial burden to me. The irony of recently receiving a solicitation email from Turkish Airlines inviting me to celebrate “Customer Experience Week” while his own experience was so negative was not lost on him. While Turkish Airlines may have excelled in providing a comfortable and luxurious flight experience, their treatment during my layover was a stark reminder that even airlines which claim to be the most premium can fall short in delivering on their promises.

We booked seats 2A and 2B together. Two weeks before the flight, we received an email about "operational reasons" changing only my wife's seat. Despite multiple attempts to clarify, we got no clear answers. At check-in, we discovered my wife was moved to 3B, separating us. bUpon boarding, we found seat 2A had been sold to another passenger traveling with a dog. I was forced to sit next to the pet for 10 hours, which was often out of its carrier against airline policy.  The advertised chef seemed to be nothing more than a food heater in a fancy uniform. They were unable to accommodate simple meal modifications. We couldn't get clear information about our seat changes despite repeated attempts, both before the flight and at the airport. Think twice before booking Turkish Airlines, especially for long-haul flights. - Don't trust that your carefully selected seats will be honoured. In all our years of flying business class with various airlines, we've never experienced such poor service and disregard for pre-booked seating arrangements.
In a long range flight the difference is important. A few centimeters more width add comfort and allow better sleep. Apart from that, the crew was nice and the food between normal and good.

Aircraft had to divert to Ankara to refuel before arriving in Istanbul 2 hours late 2. Because of the delay of 2 hours in arriving in Istanbul our group of 28 people’s Turkish airlines connecting flight to Budapest flew off without us. There was no communications between the 2 sectors and no personnel waited for us at the arrival terminal to assist us with our connecting flight 3. We had to battle a sea of other passengers (at least 100 pax) who also experienced delay from other destinations and hence also missed their connecting flights. It was total chaos! 4. We, all 28 of us, were allocated seats on a flight to Budapest the next morning at 6.05am! We hence missed our pre-booked tours and hotel in Budapest! 5. After going through immigration, we were forced to wait for 2 hours for them to search for our luggages! Very very frustrating and unprofessional! This is my first and last trip with Turkish Airlines!!
The cabin service was below par except for Fatih who went above and beyond standard of service. Food was fresh and average in taste and quality.

It cares about money. Here's why I know that: I booked business class tickets in November 2023 for flights in August 2024. When I booked the tickets, I of course chose my seats, as my wife and I were traveling together. When I booked, it was far enough in advance that very few seats had been booked in business class. Well, 48 hours before our flight from Toronto to Istanbul, I get a text and an email from TA stating that for "operational reasons," my seats were being changed. However, not only did we lose our seats that I booked 9 months before, but we were not allowed to choose new seats; we were blocked from doing so on TA's website. I even called their useless customer service department a number of times and was told I couldn't choose new seats at that time, and that I'd have to do so at the airport before the flight left. Since this all occurred 48 hours before our flight, seats at that time were more expensive than they were when I booked, so I know someone paid more for my original seats and was given them (I guess that qualifies as an "operational reason" to Turkish Airlines). I also know that TA was trying to fill the few remaining empty business class seats with the then higher prices, so I wasn't allowed to pick new seats. And I know if they had filled the seats, we'd have been bumped to coach seats. Apparently, they weren't able to fill the seats because when I printed our boarding passes before leaving for the airport, we had business class seats, just not the ones I had booked 9 months before. And as bad as that was, what TA did on our return flight was even worse. This time, I printed our boarding passes the day before our flight and they showed we had the seats we had booked. However, when we were actually boarding the plane, my wife's boarding pass wouldn't scan and the person at the gate told her that her seat had been changed (but not mine), and she was in a different row. She was also now in a middle seat because on this plane the business class seat rows are 2-3-2. Of course, when I booked 9 months earlier I booked the outside two seats together. What happened this time was that someone that was either in coach or that didn't have the seats they wanted offered to pay more at the gate counter before the flight, and one of them (it was a family) was given my wife's seat. We refused to have my wife move, although a couple of TA representatives talked to us and tried to get my wife to move, including by "offering" us seats together in another row that were in the middle 3 seat area. We said no. They ended up asking another woman that was traveling alone to move and she did, so the husband and wife in this family could sit together, although the husband was in a middle seat and he grumbled the entire way from Istanbul to Toronto. The bottom line is, we will never fly Turkish Airlines again, and I advise others not to, as well. Again, they don't care about their customers. They care only about money. Shameful.

I used the Turkish Airlines app to adjust our seating again, but then received a message stating, “your flight has been disrupted,” and advising us to change our flight. Unable to find my 14:25 flight on TK's timetable, I contacted their (stupid) chatbot, which could not confirm whether the flight had been cancelled. I then changed as advised the flight to the 12:50 flight. After speaking in the evening with their help center, a turkish friend did it, we learned that the original flight had not been cancelled; the so called "disruption" was due to a change to a smaller aircraft. Consequently, we now have a stopover of more than four hours in Istanbul. Originally, we were scheduled to depart at 15:50, which was then changed to 14:25, and now we are set to fly at 12:50. Additionally, our outbound flight from Stuttgart was delayed by one hour, despite being the first flight of the morning. This experience has been quite disappointing and is not what I expect from an international airline.

In this instance Malaysian Airlines cancelled my flight from KL to Melbourne so I got transferred to this flight after a flight from KL to Singapore. The A350 was fairly new and was in the same configuration as the Singapore airlines regional business class. I found it very clean and comfortable. It was a day flight so I was able to enjoy the Turkish airlines hospitality including their "chef on board" service. Again, Turkish airlines excelled although I have found that it depends on the flight as I have had some disappointing meals at times. The wines were a good selection of Turkish and international to choose from, but no "new world wines". The service was very good, much better than my previous experiences with Turkish. Overall this new service to Melbourne was excellent and I would fly them again if they continue this level of service.

And the Turkish airlines gave us the boarding pass in a rush, so me and my partner cannot sit together for the two flights and we have no time to deal with the seats. The first flight we encountered double seating problem. But finally it was solved by the cabin crew staff. The flight from Naples to Istanbul is amazing. We have a full tray meal with in flight entertainment for this two hour flight. (I did travelled with Lufthansa from Frankfurt to Casablanca almost a 4 hour flight we still have to purchase a single bottle of water) then we arrived the Istanbul airport almost on time and we walked to the gate and ask the ground staff whether we can change our seats to a connecting seats on the next flight from Istanbul to Hong Kong. The staff replied me that the flight was full cannot do anything for us and of course we accepted. However, when we on board, we found out the flight is not full with loads of free seats and connecting seats are definitely available. The in flight service is great again. We have amenity kits with slippers even in economy class which is very impressive. Moreover, the configuration of B777-300ER is 3-3-3. There is little airlines offer this spacious seats in economy now. Overall, I think Turkish Airlines is great if they can improve the quality of ground service.

We missed our connecting flight (Istanbul-Athens) due to confusion at the gate. Spent hours back and forth between Expedia and Turkish airlines service desk and since no one was helping us we booked a separate flight to just get to Athens. Then, without notification, our return flights (Athens-Istanbul and Istanbul-Chicago) got canceled. We found out about it while trying to check in our bags at the airport. Spent 2 hours with Expedia and Turkish airlines customer service and and we had to book new flights to get back home. No empathy from either one, no basic human decency. We slept on the floor of the airport because we had no place to stay, no money and we did not want to risk anyone else going wrong.

The 2 caused missed connections which then resulted in changed flights (around 6 hours later in both situations). I missed a whole day I could have spent with family and a day of work because I arrived back at 5AM instead of 10:30 PM the previous night as I was supposed to. The company refused to reimburse me and did not offer any compensation. Staff were very rude to me. I won't be flying with them again.

Passengers started complaining and I called a cabin crew asking her to help me because I was having an asthmatic attack caused by the high temprate but she denied to help me and she just said that they couldn’t low the temperature before starting the engines. After many passengers start suffering the same problem and got angry, the complaints arrived to the pilot that lowered the temperature. I don’t have to know all this technical details. The cabin should be in ambient temperature for everybody to breathe normally. I found cabin crew behaviour irresponsible, instead of helping me, they were just worried to blame something else and wash their hands. It is already the third time I encounter this problem with Turkish airlines, but I haven’t seen any improvement yet. They like to keep cabin temperature really high, no matter if passengers complain and sweat, but cabin crew seems enjoying so much.

review_header: “there has been a change in schedule”
review_text: I booked for a group of 4 people some months in advance, and I decided to book and pay for the seats as well. 2 months after booking, there has been a change in schedule, that I accepted, but the seat booking was cancelled for all of us. I tried to get in touch with Turkish to have the seats rebooked, I sent email, filled forms, made calls, and spent 10 days with no results; we could not even have the seat booking refunded. After some more efforts at least the refund was granted, so I could rebook the seats. Following this, not so good, start, the flight was ok, with seat comfort on the average with other long range airlines, the IFE screen working very well (since the A 350 is a young plane), kind staff and good food. Even timing was ok as we arrived on schedule.

review_header: “Food good for an economy short flight”
review_text: For some reason we left 80 minutes late. Anyway we arrived 45 minutes late in Istanbul, so we could get the connection. Cabin staff was kind, the seats medium comfort. The negative side was the IFE since the screens were a bit old and touch was not working on several screens. Anyway being a less than 3 hours flight, it was not a bad issue. Food was good for an economy short flight.

review_header: “airline used to be good and trustworthy”
review_text: It would have been an hour before but they changed the gate. They would not let us on the plane. “It’s impossible”, they said. With no explanation as to why. Directed to customer service, they said it was our fault and would not help us at all. You could tell the woman working at the counter did not agree with the decision. But to get to management you had to LEAVE the airport. That’s right, LEAVE the airport. This airline used to be good and trustworthy. We have flown dozens of times. It has become a corrupt organization. DO NOT FLY WITH TURKISH AIRLINES.

We had a short connection initially! However, without any notice they changed our flight from 8:30 Am to 9:40 and then from 9:40 to 5.00 PM (Tehran to Istanbul) and then our connection flight was also got impacted and we had to stay in Istanbul for another 12 hours of layover. They gave us a hotel outside of Airport we were so tired and all they did was send us with shuttle with no food or Drink to a maybe 2 star hotel.

Major flight delay for a business trip to Korea. I am talking 4 hours plus, this destroyed my trip, had me exhausted and I won't be able to perform my work properly. All they offered is a cheap fast food meal and NOTHING ELSE.

Upon check-in, I was informed one of the two seats I had reserved well in advance was given away to another passenger. Despite my pleas, I was told nothing could be done and that my wife and I would be seated in opposite corners of the business cabin with me at the back on the left hand side and her in the front right hand side. I made a final attempt in the lounge in IST only to be told to fill out a feedback form as nothing could be done. The lounge, as usual, offered a superb variety of food and drink options and had plenty of seating available. Boarding could only be described as chaotic with gate agents doing nothing to line up passengers in their respective queues and shouting instructions in very poor English. Boarding was delayed by 90 minutes due to incoming aircraft’s late arrival. When it commenced, priority boarding, despite being announced, was not followed with a free-for-all rush of passengers to the scanners. Onboard, the cabin was in the old 2x3x2 configuration with the hard product showing its age. Upon boarding I asked the in-charge flight attendant if there was anything she could do. She was very accommodating and apologized profusely for the poor handling of the situation on the ground. As we were now placed in the middle section of the second business cabin, she blocked the middle seat allowing us to have more space and remain together. Food and beverages were tasty and I liked the appetizer trolley which allowed tasting of multiple Turkish mezes. The FA’s were exceptional in the manner and efficiency with which they looked after the passengers and the cabin chief checked on us several times clearly attempting to make up for her ground service colleagues’ indifference. IFE had a wide selection and I took in 2 full length movies during the 9-hour flight. Seat was comfortable enough in all positions and I was able to sleep for about 5 hours. Prior to landing we were served another full meal and beverage service. Due to late departure, the flight landed late and the baggage was deleivered promptly. The ground service of Turkish Airlines with both call centers and in-person staff is the biggest handicap of this airline. The staff at the airport and at call centers are indifferent, border on arrogant, have insufficient language skills, are woefully unorganized. The airline fails to realize this is the customer’s first interaction when they choose to travel with TK and unless they take it seriously and fix their shortcomings, TK will never catch up to their Middle Eastern or Asian counterparts and become a 5-Star carrier.
The flight was delayed and I lost my connected flight. I paid for a business class but very poor service. Very stressful trip and for the money I paid I didn’t get a standard service.

If you want your flights to be cancelled a couple of days before your flight and not able to reschedule or refund, if you like hours of delays and long hours of wait at the airport, definitely book with Turkish airline!

The flight, TK1764, was scheduled to depart at 19:30, but due to unspecified issues — which Turkish Airlines later conveniently labeled as “adverse weather conditions” — our flight did not leave Finland until 22:04. As a result, we missed our connecting flight TK162 in Istanbul. This forced us to pay out of pocket for Turkish visas just to enter the country and reach the hotel that the airline arranged for us to stay in until our rescheduled flight the next day. After arriving in Ho Chi Minh City, we lodged a complaint with Turkish Airlines. We initially requested a refund for the two e-visas we were forced to purchase, a reasonable ask given the circumstances. However, Turkish Airlines responded by saying they would only refund my visa, and I would have to visit a Turkish Airlines sales office in my country to claim the money. They also demanded that we provide certified documents to prove our marriage in order for my wife — who was also a registered passenger on the flight — to receive her refund. Despite complying with their absurd request, we then asked for appropriate compensation under the EC261/2004 regulation, which is meant to protect European passengers. Turkish Airlines refused to compensate us, repeatedly insisting they were “not obliged to pay compensation where flight disruption has been caused by events outside their control.” This was despite the fact that we provided evidence showing there were no weather issues at the time of our flight’s departure, and that the delay was actually due to technical problems with the aircraft. Instead of investigating the situation or providing any clarification, Turkish Airlines chose to shirk their responsibilities, blaming an issue that was clearly within their control and denying us the compensation we are rightfully owed. The way Turkish Airlines handled this situation was not just disappointing — it was infuriating and unprofessional. This experience has left us both deeply dissatisfied and questioning the integrity of Turkish Airlines.

On August 4th, 2024, I embarked on what was supposed to be a seamless business trip to Vietnam. As a frequent flyer with a million miler, platinum status, I expected top-notch service. What I received was the complete opposite. Upon arriving in Hanoi, I was shocked to find that both of my checked-in luggage were missing. What should have been a smooth process turned into a nightmare. I wasted two hours at the airport—first, waiting in vain for my luggage, and then standing in line for an hour to file a lost & found report. The frustration didn’t end there. Despite contacting the airport every day, they couldn’t locate my luggage in the system. It was only after two agonizing days that they discovered my bags were still in Istanbul. To make matters worse, according to their system, I was still listed as being in Istanbul, which is baffling given that I had clearly flown to Hanoi. When my luggage finally arrived four days later at 00:30, I was appalled to find that the carton containing sample products was damaged, and all the samples were ruined. The delivery team acknowledged the damage, and a report was filed on the spot, but that did little to mitigate the situation. The return journey to Berlin was no better. Due to an "out of sequence" error in Turkish Airlines' system, which still bizarrely showed that I was in Istanbul, the staff couldn’t issue my boarding pass. I had arrived at the airport three hours early to avoid any issues, but despite my business class status, I was left waiting outside for three hours, unable to access the business lounge. The final insult was being issued a handwritten boarding pass—something I didn’t think was possible in the 21st century. Despite my understanding that incidents can happen, Turkish Airlines’ response to my complaints was infuriating. After weeks of back and forth, submitting all requested documentation including boarding passes, receipts for urgent expenses, and the damaged sample products, I was told that it was "impossible to evaluate my case." This dismissive response, after such a horrific experience, is completely unacceptable for an airline that claims to be a 4-star carrier. From my experience, they don’t even meet the standards of a 3-star airline. Turkish Airlines’ system malfunctions, mishandling of luggage, and lack of customer care have left a terrible impression on me. This is a true account of my ordeal, and I strongly urge others to reconsider before flying with this airline.

For medical reasons, I chose my seats on all my long flights, reserved them and paid extra charges in advance. However when I checked in at the TKA counter in Tehran airport, their employee told me that there is no record of seat reservations for any part of my entire round-trip! Without my knowledge, TKA had cancelled ALL my seat reservations (for all legs of my trip, including the return trip). Later, TKA emailed to notify me that they had simply refunded the extra seat charges, without any explanation. During the 13-hour transatlantic flight, I ended up with great discomfort on an unsuitable seat, which limited my mobility. I must mention that I am 64 years old, and extended lack of mobility puts me at risk for deep tissue thrombosis. The sudden seat cancelation by TKA, and gross mishandling of my seat on the long 13-hour flight shows a complete disregard for the passengers’ health, and convenience. I must emphasize that even though TKA had my email address, and contact number, it offered no explanation or compensation for this botched seat reservation.

Our flight was delayed for over two hours, and unfortunately, there was no staff available to provide explanations or assistance during this time. I wanted to postpone my flight for the second part of my journey, but three staff members assured me that I would still have enough time to catch my international flight. However, upon arrival, I was refused entry. I then had to go to the ticket office, where I spent a considerable amount of time explaining my situation to a staff member who initially did not speak English. Fortunately, I was eventually assisted by someone who could communicate effectively, and they agreed to transfer my ticket to the next day. This experience was extremely stressful, and the lack of support from your team was disappointing. I would not recommend your airline based on this experience, as it caused significant inconvenience and anxiety. I had to spend a significant amount of money to sleep in an airport hotel and missed an important day in my daughter's life. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I hope to see improvements in your customer service in the future.

review_header: "I don't think I will choose Turkish again"
review_text: This was their awfully poor response received: "Dear *** ***, First of all, we are very sorry for this unpleasant situation you have experienced. We pay the utmost attention to ensure our passengers' satisfaction from the first to the last moment of their flight and place importance on showing a customer-oriented approach. We would like you to know that we scrutinize the feedback on Turkish Airlines employees/employees of the service provider firms we receive service from, together with the authorized units. In consequence of our investigation based on your feedback, we have found out that the information given to you complies with the rules. We completed our investigation of the matter you have mentioned in your feedback. Unfortunately, during the interpersonal communication, misunderstanding caused by the tone of voice and style is possible from time to time. We would like you to know that we will consider your opinions absolutely while reviewing our communication processes related to this subject. However, in order to narrow the error margin, we can repeat our investigation gladly if you could send us a different detail. We wish to offer you a better experience in your future travels"

My staff going to the Turkish Airline office Us going to the airport - Eventually cutting our long awaited trip on a sailing yacht by 2 days short - having to rush to the Zagreb airport - With Nobody able to assist -- All we heard is WE are awaiting from the Feedback Centre - This was ludicrous on all levels- Had me in Tears for Days.

I was flying from Serbia to Mumbai on 30th August. My flight which was supposed to depart from Belgrade at 15:45, left at 17:00, my next flight from Istanbul to Mumbai was supposed to leave at 20:15. The first flight was not only late to arrive in Istanbul but was looking for parking for 25mins! At the airport I kept looking for help but found none, I finally made it to the helpdesk situated in one far corner and the crew was very unfriendly and had zero interest in helping out. Finally they booked me on a flight to Dubai and to Mumbai from there. The journey became much longer than what I had planned for. Given no other choice I agreed and checked if my luggage needs to be collected or will it get transferred to the new flight. I was assured that my luggage will be arrive in Mumbai. I kept checking at every boarding point of my luggage is there and I was assured that it is. I land in Mumbai and my luggage is no where to be found! I get no clear answers from the crew. No help. It has been a nightmare!

We did not get offered some drinks (like water) while waiting for departing. When we check-in we asked the attender if we can still make the next connecting flight. She told us they will arrange that. I asked if they can hold that plane for a short while and she said probably. When we arrive at Istanbul there is an attendant waiting for us and she help us leading to the next connecting gate. But on they way she got the news the gate is closed and we can't make it. They did not give us some extra time, so those flight will be delayed for 15 minutes. We are 14 passengers who missed our connecting flight and it seems there are only 7 new boarding passes ready. We were not chosen for one of those boarding passes. So we need to get a new boarding pass and arrange a hotel + transfer as the next flight will only be the next day at 6:55 am. This process took almost 4 hours before we are in the hotel room with all the waiting at several counters with very long lines. For all this time we were never offered some drinks/snacks. When we arrive at the hotel at 10:30 pm we went straight to bed, as we need to take the transfer back to the airport at 3 am. So that was a very short sleep and there was no breakfast. We took our breakfast at the airport and is cost for the 4 of us €52 for 4 sandwiches and drinks. The seller has no ticket as I ask for it and I have only cash. Further when we arrive at Düsseldorf we have to pay extra for the extra parking time. That is €25. I would like to be compensated for those extra costs.  They respond they can't give any compensation and there are no personal excuses at all. The only nice things about Turkish Airlines is that they have very nice aircraft with nice tv screens and friendly attendants and that they give the transfer and Hotel for free, although the process of getting those is too long.

review_header: "one of our bags couldn't be found"
review_text: I chose Turkish Airlines to travel back from Heathrow to Lahore via Istanbul on 23rd August 2024. We booked this flight a couple of months in advance in June 2024, however in July 2024 they changed the time of the flight and pushed it back by 5 hours arbitrarily leaving us with no other option to change flights as we had to travel back to Pakistan on 23rd August so we stuck with Turkish Airlines for our journey. We were a total of 6 passengers (family members) travelling together and booked all our luggage through Turkish Airlines Counter at Heathrow at 3:30 AM and received the boarding passes for both flights along with tags of our luggage. Upon reaching Pakistan in the morning of 24th August 2024 at 1:30 AM, we waited to collect our luggage however to our utter astonishment, one of our bags couldn't be found. We waited at the airport till the very end until the luggage belts went empty however there was no trace of our bag. We reached out to the Airport authorities and filed Property Irregularity Report and provided them with bag tag, boarding pass and picture of the bag on spot and they assured that they have received a list of missing baggage and that our baggage has been located and it will come tommorow in the next flight. To our disappointment, 5 days have passed but they haven't sent our bag yet. I have been taking up this matter with Turkish Airlines and Lahore Airport authorities on daily basis but with no luck.  I am extremely disappointed and suffering at the hands of Turkish Airlines !

A significant delay on my flight from Tashkent to Istanbul caused me to miss my connecting flight to Riga, resulting in a total delay of 9 hours at my final destination. Despite being entitled to accommodation according to the Turkish Airlines passenger rights policy due to the lengthy delay, none was provided. This was particularly frustrating as my first leg had already been rescheduled from 2:30 am to 5:40 am, leaving me extremely tired even before starting the long layover. The absence of accommodation meant I had no chance to rest during an already exhausting journey. When I later reached out to customer support to discuss this denial, I encountered further indifference with no gesture of goodwill or even an apology extended to me. The situation was made even more challenging by the staff's disheartening demeanor, which suggested a lack of understanding of their own policies or willingness to assist, both of which are equally concerning. This dismissive behaviour only added to the stress of an already tough circumstance. The ongoing mismanagement of the issue by Turkish Airlines was especially infuriating. Despite my clear rights to compensation under SHY Passenger Rights, the airline initially denied my request. It was only after I brought the matter to the attention of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation that I eventually received the compensation I was entitled to. It's truly disheartening that Turkish Airlines didn't take initiative on their own and only acted after facing external pressure. This whole ordeal was unnecessarily stressful and revealed significant flaws in their customer service. To avoid similar issues in the future, I recommend that Turkish Airlines enhance their training for staff regarding passenger rights and ensure consistent application of policies. Moreover, adopting a more proactive stance in customer service, such as promptly providing accommodation, compensation or even a goodwill gesture after the fact of incident, could greatly improve the overall experience for passengers. While I appreciated the amenities on board and the professionalism of the cabin crew, the overall experience was heavily overshadowed by the airline's lack of accountability and the exhausting process to obtain compensation. Based on this encounter, I can only give them a rating of 2 stars.

Cabin crews on the flights never smile and are very intimidating. They almost bark at you when asking for your choice of meal and occasionally show signs of annoyance towards you. That was my experience on the first leg of my flight, I haven’t boarded my second leg but have just approached a ground staff at the boarding gate. Not only do no one acknowledge you when you’re waiting to talk to them, but also the experience of communicating with is bad. My seat was changed due to operational reason which I have paid extra for and I was hoping to get a satisfactory solution to this unwanted change, either issue me a refund or change it to a seat that I actually wanted, but nope, that’s it. You just gotta suck it up and get what you’re assigned for even when you’ve paid for it. The ground staff again never smile and didn’t show the slightest of willingness to help. My first time flying with Turkish Airlines and will probably never fly again with them.

My connection in Istanbul was tight - 1 hour 15, but I assumed it would be guaranteed.  On landing, with 40 minutes to make the connection, the plane pulled off the runway and then sat for an hour on a taxiway miles from the terminal with no communication other than a desultory 'we're waiting for a parking place'. I missed the connection to KL, but when I got to the terminal saw a notification that I'd already been put on the next flight leaving at 01.35 am. I tried to get on wifi to download the boarding pass needed to go through to international departures, but wifi is not easily available. I had to find a machine (with a long queue) to scan my passport, get a code (which you couldn't print it because the printer wasn't working) and put it into my mobile. However, the mobile already showed that I was allegedly connected to the network (I wasn't) and gave no way to do so. Cue 20 stressful minutes trying to get help from 6 indifferent officials. I was almost in tears when one young man finally took pity and got a paper boarding pass for me. I then spent seven hours in the business class lounge - which is good, comfortable, and has excellent free wifi, unlike the rest of the airport - before being able to continue my journey. On the return leg, I flew into Kuala Lumpur from Kota Kinabalu and had to transfer to the international terminal by bus. This required going through immigration. Only when I reached the international terminal and couldn't find a business class lounge was I informed that Turkish Airlines had closed one of its two - extraordinarily, it had done this in the international terminal from which it flies - and kept the other one (in the terminal I had just left, and from which it does NOT fly) open. Turkish didn't provide anyone to help at the transfer desk until 3 hours before departure, so I managed to talk my way into another business class lounge and spent four hours there. The Turkish official who appeared at 8pm asked if I wanted to go to the lounge in the first terminal, but was unable to tell me how that could be done when it means going back through Malaysian immigration. The logic of closing your lounge in the terminal you fly from escapes me, but if you must do it, then for heaven's sake tell people where it is before they get the bus. Incidentally, the app had allowed me to check in online this time, which was just as well because immigration had asked to see my boarding passes. Since you can't obtain a paper one until 3 hours before departure in the international terminal, I'm at a loss to understand how I'd have reached it had ithe app not been working again. The flights were excellent. The crews were pleasant and helpful, the meal good, the seats comfortable, and I slept very well. I have no complaints about Turkish Airlines once you're actually in the air. But Istanbul Airport is just too big, and the official connection times given far too short. Lesson learned, I will leave 4 hours minimum another time. Alas, the airline app is a liability, and it is also ludicrous when passengers are being asked to do everything online, to reduce the availability of free wifi in the terminals to one hour and put them through such hoops to connect to it. When ground service matches its counterpart in the air, I will happily fly Turkish again.

If I hadn't got him £19 Big Mac McDonald's in Turkey airport he wouldn't of had any food on the plane. I had informed the attendants that he hadn't recieved a meal. They said he isn't on list. They said it not there fault, which I can understand. They did give him am adult meal which he didn't eat any of the foods available. Which is why I specifically request a kids meal when booking. Lodged a complaint was told it wasnt requested on the booking by the complaint centre. I called the call centre, they acknowledged that he was meant to get a kids meal and goodie bag. Contacted complaints centre again and forwarded a screen shot of my ticket booking (which showed a childrens meal) and still said it doesn't show. I am truly disgusted and disappointed with Turkish Airlines. They are quick enough to want to charge for anything extra but can't fulfill there actual ticket details

review_header: "16 hours late is the new on time"
review_text: Our latest trip the aircraft diverted after 2 hours before we had had any food or drink. We then sat on the plane for 7 hours and only got a glass of water after 6 hours. Communication from the captain was almost non existent. But after 4 hours we were told we would refuel and continue. Twenty minutes later the crew realised they didn’t have the crew duty hours to continue and we would return to Istanbul. An hour later we were told a new crew would come and take us to Montreal. We then sat in the closed terminal for a further 8 hours overnight before we flew to destination. Given the initial departure was late we arrived 16 hours late. On contacting Turkish Airlines for the compensation specified in their terms and conditions we were told that we were not entitled as we had arrived at destination. So I guess that 16 hours late is the new 'on time' for this airline!

The seat was broken. My seat wouldn’t recline for an 11-hour flight, and the flight attendants offered no help. Customer service was equally unhelpful when I tried to address the issue after the flight. Save your money and consider other airlines that prioritize passenger comfort and service.

I had booked my business class tickets for a round trip a month in advance to make sure I was beside my wife and newborn baby in the bassinet seat. Before taking off, a couple other passengers were switching seats and it did not seem to be anything out of the ordinary when I took the seat beside my wife. Until out of nowhere, I was informed that my seat was changed without any notice and worst of all, my seat did not even function! It had no power and no reclining even in a business class seat. Despite trying to tell the cabin crew that it must be a mistake and showing them the ticket I booked online, the male staff were rude, constantly cut me off, and kept raising their voices to tell me to switch to the defective seat. I understand that they have their jobs to do, however some common curtesy and respect would have been appreciated since they understood that we were deliberately separating parents of a newborn, forcing me to sit away from them, and giving me the only defective seat in the section! I could not get any sleep on a 12 hour flight and was shown no compassion for the airlines mistake. This was our worst experience with an airline and we will never travel with Turkish air again.
Terrible experience, will not be flying with them anymore. Why pay extra and get treated unprofessionally.

I booked a trip to Japan with Turkish Airlines with long layovers (16h and 14h layovers) so according to the website I was eligible to an accommodation. However, upon arriving at the airport, after struggling to get someone to help me to find the hotel desk at the airport, I was informed that I did not qualify for the free stay because there was a shorter layover flight available, which invalidated my eligibility to a hotel room. However, this shorter layover flight was never presented during the booking process on Turkish Airlines' website. In addition to that, to confirm if I was indeed eligible to one hotel room, I’ve contacted the customer service on the phone, which was coldly impolite and unhelpful but redirected me to another service that confirmed that I was eligible to an accommodation. This misleading information led me to sleep in a bench at the airport, with a 16h layover and no airline or airport staff support. Later I found out that even if the shorter layover flight is full, we are not entitled to an accommodation which makes no sense to me. To make it worse, at the hotel desk counter, after being denied the right of accommodation, I wanted to make sure that this wouldn’t happen again on my way back home, since I had another 14h layover in Istanbul. I kindly asked the staff at the counter if they could confirm my eligibility to an accommodation and they said that it was to soon for them to know, since they receive the list of passengers eligible to one hotel room a few days before arrival. It’s impossible to have a hold of them on the phone, and even through emails they seem so careless as if their clients problems while flying with them were not their responsibility. If you are trying to contact their customer service, I would recommend using X, they are quite helpful there. The only way to make a complain is trough their feedback page, I’ve been in contact ever since this happened (one month ago). The inflight service was nice, but the ground staff is horrible and very unhelpful which led me to experience a night in a bench at the airport. I believe what makes a good airline is more than its inflight services is its customer service. After all, we want to get help when we are encountering problems with the service/product that we've bought. This is nonexistent in Turkish airlines. I would be very careful and confirm the right for accommodation before booking your trip to avoid this problem or simply chose another airline.

I was traveling from Bangkok to the UK with a stopover in Istanbul this summer. My 13-year-old son had saved up for months to buy a skateboard, which he was understandably excited to bring on our trip. To my astonishment, despite clear assurances from the check-in staff at Bangkok that the skateboard could be safely transported as hand luggage to London Gatwick, we were met with a completely different story in Istanbul. It's incomprehensible that Turkish Airlines staff at Bangkok would have given us the green light to bring the skateboard on board, knowing full well that we would be transferring through their own hub in Istanbul. Surely, they must have some understanding of the items permitted in transit through their airport. Their failure to inform us of any potential issues is a clear case of negligence. When the inevitable happened in Istanbul, and security confiscated my son’s skateboard, declaring it a dangerous weapon, we were utterly dumbfounded. The sheer absurdity of this claim, coupled with the callous manner in which it was handled, left us stunned and bewildered. Our desperate pleas to reconsider were met with indifference. We were simply told to contact customer service, a suggestion that felt like a cruel joke given our delayed connection. Weeks later, the airline has persisted in sending automated responses denying any wrongdoing. It's clear they have no interest in resolving the issue or acknowledging the distress caused. To add insult to injury, Turkish Airlines has completely shirked responsibility for the misinformation provided by their own staff. While I understand that the airline isn't directly responsible for the rules at Istanbul Airport, they should undoubtedly be aware of the items that can and cannot be carried through their hub. Their refusal to accept any blame for this debacle is a testament to their appalling customer service. My son was heartbroken, and as a parent, it was devastating to witness his disappointment. The experience has left a bitter taste, and I wouldn’t hesitate to advise anyone considering Turkish Airlines to think twice. Their treatment of passengers, especially children, is nothing short of disgraceful.

Unfortunately, our return flight from Istanbul to Tunis was a nightmare. The service was horrendous. The gate was changed three times, and Istanbul Airport is huge, so getting from the initially indicated gate, B3B, to the final gate, A8B, took over 30 minutes. No one was available to help us, and the staff we approached claimed they didn’t speak English. It's surprising that airport staff would only speak their native language. When we checked the board, we saw that the flight was delayed from 15:20 to 15:40, and the gate was changed to A8B. Despite the delay, the flight finally departed at 16:09, but the gate was closed early, and we were told we had to buy a new ticket. We were sent to two different Turkish Airlines desks for assistance, which involved walking around 45 minutes, only to be met with incredibly rude behavior. One of the staff members laughed in my face, insulted me in Turkish, and threw our passports and tickets back at us. She outright said that the gate changes and lack of personnel at the initial gate were the customer’s problem and that the airline wouldn't take responsibility. When it came to rescheduling the flight, we needed to leave the same day as we didn’t have a hotel reservation and had very little money left. We're both students. They kept offering us different prices for rescheduling—from $320 to €420, and finally €300. To make matters worse, they withheld our luggage, which contains my vital medication. I repeatedly informed them how crucial it was for me to have it, but they just laughed. They told us that our luggage would only be transferred to our next flight if we rescheduled with them; otherwise, they couldn’t guarantee it wouldn’t get lost. Overall, the service was atrocious. I wasn’t the only one being treated this way. I spoke to the manager, who appeared apologetic in front of me but laughed as soon as I turned around. I can understand some Turkish from high school but am not fluent, which is why I spoke to them in English.

review_header: "wish I had used a different airline"
review_text: If you paid for seats or any special services then need to change the return date you will lose everything. I changed my return date and ended up paying an additional $500 for the trip on top of the $600 date change fee. They deleted my seats and baggage for the trip from America which was not changed. They changed the return as requested however the fees I paid for return were not carried over. I wish I had used a different airline.
I tried to contact them many times but their phone is busy, they are not even picking up. I do not know if should take my first two flights or not. That`s very annoying. Terrible airline

They make you board at Istanbul airport in a flight that is already delayed by 3 hours. You get on the flight to realise that the flight will be further delayed by 90 minutes and you are just left sitting there waiting for take off. This happened in both journeys, onward and return. The cabin crew is still polite but experience from delays, quality of food, etc hampers the experience. Infotainment system is also outdated on all sectors.

Upon checking my bags, I have been told that flight has been overbooked, and me and my partner got stand by tickets. At the end, Turkish airlines started asking people who would be willing to stay an extra night for 400€, they found quite few of them, people got excited, but at the end there was enough free seats for everyone to fly, some people then refused to board, flight was delayed for another hour, etc. Overall, do not recommend, will never be choosing Turkish airlines.
I would never use this airline again!

For long connections, TK offers either a suite in their lounge or, if the scheduled connection is more than 9 hours in business class (and no shorter connections were possible) they give you a hotel room to stay. My scheduled connection time was 12.5 hours, so in theory I should have been offered a room. The flight leaving Luxemburg was quite late, and arrival was about 9 hours before my next connection. When I went to ask for the hotel room, I was told that it was not possible because they were going to have to pick me up in 5 hours in order to come back to the airport, as their hotels are quite far from the airport. So I asked if I could use one of their lounge suites, and was refused because my scheduled connection time was too long, and the suites are only for shorter scheduled connections. Never mind that my connecting time was shortened by their late arrival, they calculated in the basis is the scheduled connection time and not the real connection time. In short, my option was to sit in their lounge and wait out the 9 hours. Their inflight staff are fairly attentive, but their ground staff showed no interest or initiative in accommodating a passenger with a service they promise and then use any excuse to not deliver. If you have a reasonably short connection time, this airline isn't a bad option. But when connecting times are longer, do yourself a favor and pay more with another airline. These people have zero motivation for honoring their own promises, and their only interest seems to be to say "can't help you" and get you out of their faces.

Delaying our flight in Nevsehir for us to miss our connection to Denizli for 10 min. Of course the flight was still there when we passed in front of the gate, but the terminal is so long that we couldn’t even dream of getting to the gate on time. Then they offered a meal at a fast food but not even a choice of the menu, this is restricted to options we didn’t like and no possibility to get WiFi or a place to rest when we had to wait 7 hours at the airport and they make us take a flight in the middle of the night, arriving at 3am in Denizli. Not even getting a taxi to our hotel arriving there at 3am. Horrible experience with sending us to 5 different desks to get a disgusting meal and a terrible back pain.

Despite booking our seats well in advance to ensure my family could sit together, the airline changed our seats at the last minute, separating us across different rows. This was particularly stressful as I was traveling with my young child, and the inconvenience caused unnecessary anxiety for all of us. The customer service team offered no helpful solutions, and the lack of communication made the situation even worse. We were left feeling like our concerns didn’t matter, and the whole experience made what should have been a smooth journey into a chaotic one. I expected a much higher standard from Turkish Airlines, especially considering their reputation. Unfortunately, this experience has left a negative impression, and I will think twice before choosing to fly with them again.
Every flight I've taken with them for the past few years has been delayed or cancelled. Rude staff and customer support.

We planned to fly from Antalya to Belgradeq ith our cat. Both flights were with Turkish Airlines. The first flight was domestic (Antalya-Istanbul). The flight was delayed by several hours, our connection was missed. Although we were assured that it wouldn't be a problem because most of the people on that flight were connecting to the next one. When we arrived, we were given tickets for another flight, which was scheduled to depart the next day. It took us half an hour to get a hotel voucher. Another two hours for them to sort everything out and take us to the hotel. We were with our cat, who was incredibly scared and very stressed. We were told that since we had a pet, we would be placed in a separate hotel. There was another couple with a cat with us. In the end, we were taken to a hotel where we waited for 40 minutes. When everyone else had left except for us and the couple with the cat, they asked us who we were and told us that pets were not allowed in that hotel. After much difficulty, we managed to persuade them to let us stay. They scheduled a transfer for us at 10 AM the next day. After the transfer didn’t arrive in 20 minutes, I asked the reception several times, and they told me it was normal. The transfer was almost an hour late. When it finally arrived, it turned out that a lady had forgotten her bag at her hotel, and we all went to that hotel to retrieve it instead of going straight to the airport. We were delayed by 1.5 hours. Since we had a cat (so some procedures needed to be done for him) and had to pay for our overstay in the country, those 2 hours before the flight weren't enough (they should bring us 3 hours before the flight, not 2 hours), we didn’t have enough time to catch the flight. We arrived at the gate at the last minute, and I saw the last passenger being let through and the door closing behind them just as I was standing at the counter handing over my passport and ticket. This story could have been avoided if they had waited just one more minute. We went to the Turkish Airlines desk to sort things out because if the transfer had not been delayed by an hour and a half, we would have made the flight. After talking to several employees, they told me that two hours was enough time and that it was entirely our fault. We did everything as quickly as possible in that airport but that time wasn't enough. In the end, they told us that the next available flight was the following day and that it would cost us $1800 per person. There were three of us and a cat who was already in an unmanageable state. We were left with no choice, and I had to spend $5500 to buy tickets for a 1.5-hour flight. We had to spend another night somewhere. Our cat hadn’t eaten or used the toilet for over a day. Trying to find a place to stay in the airport led us to the cheapest hotel available, which cost 400 euros per night. In the end, due to the airline's mistakes, I was forced to spend $6000, and we spent two more days in extreme stress.  I will never use Turkish Airlines again. It was a nightmare come true.

Two pieces of luggage were lost at the airport; one was returned after three days, and the other has not been returned yet. A week has passed, and we have received no response from you, and there have been no apologies or compensation. The worst airline in the world! I do not recommend this airline to anyone.

We were not able to get seats together on the app- sorry, Turkish- but charging for changing your seat-selection looks for me like a cheap cash grab, but the lady got us all in one row, 2 adults, 1 child, 1 infant. After asking (on my flight to Guangzhou I was offered that service) if we could check-in our cabin trolleys for free, she agreed. Great service. Then we got aboard and were surprised that we were given seats in one of the front rows with a baby basinet. Our little one did not sleep in there and I believe when I woke up I found that our 4 year old son had cozied into that bed...Food was nice, cabin crew was very friendly and attentive, at night we just got water bottles. I do not know anything about drink selection in the galley as I was sleeping all night. On the whole flight I managed to watch Frozen II not even whole. In Istanbul we planned a longer layover to get a free tour of Istanbul. They were extremely friendly and efficient, unfortunatelly the tour just consisted of driving around in a bus seeing some of the sights with 2 fotostops and a very fast breakfast. In the end, we returned at 11, our flight onwards was boarding 1525. In the end, I would recommend- if you are in that situtation, to ask to be left out in town and take public transport back, the food options in Istanbul looked quite delicious, and having lunch viewing the Bosphor is way better than the Food Court at the airport. Not Turkish Airlines fault, but beware: Istanbul Airport is ridiculously expensive, like a crossaint for 8 Euro, or a quarter pounder menu at McDonald*s for 20 Euro! The flight from Istanbul to Nuremberg was nice, cabin crew friendly. Can recommend Turkish.

They gave me a piece of paper promising to refund me 400 EUR. It turns out that in order to receive a refund I have to fill out a form written in poor English with too much information, send all kinds of documentation and then they say they will make a wire to my bank account instead of simply crediting the card that was charged. However after that whole ordeal they denied my refund with no explanation and with no option to respond, Only to go to their (poorly designed) website and create a new case! I'm extremely frustrated and their is no one to talk to! Their flights themselves are nice but that's it!

I called the Turkish Airlines customer service. I explained that I had just booked the ticket a couple minutes prior to the call and realized the error. I paid extra for all the bells and whistles including extra legroom. The representative would not change the ticket for the flight back. This will be the first and last time that I fly Turkish Airlines.

5 hours only to be denied boarding as we had missed the connection. Staff at Istanbul rude and dismissive, unhelpful and lied when giving information. Return from Istanbul delayed for 2 hours again no communication and as a result of late arrival missed train connection home. Hopefully never have to fly with Turkish again

Both seats were changed to standard seats because of plane changes which we were not informed about. I got a refund for the flight to San Francisco as a traveler's cheque which she could only use in another Turkish Airlines flight. For the trip from San Francisco, I got no refunds because I checked the situation before the flight and bought another extra legroom seat, seeing her original seat was not available anymore. They refused to refund me for the original seat purchase, saying that I have to contact their customer service to get a refund, so I had to pay the full amount for another extra legroom seat purchase. I contacted their customer support 6 times asking for a refund but I was rejected, saying that she already flew on an extra legroom seat. So I had to purchase two extra legroom seats for her flight from San Francisco and never got refunded for the seat purchase that got cancelled due to their plane change. Turkish Airlines used to be so good. It's so sad to see that their service quality has degraded so badly.

However, upon arriving at the airport, we were informed that we did not qualify for the free stay because there was a potential flight with only a 10-hour layover, which invalidated our eligibility. What's worse, this shorter layover option was never presented to us during the booking process on Turkish Airlines' website. It felt like a bait-and-switch tactic to deny us the accommodation we were expecting and looking forward to. To add insult to injury, while we were trying to resolve this issue with their representatives, we witnessed two other families being similarly denied accommodation. This whole experience left a bitter taste in my mouth. Turkish Airlines' promise of complimentary accommodation on long layovers appears to be a scam designed to lure customers in, only to find any reason to deny them when they arrive. It's incredibly misleading and unfair to customers who plan their travel based on these advertised perks, only to have them arbitrarily revoked. I would caution anyone considering Turkish Airlines for their travel needs to be wary of these misleading promises. Don't count on the layover accommodation offer being honored, as our experience suggests they will find any excuse to back out of it. This level of dishonesty and inconsistency in service is simply unacceptable for a reputable airline.

First leg of my journey was cancelled and missed the connection flights as a result. Spent hours on the phone with Turkish Airline with no result, no alternative flights or full refund offered. Rude operators, no empathy, no solutions offered.

Even before the flight at check in I had to pay £130 for 12kg of hold luggage. After about an hour of flight the captain made an announcement that we have to land in Istanbul due to operational issues. While I was relieved to make a safe landing in Istanbul, the ensuing chaos was unacceptable. The management of this common cancellation scenario by Ajet Airlines was horrific and chaotic. Hundreds of passengers were made to wait until 2 AM at the transfer desk section, which had only 10 seats available. There was no explanation of the process, and no provision of water or food. The hotel transportation and organization of passengers into groups was equally disastrous. Despite repeatedly calling out names to form groups, no progress was made. We spent two hours in the baggage claim area, waiting for transportation to the buses. Staff at the airport were unable to speak sufficient English to communicate and passengers had to interpret on their behalf. Other passengers were receiving texts about flights they could take the following morning which was from a different airport. I wasn't receiving these texts so instead of getting a bus to a hotel I decided to book another flight with a different airline from Istanbul airport to ensure I got back home to London. Since 4 June I have been communicating with both Ajet and Turkish Airlines for a refund or some compensation with no success. Absolutely appalled at their treatment.

Awaited until 2200hrs flight arrival hoping to get luggage. Unfortunately no. Baggage claim section officer informed they couldn't locate my 2× baggage (1 for my wife). Tried to contact Turkish airline head office via phone which was provided by Turkish airline ticket desk, Level 5. Bad luck, unable to reach via phone neither they do response on email. Just because of their carelessness I have to spent extra expenses for living & travelling as I belong to Wales hence, thought to confirm whilst I am at London. Won't recommend this airline.

First of, you should know that, any problem you have, is not solveable over the phone with Turkish Airlines. What you have to do, is to submit a web form, for any complaint you have, regardless of how urgent it might be. My latest issue is around the stopover hotel deal they have. You can find the details about it here: https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/flights/stopover/index.html So under this program, we had our hotel booked July 3rd, for 2 days for July 16-17 in istanbul. In the meantime, our ticket change due our loss of my wife's father came through on July 4th. However, 11 days after our change, a day before our stay, Turkish airlines canceled our hotel stay. I have been fighting wiht customer service on web messages over this issue. First they said passengers who have canceled their tickets are not eligible under the program. We didn't cancel our tickets, so I send another response. Then they reply with saying, they canceled it under the obscure clause of "Passengers whose flights are cancelled for operational reasons and whose tickets are changed cannot benefit from Stopover in Istanbul." Our flight was not an operation cancellation. I don't think the customer service even knows what it means. To me, operational means changes done by the airline. I'm still giving the fight but this is enough to frustrate any customer. I'm sure people have similar stories about solving problems at Turkish Airlines, which is nearly impossible. Their first answer is usually a NO. They don't even read what you're sending to them. If you're just flying with them and everything goes as expected fine, but if something goes wrong and you need to solve a problem, good luck because you won't find anybody to talk to.

Their response was abysmal. The customer service was the worst I've encountered. I identified that someone had taken my bag and left theirs, provided a photo of their baggage tag, and shared all relevant details with Turkish Airlines. Despite this, they failed to take any meaningful action. Dnata informed me that the other passenger had indeed taken my bag, yet Turkish Airlines continued to give me incorrect information, saying my bag was still lost. They refused to update my claim or contact the passenger to retrieve my bag. I waited an entire week for my bag, during my graduation trip to London, with nothing but the clothes on my back. Now, as I try to file for compensation for my expenses, their website blocks me with a vague error message: "Your process cannot be continued. Please try again." It's clear they don't want to compensate me for my rightful claim.

Because we were traveling business class, we were eligible for a 2-night stay at a 5-star hotel, but the hotel's system only showed a reservation for one night, which started at 2 pm – almost 12 hours from our arrival time. With no available rooms, we found ourselves stranded in the hotel lobby. The customer service experience was equally appalling. I spent over an hour on the phone with Turkish Airlines’ customer relations service, being transferred from one representative to another. Finally, I was told to write a feedback and was assured that an "urgent" notice was added to my case,. Despite this, we waited in the hotel lobby from 1:40 am till 4:30 pm without any follow-up from Turkish Airlines. In a foreign country with my child, I did my best to find a solution. I called all the nearby hotels and finally managed to book a room on my own, paying with my own card. Only then could we finally fall asleep. This was the worst travel experience I have ever had. Turkish Airlines’ customer relations system proved to be utterly useless, offering no assistance when we needed it most. It’s shocking that the airline continues to advertise its stopover offers in Istanbul when the reality is far from the promising image they portray. The fact that we were traveling business class makes this situation even more unacceptable, as we expected a high level of service and support. I hope my story prevents others from facing a similar ordeal. Turkish Airlines needs to address these issues urgently to ensure no other passengers endure the same nightmare.
Customer service is non existent, everyone is very rude (from call centre to lounge to on board). The food was really bad in business.

The staff were consistently rude and unhelpful, despite their promises of great accommodations. They only provided facilities under specific, unclear conditions, which was frustrating. Despite having a 24-hour layover and eligibility for accommodations according to their website, they denied me because they said there was another flight with the same origin but shorter layover available that I could have bought. Interestingly, my flight was the only choice available to me because the later flight was fully booked. But they said that doesn’t matter! This contradictory reasoning blew my mind. I was also denied lounge access and had to spend 24 hours in the airport sleeping on the floor/rock hard chairs. It was evident that their focus was on selling tickets rather than ensuring passenger comfort. This wasn't the first time I had issues with this airline; I've flown with them five times and each time reminded me why I dislike their service. In the future, I'm willing to pay more to support an airline that genuinely cares about travelers and provides a better experience.

review_header: "last time I will fly with Turkish"
review_text: While the transit was smooth with no delays, my luggage didn’t make it to Madrid with me. Turkish Airlines had no idea where the luggage is and tried to blame Jetstar even though Jetstar confirmed that they passed it on in Singapore. After 4 days the luggage was found in a completely different city, Skopje (not even on my route). The airport staff at Skopje airport acted immediately to sort the issue and load the luggage on the next flight to Madrid (again though Istanbul). I went to the airport to collect the luggage from the flight that it was supposed to be on and to my surprise Turkish Airlines has lost the luggage yet again. There is no clear way to contact them and on every attempt I’m diverted to the online complain forum. The worst part is that this is my second time chasing luggages in 12 months with Turkish Airlines. This is the last time I will ever fly with Turkish Airlines. Disgraceful service!!

(June 28 - 2024) We arrived in Zagreb, we discovered that our luggages were still in Istanbul. The plan was to travel to Dubrovnik on the same day. Our luggage came on the second day which forced us to cancel our first day trip since we were out of our luggage and most importantly our medication without a specific date on when we would receive our luggage. On the way back from Zagreb to Beirut through Istanbul again (July 5 - 2024), our first flight was delayed for 1 hour which made us miss our second flight home from Istanbul Airport. We arrived to Istanbul at midnight, they scheduled us on a flight after 6 hours without providing us with any essential services like a place to sleep or a bench to have a nap except, for a food voucher from a fast food snack that we cannot consume at midnight nor as breakfast. We even had to pay for our internet after the free 1 hour they provided to any traveler, not to mention that the communication with the staff wasn't easy and poor because of their lack of good English especially in such a critical situation.  A connecting flight with Turkish Airlines is highly not recommended.

The Boeing 777-300ER aircraft does not have individualized air-conditioning vent, and for more than 6 hours - from Istanbul to KL - the cabin was so warm that many passengers, had to use the security information card as fans. When I asked the flight attendant, she said there's nothing the pilot could do, and confirmed that the pilot knew about the problem. From that point onward, there was not a single announcement by the cabin crew or the pilot acknowledging the issue. Nor was there any apology from them when we touched down.

Last night I tried to use these, now Open Tickets, to rebook flights. After two attempts of thee system not accepting my various cards, I gave up. Today, I have  phoned 9 times. Each lasting approximately 40-50 minutes only to be met by 'it won't accept your card'. Once I was even cut off as I think the girl couldn't cope with trying to rebook an Open Ticket. I contacted my bank - all is ok with my accounts. We even tried my husband's card, no good either. On the last 50 minute call I asked for a booking reference number so I could try and pay online but apparently he's not allowed to give me one without payment yet, bizarrely, a girl had given me a reference number earlier in the day. Unfortunately I didn't think until quite a while later to try online payment by which time the Reference had timed out. Absolutely appalling organisation.
