The flights are ace but should you encounter a problem - do beware. By the way, the telephone staff are always polite but I think hours of training are needed. And I still haven't booked my flights!

The flight itself was fairly good. The food was good and the in-flight entertainment was also up to snuff. Seats were small but this is to be expected. The problem arises as soon as anything goes wrong (and it often does). Delays are suddenly sprung on you without warning and can be enormous (a delay of 9 and a half hours). Customer service is atrocious and does not communicate well and does not want to help you. Seat preferences change, online tools won't work anymore. The airline personnel do what they can, but it's clear that these are issues caused by management. Worst of all, it is nearly impossible to get any compensation even though they are supposed to give compensation according to European AND Turkish law. You will never get any flight delay compensation or money back for seat reservations not being honored. And the few things you do get are almost insultingly cheap. For example, in Istanbul for our return flight, we had a 9 and a half hour delay. We got a meal voucher. This meal voucher was only applicable in about seven fast food chains in the airport, which were all the worst. The airport has plenty of decent food establishments, but none accept the voucher. Even worse, you can only get one fixed item from the menu, which is the smallest, most unsatisfactory menu they offer, and you can't even choose your drink—it's always water. It truly feels that they want to squeeze every last cent out of you and spend as little effort as possible once they have your money. Combine that with the unreliability and the atrocious customer service, it's not worth it to ever pick Turkish Airlines if any other options are available. I will not fly again unless serious improvements are introduced.

I purchased a semi-flexible fare for my departure and a fully-flexible (fully refundable) fare for my return. I have to cancel my return due to family reasons and Turkish refuses to refund the ticket they made me pay more for. I had to option of purchasing a $500 ticket that was not refundable, or $1000+ ticket that was refundable. They advertise it as a fully refundable at time of purchase and now not only did I not purchase the cheaper ticket, I am losing 2x the cost because of their false advertising.

As a transfer passenger went straight to the TK lounge which had a vast array of tasty food and beverage options. The lounge was crowded and on the warm side. Also availed of the shower service which helped to somewhat offset the stress of a very long travel day. At the gate, we were put through a series of additional passport checks and, for some unknown reason, only economy passengers were through a final security screening. This was very strange and something I did not experience at any other airport. Boarding was delayed with no explanation from the gate agents who were surly, unprofessional and did not speak adequate English. We were bussed to the aircraft which was also strange given the immense size of the airport and number of jetways it has available. Onboard, the hard product showed its age with the old 2x3x2 seating on business class. The seat provided no privacy and not all had direct aisle access. The crew were very pleasant with smiles all around and they remained very attentive throughout the flight. Catering was excellent with two hot meal services with multiple course options. I especially enjoyed the mezze trolley with its incredible selection of appetizers. The two main course I had were delicious and drinks were plentiful. The IFE had a wide selection of movies and music options and I was able to catch a live Euro 2024 match. The hardware though was on the old side with smallish standard definition screens. The flight left late and arrived slightly behind schedule and once again, the disembarkation was via busses which is a pain after a long flight. Overall the experience was good however, TK ground services are a total disgrace and tarnish what should otherwise be a solid product. This is one aspect of TK that needs immediate attention and improvement.
It’s a really good airline! The sad part is that we had to connect to IST Airport to go to NAV.

Flight attendants were OK. The flight to Istanbul was late and I had to run at Istanbul to get the connecting flight. I was exhausted. My baggage arrived a day late. It was delivered at the doorstep but the delivery agent insists on a tip, not ethical.

They have proven to be nothing but a nightmare from start to finish. My mother is now out $1,700 for her original tickets and another $2,000 for additional tickets we had to buy because Turkish Airlines sold her seat and wouldn't let her board.  When we tried to check her in using the Turkish Airlines app, it was useless. We got error messages on every device we tried. Their so-called help at the airport was a joke. The man at the desk said there was nothing he could do and sent us back to the check-in counter, where we were met with smirks and zero help. They just sent us to another minimally staffed help desk. Their employee at MLA even had the audacity to say that since my mother didn't use her initial flight due to their denial of boarding, she couldn't use her return flight without buying another ticket. This is blatant extortion, targeting an elderly woman. We had to book a new flight with Lufthansa for $1,200 just to get her home safely, and it was clear that Lufthansa is a far superior airline. Turkish Airlines, on the other hand, is predatory and their behavior should make anyone think twice before booking with them. We'll be disputing all charges related to this mess. Turkish Airlines should be ashamed of themselves for their gross negligence and false practices.

As we were travelling with carry-on only, this forced the unnecessary stop at the counter. Boarding, like with many TK flights was unorganized and chaotic with passengers having to wait on the air bridge as the cabin crew was clearly not ready to welcome passengers. The hard product was OK but seat controls were awkward. Unlike other European carriers, TK actually had wide seats in business class. FA’s were pleasant but the service was slow and inefficient. After takeoff we were served a breakfast with cold and hot dishes and warm pastries. The portions were just right. I opted to listen to my own music and did not bother with IFE. Internet connectivity was OK. Overall it was a decent experience but TK’s ground handling continues to be its weakest spot.

I was sent to Customer Service in IST. I was helped by a nice young man Erdem Iri and his manager. They were polite and very helpful and solved my problem in a few minutes. Erdem spoke not only English, but good Russian too. I was really impressed by such wonderful representatives of Turkish Airlines. I wish all Customer Services in all counties were like Turkish.

This seemed far fetched since we had checked in quite early and there were a lot of people behind us waiting to check in and I can’t imagine that all of them were have reserved their seats. This became apparent immediately when we went to the Turkish airlines help desk and they issued boarding passes immediately. Caused us unnecessary stress for no reason

My name is Sanna Abdulhamid. On 21/05/2024, my family of seven and I traveled from Lebanon to Turkey on Turkish Airlines TK-168 for what was supposed to be a joyful seven-day trip. Our return flight was scheduled for 5:00 PM on 28/05/2024. We arrived at the airport well in advance, at 1:30 PM, and began the check-in process at 2:00 PM. However, what ensued was a nightmare that no family should ever have to endure. We were efficiently checked in until it came to my husband, the only one holding a Lebanese passport. The check-in agent struggled to process his return visa, which I eventually found on my phone. Despite this, a series of the Turkish airline colleagues spent two hours trying to resolve the issue, to no avail. Eventually, an official from the Australian embassy named Greg resolved it in just ten minutes, and assured me that it wasn’t a problem and don’t stress, This delay was the catalyst for the cascade of events that followed. By the time we completed tagging our 11 large bags and 7 hand luggage items, we were significantly delayed. We rushed to the security lane, only to be told we were in the wrong line and had to move to the family lane, causing further delays. My children, including a restless toddler, were exhausted and hungry, yet we were Adamant to get to our flight When we finally reached passport control, the process was lengthy. The airport is vast, and it took us 15 minutes of running to get from passport control to our gate. Breathless and frantic, we arrived just as the gate closed. Despite our desperate pleas and explanations, the staff showed no compassion. They directed us to the care point, where the lack of empathy continued. We were informed the next flight was in two days, costing an additional $7500. This was an unimaginable expense for us, having already exhausted our funds on the trip. I approached the desk Emotionally shattered with tears down my face hoping for understanding. Instead, I was sent on a wild goose chase to F44, only to find myself back where we started, facing the same staff who caused our initial delay. They blamed us for not arriving earlier, dismissing our valid grievances with cold indifference. In tears, I watched my exhausted children, lying on the floor of the airport, hungry and worn out from the day’s events. We felt utterly alone and abandoned in a foreign country, without the means to get home. The emotional and financial burden placed on us by the Turkish airline’s incompetence and lack of compassion is beyond words. I implore you to understand the severity of our distress. This experience has left us traumatized and financially strained. We seek not only a refund for the additional $7500 but also compensation for the emotional anguish and the impact on our family. Please show us the empathy and support that were sorely lacking during our ordeal.

They failed to inform us that if you don’t book your ticket with Turkish Airlines, Turkish Airlines will not allow you to choose a seat. They also will not allow you to check in because you have to go to the gate to get a seat assignment. We arrived at the airport eight hours early to try to get the window seat and they would not even look at assigning our seats for several hours until 4 hours before our flight took off - even though none of the agents were helping other customers. We asked at their to get assistance desk as well as two separate people at the checking counter to please assign our seats. All three were not only unhelpful, but very rude. We pay for assignments on every flight and this shouldn’t have happened. Any kind agent could’ve actually made us feel better had they just been polite and tried to be helpful in anyway. I wouldn’t choose this airline again. Terrible customer service.

As transit passengers we went straight to the lounge and made use of the suites and showers which were quite comfortable although the process to gain access was painfully slow. Food and beverage options were outstanding with a wide selection. Experience at the gate was very poor with agents totally unorganized and slow. The aircraft was one of those originally configured for Aeroflot with individual suites with sliding doors. Seats were comfortable but the placement of controls made it too easy to activate them. The seat back screen was huge and offered HD quality. Catering was great and FA’s attentive. Flight departed and landed late due to traffic in Istanbul. Overall a good experience.

Check-in was smooth and handled by a very friendly agent. Used the Plaza Premium lounge as Star Alliance (Air Canada) lounge had a long line up of people waiting to get in. The offerings at the lounge were decent with bar service. Boarding was slow and somewhat chaotic with delineating lines for business and economy not identified resulting people in the wrong queue. On board the configuration was 2-3-2 with little privacy but ample room. Seat was comfortable for including in the lie flat position. In charge flight attendant was very attentive and present throughout the flight. With the exception of one very aloof FA all were friendly and worked hard to look after the passengers. Catering was decent although my fish was dry and almost tasteless. IFE had a wide range of options. We departed late but landed on time with a painfully long taxi to our parking gate. Overall it was a good experience.

But the purposely done trick of keeping the gate for those of 1 stop flights, in the last corner from A1 to F19 is noticed by everyone and worsening the trip. I personally suffered with my 1 year baby carrying in hand running from A1 gate to F9 when it was boarding already, this was my 2nd time.

We were contacted about half an hour before reaching Naples that our flight was delayed an hour.  We have never experienced the economy queue for check in moving quicker than business class but today it was ridiculous. We had to wait over half an hour to check in. When we finally reached the check in counter, the man gave us boarding passes with seats for the 3 flights back to Australia without us sitting next to each other. When I requested to be seated together he at first said it couldn’t be done, then begrudgingly tore up the original passes and issued us new ones together and told my husband he was sorry that he was married to me. A man in front of us was very upset by the service and asked to speak to a manager, but the 2 business class check in staff said there was nobody else there that he could speak with. Then we had to queue for half an hour to enter the business class lounge in Naples airport, which when we eventually got in was awful.

If everything goes well it is an average to mediocre airline with cheap flights. If anything at all goes wrong you are in trouble. Their customer service among other things does not know about codeshares, what flight numbers are, their own miles programme, the luggage allowances for their own flights, will not read more than the first line of any feedback, will never respond to previous correspondence, cannot use any flight tracking tools or websites, you name it.  So hope that you have no problems with your flight because if you have to use customer service you are in a world of pain. After losing 15 hours that include 7 phone calls, 50 feedback requests and 13 live chats I just gave up because it was that or taking them to court.

I noted that most cabin crews for Business Class were men, but when it was time to make bed for passengers, they called the female cabin crews from the back to make the beds. The airline gave priority boarding to at least over 50 families with at least 100 children at Montreal airport, while let Business Class passengers to wait in line for an unusual long time. Normally nothing wrong with the practice, but the volume of children was extremely unusual. At least I have never experienced and witnessed that. On top of that, this practice was not consistent at Istanbul airport, when I boarded my second leg to Bangkok. The rudeness and unprofessionalism from the cabin crew, and the lack of consistency in airline practice, made Turkish Airlines a very unpleasant airline to fly with.

First I got text message that my flight from Detroit to Istanbul was moved to different time. On June 14 I received message that the second leg from Istanbul to Skopje was cancelled. No other option was given although I talked to customer services which is based in Istanbul and barely speak English. After 3 calls and several hours spent on the phone I was told that they will refund full for the flight from Istanbul to Skopje but not for the 1st leg. For the first leg they want to withhold $300 because of cancellation. I spent so many hours but nobody from management to complain to. I did not book ticket to go to Istanbul, I did book to go to Skopje. It is not my fault they cancel. the flight. No call center in USA nobody to help you if there is a problem. Turkish Airlines are opening many new routes from USA. If this persist they will loose a lot.

At Istanbul there are buggy cars to help disables and elderly but some person driving and trying to ignore you if you need help. I am disabled and stopped one and ask her to give me a lift to gate but she said it should be added to your ticket and just ignored and drove away!

Turkish Airlines issue us boarding passes all the way. Flight to Istanbul is delayed over 2 hours, so we miss the connecting flight. We go to the Turkish Airlines counter assuming they would take care of us. Couldn’t have been more mistaken. My wife was offered a business class ticket for the next day and a hotel room for the night (it was around 2.30am). I was told that my business class ticket was now worthless, that I was not entitled to anything, and that the cost of a new ticket would be USD6,000. Or I could choose to fly with a different airline if I wanted. I thought I'd misheard/misunderstood. (Side note: later communication revealed that my wife’s ticket was booked in one shot, while I booked my own in two bookings so I could connect a business trip with personal travel. I kind of get the small print after the fact, but this was not well explained at the time, and  we were traveling together and already had boarding passes sitting together for the Istanbul-Singapore flight.  We explain that we need to fly back together. They pretty much stand firm on: it’s USD6,000, or you could look for another airline. Under pressure to make a decision, I stump up more for a second (economy) ticket. My wife has her complimentary hotel room for the night, so, we say, we’ll head there together and try to get some sleep before my long-haul flight in economy. No, says Turkish Airlines customer service you cannot do that. The room is for her (your wife): you can’t share it. The complimentary transport from the airport to the hotel is for her only, not you. Really, given the exceptional circumstances you couldn’t just maybe make a tiny exception and tell the minibus driver to take an extra passenger? No, she says. Fine, we say, we’ll take a taxi to the hotel, just give us the address.  You will NOT be allowed into the hotel room. (Difficult to overstate how adamant she was that I could not, under any circumstances, share my wife’s hotel room.) So if you’ve ever spent a night in an airport, it’s not quite hellish, but it's certainly not great. The next day, after pretty much no sleep, we fly back. I send three complaints to Turkish Airlines and they send back three non-apology apologies (“we’re sorry your journey didn’t match with your expectations”), reiterating small print and T&Cs. They’ve completely ignored my real question, which is to explain how an international airline could think treating its customers like this is acceptable. There were multiple moments they could have done so much to mitigate the inconvenience, cost, or disruption (preferential pricing? upgrades? access to the business class lounge per original ticket), but they chose not to. So that’s where we are. It’s clear they’re not going to do anything – even a sincere apology acknowledging the circumstances and inconvenience would count for something, but after three attempts I can see it’s not going to come. The only takeaway I have from all of this is to never fly Turkish Airlines again.

Although we had booked and paid for a business flight, the seats on the plane were premium economy, namely economy with the middle seat missing. We were offered a glass of water - I wasn’t but my husband was. Nothing else was offered. After over 3 hours, the plane took off, we were served a meal and had the tray snatched before we were done because it was a short flight. We barely made it to the connecting flight, the gate had closed but they let us in. But our bags did not make it. Now we have to wait for them to arrive on another flight. Disaster of an airline.

When I requested tea during the flight, no one attended to my request. I requested a specific dessert, and although the flight attendant assured me he would bring it, he never did. I asked for tea multiple times, but it was never brought to me. The unprofessional behavior of the flight attendants, was  far below the standard I expected from a business class service. I chose Turkish Airlines based on a friend's recommendation, but after this experience, I cannot recommend it to others.

Our reservation code was for two passengers, and we had requested to sit together. However, upon boarding, we discovered we had been assigned two aisle seats. We asked the cabin staff to change our seats, and they moved us to the first row, which turned out to be the worst seating choice in my flight experience. Onboard experience - Despite the new aircraft with a comfortable seat the flight was disappointing due to several issues with the staff. The service was uncoordinated, not attentive, staff was very noisy. The amenity kit were distributed randomly. Mine was forgotten and I asked for.  The service started whit the menu choices (only for dinner not for breakfast) While seated a flight attendant came asking to prepare the seat for the night. I said “later please” but she never came The dishes were served very fast pushing the passenger to say “wait one moment please”.  During a dinner/lunch normally is asked the customer if they want more wine, juices etc etc. It looks like the service is on request (I need bread and I ask for; I need water and I ask for etc ) the overall impression is to do the service as fast as possible and go behind the curtains. No trolley with beverages was used despite the Turkish advertisement everywhere shows something completely different. Asked for a coffee it was served later on. The night flight was not comfortable. Having opted for the first row as alternative to the original seat assignment the staff was talking all night long. No bottles of water were served before going to bed. A couple of hours before landing I was awaked by the chit-chat of the crew members behind the curtains.  I refused the breakfast because I was really upset. The outboard greetings were done by the supposed “ chief of staff”. Other crew members were not present. Turkish Airlines claims to have more destinations worldwide than other airlines. True but must claims also to have an adequate staff to support the network. Unfortunately, not the case for this flight TK165.

I had purchased two business class tickets for a one-way flight from Istanbul to Toronto at a significant cost of around $7000. Despite arriving at the airport on time and reaching the gate with a minute to spare before it closed, I was denied boarding. I immediately voiced my concerns to the airline staff, who argued with me for approximately 10 minutes, even though the plane was still present and the gate remained open. Instead of addressing the situation promptly, they directed me to customer service, which was located a kilometer and a half away from the gate. Upon reaching the customer service counter, I was met with utter indifference. They informed me that there was nothing they could do to assist me and advised me to visit the purchasing department. I reluctantly complied and endured an additional hour of waiting before finally speaking to someone in purchasing. However, to my disbelief, they also refused to help and informed me that I would need to purchase a new ticket for an exorbitant $10,000. It is simply unfathomable that a one-way flight would cost me a staggering total of $17,000, considering I had already purchased a ticket. Refusing to accept this unreasonable demand, I was redirected to yet another customer service area, only to be sent back to purchasing once again. By this point, I had traversed a distance of approximately 3 1/2 kilometers, feeling physically drained. The supervisor I spoke to offered no resolution, and what was most disheartening was that I was not alone in my predicament. There were six other passengers from the same flight experiencing the same issues. I tried reaching out to their customer service over the phone, only to be repeatedly disconnected. The entire experience felt incredibly frustrating and almost seemed like a scam. Ultimately, I was left with no choice but to purchase a new ticket, this time in economy class, for an exorbitant price of $5000, just to make my way back home. This additional expense was completely unjustified and only further added to my dissatisfaction. Furthermore, the airport experience was marred by long and inconvenient lineups for non-business class passengers. This lack of efficiency only compounded the already unpleasant situation. In light of these distressing encounters, I can confidently say that I will never fly with Turkish Airlines again.

Our first flight was cancelled and despite several requests it was impossible to get a refund for the seats we had paid for! For the second flight we had again paid for seats, but Turkish Airlines decided to change our booking number, which cancelled our seat reservation. So we had to pay again, except that it's now impossible to get a refund for the first seats. Catastrophic customer service, a company that respects nothing and nobody. Communication is by form only, so with each exchange we have to start from 0 and each passenger has to make their own request, even if only one person has paid. Hw can you dissuade customers from not claiming their due! Instead of automatic refunds, we have to send them dozens of messages without ever getting an answer that makes sense.

review_header: "check in my one piece carry on"
review_text: Also at Istanbul airport I was targeted to check in my one piece carry on even though plenty of space inside the cabin. I requested but the guy does not listen. Food was OK and AVOD is OK, not comparable to Emirates or Qatar Airways standards

Service desk/gate attendant was extremely rude when I asked if there was possibly another option. Although economy passenger in front of me was given seat that was requested last minute & treated pleasantly. Very disappointed in Turkish Air customer service. Will look for another airline next time I fly.

The original layover was 1hr 50 min. The flight landed at the other end of the aiport from where we were supposed to take the connection to Frankfurt. We ran to the gate, passed the busy security arrived at the gate B10 , flight was gone. No info, by anyone, delay from Karachi was airline problem. Asking random airport staff we were told to contact Turkish airline care point. The staff looked at us and said calmly here is your new flight which is 4 hours late than the original connection. I went to speak with the manager of the care point who says he does not understand what is my problem because we have been issued boarding passes for the new flight. No apology for any discomfort.

I am disabled and travelled with my mobility scooter. I had entered Turkey from East Midlands Airport into Dalaman using Jet2 and then travelled on to Istanbul using Pegasus. I had no problem with the first 2 airlines. When checking in for my return flight at Istanbul my mobility scooter was thoroughly scrutinised by the airline staff and approved for transport by the airline captain. This took over an hour. Upon arrival in Birmingham my mobility scooter was not returned to me and the Special Assistance staff had to go looking for it. It was found outside where it had been unloaded and brought to me. However, it was not working and had clearly been lifted by the plastic chassis rather than the handles and as a result wires had been disconnected. It could not be repaired at the airport and needed an engineer. The special assistance staff managed to get me, my luggage and my scooter out to where my taxi was waiting. I immediately arranged for the repair of my mobility scooter and informed Turkish Airlines of what had happened using their online portal. The cost to repair was £75.00. Turkish Airlines then responded stating that my claim had been rejected as I had been carrying an item prohibited by the civil aviation authorities. Please see copy of their respond attached as a photograph. I knew that I had no prohibited items and queried their decision. It then took several weeks for them to finally look at my claim properly and they eventually paid me £74 rather than £75 as they only calculate in US dollars. Turkish Airlines treatment of me was absolutely disgusting and I have never received a proper apology. Do not use this airline if you are disabled. They have no respect or consideration for disabled people. I have travelled all over the world and have never been treated with such contempt.

Inbound went through smoothly. But outbound was chaos and torture. I was in Beijing Capital airport 3 hours before departure on 10th of May, self check in failed, I went to help desk asked for help, they communicated with airline and told me my ticket was invalid, then I went to check in counter, they called airline too and I was told same thing. So I was denied boarding. After countless communication with airline, finally they admitted that their system made mistakes, they will arrange flights for me asap, and told me to retain the hotel receipt to get reimbursed. But the earliest flight available was on 13th of May, I had not choice, so I stuck to Beijing for 3 more days. After I got home, I started communicating with the airline through the feedback. The process was terrible, they lied about the situation, they said I was denied boarding because I was not checked in on time, that’s untrue, so I asked the timestamp according their investigation, when self check in attempted, when help desk informed, and when check in counter called, they couldn’t provide.

review_header: "won't rebook me for a return flight"
review_text: "  I inadvertently booked two identical business class tickets, on separate reservations, for myself to fly to Dubai on Turkish Airlines. I showed up at the airport and boarded a Turkish flight to Dubai with no issues. I arrived in Dubai with no apparent problems. On the return flight, I was denied boarding, with Turkish claiming I had not used my ticket to arrive in Dubai, resulting in an automatic cancellation. What seems to have happened, after many many interactions with their horrible feedback form-based customer service, was that Turkish determined that since I didn't use one outbound ticket, they would cancel both of them. Of course they have no policy that states this anywhere. At best, it's a flaw in their computer system. Turkish has refused to acknowledge I was even on an outbound flight to Dubai even though I have sent copies of the frequent flyer mileage I obtained from these flights. Turkish will not confirm that I'll receive a refund minus penalities on the completely unused ticket. They will not acknowledge that I was on any Turkish flight and pretend they were both no-shows. They won't rebook me for a return flight. Speaking to someone on the phone is completely useless. No one that you actually talk to can solve the problem or has any power to do anything. Turkish uses a feedback form approach that no other major airline uses. It's truly bottom of the barrel customer service. It's like talking to a wall. At the end of the day, I paid more than $4,000 for Turkish Airlines to fly me to Dubai and then leave me there stranded.

The online booking process was straightforward, and I appreciated the option not to pay a fee for seat selection. This allows passengers without specific preferences to save money, while those like me who prefer certain seats can still choose their preferred spot. The ground staff at O'Hare Airport were outstanding. They were helpful while interacting with a full flight of passengers. Although I was sent back to the check-in counter by TSA for another boarding pass, it turned out that the original one was correct. The good-looking cabin crew did a fantastic job! I was pleasantly surprised to receive an amenity kit along with the usual blanket and pillow. The complimentary meals and beverages were comparable to (or better than) those offered by other airlines on recent trips (last 2 years) which I paid ($500 or more) for. I also tried the sleeping pods and shower service at Istanbul Airport. It was by far the best long-haul transit experience I've ever had, surpassing my previous experiences at airports like Dubai, Hong Kong, and Narita. Lastly, the pilots were amazing - my flights were smoother than the blue line train ride I took to the airport.

We were at the gate 1h, 20 min the flight departure. Additionally, the boarding was very fast and 20min before the departure, they did not allow us to get to the flight anymore because they closed the gate. We arrived late to boarding, but still in time. Boarding just finished a minute before, and the plane was still there. The staff was not only not letting us in anymore, even though this was on an important business trip/mission, they also were very unfriendly and spoke barely English. We had to buy a new flight from Istanbul to Valencia. Every person had a different price and we paid between 350 Euro up to 1000 Euro for the single flight ticket. This happened first time in my life and I can definitely not recommend this airline.

With all the heat and sweating the cabin crew started distributing bottled waters but couldn't give water to all passengers as they ran out of water just after 30 minutes of takeoff. The cabin crew desperately searched the overhead bins to find water but there were none. The plane wasn't correctly loaded. There were only big water bottles available to be served with glass. So I went to the back of the plane to ask for water but the cabin crew said that we can't give it now as they are preparing for meal service. That is when I got frustrated and the cabin crew started arguing with me. You make us sit in the plane with no AC on in the heat and moisture of Phuket. You give water to only some passengers until you run out of small water bottles, then when the passenger comes up to you to ask for water you reject and start arguing with the passenger instead of apologizing for the inconvenience and providing the basic human necessity "water". So the in flight service and cabin crew attitude is the worst. As for the beverage choices, the alcoholic drinks available are only beer and wine. Pathetic.

Despite a 7-hour delay on my flight, the airline refused to offer compensation as promised in their own policies. Stranded on a plane for 4 hours with no water, food, or explanations, it's clear their priority is profit over people. Their empty apologies and lack of accountability are a disgrace to the industry. Avoid at all costs unless you enjoy being treated like cattle. Shameful.

The cabin crew were very friendly and worked hard to provide a high level of service. The spacious seat was comfortable but was lacking in privacy. The food was as usual of a high standard as were the provision of drinks. Would I recommend Turkish Airlines on my experience, most certainly.

We sat very uncomfortable throughout the flight, because there was very little legroom (you can see it in the photo). I also wanted a glass of white wine, but there was no alcohol at all, which was very strange. I will never choose Turkish Airlines again. Not worth the money.

I reported the damage within 3 days once I noticed the bag was damaged after unwrapping the protective plastic at home. They are arguing that since I didn't detect it at the airport and report it there it isn't covered even though their policy says if the bag is discovered to be damaged after leaving you just have to create a damage report online.

I was denied boarding and I understand the reason, but the staff was very unhelpful and treated me with such arrogant attitude. First, the staff said "my manager can help you with changing your flight ticket", then when I went to the so-called manager he was very rude and just disregarded me by saying "it's your fault and you have to buy a new ticket" without looking at me at all. And he pointed out to next colleague to help me with buying a new ticket. And her service was so sour! I eventually opted to leave the airport and she just pointed to a direction to exit the airport without much explanation of how to go there. When I arrive at the so-called exit door after roaming in Istanbul Airport for 10 minutes. It was not the door to exit and I had to go to the other end of the airport.
TK never fails to amaze me with their one of the best in flight service and the ground services as well. From the attentive cabin crew who goes an extra mile just to make you feel comfortable.

All crew members with a smile, very helpful and did know about special requests. Food on a shorter flight normally not necessary but Turkish always does a great job in catering. Tasty and enough, also drinks free of charge, seats comfortable. Most impressive and best is Turkish hospitality if all crew members. Big thank you for the excellent job. 5 Stars as always and looking forward my next flights to be back "home" again.

Our Flight time with Turkish Airlines: 14:50. We arrived check in desk around 12:05 pm. The male staff at the check in said that one of my luggage was over the limit by 6 kilos. I said that I have already weighed it at home and our luggage allowance is 90 kgs as a family (me, my wife and my 4 months old child). The staff said that it will be per person 40 kgs and asked me to pay. Shortly after another female staff arrived and took over. She weighed my luggage again and started discussing the same issues. She did not give me any chance to rearrange my luggage, and just insisted that I should pay. Since my total of all luggage was less than 90 kgs, I refused. She took it very personally and kept discussing to the point where I would be late on boarding the flight. Despite seeing that I had a 4 months child with me, she showed no empathy and professionalism. After there is less than 1 hour to my flight, then only she checked in all my luggage and provided me a boarding pass. She clearly knew that it was almost impossible to reach the boarding gate as it closes 20mins before flight. As I was travelling with my wife and 4 months child it is difficult for me to make security check and immigration check within short time but I managed to reach there at 14:32 (18min before flight). I could see that people were still walking towards the plane to board the flight. When we arrived at the gate, all the staff just chose to ignore us. They had all agreed amongst themselves to ignore us and deliberately make us miss our flight. I stood there and pleaded and begged for help, but shockingly everyone just ignored us as if we were invisible. No one came forward to ask why I was asking for help. After 10 mins standing there one of staff came and told me all your checkin luggage are returned to belt number 3. After that I felt lost as it was very important flight for me and it resulted in mental stress for both myself and my wife. I then bought another ticket from Air India for the same day, but it resulted in financial loss as I had very limited budget and huge mental and physical suffering as I was travelling with my 4 months old child. I missed my flight because of the Turkish airline’s staff at check in and ignorance of their staff at the boarding gate. I asked  Turkish Airlines to review the incident and refund my money. However, they have refused the refund saying that I was late to the boarding gate. They didn’t consider the fact that I was late due to their staff at the check in. As i am a regular traveler from different airlines and I really doesn't want to refer this airline to anybody.
Cabin crew professional, polite, helpful and really good. As usual best catering, comfortable seats and punctual time. Deserve to be the best Airlines in Europe. Keep up the good work.

We arrived at the airport via 2 separate cars (costs £120) eager to return home after an enjoyable holiday, we checked in our luggage and went on our way to the gate - until we were met with the news that our flight was delayed for 2 hours (this comes after we were told the day before during the online check in that our flight had been cancelled and we were forced to book another flight). We’ve been informed by the airlines representative that we are eligible for a £10 food voucher, which I had to wait a long time to receive. After the long 2 hours had passed, we headed to the gate hopeful to board our flight - this is when we found out that the flight had been cancelled. We were forced to wait in line for an hour at the UK border control - even though we hadn’t left the country, and then went to collect our luggage, one of the suitcases had been destroyed. Then we’ve been informed that our next flight was the next day at 11am, we deny this option and chose to extend our stay in the UK until Saturday . We haven’t received a compensation for our damaged suitcase, and we had to make our way home using Taxi and train to reduce the cost. This experience left me deeply unsatisfied and disappointed

However, the airport check in was very fast. The Egyptair lounge was basic but had a range of tasty snacks (no alcohol). Boarding of this evening flight was smooth and the crew's welcome was warm. The seating was comfortable and the meal was pleasant, though again no alcohol was available. The flight operated 45 minutes late, so we missed our onward connection to Kuala Lumpur and Melbourne. It took a long time and a bit of running around from one end of the huge Istanbul terminal to the other, but TK was able to reroute our flight via Bangkok 15 hours later. They provided a nice hotel (40 mins drive from the airport by free shuttle) and we were able to get some sleep at 4.30 a.m. More information on the flight delay could have been provided at Cairo airport, but otherwise we felt that TK had done everything possible to put us back on track.

Once onboard the first flight, the welcome onboard was friendly with a chef taking food orders. The B777's seating is 2-2-2 but the seats were wide and comfortable with adequate storage, The food and drink options were good. TK's business lounge at Istanbul is very impressive with many food and seating options. For the second leg to Casablanca we were bussed to the aircraft, but the operation was reasonably efficient. Onboard the onboard service was professional, and the A350's 1-2-1 abreast seats were very comfortable for the regional flight. Both flights operated on time, and baggage was available without much of a wait. Overall this was an excellent experience for the price paid.

review_header: "cabin crew was very friendly and efficient"
review_text: At the gate, unlike all other airlines I've encountered, TK did not recognise my Australian e-visa (even though I showed a paper print-out). The rather confrontational gate supervisor took no interest in my passport, all the while looking in the passport of someone else with a different nationality and telling me that I had a problem. Eventually he conceded and waved me away saying "you may go", the way cops in police dramas talk to murder suspects being released after their interrogation. But things improved greatly from then on. The cabin crew was very friendly and efficient, the food was plentiful and tasty, and the seat was comfortable despite being from an earlier generation of business class seat. The flight arrived 50 minutes early.

Istanbul airport does not have gate information for a flight until about 1.5h prior to departure. It is also a rather large airport. By the time we found the gate information we made our way there. Due to a medical issue I spent some time in the bathroom but still managed to get to the gate 20 minutes prior to departure. Ground staff, however, insisted that we are too late and we would not be let onto the plane. We were asked if we paid for seat reservation, when I answered that we didn't, the response was: then there's nothing I can do for you. The plane was still there, people still getting on but they refused to board us. Heading to the 'Care Point', more unhelpful, unfriendly staff was encountered. In the end they extorted over 3000 Euro for a new flight the next day, 24h later. Without paying double of what the flight cost initially, they would have also cancelled our return flights. Istanbul airport is the most expensive place place I've ever been. Over 300 Euros for about 10 hours of rest in the airport hotel, 25 Euros for a McDonalds burger. The flight back from Jakarta was no different. Ground staff in IST is beyond unhelpful, extremely rude and arrogant.  Avoid this airline and IST airport at all cost. Pay more elsewhere and you'll be glad to have done so!!

My father died in February and least of all I wanted to deal with the flight and airline issues. I booked flight in January for March and when my father got worse I exchanged the flight online for 4 passengers to February. Turkish Airlines deleted my flight from the system and didn’t refund the money also didn’t notify me about the cancellation and the reason. Looked like an error. However the money was paid. I called the airline to ask why I can’t check my flight status online ? And they said your flight is deleted, submit a ticket to customer support and we will get back to you. To make it shorter they got back to me AFTER I returned back from funeral. I called about 50+ times in order to resolve THEIR mistake. When I finally got my ticket after paying another 550$ for exchange, they canceled my husband and daughters flight 48 hours before the departure and again they don’t know why and asking to submit the ticket online. Each time I called their representatives had different excuses: either their system is down or their ticketing will get back to me or they were just transferring me to Chinese line without request, I don’t speak Chinese. I had sleepless nights as my flight was canceled and airline was not resolving the issue but by dads funeral was in few days. They don’t have any support for those whose flight is within 24-48 hours or less. They just advise to submit a ticket on their website a some mysterious team will get back to you within 7 days. Even if your flight is tomorrow. So I will never ever recommend to anyone to deal with Turkish Airline if you don’t want a stress and headache.  I paid $300+ for seat with bassinet and called to add my husband and child to pay for their seats with me. I was told it is impossible and I need to buy the seats at check in. At check in they said there are no available seats near me so I would have to fly 13 hours with a baby in lap. So I asked them to give us some random seats but together on the way back due to this nonsense. Also the airline could not add my infant to the reservation. They said I will have to add and pay in the airport before departure. The amount of stress I got with this airline is immense.

During the Eid holidays I booked a flight from Dubai to New York with my husband to celebrate our honeymoon. Due to my chronical backpain conditions, we saved up quite some money in order to book a Business flight. All went well, up to our return flight from New York as I shockingly found out at the airport that they downgraded my seat to an Economy seat. I spoke to the staff at the counter and showed them proof that I had booked and paid for a Business class flight. You would normally think that the staff would investigate in what went wrong right? Well the complete opposite happened. Everyone was extremely rude, no one wanted to investigate and look into the issue. One of the staff even shouted and scolded at us saying we never booked Business Class in the first place. I am beyond shocked, never in my life have I witnessed such terrible customer service for an airline. We did not have much time before our flight was taking off and due to my health condition I am not able to sit up straight for such a long flight. The only option was for us to pay the upgrade of $1299 in order to get on the Business class. My husband gave his credit card and paid. Then the next shocking thing happened, the guy at the counter charged us twice the amount! He said the first payment didn't go through (even though the amount got deducted from the statement). We obviously didn't get a refund of the first payment, so in total we topped up 2600 dollar! Once we got back to Dubai, we tried reaching their ticketing and online customer service and no one is replying us or they are saying we will look into it and they don't get back to us. Honestly, shame on you Turkish Airlines!! You completely ruined it for me. Not just by your rude staff, also your incompetency to fix things and help your customers when needed. This is my warning to everyone to never fly with them! You are fine if everything goes well with your flight, but the moment you need customer service help, you can forget it.

Flight should be 13:20 It was delayed at 13:20 for 10 min, then the employees were too late to appear by the desk, literally no was there and there is nobody to ask about the flight, then when they finally arrived, and we’ve been standing by the line for more than 30 minutes, the lady did not accept to let us check in first because our seat number is 11 and as she said only seats number 18-36 can check in first. After ten minutes, the flight was delayed again for another 15 minutes.

I then tried to explain my issues to seven different staff who could not communicate in English well enough to understand, My father was unwell and I simply needed to change my departure date but their system and staff were incapable of booking me onto a new flight that Skyscanner and the app said was available.

Flying to Bogota from western Europe always meant that Turkish Airlines (THY) would face stiff competition from Iberia, KLM, Air France & Lufthansa. For one, passengers from western Europe needed to fly EAST or SOUTH to Istanbul and then fly WEST from IST to BOG – adding up to 4 hours to the journey when compared to the other airlines. Returning back, there was the 3 or 4 hours added to the BOG-IST journey due to a stop at Panama City (PCY) – in addition to travelling WEST/NORTH from IST. In the face of the competition, THY offered overnight free stays (in Istanbul), limousines and decent FFP rewards that compensated for such inconvenience/increased travel time. Sadly, with the changes to the FFP (Miles & Smiles) introduced on 19th February 2024, the offer from THY diminished in value. However, the biggest disincentive for business class passengers flying with Turkish Airlines on this route is the introduction of the Boeing 787-9 which – in my opinion – is a disaster. THY’s seating configuration in business class presumably aims at maximising the number of seats in a given space, but it does not work. It is natural to face directly forward when on a plane, but THY has introduced a configuration that means passengers are physically contorted when trying to sleep. I could not sleep comfortably. This was exacerbated by the feet area of the lie-flat bed, which is far too small; just turning in my sleep was virtually impossible. I felt as if I was mummified. The space was completely claustrophobic. Even when awake, I needed to twist my body to look forward. I thought to myself ‘Is this just me?’, but when I looked at other passengers’ postures they were equally ‘skew-whiff’. The windows in business class are completely redundant – they are blocked by headrest extensions that protrude to obscure virtually all of the window. I looked at all of the seats and realised that the design was fundamentally flawed, and these headrest extensions were aimed at providing privacy from adjoining passengers. However, THY appears to have done it on the cheap and applied the same seats to the window seats (which obscures the windows). It was noticeable that the ‘chef-in-the-sky’ seems to be losing favour; on previous journeys they seemed to be in abundance, but thankfully this was not the case on this flight. In my opinion, the chef-in-the-sky is a pure gimmick – they just arrange food; passengers cannot ask the ‘chef-in-the-sky’ for personalised food preferences (maybe having their meal a little later). The fact is that in one aisle, you have a ‘chef-in-the-sky’ and in the other aisle you have traditional cabin crew performing exactly the same function. Utilising the >9 hours stopover hotel, I made my way to the hotels desk and despite being assured of personalised transport - it did not materialise; when approaching my ‘personalised transport’ (a mini-bus), I challenged the member of staff who did not previously notice the codes on my boarding card indicating ‘Elite Status’ and then went on to demand to see my digital card – trying to imply that it was my fault for not presenting the digital card previously. I boarded the mini-bus because quite simply the alternative would have taken much longer to get to my hotel. All of this considered, I think I’d go with Iberia or KLM in future – it is simply not worth it with THY.

Despite a minor delay of one to four minutes, seven others and I were denied boarding. The conduct of the staff during this interaction lacked both courtesy and constructive problem-solving. Upon reaching the customer care counter, we encountered a disarray of conflicting information from various personnel. Despite requesting to speak with a supervisor, we were met with contradictory statements regarding their availability. Eventually, a woman claiming to be the supervisor approached us, exhibiting unprofessional behavior and ultimately dismissing our concerns without offering any viable solutions.  During our three-hour ordeal, it became apparent that the airline's response was inconsistent. Of the eight passengers who missed the Dallas flight, only two received accommodation for the following day, inclusive of hotel stays and meal arrangements. Three passengers received tickets and meals but were left without lodging for the night. I was provided with a solitary meal voucher. In contrast, a family of five who encountered a similar situation, missing their flight to Chicago, were offered five complimentary tickets without any provision for meals or lodging. This disparity underscores a significant inconsistency in the airline's policies and customer treatment. Despite these challenges, I was compelled to purchase a new ticket from Istanbul to Dallas at a considerably higher cost ($1327) than my original four-leg itinerary ($1052).  Upon returning to the United States, I submitted a complaint through the airline's designated Feedback Form. However, the promised response within seven days was not fulfilled; it took a total of 16 days to receive a reply. Regrettably, the response appeared disconnected from the detailed grievances outlined in my initial complaint, indicating a lack of thorough consideration. Subsequent attempts to address my concerns via customer service calls proved equally futile. Despite numerous inquiries regarding escalation to a supervisor or a competent representative, I have yet to receive a satisfactory resolution. This persistent inability to engage with competent authorities reflects a concerning disregard for customer care. In conclusion, I am deeply disappointed by the inadequacies demonstrated by Turkish Airlines' customer service.

Flight left slightly behind schedule nevertheless arrived in Istanbul on time. Service onboard was so so with crews disappearing after serving meals and people had to call for water. Food quantity wasn't enough for this twelve and half hour flight. Upon landing at IST it took us almost an hour taxiing to our gate.
40€ fee to have to check in my hand baggage for overweight. New policy max 8 kg for both personal item and hand luggage. So they expect people to pack air?

Firstly, I had to wait on the plane for three hours during the flight from Zurich to Istanbul due to two technical issues as well as passengers disembarking. These delays were annoying and caused considerable inconvenience. When I arrived in Istanbul, I was informed that my onward flight to Zanzibar was overbooked and I could only fly the next day. Turkish Airlines offered me a "5-star hotel" to stay overnight, but this was almost 50 minutes away from the airport, which caused additional inconvenience. Despite the assurance of a refund of 600 euros, which Turkish Airlines had promised after numerous feedback messages, I have still not received this amount after 12 feedback messages. When I asked again three months later and tried to collect the money in person, I was referred from Istanbul to Zurich and then back to Istanbul. In Zurich, I was finally told that a cash payment was not possible. Despite further attempts to resolve the issue via the feedback form, I received a reply yesterday claiming that the money had already been paid out, which is not the case. When I then contacted customer service in Switzerland, I was transferred to customer service for feedback, where I spoke to an extremely unfriendly, incomprehensible and aggressive person. This experience was incredibly unpleasant, I have never had such an unfriendly person on the phone before. Overall, the customer service and service provided by Turkish Airlines is unacceptable. The unresolved issues, lack of communication and unfriendly staff make this airline a disappointing choice for travelers.

review_header: "made an error and switch my seats"
review_text: Do not fly on this embarrassment of an airline.

Despite providing my reservation code, the two different representatives informed me twice, that my ticket did not exist and had been cancelled and I had to buy a new one. This forced me to purchase a new ticket, which cost double the price of my original booking. I later discovered through Turkish Airlines' own online system that my initial ticket was still valid, leading to a situation where I had two active tickets for the same flight. Realizing this, I cancelled the newly bought ticket within two hours of purchase. Unbelievably, I was charged a 200 CHF cancellation fee for a ticket I had bought solely due to misinformation provided by their team. My attempts to get refunded for this charge have been fruitless. Despite multiple communications and a formal complaint, all I've received are responses that range from irrelevant to denying any record of my calls—contrary to their claim that all calls are recorded. This experience has left me deeply disappointed and questioning the integrity of Turkish Airlines' customer service. The lack of accountability and transparency in handling what was clearly an error on their part is unacceptable.

I have done everything they asked me to do (wrote feedback, emails) etc. and nothing works, I've been waiting, calling them for 3 weeks and for 10 days waiting to fix the airport code which is 3 letters and they keep saying it is in progress and will call me back in 2-3 hours and they never call me back. They refuse to provide any details about what is being done to solve the issue, what has been done until now, a phone number of a supervisor, nothing. I am getting the feeling that they don't want to fly by back home with the ticket that I already paid them for and they want me to buy a new ticket. On top of that they are asking me to pay almost the full amount of a new ticket to setup the date for departure for my open ticket that I paid already (I paid for the round trip). The Feedback department just hang up on me, refused to provide any details and said, that I need to wait because the feedback is in progress (has been in progress for 10 days and no updates). Refused to provide supervisor information, phone number, name or to connect me with him to solve the issue.

The departure was delayed making our connection from Istanbul to Belgrade extremely tight. We had to run from terminal C to F, which is a long way. We tried getting a ride on one of the golf cart-like shuttles, but were told no. The outdated entertainment system included a networking port (RJ45) and headphone connections on the arm rest, which I haven't seen in 30 years. The stewardess was mildly rude and nowhere to be found outside of meal service. The food was minimum quality.

Food was not good, and the check in process is a joke because they charge for seat selection (even at online check in time). Our 4 year was seated separately to us, eventually it was resolved. The free WIFI didn't work.

If you are English speaking and there is no in country Turkish Airlines service centre, don’t bother calling the centre in Istanbul. It is in Turkish after you choose English. Try calling the US line. Second, biggest mistake was to cancel flight and chose the option to refund money into the Turkish Airlines wallet. Tried to rebook my flight but there was no pay option to use Turkish Airlines wallet. Last, wrote in to request for assistance to either rebook or refund my money. Turkish Airlines replied that it would refund my money. Months later, they changed position that money in wallet can’t be refunded. Tried again to use book another Turkish flight but still unable to pay using the Turkish Airlines wallet. Wrote in to appeal several times to refund, but Turkish Airlines replied money cannot be refunded and offer no assistance on how I can use the money to pay for new tickets.

I had a flight from Barcelona to Singapore and I requested a paid upgrade to business from Istanbul to Singapore but they didn’t accept. There was empty seats in business but they denied. In Barcelona, the ground team told me that i will be upgraded in Istanbul. This is really annoying. Also my flight from Barcelona delayed 2 hours and I barely catched my flight. Nobody helped me in Istanbul.. Never again.

The customer service team from Turkish Airlines did not do anything to compensate for a 6 hour delay. The flight was supposed to depart Istanbul at 1:45am and arrive in Miami at 7:45am whereas instead we departed Istanbul at 7:55am and arrived in Miami at 2:47pm. It is currently April 6th, 2024 and it has been 4 months since no compensation has arrived.

although there was a meal choice, the rude staff imposed on me and directly served me what she decided, not even asking! I had to protest to get her to tell me the other choice which I took in the end. I complained later to the head and she came to fakely apologise. They said she was new, however she gave others the choice .. also the check in staff rude and aggressive.  I used to enjoy the food on this airline, but I dread it now. It was rich big, flavourful, now it is dry, bad quality,. Portions cut down stingingly.  Also the films are very old and limited. I travelled 4 times these last 3months and there were 2 or 3 new films added in the new releases.

Booked Economy but being Star Gold gives this privilege. Huge queue at the three Business Class desks, stretching out into the passageway behind. I counted - 45 people in the queue. Thought it odd as I knew the aircraft would be a narrow-body Airbus with only 20 Business Class seats. At 15:20 one agent appeared and opened one desk. Finally at 15:30 two more agents came and opened two more desks. A fourth then came but by then the first one had left! It took me 30 minutes queueing time to check-in. Finally a charming lady efficiently checked me in. I commented on how many people queueing and asked if all "Star Gold". She said that a lot of Economy Class passengers come there too. I accept that many may not understand English, but it is hard on the elderly. If I was 20 years younger and still in my 60s it would be less of a struggle. Came time for boarding. Orderly queues - passengers seemed to know the difference between Business and Economy by then. Settled into my seat. Then along came a lady whose boarding pass showed my seat number. I learnt that I had been up-graded. (Thanks TK! An occasional perk of being Star Gold.) So moved forward into Row 1. After that the usual comfortable seat; smiling crew; lovely meal and great relaxation. Before take-off from London I received a message telling me my luggage belt number in Istanbul. though it changed before I reached there, again having sent me an update message. And thankfully the belt not at the far end of that beautiful but enormous terminal. Another great flight.

Overall, good experience, good check in, option to upgrade to business class using money or Turkish airlines miles. Cabin crew, friendly, younger, well trained. Loved the free internet in business class. Feel the way they serve food can feel slowish as they prepare it with cooks (or cabin crew dressed as cooks) Had a so so experience in Istanbul airport, wherein I had just a 70 minutes connecting flight to Madrid and my suitcase did not come with me, despite both legs being Turkish Airlines.

Never flying with Turkish airline again.  On Aug 29 booked for flight from Nairobi to Houston on Dec 1. I paid for seats for two passengers. On Nov 28 received email that seats had been changed no explanation. We were given separate seats different aisle. Luckily I was able to change the seats because rude customer service only directed me to the feedback form. On January 24 lost all my access for the web browser and could only view on the mobile app. On March 8th I paid for 4 seats and got confirmation. 36E, 36D, 22C, 22B. On March 16th seat 36E was missing. Called Customer service and was told to repurchase seat 36E. Still trying to get a refund for the second payment.

5 years old baby girl. We were flying from Lisbon to Lahore . But we have a transit via Istanbul for 1 hour 45 minutes. After reached at Istanbul airport my little baby was sleep on my lap and we was a little bit late for my transit plane. It was gone. After that we buy a new ticket amount €1200 with extra pay and wait more 24 hours for the next flight to Lahore with 1.5 years old baby.  I saw 40-45 people were come with same problem flight delayed. And at Istanbul airport the food was too much expensive as compared to Europe. Everyone looting at Istanbul airport.

But I have a transit via Istanbul for 1 hour 15 minutes. My plane was delayed by Turkish airlines for 30 minutes and I was a little bit late for my transit plane. It was gone. After that I changed my flight ticket and I have to wait for 5 hours then. I do not understand why they did not manage delayed flight. Services are disappointing. I do not recommend Turkish airlines it was my first try and last one.

Her kindness and professionalism went above and beyond our expectations. Despite my husband's disability, Jennifer's caring demeanor and willingness to help made our experience truly memorable. Keep shining, Jennifer, and continue spreading kindness wherever you go!

The guy who was helping us explained the food court etc. to us very kindly. Inflight service was wonderful, food/beverages, entertainment system was ok, wifi was not good. Value for money was good, Crew was friendly.

Dreadful experience: - Rude customer services staff (no apology) - No explanation for cancellation - Shipped us to a hotel for all of a 1.5 hour stay (took nearly an hour each way to get to hotel in the middle of the night) - we had an option to stay at airport and wait but wanted to freshen up -Food vouchers were for fast food with only limited items to choose from - dreadful quality - Flight food was below average to inedible - I declined two meals - Limited alcohol - beer or wine - When we complained via email they basically just said they met their obligations, no apology. I would recommend using a different airline. And if you want to take extra baggage they do by kg and the cost is extortionate.

After reading the reviews on here I must be flying with a different Turkish Airlines. Ground staff at EDI polite and helpful. However where TK really excel is onboard. The crew are fantastic, service delivered with a smile and they engage with passengers ensuring everyone comfortable.

My journey with Turkish Airlines involved a codeshare flight operated by JetBlue Airways, and unfortunately, it was marred by numerous issues and a lack of accountability from Turkish Airlines' customer service. Despite purchasing my ticket through Turkish Airlines, I encountered difficulties when seeking a refund for a disrupted flight. When contacting Turkish Airlines, I was directed to JetBlue Airways, with Turkish Airlines absolving themselves of responsibility due to the flight being a codeshare. However, upon reaching out to JetBlue Airways directly, I was informed that Turkish Airlines was  responsible for processing the refund as the issuing carrier. This back-and-forth between Turkish Airlines and JetBlue Airways has been incredibly frustrating and has highlighted a lack of communication and accountability within Turkish Airlines' customer service department. The conflicting information provided by Turkish Airlines has only added to the confusion and inconvenience of the situation. Furthermore, the lack of assistance and clarity from Turkish Airlines' customer service representatives has been disappointing. Despite providing all necessary information and documentation, I have yet to receive a satisfactory resolution to my refund request. The lack of accountability and poor customer service have left me disillusioned, and I will be exploring alternative options for future travel.

I have connected in airports with that amount of time before but was worried it will be tight, therefore I contacted customer service numerous times over a one month period, asking if I can get a different flight or receive a refund to rebook a different ticket. The replies were slow and copied from a template, and the alternative flights they suggested would have added 24 hours or more to my total travel time, which would have made it impossible for my schedule. The refund they offered was 1/3 of the ticket price I paid, which I thought must have been a joke. Since the airline allowed me to accept my flight changes with a 40 minute connecting time, I stuck to that and hoped that no delays would occur. The first flight was delayed, which caused the second flight to leave by the time I reached Istanbul. I had to run around the huge airport and figure things out myself with no one to guide me on the next steps. I got rebooked on the next available flight which was 12 hours later, and I had to stay overnight in Istanbul. At no time was I told what my passenger rights are or given any assistance with regard to food and drink. Since my delay was so long, I qualify to receive 600 Euros equivalent of compensation. However the airline keeps denying any responsibility when I submit feedback about my experience. The whole debacle cost me a 12 hour delay and miss the first day of work at my new job. Through the whole process, which is approaching a month soon, Turkish Airlines customer service was unsympathetic and replied very slowly, using fixed templates that would have taken seconds to copy and paste. Personally I think the cabin crew on both my flights did a great job, but with the kind of uncertainties that are bound to happen during air travel, this airline is abysmal at handling passenger needs and customer service. I will certainly not fly with them again, especially if a connecting flight is required.

The business class experience is a bit of a joke: don't waste money on Business and just fly economy where you will probably get three seats to yourself and decent food/drink. In Business, he menu has been changed and has been reduced to an omelette or Indian vegetables. Whilst allowances could be made for THY return flights to IST from KTM, it is inexcusable for such a poor food offer to Business Class passengers. The pre-arrival offer (food) was samosas. On arrival at KTM, business class passengers did not get express treatment to the arrival lounge (unlike all previous flights) and I spent nearly two hours before exiting the airport. The IST-KTM route offer has deteriorated to such an extent that I - despite 10+ trips on this route in business - would not recommend using THY.

I tried to engage the cabin crew but they seemed indifferent and just shrugged their shoulders. The power supplies are completely useless as they are in a confined / dark spot which you need your phone torch to be able to see - do not bring an oversized electric plug (the ones you get with most laptops nowadays) as it will simply not fit. I ended up using two travel adaptors to extend the the power plug which I then wedged with my mobile phone. The 'sky-chef' is a complete gimmick. They simply arrange food on a plate and are totally inflexible. I asked if I could have my meal a little later than scheduled but was met with a stern 'no'. I have photos of the defective footrests and the power supply.

review_header: " request you to send us the invoices"
review_text: The airline claimed they would provide a hotel, transfer and food at their expense and sent us to a 3rd party service desk for formalities. There were a few desks and it was very confusing. They provided no food vouchers, put us into a car and sent to a hotel. Turned out we needed to pay for transfer - about $180 for round trip. The hotel was provided for free. For the food we needed to order and pay cash at reception and it was later delivered to our room. It was a terrible food. We didn’t manage to get a receipt for that while they promised to give it to us a few times. After arriving to SFO I had 2 calls with their customer support. They always direct you to file a "feedback" at the website and can’t do anything even put through with their supervisor. In process of conversation with Sereda she was just quietly disappearing for minutes with no explanation nor excuses. An attempt to use a Facebook chat started promising until the other side suddenly stopped responding. Now to feedback forms. I filed 4. Attaching my single well-pictured receipt that everything there - my name, purpose of the expense, place, date, amount and signatures. I think I was communicating with AI generating slightly different but generally similar responses. Have a look: Feb-26: "We are sorry that events outside our control disrupted your journey. We have found out that the adverse weather conditions caused 33 minutes of delay on TK1086 Podgorica/Istanbul flight on the date of 13th of February, 2024, due to which you missed your onward flight specified in your ticket and completed your travel on TK289 Istanbul/ San Francisco flight. ... As per your request, for evaluation of expenses, we kindly request the expense bills that are issued by the establishments the expenses are made at, with the place, date, contents, name and the total amount of the expense visible on the receipt. Thank you for your understanding and wish to host you better in your future flights." Follow up on Feb-26 : "We kindly inform you that as it will breach the security and documentation protocols, our accounting department is unable to process compensation for the expenses without the original invoices or receipts. For evaluation of expenses, we kindly request the expense bills that are issued by the establishments the expenses are made at, with the place, date, contents and the total amount of the expense visible on the receipt. Also in order to evaluate your reimbursemnet request of your visa expenses, you can share your e-visa doucmnet or image of your visa. Thanks for understanding." Feb-29: "As per your request, for evaluation of expenses, we kindly request the expense bills that are issued by the establishments the expenses are made at, with the place, date, contents,name and the total amount of the expense visible on the receipt. Additionally, referring to your message we would like to state that, our compensation and reimbursement transactions are being held within the accordance of the Civil Aviation Passenger Rights Regulations. " Mar-1: "We are not able to evaluate the process without the invoices which are official. We kindly request you to send us the invoices which includes your name, date and the amount and also it must be official.

Nearly everybody in the limo seemed to be travelling on Turkish and to beyond Istanbul. The driver said all their services are full of passengers for THY. If you are listening Turkish Airlines, think about a few flights to San Diego with its upcoming new terminal! Check-in was open very early, and painless, by a very polite agent. Boarding was chaotic. The first boarding announcement began half way through another announcement about another flight being made throughout the terminal. The agent spoke with her back to the boarding gates and said which passenger groups to wait on the left and which on the right. But it transpired she meant on our left and right even though she indicated her left and right. Consequently the lines were totally full of the wrong passengers. Eventually we found the right lines and entered through the boarding gates which also took our photos in the process. Apart from the boarding mix-up, I would say the process in LAX was very good. After boarding the Captain announced 20 minutes delay in start-up due to some luggage compartment problems. My seat was near the back and I could hear loud noises of containers rumbling around. But she was exactly right and after 20 minutes we started up and took off. Amenity packs and Menus were distributed, followed by the first meal. The crew on this flight were very relaxed and courteous as they served us. On my way out from Istanbul I had been in Business Class but the crew there all seemed in a rush, even though the flight was over twelve hours. Everybody settled down to sleep as the sun could be seen coming up and then setting again through a few open window shades. A self-service snack and drinks were available in the galleys during the night. Near the end of the flight another hot meal with choice of entrée was served. We landed on time and endured the inevitable long ground time at Istanbul Airport before we reached our gate. Long long walks to İmmigration, and another long walk to the most distant luggage carousel, even though there were many empty ones near the centre of Arrivals. But. Our luggage was already going round; Istanbul Airport luggage is always so fast. Overall an excellent flight.
Ground staff rude and nonchalant. Even laughing when asked why no information. Please read previous reviews. Would rather pay extra for an alternative option. I would not recommend this airline.

First they messed-up our seats, and me and my wife were separated during the self check in at the Istanbul airport. It took a lot of back and forth with the ground staff to get them to switch our seats so that we can sit together. The staff was of no help, and kept trying to persuade me that seat reservations don't matter even though I paid for them. They did try to offer me to pay for an upgrade to business class. The plane was really old, seats were far too small.
Tried to check in 10 mins after check in opened, but the website and app showed no seats available. Contacted the helpline and they could not support.

We had a few mins to make it from gate A4 to F8 and our security checkpoint was only manned by 1 team with a second added for the last few minutes and once we cleared this 7:50 I ran to the gate making it there at 8:00. Being informed the gate had closed I was directed to customer service.
