The next day, we saw the price dropped to $358 per ticket, so we contacted customer service (the call was on hold 30+ min) to either get our price matched or cancel the flight. The customer service representative said I can get $418 full refunded to my credit card, which really didn't make sense so I confirmed it multiple multiple times and the associate confirmed that that is going to be the case. After a week, I only see $118 posted on my card. Contacted them again waiting 30+min again, they said they did refund $418 to the card and asked me to contact my credit card bank to confirm the refund amount. Did that and American Express confirmed that they only see $118 from Hawaiian. Called Hawaiian again, holding 30+ min again, and finally, they transferred to the supervisor (which took another 30+ min). Finally, the supervisor says they cannot do a full refund since $300 was charged by travel credit, and they can re-send the travel credit via email. I complained about my wasted time and also told him to please educate the customer service associate about this non-refundable travel credit information so people like me don't have to waste their precious time, and the supervisor just hung up on me without any answer! I don't know when or whether I'll be receiving my credit, and I really don't want to call them again for the credit not received yet, but I may have to. Worst customer experience calling them, never had a clean flight with them, plus they are usually more expensive than other airlines, so I'd highly highly recommend flying with some other airline.

review_header: "attendants were all very nice and cheerful"
review_text: Hawaiian Airlines use all of Terminal 1 in HNL airport. Announcements were made frequently regarding flight status and gate updates, really good. Boarding is quite organized and people were called to board by zones. The airplane for flight HA 216 was N488HA, a 23 years old B712. We opted for the over wing emergency exit with extra legroom. The seats are very standard plastic backed type and at the emergency exit the tray tables were located in the armrest. However since the trip only takes minutes we don't really have the need for the tray table. We only bring our backpacks for the flight and were able to put them under the seat in front of us. The overhead bins are on the small side, and based on its size can accommodate slimmer carryon only. We depart around 15 minutes later than schedule (which is a big deal for the 20-30 minutes inter island flights like these) however we land around 5 minutes ahead of schedule. The flight attendants were all very nice and cheerful, and within a short 20-25 minutes flight were able to serve us drink (water or a delicious POG juice cocktail - Passion fruit-Orange-Guava) and collect all the trash within minutes, and we are ready for landing.

The flight HA 395 OGG-HNL was using N484HA, a 23 years old B712. The incoming airplane arrived early but there was still another airplane at its designated gate; and after waiting for a few minutes they were able to use a different gate so there will be no delay. A relief, since we have to catch a flight out from HNL later that night. Boarding was quite orderly and we were boarded by zones. The flight left on time and arrived in HNL around 10 minutes early. The FAs in this flight were very nice and cheerful, and they have good interactions with the passengers. Within 20-25 minutes flight the FAs were able to serve water or juice for passengers, collect all the trash and getting ready to land again. Hawaiian Airlines is a good airline to use for short island hop trips like this, and we enjoyed our flight with them.

So if you went shopping they count that as a personal item so you can’t bring it on the plane. Doesn’t everyone go shopping for souvenirs? How is one suppose to bring it back? How about food n snacks if you carry the snack in your hands it’s also consider as a personal item. Even my small Fanny pack was consider a personal item so I ask what do they want me to do they rudely reply as “that’s for you to figure out!” While rolling their eyes. Never will I fly Hawaiian Airlines.

Very friendly, efficient staff served a nice meal and snacks later on along with drinks and regular cabin pass through checks. IFE is clumsy and limited but fine for five hours. Seat is comfortable and does recline. They need a more world class front cabin but the aloha goes a long way

Tried booking on the website using our Hawaiian miles but couldn’t because of a website error. Had to call and book the reservation instead. Took 3 hours just to get through to someone. Finally was able to book the reservation only to see that my card was charge 3 times. Called again, waited 4 hours, tossed around from operator to operator each one telling me they were unable to refund. After 12 hours finally got to someone who told me they could request a refund for me. Fine.  Two days later I see they charge me 2 more times! And the nightmare continues. Once again calling and being told they cannot refund me. I will never book with Hawaiian again.

review_header: "HAL got us where we needed - eventually"
review_text: For their part, HAL got us where we needed - eventually...but not without a lot of wasted vacation time and unnecessary anxiety. 1) An hour before check-in for the next day's flight to Kona we get a text from HAL that our flight was cancelled. Okay, cutting slack for COVID or whatever reason (none was given) we were still worried about how to continue the next leg of our trip. We had no place to stay if we couldn't travel, and expensive reservations waiting the next day. They gave us a Toll-Free number to "call", after hours of trying, all we got was busy signal and we never got through. There was no way to rebook on HAL website, since ticketing was through Delta. So, spending 4 hours on hold getting through to Delta we rebooked for a later HAL flight - but had to pay fare difference, even though it wasn't our fault we had to make a flight change. 2) Arriving at the airport, HAL was a mess. Although our reservation included checked bags, they insisted we had to pay because, "we're not Delta Airlines." I get that, but we paid Delta - who already paid HAL for our seats and baggage. 3) Finally getting on the plane, there were a ton of open seats. My guess is the earlier cancellation wasn't COVID related, just saving expense to consolidate flights. We were in Economy seats and after boarding, all Exit Rows were open. On any other airline, we've been allowed to move to open seats, but not on HAL. At first, the flight attendant said we couldn't sit there because of Exit Row requirements. I responded, "as long as we meet Exit Row requirements, why can't we sit there?" His response, "more money." I get it, they market them as Premium seating. After cancelled flights, additional charges and vacation time lost, the least HAL could have done was let us sit there. The Customer Service value would cost them nothing. No. Who sat there instead? Uniformed HAL employees, probably being repositioned. I'm not begrudging that staff deserves to be treated well, but aren't we the paying customers? Through everything it seemed the message HAL was sending was, we don't need you - you need us - so live with it. Easy fix - Obviously, HAL had our cell numbers, because they texted us that the flight was cancelled, due to low occupancy. It would have been easier for them to simply put us on another flight and tell us of the time change. Better yet, since there were only about 30 people booked, they could have called us. Rather than have us keep calling their toll-free and never getting through, one of their agents could have called us (same amount of time on the phone for their agents). We paid a premium for everything on this trip, costs were about 30% higher than in the past. We knew that going in. The cost of more than a half-day of lost vacation time and toll of having your itinerary cancelled mid-trip - priceless.

They canceled my flight but I can't reach anyone to receive a refund. When I did finally get someone on the phone, the call was disconnected before a refund was processed. They didn't call me back and the wait to speak to a representative no matter when I call is almost two hours long. I've tried both chat and text customer service options. They responded over 36 hours later when I was asleep and closed the thread before I responded a couple hours later. This has happened three times! Not even given a chance to respond and I still do not have a flight or a refund!

review_header: "shouldn’t have to take two hours to recheck bags"
review_text: I had a 4 hour layover and needed to recheck my bags since i was transferring airlines. I spent an hour getting to Hawaiian Airlines check in since is in a different terminal? I guess Hawaiian Airlines with international flights instead of the domestic where i landed. I got there with my 5 bags from my extended trip and the check in was closed! Apparently they close 30min after each flight and open 2.5 hours before each flight. So I'm stuck here till 11:30pm for them to reopen. It shouldn’t have to take two hours to recheck bags. It’s ridiculous.

review_header: "The kiosks to check in were closed"
review_text: I booked a quick inter island flight from Kauai (to Oahu where I live). For internet island travel the boarding pass says to check in 30 minutes before. My flight was at 7:45 so I was dropped off in front of the Hawaiian Airlines check-in at the Lihue airport at 7:15. I wasn’t checking a bag so literally just needed to complete the 30 second check in on the kiosk. The kiosks to check in were closed. When I went up to the counter the lights were off & the two agents were walking around the counter. They said “the counter closes at 7:15, no one was here. You can’t check in now.” I said “it’s literally 7:16 right now, I was here trying fo check in but your kiosks are closed.” The agent speaking to me was very rude saying “well we closed at 7:15, you were supposed to check in 30 minutes before your flight.” (which is what I was doing). When I asked what I could do she shrugged saying “we are closed, come back tomorrow.” I have never seen an airline close all it’s windows before the last flights leave and they should definitely put this on your boarding information and say 45 minutes or 60 minutes since they don’t disclose that they close beforehand. I had to pay for a ticket the next day & I think it’s completely unacceptable that this airline closed before their last flights take off and they were definitely closed before the 30 minute window and were not helpful to reschedule me. I will be using Mokulele from now on for any of my flights since there’s no aloha from this company.
Other airlines are so flexible at this time but Hawaiian airlines are the worst.

I am 18 years old and have flown quite a bit, both internationally and within the US. I am a female and I was on my period. I had run out of some stuff and needed to get to my sister who had some feminine products in her bag. She was on the other side of the plane all the way to the back. I quickly made my way back there trying to not get into anyone’s way. When I got there the flight attendants were getting ready to do the food runs so I moved out of their way. When I was ready to go back they were in the way so I sat in an empty seat to talk to my sister. I was then told I had to go back to my seat. I informed the flight attendant that I would as soon as they weren’t in the way of the isle. She argued for a bit then finally left it alone. As soon as the isle was clear I went back to my seat but was stopped by a flight attendant physically blocking my path and stopping me with her hand. I told her I wasn’t going to walk through there again and just was getting something from my sister. She then accused me of going back and forth over 3 times. I corrected her and she continued to complain about what i was doing even though I was not causing any problems. After the flight my sister told me she had also had issues with a different flight attendant. That makes 3 different attendants who were rude. When we got my sisters bag out of baggage claim it was soaked and the metal badge had been ripped off. They honestly were so rude and unkind it was shocking. I have never written a bad review because I try to assume people are doing their best, but this was just awful. I will never fly with them again.

Apparently, he thought I said something else and immediately got in my face, yelling, screaming, threatening etc.. Then proceeded to tell me my credit card, which I used 10 minutes prior, was bad, obviously trying to jerk me around and embarrass me in front of everyone else in line. I am a business manager, if one of my employees treated a customer in such a disrespectful manner, they would be fired on the spot! I will never use Hawaiian again nor recommend them to anyone! I do hope that management from Hawaiian Airlines makes necessary changes so that others do not have such a horrible experience. They are totally unprofessional and arrogant with the way they treat their paying customers!

I purchased 5 tickets costing $1870 in August and tried to get a refund in September, 40 days before our flights were scheduled for. Hawaiian Airlines said they canceled the flights but the money would be credited to my account and needs to be used with the next year or forfeit your money. If that isn't the textbook definition of extortion then I don't know what is. All their tickets are non-refundable. You need to purchase a 3rd party insurance to protect your travel which I have. But why should I use the insurance when I didn't use the Airlines services. My hotel and rental car refunds were returned in one day. The customer agent lied to me and said when you purchase the tickets it says refundable or nonrefundable which it doesn't add she called me a liar. The worst customer service ever. I've written numerous complaints to Hawaiian Airlines all with returns saying they will not refund my money.

review_header: "Very disappointed with the treatment we received"
review_text: Flew first class both times and I will say the flight attendants and service were wonderful both times. The check-ins not so good! Both airports we ran into extremely rude check-in clerks. At Ontario’s check-in we had a male clerk that was extremely rude. He wouldn’t even look at our paperwork showing we’d been vaccinated and tested negative for COVID-19. Wasn’t about to help us and told us we’d have to get out of line to download our results even though one of our results had been downloaded. Isn’t his job to help? On the way back at Honolulu airport the clerk looked at us like she had doubts we were in first class even after showing her our boarding passes. Had the nerve to asked us twice and looked down her nose at us. I’m not sure what the problem is with their customer service, but they definitely need to work on it. I’ve worked with the public for over 45 years and know this is not how you treat your customers. Very disappointed with the treatment we received from them at their check-in counters.

Governments new mandate 8/21. Hawaiian said due to Covid cancellations they will hold your ticket for your next trip. What they don’t tell you, is that they only waive the change fee, and you have to rebook within one year of your original booking date. In my case that was March 1, 2021. (With our timeshare we are only allowed to book 1 year in advance) Also, they will collect any additional fees if there is a change in your ticket cost. No accommodating for Covid/Government hotel/timeshares etc shut downs for restrictions. Do not book on this airline. I’m now out $500.

It looked like they decided to have every flight for the day leaving all within a 2 hour window due to the extreme amount of people trying to check in. It took over 1 hour just to have 1 bag scanned through to check for fruit / agricultural items. Then we sat in line for 2 hours just to check in one bag. This line moved at a snails pace and only had 2 employees checking baggage in. I have never seen such a slow process in my life. It literally took around 10 minutes per person. There was no sense of urgency from any of the staff at any time. The lines grew so large that they stacked up down the street. I have 3 small children who had to stand in the heat the whole time.. Then we had to stand in another line to go through security. There must have been 500 people wrapped around the building. I had to beg another family to let us cut in line because our flight was about to leave and would have had to stand in line for at least another 3 hours. We somehow made it 5 minutes before boarding. The worst part of the day was the male flight attendant (Dark spiked hair, glasses, approximately 35-40). He must have been having a bad day because his customer service was terrible. He was rude, grumpy, pushy, conttoling, and had a poor attitude. He constantly baggered people about wearing their masks even though this was during the time they kept serving food and drinks. What are we supposed to do? Cut a hole in the mask for a straw? Overall just not the kind of person I would expect to be a flight attendant. I could tell that the other female staff members did not like working with him. Doesn't seem like someone that should be working in customer service. The flight from Oakland to Maui was wonderful. I work in customer service and depend financially on receiving good surveys. This is actually the first time I have written a negative review on anything online in my entire life, I never complain unless in person. So that should tell you how bad this experience was.

We, the parents, fully cooperated with the personal by putting on his mask, but he refused to use the mask because he was hungry and drinking his bottle in this moment. We made clear to the staff that he will be wearing his mark as soon as his finish his bottle but even though we were asked to deplane and stay in Honolulu at our own expenses. Our flight was rebooked to the next day. During the check-in and boarding time, we were given a special treatment by not only being allowed to do online check-in but also by being closely checked by the staff if our son was wearing the mask. As the feeding time of our son mashed with the boarding time, we faced a same situation as the day before. Our son woke up asking for his baby bottle. We gave the bottle already sat in the airplane. It resulted in a clear procedure to again deplane us (as we were threated).

review_header: "We ended up having to buy three new tickets on United Airlines"
review_text: Check-in had already been done the day before on the HA app and we also paid $30 for a checked bag. The situation at the airport was complete chaos. Huge lines apparently just for bag drop off. Self check-in kiosks were not working properly and not printing out bag tags. We ended up having to wait on one of those lines. But before that (and several times more during our wait) we talked with someone from the HA staff and explained our situation: I have a heart condition and need to be medicated every day. Losing our flight (even though we arrived at the airport 2 hours in advance) could have drastic consequences. The staff person guaranteed us that we would board the plane and that the flight would wait for us if needed. Again, we were guaranteed multiple times that the flight would not depart without us. At 1.50pm we finally reached one of the bag drop off desks… but the HA assistant suddenly left the desk and said she couldn’t help us. No one apparently was available to help us so we waited a few minutes until finally we went to another line and asked to be helped - it was 1.55pm. When we were about to check our bag (which had been already paid for) the new HA assistant told us that the boarding for our flight was already closed and we couldn’t board. I explained my health condition and what we had been told before by other HA staff - that the plane would wait for late passengers due to the chaotic situation at the airport. Unfortunately, the HA people were still not able to let us board our flight and, even worse, were not interested at all in offering any kind of alternative to help us go to San Jose (or San Francisco) on the same day. Finally a "manager" came to help us but, of course, she was also completely useless. Her excuse was that all passengers are advised to arrive 3 hours before their flight, for a domestic flight! She said everyone received an email with this notification. Obviously, we didn't get anything remotely similar to it. At the end, she apparently was got tired of dealing with an upset customer and decided to ask for security to get us removed. Right. We ended up having to buy three new tickets on United Airlines for that night - in other words, we paid an $1k+ more, waited in OGG for 7 hours and arrived home one day after. I lost one cycle of my medication - hopefully there won’t be other serious consequences. The lack of concern, ridiculous handling of bag drops at the airport and total misinformation by the HA staff are all reasons for our disappointment. Because of HA, we had to buy three new tickets on a different airline.

Spent 2 hours inside the plane and were deboarded. Right after that it was announcement about 14,5 hours delay! Finally around midnight we took off. The flight attendants and gate agents were very rude. It was very cold inside the plane. I was lucky to get a blanket, but my husband was not. When he asked for the blanket, the flight attendant offered him to purchase, no free blanket any more! It was 11 hours of torture, literally. The food was not edible. I am not a picky eater, but what they served was not a food, it was a garbage. The worst airline I've ever flown on. Never again.

I called in and was told that a change had been made to my flight, that there was no alternative flight I could be booked on and my only option was a refund. I wondered "where was the call when you changed the flight?" If I hadn't called in I could have shown up in LA with no flight to Hawaii. And there was no “we're sorry for the inconvenience please enjoy______” (fill in the blank - maybe some free air miles or something? I've been a Hawaiian air miles member for over 10 years). The impression the customer service rep gave me was that she was just waiting for me to accept the refund so she could say her rehearsed "I do really apologize is there anything else I can assist you with?" line. The refund takes 7-10 business days so I couldn't even use my money to book a replacement ticket with another airline. Super disappointing.

No compassion or understanding or willing to work with their customers. Which I think they should appreciate given that the pandemic happened and airlines are hurting. I said I was willing to pay the difference to change the dates and all they want to do is say no and not work with someone in a tough situation. Even tried to upgrade. This is whole thing ridiculous and I should have never booked with them. They are forcing someone to spend more money to because they are greedy for not being able to make money last year. This is a scam and an insult.

review_header: "never fly with them for future trips"
review_text: First, already annoyed that they couldn't just divert to LAX, which was an hour away, opposed to HNL, 2.5 hours flying back. When we arrive back in HNL, we're told to deboard so the passenger can be cared for and the plane can be refueled/cleaned. We were given an estimate of an hour. Well it is now 2 hours and we should have already re-departed. Now there has been an "incident on the jet bridge" and we are still waiting to board. So in my opinion a re-route back to our original destination, a 7 hour delay, rude and grumpy flight attendants and gate agents, and no compensation or meal vouchers offered, are all valid reasons qualifying for a 1-Star review and I will never fly with them for future trips.

I’ve seen them harass military members and just because I was military they literally told me that I’m not welcome and cancelled my flight. I did get a creditable refund but even trying to get that utilized is ridiculous. They are unprofessional and wouldn’t recommend them to anyone. I’ve flown on virtually all airline companies and this is by far the worst. Please spend an additional $20-$50 and avoid the hassle.
Pay the extra money to fly another airline so this doesn’t happen to you!

This airline, who market themselves as selling the warmth of the Hawaiian Islands is actually a heartless, cut throat business which in practice can care less about their customers. They literally lie about their benefits (such as being able to upgrade on line if seats are available in first class within 24 of your flight). Once I was flying and an engine caught fire. We had to make an emergency landing and stay in Maui for hours. Hawaiian issued $50.00 credits to the passengers on board. When I tried to use it the credit it was denied. The culture is one of profit only, customers.  I've had enough and will now fly Southwest.

review_header: "Since when did Hawaiian start lacking this much?"
review_text: First of all they didn't have earphones for the passengers to watch their inflight movies. Or they ran out. Whatever the case, how are you a major airline and not have what is needed for the flight? Then it was cold, but guess what. They had no blankets! Come on now really?! Since when did Hawaiian start lacking this much? They finally served a sandwich for the 5.5 hour flight. A sandwich with lettuce, tomato and no meat. They need to go back to the days when they actually tried. Because this was not the best experience for my wife and I.

review_header: "worst trip we have had on Hawaiian"
review_text: Perhaps Covid was part of the problem, but the cabin crew was not concerned with the passengers. Seemed almost irritated that we were there. We had pre ordered a special meal. No explanation and no special meal, either. Maybe things will change after COVID, but right now we would not fly Hawaiian again.

My recent flight was different. I still admire Hawaiian’s efficiency and courtesy, but the food is a different story. I realize the COVID-19 era is challenging, but there is no excuse for the utterly disgusting food served. On the flight to Honolulu from Los Angeles, the meal was a warmed sandwich: a huge grinder bun with some cheese slopped on it and a sun dried piece of tomato. It was inedible. On the flight home, they served what was called a chicken sandwich. It was another bun with bits of chicken in a sauce of some kind. My husband, who will eat anything, took one bite and declared it “nasty,” I looked at what was inside and threw it away. There has to be some acceptable alternatives. Try harder!

review_header: "They simply refused to honor 3 of the 4 vouchers"
review_text: Due to covid we were unable to travel and had to cancel our flight. When contacting the third party, they said I should cancel the flights through Hawaiian Airlines. We called Hawaiian Airlines, who said we couldn't be refunded, but offered vouchers for a later trip. I accepted the vouchers. When I called Hawaiian Airlines to rebook the flights, they said that 3 of the 4 vouchers had been refunded. I received no refund. When I asked who authorized the refund they would not tell me. When I asked why they would give me vouchers and then cancel them, they refused to answer. When I asked why only 3 of the 4 were "refunded" they also refused to answer. They simply refused to honor 3 of the 4 vouchers totaling $1321.85. Don't fly with them, they will steal your money.

review_header: "now been changed to a connecting flight"
review_text: When I originally purchased the direct flight, it did cost more than the connecting flights that I am now on. I was willing to pay more for a direct flight due to obvious convenience and an earlier arrival time. I strongly believed that I should have been compensated for the following inconveniences: 1. The connecting flights are cheaper, and just on principle, we should receive the difference. 2. My experience dealing with the above changes: a. I get the change email, I try to contact via text, wait 2 hours for someone to text me back, once they do, I ask my questions, with hardly any answers, other than “due to current demands the direct flight is gone till May.” b. Due to the lack of help via text I decided it would be better to call someone. I waited on hold for another 75 minutes. I got someone nice enough to answer my questions and send me to this form. I filled out the form once, it did not send and erased what I originally put in this box plus a ticket number that I now have forgotten and cannot look up due to my flight change. c. All this just to find out that you choose my flight for me and even if I did have a choice, and I found something cheaper, such as the day before or after, you wouldn't automatically refund the difference!? 3. Inconvenience the actual flight change inflicts upon us. a. The original flight got us to Maui at 9:30 AM, new flight arrival is 3:30 PM, which takes away 6 hours of our vacation. b. The rental car that has already been booked now needs to be changed and may incur a fee. c. An early check-in at our hotel that we paid extra for, which we will not be refunded for. d. The added stress of finding a connected flight Customer service did nothing when I reached out to them about this, I also cc'd the CEO and he had no response as well.

We intentionally booked with them to avoid connections (we're trying to limit our time in airports to not get COVID). They had an alternative direct flight on the same day that departed from a nearby airport. We called to ask to be switched to this flight, they said if we made that switch we would have to pay a $400 switching fee per person! I spent an hour on the phone with them, and they said that it was within their rights to switch the route on us. Though technically this might be true, it is terrible customer service to refuse an option that would avoid connections as we originally booked (and actually would be better for public health). Really terrible experience - I would recommend that they reconsider their customer service during COVID.

review_header: "not be getting any more of my business"
review_text: American cancelled our flight two and half hours before it was supposed to take off. Our flight from MSP was delayed a little due to weather, and we were told our connections would probably be delayed as well, but we had a 3 hour layover in Dallas-Fort Worth so we figured we'd be fine even if it wasn't delayed. But while we were en route to Texas they completely cancelled it. By the time we landed there was only one flight available and that one was in the middle of their final boarding. We ran as fast as we could but it was in another terminal so we were very screwed. The gate agents we talked to were rude, ignoring people and offering a bare minimum of help. The first desk never asked what we needed, just walked the people before us off to the helpdesk to rebook and left us standing there. We ran around to a lot of different desks and I asked one of them if there were any later flights to Knoxville. She said "oh yes there's one at this gate over here" and when I told her no, that one was cancelled, she looked surprised, said they were always the last to know, and started packing up to leave! No offer of help until I asked again if there were any later flights and she pointed me to yet another desk. The gate agent there was one we'd already seen and she was annoyed when I asked her where to go to rebook because she'd already pointed those other customers there earlier in my hearing. I'm sorry I couldn't remember! You didn't care enough to ask what I needed the first time I was at your desk! We finally found the helpdesk and those agents were the only helpful American employees we met the entire time. They actually cared. The airline kept telling them to clock out while they still had a line of 40 people waiting, and the helpdesk agents were not happy about it. One of them (I wish I remembered her name, she deserves a raise) came back to keep working and I think she might have done it without any overtime pay. From what I heard, there were people having to rebook cancelled flights going all over the country. There could not possibly have been weather everywhere in the U.S. I think American just felt like cancelling. What sense did it make to cancel the later flight to Knoxville two and a half hours early and leave the earlier one alone if there was bad weather? Why didn't they wait to see if it cleared up?  I also mention, the gate agent we asked directions of at Spirit Airlines was so much friendlier. The budget airlines are beating you. Get it together or go broke, American. You will not be getting any more of my business.

We landed in Dallas and told our connecting flight was delayed due to mechanical issues. After additional delays we were told NO FLIGHTS out until the next day. We stood in line for over an hour to obtain a voucher for a hotel and the extremely rude agent told us they were ALL OUT? My mother slept on a bench in the airport. The next morning we were one of the first people in line to get re-booked to get to El Paso. They didn't have any seats available so they re-routed us to Albuquerque, New Mexico where we had to rent a car and drive several hours to get to El Paso (car rental was over $300 PLUS we had to pay for the night we missed at our hotel in El Paso) When we arrived in New Mexico our luggage was no where to be found! After our return home I reached out to American Airlines and was offered miles on both our accounts - seriously where do they think my mother is traveling to again any time soon?! It wasn't until I posted a review on Trip Advisor that I received a phone call from the airlines customer relations department saying "this is their final offer and it's the best they could do" The airlines "graciously" offered us $75 airline credit to be used in one years time - AGAIN, where is my elderly mother going to be flying to?!!! While ALL this has occurred my sister has a flight in DECEMBER that DELTA airlines had to change her time and without asking they offered her miles on her account for any inconvenience that this may cause. NOW THAT'S CUSTOMER SERVICE AT IT'S BEST! American Airlines should be ashamed the way they treated all of us on that scheduled flight but the fact that they had my 87 year old wheelchair bound mother sleep on a bench and then offer us $75 compensation is beyond insulting. This airlines has been in the news for negative customer service for quite a while - My advice is avoid American Airlines at all costs if it is possible. The lack of friendly, compassionate staff it lacking, Customer service is not part of their mission at all!

We were re-charged for seats on our next flight. We petitioned for a refund and were denied. This is the message I sent them.  Your representative called me the night they canceled the flight and then gave me only options that charged more for seats. The agent told me I would get a refund for all three charges, then did nothing. I called week later and another representative told me I would get a refund for all three seats. I got one for one vs three. I called back another week later. This time your representative told me they couldnt help me and the request can only be made online. Not your company will not honor the other two refunds.

We had a two legged flight and our second leg got delayed twice and eventually canceled. We were unable to obtain hotel vouchers because the agent said she simply ran out when I explained my mother is in a wheelchair and elderly she said that the couches are very comfortable. The next morning we got rerouted to Albuquerque New Mexico and we were forced to rent a car and drive 4 1/2 hours to get to El Paso so that my mother can attend her last siblings funeral. However, our luggage wasn’t with us. The airline managed to lose it for a couple of days after our flight was completed I contacted the airlines and was offered some extra mileage in our account for future travel. When I explained my mother‘s age and all of her ailments and said chances are she probably won’t ever be on an airplane again the response I got was no worries. The miles don’t expire

What started as a simple flight from Mexico into Dallas turned into a multi-day ordeal of missed connections, unprofessional staff, and zero solutions. After an hour-long TSA line in Dallas, I missed my connecting flight home. American Airlines rebooked me on a 5 AM flight the next day and put me up in a hotel. Arriving at the airport at 3 AM, we boarded the flight only to be told the captain hadn't shown up! After a delay, a new captain was found, but then they discovered "break fuel" on the ground, leading to another cancellation. Rebooked again, the customer service agent suggested a flight to Chicago to catch my original connection – which I missed AGAIN! Stuck in Chicago, I was put on standby, but American Airlines had overbooked every flight, even paying passengers to give up their seats. Now, on my second unexpected hotel stay, all I can say is this entire mess was avoidable and entirely American Airlines' fault. Not once did I receive an apology or a guaranteed solution. The customer service agents in Dallas were incredibly rude, even telling my teen daughter to "fix her face." I will never fly American Airlines again, and neither should you if you value getting home.

Tried telling me I’m on the wrong flight even though my flight was correct and proceeded to give more attitude when I tried showing them I’m right. Then the male scanning tickets was rude and gave attitude when I scanned my ticket when I scanned when asked to. Overall horrible experience due to the workers for the airlines I would not recommend flying with them.

I will avoid them at all costs in the future. It started with a flight that was slated to leave at 2:45PM. I got a text informing me that it was delayed until 6 hours initially (eventually delayed 10+ hours). Upon discovering that the flight was delayed around 1PM, I tried rebooking my flight to another airline. However, the customer service representative at United told me that there was a "50/50 chance that they will take your checked bag off the plane because it's hot outside." Basically holding my bag hostage so I couldn't change flights to another airline. After a few additional delays, I eventually cancelled my flight 6 hours before the flight time and asked for my checked bag back. They promised I could get my bag back but low and behold, they sent my bag to San Fransisco anyways. This is hot off the tail of me spending 8+ hours at the airport trying to find an alternative flight or get my checked bag back. It then took me multiple calls across 3 days to beg for my checked bag back in which the customer service team basically told me they had "no power to help me" and just to check my bag status on a website (which showed a timeline they missed and couldn't even stick to). It's now 11PM on the third day and my bag "may or may not arrive today". This is far and away the worst airline I have ever dealt with. I have missed work obligations due to this whole situation and I deeply regret choosing United. I would NOT recommend united if you can avoid it.

American delivered a solid product on this flight. Extra special kudos go to the flight attendant (sorry lost her name) who, by herself served 20 people drinks dinner and ice cream sundaes graciously and efficiently. Watching her determined and extremely pleasant work was a pleasure.The food, seats, and entertainment were all fine for 5 hours of flying. On time arrival made it a perfect trip except for the frightening ICE agents who “greeted” our arrival.

We flew to a destination with a dog in carrier without issue on a different airline. However, when flying home, American highlighted that they have a strict dog carrier size policy. They are an anomaly compared with other airlines. They have different measurements from Delta, Southwest, and other major airlines. After about 20 minutes of negotiating, they finally let us go. We took pictures, and the dog carrier fit under the seat with plenty of room. American Airlines should really revisit this. American also does a lot outdated admin. They use pen and paper quite a bit and are not technologically up to date. They have even bounced passengers off of planes simply for checking to see if there's room on a different flight.

review_header: "11 hours making my way home via train"
review_text: I waited at the gate for over four hours before discovering the cancellation. Had I known earlier, I could have made alternate arrangements. When I called customer support, the best they could offer was a flight two days later. They would not disclose the amount of refund I would be entitled to or the reason for the cancellation, and informed me that I needed to contact customer relations for any additional compensation. They explained that I would have to go to the in-person customer line to inquire about the status of my baggage. After waiting in the in-person line for 30 minutes, I was told to go to baggage claim for information about my bag. At baggage claim, I learned that my bag had been expedited to a flight the following day. I spent the next 11 hours making my way home via train at a personal expense of $250. There is no excuse for putting customers through these hardships. Information regarding the reason for the cancellation, entitlement to a refund, and the status of bags is purposefully obscured. This information should be readily available on the app or at least over the phone. Why should I have to call and wait in two lines to gather this information in a piecemeal fashion?

We were flying from Athens to Philadelphia with a connecting flight to Charlotte. After landing in Philly, we sat on the tarmac for nearly an hour before reaching the gate — which already put us at serious risk of missing our connection. Unsurprisingly, by the time we deplaned and got through the lengthy customs process, we had missed our flight. We were then directed to the American Airlines customer service line, where we waited another full hour. Once we finally reached a representative, we were told we’d been rebooked for a flight the following day. No discussion, no options — just a delayed flight and more stress. Meanwhile, we had to pay additional fees for our dogs to stay another night at the kennel — an unexpected and frustrating cost. We were given a hotel voucher, waited 45 minutes for the shuttle, only to arrive and be told the hotel was fully booked. No rooms available. Overbooked. Exhausted and with nowhere to go, we had to pay out-of-pocket for a different hotel, transportation, and meals — none of which were covered or acknowledged by American. The next morning, we returned to the airport early to try to get reimbursed, only to be told, “We don’t handle that here — you need to call customer service.” So we called, and were told that we have to wait until our entire reservation is complete before we can even request reimbursement. Absolutely unacceptable. Once we land in Myrtle Beach, I will not rest until we are properly refunded. The level of inconvenience, disorganization, and lack of accountability is staggering. Do not fly with American Airlines. They have made it clear that they do not value their customers, and I will absolutely be warning friends, family, and fellow travelers to steer clear. Spend the extra money and fly with an airline that treats passengers with basic respect. We will never fly American again.

Apparently they changed our airplane to a smaller plane so they had to bump people.  I’m 6’ 6” tall. I don’t fit in regular seats. I pay for extra legroom. I was offered to upgrade to 1st class for only $149. I took it. I was probably bumped because I didn’t pay as much as other first class tickets. It was a 5am flight. I arrived at the airport at 3:45 to check a bag. I wasn’t told I didn’t have a seat when I checked the bag. My boarding pass on my phone didn’t tell me anything or inform me I should check in with the gate agent. I proceeded to the gate and was only informed I didn’t have a seat as I was boarding. How crazy is that? Then they let everyone else board and luckily there were a few extra seats so I was given one. It was a painful flight as I don’t fit in the seats because of my height. I should have been informed earlier. They should have moved me to an extra leg room seat instead of totally bumping me. I have Platinum status with this airline. I fly nearly every week. There were so many better ways to handle this situation but they chose the worst. I wonder how they will compensate me. I don’t think it will be satisfactory.

The flight from SLO to PHX was delayed for more than one hour so I lost the connection in PHX, they booked me on the next flight that was supposed to be to leave at 4:45p It is now 6:15p and we are still sitting on a very warm plane waiting for a scratch on the door to be repaired No snacks or any kind of drinks are being offered to us. I asked the flight attendants to explain to me how a scratch on the door makes the plane unsafe to fly and they don’t have a clue.

I had the worse airport experience in 30 years of flying. Flying from Heathrow on American Airlines, we were checked in to a smaller waiting area before the crew even arrived. The space was extremely hot, people were crammed in and having trouble breathing and there were no bathrooms available. When some of us tried to go to the restrooms after we were told that the flight crew was delayed, we had to try to squeeze past a bunch of people waiting in line in front of the only entrance. When we continued on, we ran into a locked door that would not open. We were trapped in a space that was too hot with no access to any bathrooms. Once we got on the flight, the crew was extremely rude to the customers.

I called customer service they told me the only option is to go and be put on standby but only 1 spot was available. I told them I paid for 2. I was then told they can put us on a flight out of Houston hobby, I said okay we don't have much options than she tells me there may be an additional charge, I was like how we already paid and this is not our fault they finally said they got the fee waived. Plus I lost the money for our parking that we prepaid for since we are now having to go out of a different airport. We get there and then they delayed the flight to Dallas, by the time we got to Dallas they delayed the connecting flight to Vegas. We were originally supposed to be in Vegas by 430pm we arrived at 1am the next day. Nothing was offered as compensation or anything more like we should be appreciative we didn't get charged more. On our flight back I get a message around 3am saying our flight out has been delayed in which would make us to late to make our connecting flight back to Houston. I again called customer service and we had to get up immediately and get to the airport to catch a flight almost 4 hours than the original one. We were told they would give us priority boarding and 1 free drink for the situation. However when we got to the airport and checked in there was no priority boarding or free drink and did not even have us sitting together, but honestly we just wanted to get back to Houston. I fly somewhat often and by far this has been my worst experience ever. Spirit and Frontier are always the butt of all jokes but besides having to pay for everything on those airlines I have never had these issues with either one of those airlines. I took pictures of the terminal in Dallas on our way to Vegas and the pictures were taken within 2 minutes of each other. Look how empty the airport is and how busy the customer service line is for American airlines.

I used the chat for 10 minutes a lot of back and forth with questions, btw I answered all of them, and with the same, the person ended the conversation without leading me another way to fix my issue.  I will never use an airline that charges me $$ without providing service.

review_header: "I am tired and sick of this"
review_text: This June 2025 was a lot of things: first, at the airport in Raleigh, NC, this lady was taking her time when we were checking in, and we were 3 adults. We got on the airplane at the last minute. At Miami, when we were about to take the second plane, they asked early if anyone wanted to bring their carry-on to be put with the other luggage for free, and this is always. I think you have the option to decide what to do, especially if you have fragile stuff in your carry-on. A staff who thought we didn't speak English, just made signs with his hands to move us to the side of the line. He printed the stickers for our carry-on and put them in. I told him we are not leaving our luggage because of the fragile stuff we had, and he disappeared and let us on the side by the counter. He came back eventually and took off the stickers from the carry-on and let us go, but with an attitude. We got on the plane, and there was plenty of room for carry-on. I don't like this attitude every time we fly. I am tired and sick of this.

My family of 6 and I flew one way and waited 5 hours for a delayed flight ... the return flight was delayed again and in the end we didn't have time to transfer to another one and again had to wait the whole night (7 hours). In the end we spent the night at the airport with small children, we were given a hotel to which it was unclear how to get there in 20 minutes. They allocated $12 for food for each person .

The airline cannot seem to keep anything close to a schedule to save its life. I've probably been on 20 American flights at least this year and maybe 3 have actually been somewhat close to arriving on time. It doesn't help that all they offer is cheap pretzels and no wifi. Imo this must be about the worst airline in the US. Strongly reconsider if you want to ever get anywhere on time.

review_header: "I am out the money I had to pay"
review_text: After 2 hours sitting on the plane the captain announced the brakes had been fixed. We were pushed back and brakes again locked. Captain announced they’d had issues the day before and we were asked to deplane. So if it was a known issue why wasn’t it fixed the day before? It was announced that the brakes were again fixed; however, the crew was exiting the plane. The crew announced that they had timed out and could no longer fly the plane. The gate agent then announced that we would have to wait for a new crew to arrive from DFW. At this time I got a notice that I had been rebooked on a flight to MIA, even though I needed to go to FLL. Stood in line at the gate and after approximately 2 hours in line, I was able to get my flight changed to go into FLL on 7/5/25 since there were no flights to get me there sooner. The gate agent told me I would get a $12 voucher for food and a motel, but to just stay at he airport sine I would only have about 4 hrs until I departed out of DFW. Was able to finally get to DFW about 1:00am and just stayed at the airport. Was at the gate at 5:00 am to board my flight to FLL. I asked the gate agent about my bag that had been kept at the airport. He was VERY rude and told me that it was either already at my destination or would be on my flight. When I tried to ask him for more information, he repeated what he had said before and informed me that was what they are instructed to say and walked off. They started getting ready to board, when he realized there was no plane at the gate. He announced they needed to have someone get a plane out of the hanger. Did they just realize they needed an aircraft? I made it to my cruise with an hour to spare. On 7/11/25, still on the cruise, I checked in for my flight home, however it would not let me pay for checked bag fee. Got on the chat with AA and was told I could only do this once on line.  After discussion, he told me he would make a note and told me I would have to check my bag at the airport and would pay the higher rate. I cannot find anything on the web page that states this. On 7/12/25, boarded plane for my flight home. Upon landing in DFW, I received notice that my connecting flight had been canceled. No gate agent at our arriving gate. Went to the customer service desk, about 100 people in line and 2 agents. About an hour later a 3rd agent arrived. After 2.5 hours of waiting, the agent told me I was not entitled to any vouchers. I paid for food and a motel. Arrived back at the airport at 6 am for my 8:00 am flight. The gate was changed 5 times before we were to board. People that were on the flight the day before said they got no compensation, however, a group of 4 on the same canceled flight www given motel and food vouchers! Why tell some people no and others get compensated. Finally made it back to BZN, only to find out my bag was broken. It was fine when I left FLL. I am out the money I had to pay for my motel in FLL for July 4th since it was too late to cancel, I am out the extra meals I had to pay for, out the cost of the motel in DFW on July 12 as well as meals, and an extra day of parking at the airport. Now I’m trying to get through AA’s mess of a website!! They just repeat the same thing and dont listen or read what has been written.

review_header: "be the last dime they get for me"
review_text: The culture has gotten so bad. I purchased a ticket. They had a schedule change which calls me to have to cancel it. They gave me a credit. I went online to rebook for another flight however I was not allowed to use my credit because it was a different "category". Money is money. A credit is a credit. It's not like this is a cruise. In addition to that they want to charge $99 for a cancellation fee. Absolutely ridiculous. They must be hurting. Even Spirit allow you to change for free. I forfeited my ticket. That'll be the last dime they get for me. I booked with SWA instead. The only thing American is still good for is multiple time departures but I'm sure I can figure that out with another airline.

Do not touch them. We had constant IT issues which we kept being told were resolved, but they weren’t. The transition through the US document I was sent just before travelling wouldn’t let me log in, so we wouldn’t have been able to transition through and our passport numbers were missing, which had been highlighted to them twice directly speaking with the airline. Twice we were told it was sorted, but on checking in online they still weren’t there so we were not able to check in. We had previously tried adding them ourselves, but were unable to. Just nothing IT seeks to work. We therefore had to pull out of our trip at the last minute because of their IT. How can we travel if we can’t check-in or transition through? Their fault not ours. We had booked seats disappear too. How if speaking directly to the airline twice still didn’t sort the issues were they ever going to be sorted. They are refusing to accept responsibility or any refund/compensation. If you complain they just thank you for contacting them and look forward to welcoming you aboard again! I’m told I’ve been called but that’s a blatant lie. No one has called me I just get emails apologising and basically admitting fault but no compensation and then tell me they have found a resolution! They have ruined a trip of a lifetime we’ll never afford again. I’d wanted to visit Costa Rica for nine years and we were using some money from inheritance from my late mother. It’s completely wasted and we’ll never be able to afford another big trip. I wonder how anyone who works for American Airlines sleeps at night. If you want an airline that has IT that works avoid this one at all costs.

Unfortunately, my overall experience with this airline continues to decline, and my most recent trip was yet another reminder of how far service standards have fallen. On this trip, I encountered an agent at check-in who enforced a payment rule that had never been brought up in over five years of consistent travel. While the agent may have been correct, the way the situation was handled felt unnecessarily cold and dismissive. There was no effort to listen, no flexibility, and certainly no kindness in the interaction. More broadly, I’ve grown increasingly frustrated by how often I experience delays with American, as well as the recurring sense that staff are indifferent at best and actively unpleasant at worst. For the price of flying with this airline—including extra fees for pets or baggage—I expect a higher level of service and professionalism. Sadly, it’s become clear that American Airlines is not consistent in their customer care. Each experience feels like a gamble—sometimes decent, but too often frustrating. As a paying customer who has remained loyal for years, it’s disappointing to feel like that loyalty is not returned.

We were scheduled to depart at 7:24 AM and were planning on getting to the airport two hours early. It was scheduled to arrive back at our home airport at 2:30 PM. At 3:20 AM my phone woke me with a message stating the flight had been delayed until 9:43 AM. There was no mention of showing up at the original time. We chose to sleep in one hour and then at 6:50 AM my phone said the plane was now loading and had been switched back to 7:24 AM departure. We tried to hurry, but did not have enough time to get through security. The staff said we should have shown up at the original time because this happens all the time. They offered a flight to Harrisburg scheduled to arrive after midnight and then we would still have to rent a car and drive two hours to get home. My wife and I decided to rent a car and drive 10 hours home instead of waiting. The AA staff insisted on giving us the Harrisburg tickets without telling us that this would negate their legal responsibility to refund our money. This was unethical and should be illegal. I hope people read this complaint and learn about their greedy and unethical business practices.

Multiple delays after they cancelled our first flight. Hours of waiting in the airport with young children. Multiple people missed their connecting flight already and we have a few minutes to get to ours.
They also kept changing gates 3 three times. And even after when I were arrived, they delayed gain. I'm never using this airline again.

I quit using American for years bc of their poor service and it’s not gotten better. They have trouble boarding customers & it’s worse trying to get off the plane. Delayed flights and missed connections and they don’t care. Horrible agents at gates. I will never be flying American again.

They delayed the flight original flight from tulum and forced us to check in bags saying there was no space in the plane. (When we boarded the plane multiple spaces were available), so us and a lot of other missed the connecting flight to Vancouver because we only had 40 minutes to go through security.  We given a very cheap and filthy hotel. They only gave $12 for food and rebooked us the following day in the evening and they took our luggage so we had nothing but the clothes on our back. The following day we came and they delayed the flight multiple times, as soon as we sat in the plane they canceled the flight and did not give a hotel or anything and again rebooked us in the evening for the following day. We had to get our own hotel, new clothes etc. finally came back to the airport for them to delay the flight again multiple times and now currently we are stuck in the airplane for the past hour waiting for them to put luggage into the plane so we can leave. Pilot is annoyed as well.

JFK on June 25 2025 was a pain to get to and was insanely busy. There was at least 40 minutes of traffic on the road to the airport. Our flight departed at 9pm, we arrived to JFK at 6pm. We used a rental car and dropped it off in the rental car lot and went on the air train. We checked in at t8 and security was hell and chaotic. We got out at approximately 7:08 and had 45 mins to spare. It seemed like JFK was absurdly busy. I got on American’s new and modern Boeing 787-9. Seat was nice but a little stiff and cramped but it is okay because United is even worse on their 777-200. The inflight entertainment had all of the up-to-date movies and all of the Harry Potter movies. The status said that we would land at 7:30pm IST.  We took off at 10:12pm and will land at 9:02pm in Delhi. The meals were solid, they ran out of non-veg but it is okay cuz I am vegetarian. They gave us three meals. The cabin crew was fantastic.

Flight was rerouted due to poor weather in Dallas, so we landed in Houston. It took them 1 1/2 hours to let us off the plane. Then told us to meet at the customer service desk which we waited another hour for someone to show up. So by the time we got a hotel voucher they were all taken. My family and I had to sleep in the airport just to catch another flight at 11pm the next day. Poor customer service, very unprepared, and no one was knowledgeable what so ever at the job.

review_header: "not being able to us the Admiral lounge"
review_text: I could not believe it. I used American Airlines 100 times to south America pre pandemic but not once since. Now I remember why.

Main Cabin Extra provides plenty of legroom and is now our cabin of choice when flying domestically. Connecting to inflight WiFi was very easy with a good selection of movies, music and live tv. Flight crew was very pleasant providing friendly and efficient service.

I hadn't received real id in the mail yet so I canceled my flight out. Ok that one's on me. Caught a train to Chicago instead. Upon checking my return flight realized without my knowledge or consent they had cancelled my return ticket also. They say this is policy. What policy? I did not cancel my return ticket. They did.

Garbage customer service, zero services for international flights, 24+ hours stranded in London without a hotel voucher, meal voucher, or rebooked flight after they delayed me over 4 hours to make me miss my connection. Instead of getting me home they booked me an extra layover and an extra 12 hours because upgrading is against their policy. Truly the single worst airline in USA. By a landslide. Garbage. Would rate negative numbers if possible

The first flight was delayed by hours and at the time of boarding my first flight I was told that my second flight was canceled all together without any explanation. I had to spend a night at my connection airport terminal, No hotel or meals were provided and after that I was downgraded to economy even though I did pay for business class for both flights. I had no idea AA was such a terrible airline. Makes me wander how an airline with such a terrible service, including cabin service and food can stay in business. From now on I will be avoiding AA at all cost. AA never again.

We boarded our flight, then were suddenly asked to deboard around 6:00 PM. We were told the delay would be short—no more than two hours. As someone with a connecting flight in Dallas, I immediately asked about rebooking options. Gate agents only helped international passengers at first, and then just whoever happened to get in line—so much for prioritizing connecting flights. There was a 7:45 PM flight to Dallas available, but we were never moved to it. By the time we realized they weren’t helping others with connections, we joined a painfully slow-moving line. The gate agents were overwhelmed and clearly inexperienced. When we finally spoke to someone (around 9:00 PM), the flight had already been fully cancelled. Then came the cascade of failures: No hotel accommodations, despite American’s own policy promising coverage when a disruption is their fault. No rental cars, since they were fully booked due to the weekend. -The airport closed for the night—lights off, no staff, no food, no pillows or blankets. Dozens of passengers slept on hard plastic chairs near baggage claim. No alternate flights. We were rebooked for the next day, but the flight kept getting pushed back. By midnight, the earliest available option was 5:00 PM,with two connections and downgraded seats. We were looking at more than 24 hours stuck in an airport with no help and no certainty. We ended up having to book new flights on Delta—out-of-pocket—at a cost of over $1,600, just to get home. Delta was on time and professional. American, on the other hand, is now refusing to reimburse those costs. All we’ve received is an apology and a refund for the flight we never even got to fly — nothing more. Let me be absolutely clear: This was not weather-related. This was 100% an operational failure. The largest airline in the U.S. couldn’t source a backup plane from one of its many nearby hubs? There were no contingency plans? This tire issue should have been caught through routine maintenance. They made no attempt to send a replacement aircraft, reroute passengers, or offer meaningful assistance of any kind. Per American’s own Contract of Carriage and DOT regulations, they are required to provide hotel accommodations, rebooking assistance (including on other carriers), and meal vouchers for controllable delays. I was handed one meal voucher after the airport food services had already closed. The fact that a company of this size had no plan, no backup resources, and no empowered staff is beyond frustrating, it's inexcusable. We were left with no food, no hotel, no flight, and not even the courtesy of a blanket. Just a canned apology email and a refund for a service they failed to deliver. This wasn’t just inconvenient. It was negligent. American Airlines failed to uphold their obligations and left dozens of paying customers stranded. If this is how they handle something as simple as a tire issue, I can’t imagine how they’d respond in an actual emergency. Avoid American Airlines at all costs. You are truly on your own when things go wrong. I fully intend to pursue every channel available to recover these expenses!

Having to arrive 2 hours early made it a 5 hour wait. Very little communication by the airline staff. The ground crew appeared lazy and very slow. When we finally took off we were told it was a weather delay by the captain. During the flight, they had no cabin service due to what they said were dangerous turbulence. However, we had hardly any turbulence during the whole flight. I was given some pretzels by a flight attendant even though there was no service, but I had to ask. We arrived in Dallas very late, and I should have missed my connecting flight even though I had a 2 hour layover built in. The connecting flight was also a 2 hour delay from its original time. It ended up that I still had to run from one end the airport to another end because Dallas is so spread out. Terminal E to C is a long way even when using the skylink. Fortunately the Dallas to KC flight was also very late (great job American), and I made the connection, barely, but my luggage did not make it. The Dallas to KC flight was fine, but it was fully packed with crying babies and unhappy travelers. I didn't know my bags didn't make the connection until all the luggage was finished at the baggage claim area. I went to the American luggage claim person in KC who was less than helpful and not pleasant at all. The lady directed me to scan a code outside her office and make a bag claim. She gave me no direction with how to do the claim, and said it was self explanatory. It wasn't! She did tell me my bags were stuck in Dallas and didn't make the connection. Total frustration. After getting home at 3 am, I had to go back to the airport in the afternoon to retrieve my bags. When I picked them up, there was no real apology. No offer to compensate me for my troubles. I will never fly American again. From now on, I will fly into Atlanta on Southwest and drive the rest of the way...just to avoid American Airlines.
We had to book a second ticket which cost us 28,000 miles. I have asked American Airlines to refund our money but they keep telling me to contact someone else and that they cannot be of any help.

Aircraft was very clean with a friendly flight crew providing the usual no frills service. IFE worked flawlessly with a good selection of movies, live television, TV shows and music. This aircraft had a power port to charge personal devices. The seating on this type of aircraft is 2x2. Surprisingly, there was more legroom in economy than on bigger aircraft meaning there was no need to upgrade to premium economy as I normally do for bigger aircraft. Overall, an enjoyable flight on the regional jet.

review_header: "refused to reimburse for the destroyed luggage"
review_text: Upon arrival, we walked about 3 blocks at Ezeiza Airport with our damaged luggage. Two agents verified that the bag was destroyed. We spent 20 minutes completing the forms at the airport. We then uploaded more forms and documents, pictures included, online. We were requested to send pictures several times. We were requested to submit a receipt for an item purchased over a year ago. They declined to pay since we did not have the receipt. They are so unprofessional in handling bags, and then they do not accept the liability I opened a case at DOT, and they started to call me and email me. All they want is to push you to give up the claim.

My wife and I will NEVER EVER fly American Airlines Charlotte to London on this 777-200R. The seats are so short you cannot get your neck on the neckrest without sliding right forward - but there is no leg room to do this. The headrest only adjusts upwards about an inch which doesn’t help. My wife could barely touch the ground with her feet and kept sliding off. Neither of us slept at all and my neck is agony. Just appalling.

review_header: "Somewhat of a slap in the face"
review_text: I know that I am delusional. However, on a recent trip, I had booked travel on American Airlines, through no fault of my own, and admitted errors on their part, I was forced to spend 8 hours in DFW, rerouted to Charlotte, to spend the night to catch a flight the next day to my destination. I was not offered a hotel voucher. I spent about $284 for hotel and lost $600 in condo costs missing a night stay. I reached out to AA the following is what I received. They could have offered travel credit or something, however, they didn't use these words, but basically "too bad." Somewhat of a slap in the face. "Hello Mr. xxxx: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me. I appreciate you sharing your perspective. Again, on behalf of all of us here at American Airlines, I am very sorry to hear about your experience on flight AA 1168. I can certainly appreciate your request for your hotel expense to be fully reimbursed. However, when situations occur that prevent us from getting our customers to their destinations as planned, we have a plan in place to help minimize inconvenience, which includes providing arrangements at hotels with which we have agreements. If we can't, we'll provide reimbursement for reasonable and approved hotel costs. In this case, the rate for Charlotte is $100.  We appreciate your AAdvantage loyalty very much, Mr. xxxx, and hope to have the opportunity to welcome you on board another American Airlines flight.  Sincerely,  Customer Relations American Airlines."

Flight departed on time. Boarding at the Athens airport was weird; our flight group / gate was sectioned off into a walled section. We only had to show boarding pass once to "get in", but it was awkward leaving the area to do anything outside of that walled off section. As I had a toddler, he wanted to run in and out 1000 times. The staff was very courteous but it was still not ideal. In flight staff was ok, not the friendliest, not the worst. Food was abysmal. Truly hard to remember the last time I had such inedible meals (an issue with food prep skill and not the actual food ingredients). By the time "breakfast" rolled around, I was wishing I had Lufthansa food and that's saying something.

Our flight was delayed coming into Charlotte and we missed our connecting flight to Augusta. Tia went above and beyond in assisting my family to make the best of the situation. If there is any way you can thank her and provide any recognition that would be great.
1 had an engine failure, and the other had undisclosed issues. Plane was supposed to take off at 758, and it is now 1109PM. Still sitting on the plane with no answers.

My recent experience on a flight from LAX to Charlotte was hands-down one of the worst travel experiences I've ever endured—and I’ve traveled enough to know what “bad” looks like. The flight was delayed for 7 HOURS, and throughout the entire ordeal, American Airlines showed a complete lack of organization, professionalism, and basic human decency. There was no clear communication about the delay, just a series of vague announcements and shifting gate changes. Even more infuriating was their refusal to offer any form of compensation—no meal vouchers, no miles, not even a genuine apology. This wasn’t weather-related, and it wasn’t an act of God. This was sheer incompetence from a company that clearly no longer cares about its passengers. Delays happen—but the utter lack of contingency planning or customer care was nauseating. Avoid American Airlines at all costs if you value your time, your money, or your sanity. There are too many other carriers who actually respect their customers.

While I was waiting to be boarded, there was an announcement that they needed volunteers to give up the seat. I went to the desk and told them that I am willing to give my seat. After some minuets I was told they no longer needed seats. I boarded and they announced that they needed three seats. I volunteered again. The reason was that the flight was delayed, and I have a femurs thrombosis in my leg, and I did not want to stay seated for a longer time. They again did not consider my request even though I am a senior and have a medical issue but accommodated three other passengers. The flight was delayed about 1hrs and 30 min. I sent a complaint, and I received only a response acknowledging the email. No refund, nothing.

There were no reasonable efforts made to make sure I have enough information or time to change my itinerary to catch this flight. I left all my contacts when booking the original flights, they could have called or text me, but only an email was received and it just told me my flight was rebooked, only in the fine print details it mentioned a different airport. I arrived to the airport the original flight was supposed to departure from like an idiot, only for the check in clerk to be sarcastic at me telling me the flight has already left from the other airport. I tried to make rearrangement online or get a refund but they made it almost impossible to get support without an AAdvantage account.  You will pay the price for a mainstream carrier, but get the reliability and service quality worse than a budget carrier like Spirit Airlines. It is objectively the worse airline all around.
This level poor maintenance is preposterous. Poor concept for customer concerns, connection etc

There was no weather in NYC, OKC, or on the east coast to Oklahoma, no matter the route of the place. However, our flight was cancelled claiming weather even though no other flights leaving NYC or arriving at OKC from American Airlines were cancelled that day. No other flights arriving at OKC from any airlines were cancelled. When American Airlines re-booked us, it was on a flight to Dallas/Fort Worth with a 9 hour overnight layover with a flight to OKC the next morning. No hotel accommodations were offered or provided. When I called to ask about cancelled the layover and requested a rental car I was told we would get a refund. However, when I requested for the refund, I was told they do not give refunds for weather related cancellations. I am confident this flight was cancelled due to low passenger numbers and not weather. We have used AA for a long time but will not be returning as this is ridiculous. Not only did they take a substantial amount of our time away from us, we also spent nearly $200 more on a rental car to drive home, otherwise we would have had to sleep outside the airport as security was closed and our luggage was outside security. AA needs to do better.

It was never great (late flights, surly attendants and desk agents) but it was convenient and I have status. That all stopped about 4 months ago. I flew maybe 30-40 times per year. For the last 2 years that has included about 26 flights per year (IAH-dfw-cou) RT. With advance notice the flights typically cost $300-350 RT. About 4 months ago, the price jumped overnight to $1,000-1200 or more. Unless there is no alternative, I will never fly AA again, regardless of status.

Hand carriage need to be checked on all three flights during boarding process. Ok for me on the 2 smaller aircrafts, but in the B-737 there was plenty of space in the overhead bins. Service was ok for the short flights. Non alcoholic beverages have been served free of charge. Seat space was ok for short flights. Baggage claim was uncomplicated. For the flight ECP to ORD via CLT the transit time was only 40 minutes and this was definately a hassle in CLT as it was a long way in a cramped airport and i made it last minute to the gate for connection flight. I already worried if my luggage would made it as well, but to my surprise i got in Chicago, good job. What make me more surprised was security on the plane. Nobody cares that window blind have been open during take off and landing and also back rests havent been in upright position. I am a frequent flyer and i never experience any airlines breaking this rules. Therefore the cabin staff get only 1 point and i also could not recommend this airline as safety should be first priority.

I asked for them to change her to a flight traveling to Lehigh Valley vs. Newark to forego any unforeseen problems. Due to her flight being a basic economy, I was told no. I asked to speak to a manager, was given one, then told managers above that level don't accept phone calls. The absolute unwillingness to help an 88 year old woman, and the complete lack of customer service has turned me off to AA forever. We will never fly this airline again.

Our Friday evening flight was delayed from 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM, pushing our arrival to 1:30 AM—well past our car rental pickup window. Since my wife had plans to stay with her aunt, we accepted American’s offer to reschedule for a 9:00 AM flight the next morning. We rearranged our entire trip—appointments, schedules, everything—around that new plan. Then, without warning, the morning flight was delayed again… to 5:00 PM. At that point, the entire purpose of our trip was ruined. We had to cancel everything, and now there’s absolutely no reason to even go. American Airlines completely derailed our plans, wasted our time, and left us with zero confidence in their ability to manage or communicate effectively. This was our last time flying with you. Never again.

Was delayed by about an hour. Got to DFW late for connecting flight. That got delayed and then canceled, rebooted delayed canceled, rebooted, delayed canceled, rebooted again and still wound up having to stay in DFW for over 12 HOURS. Got told that they don't do refunds, which is actually against their own published policy. Basically, a 5 and a half hour total time flight turned into a 17 +/- hour long flight.
