While I was left stranded at DFW, I witnessed several other flights being canceled for various reasons.

The agents basically shut the doors in my face and were not helpful, kind or understanding. The situation required me to get on the most immediate flight on any airline that would get me there as soon as possible. Eventually, I was given a flight credit but American Airline did not explain the short nature of the credit and never sent a courtesy email or anything. Now I find out they have erased my credit. I don't expect the airline to care enough about me to do anything so flying American would bring up many bad feelings and memories.

That is – unless you’re flying with American Airlines from LAX to JFK. If so, make sure to fly on their direct flight with an Airbus A321 aircraft that was specifically designed and configured for these transcontinental flights. In fact, it has it’s on aircraft type – an A321T (the T stands for Transcontinental). First Class is a separate cabin at the font of the aircraft. Here you’ll find 10 individual first-class open suite - 5 rows with one on either side so each has windows and direct aisle access. This was quite a surprise for a single aisle narrow body jet. There was one dedicated flight attendant for all 10 passengers so kept pretty busy for the entire flight. He was bright and attentive. The breakfast meal was a pretty average affair but my expectations were low based on the airline’s reputation. The seat converts to a full lay-flat bed and was very comfortable and with fluffy pillows and blanket. I fell asleep easily and slept well for a few hours and woke to the smell of cookies being freshly baked in the forward galley. This was a nice touch and something the flight attendant clearly enjoyed doing. The wait for the luggage to arrive at the belt was particularly long and stressful when you are getting constant phone calls from your driver to check if it’s arrived.

This review refers only to American Airlines telephone customer service; before my return trip next week I needed to ask AA something concern my flight. The local number that I had is disconnected and no new number provided. Consequently I had to make a long distance overseas call for which I was billed long distance telephone charges that lasted almost fifteen minutes before the AA representative was able to give a local number which was not disconnected.

review_header: "one of the worst flights I’ve had"
review_text: They had removed the cover off a rather large panel and were pushing buttons and muttering. My suspicions were confirmed when there was no safety video and they did it the old fashioned way with the crew standing in the aisle with an oxygen mask in one hand and a life vest around their necks. However, they didn’t say a word about it to the passengers until we were in the air and well on our way to Sydney. I guess they figured the reaction of learning you faced 15 hours without movies, music or games would be less in the air than on the ground. Well, at least I could enjoy the leisurely pace of the first class meal service; so I thought. But clearly the 2 male flight attendants looking after the first class cabin had better things to do. The service was practically over before it began. The courses came so fast I could barely keep up and the food was terrible. All in all it was one of the worst flights I’ve had in years and the 2 guys looking after first class should retire and pass the mantle to someone less jaded.
Chance and Erico were fantastic, spectacular service and took great care of us.

We had a flight that was suppose to depart at 8:06AM leaving from Norfolk with a connection in Philadelphia then on to Boston arriving around 10:30-11am. We were at the Norfolk airport at 7am waiting for our flight to board when the 1st delay was announced for 2 hours. We went up to the ticket counter and the agent was able to rebook us on a different connecting flight only delaying us about 2 hours. The second delay of 6 hours was announced about an hour before the second boarding was suppose to happen. And the announcement was to call American customer service to rebook again. I did call customer service and was rebooked on a different flight going to Laguardia airport and we had to wait 3 hours for this flight to depart. This short flight on a smaller plane was extremely turbulent on the last half and my daughter and I were so nauseated and exhausted. The layover in Laguardia was another 2-3 hours. At least Laguardia had a nice food court and we were able to sit and have lunch. The flight to Boston was uneventful.  I am very disappointed in the delays and handling of passengers by American Airlines. This delay should have been called much earlier. They announced it was due to mechanical issues. Why not inspect the planes more frequently and cancel flights at least 6-8 hours before the flight departs if any issues. That way passengers can be rebooked and notified ahead of time. And if this does happen last minute airlines should be required to offer cash or gift card or something. It was a horrible experience and day and one I will never forget. I plan on never flying with American again. And I will be letting my friends and family know what a bad experience this was so that this does not happen to them. I was not the only angry and disappointed passenger. I overheard other passengers stating this happens alot with American airlines,

Each one has been delayed over 5 hours for mechanical problems. When you contact American Airlines they don't care they just blow you off. They don't care that they're delaying you missing appointments and connections.

review_header: “may as well be a greyhound station”
review_text: I was issued a new ticket that required me to be stranded in Phoenix Arizona for 11 hours. I was originally supposed to arrive at my destination (Minneapolis) at 2:14 pm. My 6 hour trip turned into an all day event. Also, I just got word that my flight to Phoenix is, once again, delayed. I spent a lot of money for this trip... this may as well be a greyhound station.

C. (DCA) to Philadelphia (PHL) with American Eagle, operated by PSA Airlines, was smooth and efficient. We experienced a minor maintenance delay, but on a 27-minute flight, it hardly made a difference. The crew was pleasant and professional, ensuring a comfortable experience. The aircraft, a CRJ-900, is the largest in PSA’s fleet, offering a bit more space compared to their other planes. Given the short duration of the flight, there’s really nothing to complain about it was a quick, easy, and well-handled trip. Great job PSA!

We were extremely pleased traveling home on this plane. This was mainly due to Flight Attendant DeJon. DeJon made sure we were comfortable, asked us what drinks we wanted, and served us snacks and a very nice lunch. Mostly, he was so congenial and I could see he was working so hard taking care of the passengers. My Husband and I are seniors and I can honestly say that we very much appreciated DeJon. It made our flight enjoyable, and we were glad we flew with American Airlines.

Louis and Chicago to meet up with friends for a vacation flight out of Chicago. There was impending weather, snow. I changed my flight on February 12 in the evening to 3:10 in the afternoon in order to get to Chicago in time for the next morning flight. I had to pay an additional $188 to change the flight. The flight was cancelled by the airline and I ended up on the same flight I was originally booked on! That flight was delayed but I did get to Chicago late Wednesday night. They refused to reimburse me for the extra amount paid for the cancelled flight! I should not have had to pay that fee when they cancelled the flight! On the way back to St. Louis there was potential weather. However, our flight from Mexico got into O'Hare with no problem. But my flight from Chicago to St. Louis had been delayed earlier that morning and there were no flights out of O'Hare (according the the RUDE American Airlines person) so I had to either sit in the airport for 13 hours or pay for a room - they refused to get me a room! They claimed weather as an excuse but there was no weather they had just tried to out-guess it and got it wrong. So I had to pay for a room, my bag again the next day because it couldn't be transferred, an extra day of parking and an extra day of care for my pet - $309! No customer service. Their supervisor was also uncaring and rude. I ended up falling on an escalator trying to get my bags around by myself due to them!!

Still no guarantee it will take off. Had to buy blankets, $60, and kids sleeping on the disgustingly dirty floor. Trying to get to a family member before they pass. How can you stay in business with this poor customer service? Your company needs a major overhaul. Someone has to be held accountable.

review_header: "forced us to give up the luggage"
review_text: The online check-in didn’t work and the airport check-in experience was super complicated and took 1.5h so we almost missed our flight. My partner & I were assigned separate seats even though we were on the same booking. The agents there were very accommodating and were doing their best given the system restrictions. Apparently, the system didn’t recognize that we were only transiting in India and needed us to submit a visa for India which is not needed for transit. The agents specifically told us that it’s good that we didn’t bring checked luggage because we cannot leave the transit area. The agents at the gate forced us to give up the luggage under the premise that we would receive them directly when we exit the plane. There was lots of space on the plane to put carry-on luggage. Upon arrival, of course, our luggage was not there and the New Delhi staff told us we needed to pick up the luggage at the belt. So now, we can‘t receive the luggage and have been stuck at the airport for 2h at this point and missed our connecting flight while they‘re trying to figure out the situation. Also, our initial AA flight was 2h delayed as well. No food vouchers or any other compensation offered. Better communication and coordination among their teams would be appreciated for an airline that calls itself American Airlines.

review_header: "no desire to fly with them again"
review_text: Both flights, DFW to Miami and Miami to St Thomas were through American Airlines. Out flight from DFW to Miami was delayed by 2 hours due to mechanical failure, and all passengers were put on a different plane. The new flight landed in Miami 10 minutes before our connecting flight (Miami to St Thomas) took off, but American couldn't delay their flight 5 minutes to allow 9 passengers to make the last connecting flight out of St Thomas. So basically, we were stuck in Miami for the night and were booked on the first flight (8:30 am) the next morning. We were offered a hotel voucher at a cheap airport hotel; which was a far cry from the beach front resort that we had purchased (priced by the hotel at $620/night). My wife and I also had checked the bags with all of our clothes, so we didn't have a change of clothes until we reached our destination (St Thomas). On the next day we reached arrived at our gate early, but were told that our flight had been delayed due to weather and that we would be flying out 7 hours later. We later found out that this was a lie, and that really the cause for delay was that an emergency landing had been made on St Thomas' only landing strip, and that an hour and a half cleanup of the landing strip was required. All other airlines resumed flights within 2 hours. So, we spent another 7 hours in the airport waiting for our flight. All-in we spent 24 hours stuck in Miami without a change of clothes, most of it spent in the airport, when a 5-miute delay of one flight (that was on time) could have solved their own failure entirely. American Airlines' first attempt at compensation was to offer my wife and I 2500 aa points each. If you figure those points are worth about $0.01, then the total value of their compensation was $50 = 2 x 0.01 x 2500. After writing them an email explaining that I am prepared to take them to small claims court, they offered me and my wife each $100 travel vouchers. After I denied again, they offered us each $150 travel vouchers. After I denied again, they apologized but said there was no other offer. I also asked how much money American made on the sale of our seats, and they said the representative said he didn't know. Basically, American Airlines believes they are entitled to screw you over and doesn't care to compensate you for damages whatsoever. Not only that, everyone of their agents (rebooking/gate) are entitled and have a terrible attitude. Personally, I have no desire to fly with them again as any trust in this company's capacity to conduct honest business has been eviscerated.

There is an issue with delays, maintenance, forced rebooking, sitting on the taxiway both prior to takeoff and after, at least 80% of the time. It is not an exaggeration. It's mind blowing how they are never held accountable for terrible service and especially at the prices they charge. Too many times I've found myself in a dead sprint in the airport (Phoenix, Charlotte, Dallas, Philidelphia) trying to make my gate because of this poorly run business.

Legroom was excellent. The hard product is very good. The soft product is abysmal and food is unacceptable. Communication is poor. The staff is truly detached from their customers. Not just the flight attendants, but the gate agents and counter personnel. It seems like they don’t want to be at their job jobs. So detached that when we landed in Madrid, the purser welcomed us to Paris, France. I almost always fly British Airways. This time a segment was on American. Never again.

First flight was delayed, forcing me to not walk but sprint to my connection which was on the total opposite side of the airport. And when I arrived at the ticket scanning desk, was met with an extremely rude attendant who gave me quite the attitude when she clearly saw that I was huffing and puffing in order to make this connection. She made me check my small suitcase at the gate because it “wasn’t gonna fit” in overhead storage. Meanwhile there was plenty of overhead space upon entering plane. This is important to remember for later. The second flight was fine, but after landing, made my way over to baggage claim after being met with, again, a very rude and dismissive agent who informed me that they put my suitcase with all the other large checked bags. Well, now I have been waiting at baggage claim 9 at JFK for over an hour with no sight of any suitcases. Not mine, not anyone’s! And quite honestly this is not what I needed after an exhausting work trip on a Saturday evening. I have serious beef with you American Airlines and will not be using you ever again.

First you oversold the flight (again), which caused my wife and I to be the last two ticketed passengers for the flight despite the fact I purchased the tickets over 3 months prior and attempted to check in early. And while we barely made the flight, it caused a significant amount of stress to ourselves and our traveling party since we were the trip leaders of our group. Then you made us check our carry on baggage (which had become a common problem with AA for us), which caused additional problems at our layover since my wife had put her passport in her carry on. And when we finally were able to board, we discovered that there was plenty of room for more carry ons (one overhead bin was completely empty, plus other spaces). On our return flight, we were again required to check our carry on baggage and upon boarding found there was, again, plenty of remain space for bags. This made us run tight for our layover coming back to the US and required us to wait FORTY-FIVE MINUTES for our "carry on" baggage at our final destination, which was almost a midnight arrival already ( thanks to a 1 hr delay). As icing on the cake, the flight attendants from PUJ to ORD were quite testy with passengers and even each other. Overall, what a fun story to tell my friends. You guys need to change some policies.

review_header: "as if we were nothing but a burden"
review_text: No temperature check, no hydration, not even basic concern. I was left to tend to him, using a cold towel on his head while the crew ignored us.  When I approached them again a crew member rolled their eyes, made a face, and sarcastically muttered, “Oh, perfect. What do you need now?”. A high fever in a pressurized cabin is a serious concern, yet they acted as if we were nothing but a burden. They handed out meals with no regard for meal preferences and both times, I ended up with nothing because they ran out of choices.  I repeatedly asked for hot water for my husband. One crew member said, “I don’t have it on the cart.” Another promised to bring it but never came back. Yet this same crew member walked past my seat multiple times, ignoring me. The crew on this flight were rude, dismissive, and downright incompetent.  This was, the most emotionally draining, physically exhausting 14 hours of my life.

He was our flight attendant from Fayetteville Regional Airport while on our way to Hawaii.  He was exceptionally lovely, fun, and caring! This tiny plane flight went from Fayettville to Charlotte, and even with the flight being so short, he gave us water. I am pregnant and he was extra caring for me to give me water and pretzels to help with the nausea. Thank you Kimo for being such a great part of my flight experience!

Customer service atrocious. Check in was nice that’s all, but boarding attendants and flight attendants were the rudest people I’ve ever encountered. Not family oriented. Seems like they tried to make my trip harder with a toddler. Everything seemed like a bother. Asking us if we wanted a drink or snack annoyed them. Literally if you dislike people and want to ruin someone’s day apply to American Airlines.

The flight was missed due to mechanical issues. The surly gate agent issuing my ticket for a later flight informed me that although I was not in an exit row seat or Premium Economy, the price difference would be refunded. She lied. This never happened and when contacting customer service I was denied a refund. This is not the first time I’ve had issues with this paltry excuse for an airline. Delayed flights are standard as is a subpar onboard experience, including their onboard entertainment never working. In short, I will avoid flying them if there are any other airline options and would encourage others to do the same.

Charlotte airport easy to manage, easy check in and fast security line. Admirals Club available but not as good as the premiere lounges in NYC and MIA. Boarding on time, by groups. Once on board, crew nice but nothing special, seat very comfortable for PE, nice amenity kit. Service ok, hot towel to start with, then drinks and dinner. All in nice served and well managed by crew. IFE very good selection. Manage +4 hrs of sleep on a 7hr flight, so really good. Did not have breakfast since I was sleeping, no comment on that. Recommend this airline.

My husband's knees we against the seat in front of him for the entire flight. The plane was late, then we sat on the runway in Miami for 2 hours waiting to taxi. The ac didn't function properly. Heat was blowing out for 1 hr of the flight ... when it is 80 degrees outside. The flight attendants were very helpful during a medical issue, which was truly a blessing. Everything else was horrendous.

Gate changed 2 times and delayed 4 times causing us to miss our connecting flight and now we have to wait 18 hours for the next one with no access to checked baggage so no clothes and toiletries. Nearly every flight around us was expecting delays. Had a timer saying boarding in 15 mins when plane had not even arrived in the terminal yet. What's the point of timers if you're just going to lie. Not just the delays were the issue, the service desk only had 1 person working with a line of 15 people waiting due to multiple delays. Horrible service, will never fly with them again. This was our 4th flight this month have flown delta, united and Alaska airlines and all were so much better.

Boarding process was speedy, and we found ourselves very lucky as there were only 57 passengers on board allowing everyone to spread around the aircraft and have the chance to lie down for what turned out to be a longer than usual, 8 hour 15 minutes flight. Soon after take-off the crew came by with a hot meal, with a choice of either vegetarian pasta or a rice and chicken dish. I opted for the latter and it was surprisingly delicious. Around 2 hours before landing the crew came around again to hand some ice cream, and then they serviced us one more time shortly before landing to give everyone a hot pocket. The cabin crew were very nice and attentive, and throughout the whole flight walked around the cabin to ensure everyone was comfortable. Overall, quite happy with my experience and will fly American Airlines again in the future if I have the opportunity.

Even though my tickets were nonrefundable, they worked with me to either change my flights for free or issue a full credit or refund. Their customer service demonstrated genuine care for their customers and valued loyalty. American Airlines, on the other hand, has shown me exactly why I will never book with them again. I found myself in an awkward situation needing to cancel a non-refundable flight that was meant to be a gift. Rather than allowing the full credit to be transferred to the recipient, American Airlines deducted the $99 cancellation fee from the credit (per their policy)—a fee that amounts to nearly half the cost of the original ticket. Instead of showing even the smallest amount of understanding, American Airlines rigidly clung to its policy, offering no meaningful assistance. The $99 fee has effectively diminished the value of what was supposed to be a thoughtful gift. This experience has not only been disappointing but feels needlessly punitive. I want to be clear: this situation wasn’t entirely within my control. I didn’t choose to book with American Airlines, nor was I the one to purchase the group flights without considering refundability. (We have a group of 15 with all flights booked at once by someone in the group who was trying to help out.) Yet somehow, I’m the one penalized because American Airlines refuses to provide flexibility in situations that clearly call for some level of human empathy. For context, I travel frequently—4 to 5 domestic trips per month for work—and I’ve been researching airline credit cards to decide which one best fits my needs as a frequent flyer. This may have been an inexpensive This may have been an inexpensive, leisurely trip, but with my business expense card, I'm enabled to travel business class for 3 to 6 trips per month. I can say with certainty that I will not be choosing American Airlines. This experience has solidified my preference for other airlines that consistently prioritize customer service, loyalty, and common sense. To anyone reading this, I urge you to think carefully before booking with American Airlines. There are plenty of other carriers that offer better customer service and greater flexibility when “life happens.” American Airlines may not care about losing a customer like me, but if they’re wondering why they don’t command the loyalty of frequent travelers, this situation should provide some insight. Goodbye, American Airlines. You’ve lost not just one potential loyal customer but also my trust and recommendation.

The flight from Sydney was fantastic with a great and attentive crew, excellent food and a super comfortable ly-flat bed. Took so long for the luggage that I barely made my connecting flight to New York. Domestic First Class seats on the A321 are a bit claustrophobic and not so comfortable - only 1 flight attendant for 10 pax but he tried his best and the food was average. SYD to LAX = 9/10 LAX to JFK = 6/10

review_header: "last time we will be flying American"
review_text: Every flight I took on this trip was delayed. We have tried to give them another chance but this is the last time we will be flying American.

Croix, now we have to spend the night sleeping on the concrete floor somewhere in San Juan airport until the first flight at 7am. All the hotels in San Juan are fully booked and nothing available. Rotten start to our vacation. Plus they have lost our luggage. This is the second time American Airlines has ruined a vacation leaving me stranded in a strange place

review_header: "refused to allow me to enter Admirals Club"
review_text: While the service was good, I think the food made me sick. I've flown in coach on American and they tiniest, most cramped seats you can imagine. Shame on them for treating people like cattle.

I thought, “Ok, it’s fine; this sometimes happens. This is okay.” Then I put my arm on the armrest and was surprised to see that the entire armrest was covered in duct tape, and I thought to myself, “Duct tape? really?!” If I rent a car, and upon getting in, find the seat is covered with duct tape, I would consider this unacceptable. So, for American Airlines, which has aspirations for excellence. My question is this: Is this acceptable?

On the way there, our flight was delayed, and we just barely got to our other flight in time. then, they lost our checked luggage. the worst part is, we were flying with another airline to another destination in Mexico, and simply couldn't wait. The airline staff was either rude, or they didn't know what they were talking about for our lost luggage. The airline then took 2-4 days to get it back to us, near the end of our trip. they also refused to answer our phone calls to customer service. we sat, on hold, for over 5 hours just for them to hang up. On our way back, we got stranded in DFW and it was American airlines' fault! It was a real hassle due to their truly awful customer service.
She is definitely an asset to the organization.

Avoid American Airlines at all costs. First, they changed our itinerary and forced us to add 3 hours flight time and a 4 hour layover to our trip. Next, our flight was delayed due to mechanical issues with the plane but they wouldn't tell us what was happening they just continued to delay for short periods of time so we couldn't leave the gate area and couldn't make other arrangements. Then they announced a new gate, new aircraft and boarding time and again started announcing delays without explanation. The second plane was eventually taken out of service as unrepairable and a third gate and flight was assigned. This time they let us now the departure time was uncertain because they didn't have a crew (it was Thanksgiving and getting late). We finally got them to agree to change our reservation to another airline with a flight leaving later in the evening and they assured us that they would transfer our baggage because they had over an hour and a half. In total, we spent over thirteen hours in Dallas/Ft. Worth airport, our original 4 hour layover and an additional 9 hour delay. Our arrival in Madrid, originally scheduled for early the next morning ended up being 2:30 in the afternoon and we still had to wait for the baggage which, of course, did not make it onto our flight. One whole day in Madrid gone. After i posted a complaint with American Airlines I received one phone message from someone who never returned my phone calls and several apologetic messages without any offers of compensation or resolution. Ultimately they gave me 7500 air miles while they researched my claim and in keeping with their policy of customer neglect, no real satisfaction. I will certainly never fly American again.

Bag 1 Bag 2 Bag 3 To Cuba. $0 / $35*^ $150 / $200**^ $200 They charged $400 for each of us. I have different phone calls and they refused to get back our money. On top of that, last phone call they hang out. On top of that, they left behind a check in bag in miami when returning back, the bag was broken and also refused to pay what it cost. It was a bad experience and I hope I don’t have to travel with them anymore.
They have no manners in speaking with passengers. Very impatient with seniors that required assistance using the totems to check in.

They have no regard for you as a passenger. We are delayed 30 hours and counting. Just as we are preparing for take off on a 15 hour flight, the Captain realizes he is over his hours. Now we sit on the plane and wait for a new Captain? I had a similar experience returning from Peru in August 2024. The most frustrating part is the complete indifference towards the passengers. I was a loyal customer. Now I just hate this company and will do my best to avoid them in the future.

Left New Orleans at 3 am, it is now 8.45pm and still waiting on a delayed flight. 6 of the American Airlines flights are delayed at this time. Will never fly American again, would rather rent a car and drive for days. Will try Delta next time. Pathetic customer service.

Left sitting on the plane for 10 hours with no food and no water. They did not help us find or even offer to help find ways to our destination We lost our once in a lifetime trip, NFL game tickets and hotel. We were given no hotel voucher and no flight home. We were stranded in Dallas, had to rent a car to drive home and pay for our hotel. There is no person you can talk to because they don't have a phone number to even call customer service. I will absolutely never fly AA again.

The stewardess just said I don't know what to tell you. I had noticed way before & asked before we boarded. They just said ok just keep an eye on it. We traveled to NY and on way back our flight was canceled then rescheduled to 3 connecting flights and overlay of 8 hours. We're getting home a day late.

American Airlines has made this whole Christmas Holiday Hell. I can't spend Christmas day with my family because I have to wait for this flight and go to work within an hour after landing. This is my absolute worst flight experience ever!

None of the staff were available until 3:30am. They were very rude to customer, even tho they were the ones that came in and started late. Also, my wife and I are both Active Duty military members and they didn't give us our TSA pre-check even after ID and order verification. I've traveled all over the world and this has to be one of the most poor airport experience I've ever had in my life.

The first connection in Dallas had over a 9 hr delay. Two planes were taken out of service due to mechanical issues. Two flight crews timed out waiting. At 9pm they had found a third plane and were looking for a flight crew that was available. The flight that was to take off at 1:40pm finally took off just before 11pm. Due to the delay my connection in Madrid was rebooked 3 times and ultimately rerouted to Jerez, Spain. There I was to board the cruise at the second port. Due to the delay, rebooked flights and rerouted flight my luggage was lost. I was reunited with it on day 5 of the cruise. American Airlines customer service is mostly nonexistent. For my trouble AA is offering 10000 miles. That is unacceptable!

review_header: "canceled my flight in the middle of the night"
review_text: They did not offer me anything additional for them canceling my flight and leaving me to figure out how to get to back to my home city. Since then I now have to stay an additional night at another hotel before I can get home. No incentive if you want to book with American Airline just know the possibility of being left to check in with another hotel and your flight being canceled on a whim.

Despite a slight delay due to crew staffing, the team handled it with professionalism. Once onboard, we were promptly offered a pre-departure beverage, which was a nice touch. During the flight, which lasted just over an hour, the service was impeccable, with a full-service offering that far exceeded my expectations for a short flight. The captain and flight attendants went out of their way to apologize for the delay, and their politeness and attention to safety stood out. Overall, it was a very positive and enjoyable journey.

19pm and we still in Miami, it's been an hour in the airplane at the gate door, waiting first for mechanical issues and now for pilots, not a voucher, not a refund, or partial refund, nothing is offered to us for wasting our time after charging skyrocket prices for a flight

Upon discovering that my luggage was damaged, I approached the baggage service counter to file a claim. Instead of assisting me, the staff misled me by claiming that claims could only be filed through customer support. They forced me to leave the baggage service area and insisted my bags were not damaged. To make matters worse, a staff member who identified herself as a supervisor used derogatory language and laughed at me. When I contacted customer support the following day, I was informed that claims could be filed at the airport and that the staff should have assisted me if I was unable to use the QR code. Acting on this information, I returned to the airport on July 25, only to face the same unprofessional staff. They not only refused to assist me again but also yelled at me, humiliated me further with derogatory remarks, and denied me the ability to file a claim. Following this incident, I emailed the manager to express my concerns. He assured me that my complaint would be escalated to HR and upper management. However, I have yet to receive a response or see any indication of an investigation into the abusive behavior and refusal of service. This lack of accountability has further eroded my trust in American Airlines. This experience has highlighted the severe inadequacies in American Airlines’ customer service and staff behavior. I would not recommend this airline to anyone. The treatment I endured reflects poorly on their commitment to professionalism, respect, and customer care. I urge potential customers to consider other airlines and avoid American Airlines.

Check in with dog in cabin went extremely smoothly and was actually a pleasant experience. As during lunch hour Terminal 3 in Toronto is fairly empty security control and USA passport control was very quick. Boarding started a few minutes early and was civilized. Experience on board in business class was nice and pleasant. Excellent flight attendant and to my surprise the served lunch was one of the best inflight meals I ever had on this route. Arrival a bit before time and even the checked bag arrived quickly. All in all - could not have been a better experience. All perfect.

As we approached LAX I asked for a wheelchair, and subsequently was taken to the emergency room. I was hospitalized for several days, during which I called American about my reservation. I explained the circumstances and was told they were holding open my reservation (first class from LAX to Phoenix). When I called the next day to rebook, they had no record of my reservation or the conversation. I gave them my ticket number and they found my record but offered absolutely no credit for my original business/first class ticket. They did however offer to sell me a ticket in the main cabin. (I hung up and used my points for a ticket home on Southwest.) This is a terrible excuse for customer service, and I will make a point of avoiding American in the future, even if I have to pay more to a competitor.

However, this trip with American Airlines was a disaster. On the trip out to CA, every plane was late (not a terrible thing). On the trip from Ontario, CA to Pensacola, FL (with a layover in Dallas, TX), the plane in Ontario was on time, but because of an earlier flight that had mechanical troubles, the flight was packed and several of those passengers were stuck for several hours and missed connections. The real problem was at the loading gate in Dallas on the final leg to Pensacola. The gate attendant was arbitrarily picking people out to have their carry-on bags checked to make room on the overhead bins. He singled my backpack out and told me to place it in the device they use to check if it will fit in the bins. My backpack fit, but he still wanted to check it. I argued with him about it as several bags that were obviously larger than mine rolled onto the flight. After removing my computer, the attendant told me I could take the backpack on and hold my computer. I was extremely frustrated by then and while packing up my backpack I mumbled under my breath "dumb ass." The attendant heard this and returned to me and told me I could not board the flight. I apparently hurt his feelings, and he felt that was sufficient to kick me from the flight. I was allowed onto the flight after his supervisor came over but had already called my ride from Pensacola to home to stop them from coming to the airport. I strongly advise avoiding American Airlines if you have to travel through Dallas. The airline has empowered their thin-skinned attendants to ruin your trip for arbitrary reasons. You don't have to pose a danger to the flight.

I placed myself standby on the earlier flight, I checked in early at the airport and was number 2 of 13 passengers. I informed the gate agent she replied 35 minutes before boarding seating would be assigned. American Airlines assigns seating according to the standby list to my dismay she placed me economy in row 32C by the bathroom and gave all the passengers on standby after me premium seating. I did inform her of my premium seating voucher used for my confirmed flight. She lied and said the computer assigns the seating. Upon my return to CLT I asked a reservation agent had American changed their practice on assigning standby seating they replied no therefore it leads me to believe I was discriminated against by this gate agent cause I was African-American. To this review American has failed to give me a reply on the complaint I filed. "American Airlines November 23, 2024 Hello, Thank you for contacting American Airlines Customer Relations. This is an automated acknowledgment letting you know that we received your comments and will be responding shortly. Should you need it, we've included a reference number assigned to your correspondence. It is located at the bottom of this message. You're in good hands Customer Relations is here to help. We're committed to answering every suggestion, inquiry and complaint we receive. We know that you are eager to hear back from us as soon as possible. One of our team members will review and address your comments personally. The review process might require some research therefore we may need some time to respond. We respect your time and will be doing all we can to get back with you as soon as possible - and in no case longer than 30 days. Haven't traveled yet? If you are inquiring about your reservation, please contact Reservations at 800-433-7300. They are available 24 hours a day and are able to answer questions and make routine arrangements for our customers requiring a certain degree of assistance when traveling. We also have an exclusive team of Special Assistance Coordinators who make the necessary arrangements to ensure that travel is comfortable and safe for our customers with special needs. No matter which level of assistance you prefer, our Reservations team can assist you. Calling from outside of the U.S.? Refer to "Worldwide Reservations Phone Numbers" listed on aa.com. Thank you for flying American Airlines. American Airlines Customer Relations"

There was no entertainment but, I was able to watch some movies on my laptop and the movie options were spectacular. There was onboard wifi which was nice, ground service was fast and efficient since a TSA helped us and the check-in guy was very friendly in offering us the boarding pass even though my dad said no, food was very very delicious. Landing/departure in Santa Ana and Miami were very smooth, value for money was over and beyond my expectations. Will fly with them again!

JFK to DFW encountered a storm at DFW and were diverted to a nearby small airport. We did have to sit there for a while, but the storm had caused havoc to all flights. Crew was fine. We got back to DFW around midnight and had to spend the night in a nearby hotel (all very full due to storm, but found one) and booked a flight for the next day - we did this on our own, not through Customer Service (too long a line). At check-in, the agent found a sooner faster flight for us, which was great. Back home, I wrote an email to AA customer service requesting reimbursement for hotel and taxi, which they are not required to due when delays are caused by weather. They wrote back within an hour, apologized for the inconvenience and asked for the receipts. The next day they sent approval and within a few days I received a check for the full amount. I thought they did a great job under the circumstances. The rest of the flight(s) was normal - I don't fly for fine dining nor do I expect anything beyond the normal - older planes a little less fun, newer ones better. So I'm just commenting on the Customer Service which was great.

I came in asking for help with my luggage because I was juggling with a lot of other things (including a baby etc) and this steward said sure but proceed to “air lift” his hands were NOT touching my luggage and said “please leave most of them and I can help after”. After what? After I lift it up myself? Then he proceed to say it’s not in his contract to help. This is not the first time I am appalled at American Airlines attitude. You’re in service industry. If helping is not in your bone go get yourself an office job. Total disgrace and why American airline will NEVER be close to any leading airlines like Emirates, Singapore or Qatar. Please do better and train your staff.

review_header: "the service seems to be dropping rapidly"
review_text: The counter person was announcing the flight and absolutely no one standing nearby could understand what she was saying, either English or Spanish. When the announcement to board came, no one knew whether it was priority, group 1, so everyone just swarmed to board, which meant that priority, group 1 passengers had to wait in line, about 15 minutes snaking down the ramp, to get to row 2. Nothing was offered to drink for business class while waiting to depart, not even water. There are 16 seats in first/business class. The attendant started taking menu choices from the rear row, when she arrived at row 2 there was NO OPTION, there was sea bass. We’re coming from an island where we had fresh fish and lobster for 8 days and we are given fish while heading home. This is inexcusable to not prep enough meals for a 16 section business class. As you can imagine, the sea bass with couscous was underwhelming. The offered dessert was a banana something, and having flown business class for 30 years I can honestly say it was the worst excuse for a dessert offering I have ever had - in appearance, taste, freshness, simply mediocre. Even though business class anymore always seems to be full, these seats are not cheap but the service from out of the US back in seems to be dropping rapidly to a point where it is nothing more than extra legroom. All airlines are pretty much the same, the only step from here is private flights.

I have been united 1k for 4 years, never will recommend American. They reassigned my ticket in front of me, even when I was 15min before departure. Travel on your own risk, get are monopoly you can avoid them I got platinum pro this year, will go back to United

review_header: "go back to airport to stay overnight"
review_text: Rebooked automatically to have us fly to Phoenix and be stranded overnight and take a flight to Portland Wednesday 11/13 in the morning. Flight in Miami delayed again so we would miss our rebooked connecting flight in Miami to phoenix so stranded in Miami overnight. Rebooked flight from Miami to PDX but it is not a nonstop like original, have a layover in Texas. American Airlines Booked us a hotel overnight only to show up and have them tell us there is no rooms available, this forced us to go back to airport to stay there overnight with our two kids. This forced us to pay for an Uber back to the airport. In total we are now going to arrive home more than 16 hours later from the original time that was booked. Loss of wages for two people, pet sitter additional day and night, uber rides to hotel, both kids miss school, extra day of parking fees at airport

I stood in line for 45 minutes at the help desk to receive a voucher as promised. Upon receipt of a free hotel and a $12.00 food credit, I left to pick up my luggage, which was pulled at my originating airport to be picked up in Dallas ft worth since I knew ahead of time I would have to spend the night in Dallas and was told I would receive a voucher for my hotel along with my luggage. I waited for all the bags to come off and my luggage was not there as promised. I went out to call the hotel, and the phone just went voicemail after numerous attempts. I googled the address of the hotel, and could not get anyone to answer to even get a ride to the hotel. After having this happen to me on a previous trip with American Airlines, where I received a voucher to a hotel, got a bus to the hotel and there were no reservations available. I realized I did not want To pay for an uber to a hotel that clearly either wasn’t in business anymore or were overbooked. I realized that since it was after 9:00pm, I would need to secure my own hotel. I got the last room at the Hyatt which was almost $500. I called every low cost hotel in the area and there were no rooms. I left early the next morning for my charlotte connection and went to use my food voucher and was told it was only good at Dallas ft worth airport. I was told at the help desk it was good at any airport on my itinerary. I arrived home with no luggage until the following day. It was raining, and the courier service just dropped it in the pouring rain and drove off, not even ringing my doorbell. My luggage is expensive Hartman tweed favric and was soaked. I sent a complaint to the customer relations department to complain and was told that although they understood my frustration, they would not be sending me one penny for the vouchers that were of no value. If a company promises vouchers yet won’t stand by them, they are dishonest and lack integrity.

We were told to standby for the connecting flight to MBJ. After spending over 5 hours in the airport gate lounge. They canceled the flight and rescheduled a flight for November 6th. The airline staff was very rude and did not offer any suggestions or a hotel accommodations. Suggested we collect our luggage and re-board/book the next morning. The group reported to baggage claim. The attendant strongly suggested do NOT checkout your luggage. The luggage will follow on to the next flight. As well as, suggested the Airport Marriott. Appreciated his input. American Airlines already made up their minds to rescheduled a flight for November 6th. Disregarding customer service or respect.

I had initially requested assistance for my flights, but decided to cancel assistance for departing due to having my own support. For the remaining journey, the airline failed me terribly. On the flight from Reagan Airport to Toronto, no assistance was provided, and I visibly struggled while waiting for everyone to board. Although my carry-on met all regulations and was allowed on all my previous flights, I was forced to check it this time. Despite explaining that without assistance retrieving my bags at the claim would be almost impossible, I was assured there would be support in Toronto and given a valet pickup tag for my luggage. Regrettably, no assistance appeared upon arrival, forcing me to struggle down the ramp outside. Furthermore, my luggage wasn't available at the valet pickup, so I had to struggle all the way to baggage claim. It was truly horrible

We’re early because of having to drop a car off and wasn’t sure how long that would take. So we ended up having to sit on the cold floor, because there was limited seating . After a long delay we finally reach Chicago airport, get to our gate and we find out we’re delayed again, according to the pilot they sent our crew some where else, I’m sure someone knew way before we were informed, leaving us wondering who’s flight was more important then ours! They took our crew, but no one seemed to think hey get another crew right away. Finally a crew shows up and as I’m checking in there was a woman calling for help because an older man almost collapsed asking for a wheel chair to help him board the plane , all 4 staff just stood there and didn’t even rush to help a customer! The guy taking my ticket told her His words not mind “Jesus Christ just give us a break” that’s when I walked on the plane. I contacted customer service and even though this was the Airlines fault the best they could was a $ 50 trip voucher. How insulting is that! Worst part of our trip was flying with American airline!

I’ve been a frequent flyer for 23 years now, and I can confidently state that of all the airlines I’ve flown, AA by far has the worst customer service, even within the US, which is already a very low bar. Delays, cancellations, and other problems are bound to happen with any airline, but the flippant, glib and couldn’t care less attitude with which these are handled by the AA staff is infuriating. Stay away.

The price was approximately $3800 dollars with a standard ticket costing about $700 at the time. Due to a knee injury, it was important for me to have the ability to lie flat, which is why I purchased that specific seat type. Upon boarding the flight, I was unaware my seat was broken. After the flight reached a safe altitude to adjust our seats, the captain allowed us to unbuckle our seatbelts and walk around the cabin. I realized my electronic control panel was not working and I was unable to move my seat. I called Michelle and Mats, the flight attendants serving our area, and notified them of the issue. Michelle let me know the seat was known to be broken and could not be adjusted through the control panel due to a power failure. Any seat manipulation would require it to be done manually by two flight attendants. I requested another seat due to seeing a couple available, and she informed me they were for the cabin crew. So, I let her know I needed to figure something out due to my seat being broken. She then requested another attendant to help her manually move the seat, and after attempting this, the seat jammed and was left pushed forward with the seat back leaning forward, as well. For the entire duration of the flight, 10+hours, I was unable to sit upright, recline, nor was I able to use any electronic functionality of my seat. Furthermore, due to the seat being stuck leaning forward, the tray table to eat was also unable to be opened, so I had an issue with dining. Michelle realized this was an issue and contacted American Airlines Customer Relations during the flight to request they reach out to me about this ordeal. Michelle let me know that AA knows about damaged seats and plane issues but were opting to wait for major renovations to their fleet in October. I questioned why they would sell a premium seat knowing the seat was damaged, and she told me it is a known frustration throughout multiple flight attendants. No matter what, American will not refund my money.

Plenty of legroom in the Main Cabin Extra seats. Connecting to inflight WiFi was very easy with a good selection of movies, music and live tv. Flight crew was very pleasant providing friendly and efficient service.

I was seated in the emergency exit row at seat 17A. The crew only asked the passengers sitting in the emergency exit rows for verbal confirmation that we would assist in evacuating passengers, although three of them were elderly. One of them had difficulty moving and appeared to be over 80 years old! I respect the elderly, but how can a person help in a real-life emergency if they cannot respond quickly? The emergency exits were cluttered with passengers’ hand luggage, and none of the crew asked to place it in the overhead compartments, which had enough space available. On the next flight, all 12 seats in the emergency exit row were empty, which contradicts safety regulations. In the event of an emergency, there would be no passengers who were briefed and responsible for opening the emergency exits. This would hinder an effective evacuation of the passengers. In my 8 years of working in aviation, I have never seen such disregard for safety.

review_header: "will never fly with that airline again"
review_text: That to me is deplorable and predatory practice and the customer service agent I spoke to was rude and completely unapologetic about the matter as well. I will never fly with that airline again.

We chose our seats at the time of purchase. After flying into Dallas for our connection we were informed that our seats had been moved to standard seats. I called and was told I'd receive a refund within 24 hours. When I didn't I called again and was told I had to call after our trip was completed. So I did and was told I had to email them for the refund. So I did. Now I'm being told that they won't refund me because those seats are 'if available'. How do you charge someone $140 extra per seat, have them chose the seat and then tell them they're not available but keep their money? What a scam. And to top it off we paid for seats together and were switched on 3 out of 4 flights and were nowhere near each other.

Old outdated plane. Uncomfortable cramped seats with the shortest leg room I have ever seen in a long haul flight. Makes Ryanair feels premium in comparison. On top of that for what ever reason, at last minute before boarding they asked me checkin my hand luggage because overhead compartments were supposedly full. But once in the plane, it was obvious half of the overhead compartments were empty. Is this what the supposedly most advanced country in the world has to offer as a company?
Why do I continue to fly with this miserable airline? Well, if there is a specific airport I want to fly out of, on a specific day and time, sometimes AA is the only choice I have.

review_header: "I was forced to check my bag"
review_text: I was forced to check my bag even though I saw we had bin space. I had a bag sent to be picked up for not other reason the young lady boarding the plane’s arrogance and her unwillingness to listen. The plane had plenty of overhead space. I asked if I could have my carry on with me. This isn’t the first time something like this happened. The stewardess attempted to get my bag on board. However the rep letting us on the plane rolled her eyes and refused and said I’d have to wait. Three empty bins from my count.

They wouldn’t accept my son’s ID, the guy was shaking his head at me. The TSA workers singled me and my disabled son out checking out bags rifling through them carelessly saying that there were chemicals on our bags. Telling us to “stand over there!” Very rudely. The plane we went on had an hour delay. Then we get another surprise and had to pay an extra $115 for seats that I thought I already paid for. I couldn’t sit next to my autistic son, even though I had to pay extra for our seats and my son was vomiting on the plane. I will never fly with American Airlines ever again.

They offer no refunds, no reimbursement, and no apologies for wasting days of peoples’ lives. They will not ensure you make connecting flights. They will simply continue to overbook and underperform. Fly any other airline and save yourself the trouble. Literally any other airline.

200 passengers sat in the plane for over two hours with very little air flow while we waited for the extremely late pilot to arrive. Afterwards we didn't get any kind of apology from American Airlines. No flight credits or even an email that said sorry. We suffered for 2 hours in the Miami heat waiting for a late pilot and American Airlines did nothing about it!!This is what you can expect from these big corporations now. It wasn't long ago that my tax dollars bailed these airlines out and they can't even bother to apologize when they make a mistake.

I am a a platinum member of AA since 2006 , purchased a confirmed business class American Airline ticket to India code shared with Qatar Airways. On my return, I checked online a day ahead as usual but on the night of the flight when I went to the counter at the airport Qatar only issued me a boarding pass to DOH not to my final destination to Chicago, I was told that AA has cancelled my 2nd leg after so many calls with AA customer service , i was rudely informed that AA has the right to cancel all or part of any confirmed ticket involuntarily without explanation and they did an involuntarily cancellation to my ticket. Qatar Airways got me an economy Class ticket on the 2nd leg, AA has cancelled the 2nd leg of my flight and would have left me stranded in a foreign country.

Unfortunately, this was insufficient time for customs, and I arrived just as the gate was closing. American Airlines should have known that Miami was a busy airport and that this layover was too short for a smooth connection. When I arrived, they directed me to their "rebooking counter." I had never encountered such a counter before, but it turns out they have at least two, staffed by 4-5 employees, likely due to frequent rebookings. There was even a sign indicating that they often overbook flights. They managed to book me on a flight the next morning that would stop in Dallas, arriving in Seattle at 3 PM the following day. When I asked to speak with the manager, she was dismissive and told me that they were only legally obligated to provide a layover of between 90 minutes and 2 hours. She added that if I had been flying to Canada or the UK, they would have had to provide hotel accommodations and meals, but because my final destination was within the U.S., they had no obligation to assist me. She insisted I should feel fortunate to be rebooked at all. This led to a long night spent at Miami airport. The next morning, my flight to Dallas was delayed on the tarmac for over two hours because one of the engines wouldn't start, necessitating a mechanic's intervention. As a result, I arrived in Dallas 15 minutes after my connecting flight had left. I had to return to the rebooking counter yet again, where I finally secured a new flight for 5 PM. Ultimately, I arrived home a full 21 hours later than my original schedule.

review_header: "flight from DFW to Philly was great"
review_text: I go with American because I think the regular economy seats are more comfortable if comparing the two airlines. This trip however, I did pay $68 dollars more for the extra room seat in row 12. For a 5.5 hour flight it is so worth it. There was nobody in the middle seat either. The trip to Seattle from Philly the plane left on time and there were no problems. I do love American Airlines mobile app. You don't need to print boarding passes, you can purchase your checked baggage ahead of time. Best of all, if you need to make a transfer in a confusing or large airport, they provide a step by step map for you. This was a life saver for me on the return trip to Philly which first stopped in DFW. The flight from Seattle left a half hour late, which caused me some minor anxiety on the way to DFW (because there was only a 40 minute gap between the 2 flights on a normal schedule). The pilot did make up some ground on the way to DFW, so we landed on time, but I lost 20 of the 40 minutes I had taxiing to the gate, and physically getting off the plane. Stupidly I had sat in the back for that flight, lesson learned! So dramatically I had to run a little to the Skytrain escalator, and go to level 5, but at least I knew where I was going thanks to the AA App! The train took 10 minutes, then I ran down the escalator, and jogged to the gate where I made it to the gate to Philly with 3 minutes to spare! I couldn't believe it I was just so happy that I made the flight and if they waited for me and my bags, thank you I really appreciate it! That 3 hour flight from DFW to Philly was great, they had pretzels for snacks and again I sprung for the more expensive seat in row 12. What a day that was! One of my return luggage pieces, was a 36 lb. box of beer cans and crowlers from Seattle that I packed up myself and gratefully it survived loading, take off, landing and unloading twice! Yay!! Even though this airline is poorly rated I can tolerate it because I always fly after 12 noon, and usually late afternoons, when there are hardly any wait times for security checkpoints in airports, planes aren't fully sold out and the flight attendants seemed to be more chill.

I travelled September 28th from tampa to New-York. I was supposed to be there around 5pm but we landed at 8pm. I missed the reason for what I went. My ride left without me so I had to book a hotel for the night and came back September 29th from New-Jersey to Tampa. This flight was delayed too. We were supposed to land at 9pm at Miami and I had connection at 10:15 for tampa. I missed this flight too. When we landed before getting off the plane, nobody was in any of American Airlines gates. One guys told me to go to receptiin and there I found an agent who told me AA can not provide hotel because it was not AA fault. Was it my fault if the flights were delayed? And the next flight from Miami to Tampa will be at 5:11am "if it is on time" . I have life, I have my job. I missed why I went to NY it like I went for nothing because of AA. I am going to miss my work tomorrow and I can be fired because I did not tell to any of my managers or took days off. If you can, avoid this company. You will lose your connections flight, your money, even your desire to travel.

How does this not secure me a seat on the plane? They put me on a United airlines flight later in the day, told me my bag would be forwarded on, and it never was. 10 days later, my bag and everything in it is officially "lost" and no one can tell me where it is. Thanks American Airlines for overselling my flight, kicking me off at the last minute, then loosing my luggage. Your customer service team has been terrible. No accountability. Absolutely terrible.

Depart flight left Atlanta stopped in charlotte and then connection - as expected. Return was a bus booked through aa.com. This feels like fraud (not an expert - I'm assuming there's some way they can get away with this). I hope at least some of you can save themself this horror and book an airline that uses all planes. My ticket shows four plane icons ... one for every leg of the trip.

At airport, flight delayed, all of which can happen with any airline, however American do not issue apologies, even asking customers on boarding to please hurry as flight is already delayed, without a hint of an apology. The departing gate on return was changed several times, leading to us walking up and down airport again without an apology, the need to vigilant with app & airport info paramount, no American airline reps in sight.

First maintenance issue then a passenger wanted to get off so they had to get just luggage off the plane then we waited for the push off from the terminal. Absolutely unbelievable. We weren’t offered any credits for future flights. We will never fly American Airlines EVER again.

We were going home to Michigan from North Carolina to introduce our 4 month old to our family. We departed ILM on 8/30, this flight was initially delayed taking off to CLT due to a mechanical issue. This late departure caused us to hit severe storms around the CLT airport leaving our plane unable to land in CLT for which we were re-routed to Greensburg-Spartanburg, SC airport. We sat on the tarmac (not being allowed off the plane) for 4 hours with our 4 month old and our dog onboard. When we were finally allowed to go back to CLT our plane to DTW had taken off ~20 minutes prior to us landing resulting in that flight to be missed. When we landed, the flight attendants promised us that there would be an agent at the gate to help us all rebook our flights. After all of the passengers deboarded, that attendant at the gate helped 3 people and then left the rest of us standing there with no explanation or help, never coming back. I was finally able to get our flight rebooked for 11am on 8/31 and then we went to collect our luggage and, to my surprise, an AA employee in baggage claim told us our bags were going to be sent to our final destination regardless of rebooking and refused to give us back our car seat for our 4 month baby. After AA left us stranded in CLT (3 hours away from our home in ILM) we had to book a hotel to stay overnight and had no car seat for our baby making those rides extremely dangerous. AA refused to refund our tickets and baggage fees because we "rebooked our flights". We had NO choice but to rebook because our car seat would have been sent to Michigan anyways and there was no way were were taking a 3 hour car ride back to ILM with no car seat for our baby. Then on the following flight for 8/31, our flight was delayed again due to a missing flight attendant, for which no one knew where she was.

Our class of service was downgraded and when we attempted to get a refund for the difference in fare price, were offered a ridiculously small amount as a refund. After multiple e-mail requests, we were continually referred back to the AA web form for complaints, no one would call to speak to me, and the refund amount was not adjusted. It's rare that I experience customer service this poor. AA should be ashamed at the way it treats it's customers.

Missed our connecting flight to Aruba. Paid for 1st class, and rest of trip had to fly Main. Hassle rescheduling in CLT as well. Lodging provided in Houston was deplorable. Room smelled. Trip to Aruba was for a marriage proposal and stress of not knowing where our luggage was awful. Lost a day in Aruba as well (~$900/night) at Bucuti and Tara Beach Resort. After the missed connection flight, dealing with AA was an awful experience. First AA booked us flights thru Dulles with one of us flying standby to Aruba on an oversold flight! What a hassle with 90% of the reps we worked with to get to Aruba. We chose AA as we wanted to sit together in first class for this special trip (she was not aware of the pending marriage proposal). Our experience with AA was the worst experience we both have ever had flying and could have been avoided had the initial flight not been delayed for (2) late non-flying, non-paying pilots to catch a flight back to CLT. I blame AA 100% for this horrendous experience. Their lack of consideration for the customer is enough to avoid this airline going forward. Upon returning home, dealing with Customer Service seeking retribution was just as awful. Never again!!

Cathay said they can't help, because it's AA that is delayed so they have to rebook you. Customer is being treated like a number/toy, passed around back and forth like a ball. After rebooked me to Qatar, then they said you have to wait around for 7 hours here. I am standing here with 5 yo daughter, unable to get in, haven't had food/drink for 14 hrs. Never again fly AA! They don't care about you even if you pay the most expensive tickets, you are just a number.

It was one of my flights that day. My starting point was Muscat, Oman. It was an exhausting day after multiple flights and this flight was going to be the last one. I bought a business class ticket. The were two things that happened. First of all, my seat was broken: I can't even understand how could that have happened in business class and no one of the crew noticed it. Secondly, the stewardess was really rude to me. I told her about the problem with the seat, but she didn't care at all. In fact, she started shouting at me, saying that she wouldn't transfer me to another seat, and that she could only put me at the seat that was near the toilet. However, that seat didn't lean back and it was in economy class.  I was offended in front of many people as well as this flight was one of the most uncomfortable I've had in my whole life. I don't recommend this airline to anyone. You will spend money for nothing, no service, awful behavior. They don't even want to make a refund for that, just leaving me with raw apologies. Hopefully, I have helped someone to make a right decision after this review.

Gave me a voucher that did not work after a flight I was on was immediately landed due to "mechanical failure" which was later revealed to actually be due to the fact the pilot was too old to legally fly the aircraft and had to land urgently to avoid this coming to light. Then, we are treated absolutely horribly, given zero information or support, and not told when we'll be able to get home. For this horrific experience I was given a $125 voucher! When I was entitled to a full refund and the voucher did not work. When I tried to use it to book a flight (which I was doing through American Airlines so I could use the voucher - I would never willingly fly with this despicable airline again) I was told the voucher was invalid. I purchased the flight with my own money and contacted customer service requesting to be reimbursed for the value of the voucher, and explained the situation - only to be treated abhorrently, my request refused with no alternate care or solution provided, and then simply ignored when I tried to find another remedy. The customer service AND flights themselves with this airline are the worst I've experienced.

review_header: "$1200 we had to shell out just to get home"
review_text: While standing in line after deboarding, they gate agents were very rude to passengers trying to get on different flights in order to not miss their connections. Arrived in Chicago and stood in line for over 2 hours while also on hold with customer service to be told the earliest we could get to Bozeman was in 2 days. The closest we could get was to Salt Lake City in which case we had to buy additional tickets from Salt Lake to Bozeman for $400 each and we still lost a day of travel. We lost one day of work and the tickets on Delta (total $1800 loss) just to get back in time to not lose more $$. They did refund the ticket from Chicago to Bozeman ($89 each) and gave us a $50 travel credit. Doesn't really help with the $1200 we had to shell out just to get home.

I've traveled a lot for business and vacation, so I know to expect minor annoyances that can occur like lost baggage and even storm delays however what shows me an airlines quality is their consideration to passengers in how they handle these things. American Airlines completely failed on all levels of customer service, good judgment and common sense on our last trip from PGV to MCO. Both our departing and returning flights connected in Charlotte airport and that is where American had problems both coming and going. Our flight down to Orlando was delayed in Charlotte for over an hour and caused us to miss dinner plans. Not a big deal, just annoying. But on our flight home from Tampa, we were again delayed in Charlotte. This time, we were delayed over an hour and half in the CLT terminal, gate agents were extremely rude and sitting with us were a few American Airline pilots also complaining about how they never allow their family to fly though Charlotte because of the frequent delays. Not a good sign when their own pilots are complaining about their experience with the airline. We boarded the plane despite storms on the radar and then they delayed us again in the plane for another 2.5-3 hours. I lost track of how many delays were extended in the plane because they just kept us there with little communication other than another delay. It would have been more comfortable to have left us in the terminal where we had food and AC. Yes, on the plane, there is WARM air coming from the vents that does little to cool off the plane. Also, only cookies to eat and I'm gluten free so I wasn't able to eat any dinner. To top it off, the baggage handlers left our luggage in pile on the tarmac in the pouring rain for hours with no protection, so our bag was soaked through and the clothing contents needed dry cleaning. Trying to make a complaint or request compensation with American is another nightmare. I was bounced from several different departments, directed to emails and online forms to fill out because you can't call them to ask for cash refunds. Then i was offered an insulting credit of miles and $50 trip credit for future travel with them. What makes them think I want to spend more money on travel with them in the future to use a credit?? I dont trust them to make good decisions in the passengers best interest or to even treat us with consideration. Their pilots, gate agents, baggage handlers were all disrespectful and rude. Our flight experience was awful and customer service just avoided a resolution or refund. I could have flown with a cheerer airline to get this low quality experience and paid half of what I paid American. I will never fly an American flight ever again. Not only did they cost us time on our trip, leave us uncomfortable and hungry but they also added further work for me after the trip with taking clothes to dry cleaning and wasting more of my time with phone calls and forms to file complaints which have been basically ignored or auto replied. Never again.

Well over 50% of flights I've taken the last 3 years have been delayed. On two separate occasions I have had to reschedule international flights because the domestic 1st leg was delayed and I could not make the scheduled connection, resulting in losing half a day or more of hard-earned time on the ground at our destination. AA has offered no explanation or compensation in any case. I will do everything in my power to avoid ever flying AA again.

Without a doubt this is the worst service I've had on any flight, especially on an international business class flight, in 30 years. Old, grumpy flight attendants. Never smile, never engage. Always slow. Asking for a glass of water would take 3 attempts and 20 minutes before you got anything. This is international business class! (there's no first class on this plane, this is as good as it gets). They rush out a mediocre meal at the beginning of the flight then go hide away for 6 hours. Literally not a single attendant moved through the seats for 6 hours. I had to go find someone for a glass of water. Unbelievably bad. Disappointing. I've held onto this since of loyalty to AA since I was a kid. We used to fly Piedmont Airlines all the time, which became USAir, not American. These people have stripped everything of ANY value out of what used to be a wonderful airline. Oh, and we were 6 hours late on the outbound flight and 2 hours late on the return. All airline issues, not weather. Avoid at ALL COSTS! If you still have AA status, as I do, leverage it to buy a ticket directly with BA. American is a joke and has no place whatsoever competing against real global airlines on these international route. Only thing AA is good for is that upgrade from Charlotte to Akron Ohio, or whereeverthehell they fly; but don't waste your money on AA for real routes.

review_header: “the worst experience we have ever had”
review_text: We had left for vacation overseas and on day 2 our 6 year old daughter had a life threatening emergency that required immediate surgery. We dropped everything and arranged to change our return flight home from days in the future to within a few hours. Making this change AA then charged us an additional $2,300 dollars just to make this change! We contacted customer service and were told this was due to flight being full. We get in the plane and it was maybe at 60% capacity- so first lie. Once we got home and ensure our daughter was safe after surgery, we reached out to customer service to see if they would be willing to reimburse us the additional $2,300 and not for the original cost of the pre-paid flights. Since then it has been over 90 days. They have purposely bounced us around, spelled our last name incorrect, asked for documents and then never acknowledged they were received and blatantly ignored all follow-up attempts. We then just simply asked for a statement that we were not reimbursed for original pre-paid flight to complete our travelers insurance claim through a separate company and they have not provided. This has been the worst experience we have ever had and never imagined that following the awful scare with our daughter, we would be dragged through the mud by American Airlines.

However they booked me on a bus! Their first several responses were essentially "sorry you should have known". The last response was "you can cancel your trip and we'll review if we give you a refund". Again ... a bus. I booked on their website AA.com. This feels like a scam.

Me and my partner worked half the day at our job to ensure we didn't miss out 5 pm flight just to be delayed almost 3 hours on top of that we ended up in Dallas without another flight till the morning. We asked about getting refunded if we got a rental car and drove the rest of the way and the girls at the airport said they should be able to fully refund you so we paid for a rental that was almost $300 & arrived in San Antonio about 5 AM ( When we should have originally landed around 9 pm)we paid for a night of the hotel that we didn't even spend the night in then tried to put our claim through hoping to get the rental reimbursed at least but they ended up only giving us 50$ airline credit and 50$ back on each ticket from Dallas to San Antonio so all together about 150 back half of what we spent on the rental and our hotel we missed out a night on that money was lost which was 282 a night so including half a days of being paid at our job and spending money on a rental we lost out on well over 600$. I have been on multiple airlines, and this is by far the worst, spirit was even better than this.

We had AirTags so we could tell the bags made it to Charlotte, NC but AA decided to send them to Chicago before routing them to us in Quebec. Inexcusable. We had to buy underwear and clothes (not to mention personal hygiene products for 2 people). Probably set us back $200. But that’s not even the WORST aspect. Four days later, we left Quebec and were headed to Top Sail, NC (via Charlotte) for a beach week but you lost both bags a SECOND TIME! We had to buy all new personal hygiene stuff because the baggage guy in Wilmington was out of any emergency hygiene packages (and he could have cared less about us and our missing bags.) He needs training since he was extremely rude to us. Typical Gen-Zer who was disappointed that he had to work at all and we added to his workload by filing our 2nd LOST BAGS FORM IN FOUR DAYS! We predicted that AA would cancel our Charlotte flight to CVG (since we noticed it was only half full). And we were right. You managed to delay and eventually cancel our flight and we had to rebook for 4 hours later. thanks for making a long day even longer. But that's really not the worst part. You rebooked us in the last row middle seat and the next to last row middle seat. So those cushy up-front seats that we paid extra for evaporated and I couldn't even lean my seat back. We rather despise your airline now. The lost bag guy in Quebec’s airport deserves a shout-out since he was empathetic and kind to us. Not that it helped.
