She responded by saying "If that's what you want to do" I wanted to be on a plane but every step of the way Delta was rude and unhelpful. When I called customer service they told me there was nothing they could do and in order to get a voucher I would need to go to the help desk (the one I just came from). The level of care is non existent in this company. I had to argue over the fact that my tickets said boarding ended 15 minutes before departure ar 1120am. I was there at 11am but on the app that moved the time to leaving early at 1115am. And in addition the Delta employee told me the 15 minutes wasn't true and it's actually 20 minutes. It seemed like every step of the way they tried to find a reason why it was my fault I missed the fault. Now I'm writing this, stranded in an airport for another 19 hours, with no help, no care, and an absolute disdain for Delta Airlines.

review_header: “wondering what flight insurance is even for”
review_text: My wife is battling stage 4 pancreatic cancer and we have been told it is terminal. This will more than likely be her last trip to see her mother. I paid for first class tickets so we would have room to move around and so my wife does not have to walk down the tight aisles of the plane. I requested special assistance in the airport to get her to our gate and have done all the right steps to get her medical equipment approved for the flight. I bought flight insurance in case we could not make the flight or we needed to change the flight. Mind you, the insurance alone cost me half of what the ticket cost me. Two weeks prior to our flight I came down with pneumonia. As our trip got closer, I only got more sick. 4 days before our flight I worked out to have my sister in law take my place on the flight so my wife could still go to WA and I can stay home to rest. I called Delta to request to change the name on the ticket. I was told that they have a policy that will not allow them to change the name and there is ZERO exceptions to that policy. I explained the situation, spoke to a supervisor, and was still told no. I was told I could refund my ticket and then repurchase a new ticket but I would have to repurchase the ticket at the current days prices. Furthermore, i couldn’t use the money I paid for my first ticket to buy the new ticket. I was told they can’t do a fund transfer either. I had no choice. I refunded my ticket. But I have to wait 3-5 business days to see my money back. But I couldn’t wait 3-5 business days for the money as I needed the ticket sooner than that. So, now Im figuring out finances to pay for a new ticket AT THAT DAYS PRICES. As they were booking the new ticket I was then told that there was nothing left in first class like I had originally bought. I asked them why I can’t just buy the seat I just refunded and I was told that when I refunded my seat it was automatically given to anyone who has requested an upgrade and is on an upgrade wait list. So my original seat is no longer available. (This all happened in a matter of minutes as I refunded my original ticket and bought a new ticket all on the same phone call). Now this means that my wife and sister in law are in separate seats on the plane. on top of all this, a round trip ticket in comfort plus is costing me more money than my original round trip ticket in first class because I have to pay that days prices. Delta won’t honor a name change, won’t honor me to put funds from my current ticket to a new one, wont honor the seats I originally booked, and won’t allow me to purchase at prices in the day I originally booked the flight. I’m wondering what flight insurance is even for and why it’s so expensive if it doesn’t do anything for you. Delta Airlines: I hope you see this, and I hope you have more of a heart for your future customers. as for me and my entire family, we will never fly with you again!

When we got to Paris, the connecting flight had closed the doors and boom, we had our flight rescheduled. Very inconveniencing to customers, and the customer services are just non empathetic and seem to careless. This is not the first time Delta is inconveniencing. Since July 2024 after there was global network outage, delta airline have not been so good to me. Never again, even if it’s the last airline in the world, I will never again use Delta!

Every time, it’s attributed to a "technical issue." However, the flight from SFO to JFK consistently has Wi-Fi without any problems. Currently, I’m at JFK waiting for my flight to ACC, and I just received a notification that there will once again be no Wi-Fi on this leg of my journey. As a loyal Delta customer and SkyMiles member who frequently flies within the U.S., I’ve never experienced this issue on domestic flights. This repeated lack of service on the Accra route raises serious concerns about selective treatment of certain destinations and passengers. It almost suggests that some routes and individuals are prioritized over others, despite everyone paying the same—if not more—for their tickets. This is unacceptable and not reflective of the equitable service Delta should provide to all its passengers, regardless of their destination. I urge Delta to address this inconsistency and rectify the situation immediately. Every customer deserves the same quality of service. Do better, Delta!

I was boarding zone 8 and at the gate the Delta agent announced that the travelers can check the carry-on for free. I had a connecting flight in Atlanta, and I decided to keep my carry-on and went boarding. When approached the plane entrance, Delta male flight attendant told me that he won’t let me in the plane with carry-on. I tried to explain the reason I need my carry-on with me, but he called another person and that person laid a hand on me by pushing me away. I asked him to stop it and return to the gate to check my carry-on. After I checked my carry-on and returned to the plane the same male Delta flight attendant refused to let me in the plane and threaten me by calling security. I missed my two flights and was stressed. The Delta flight attendant was very rude and demonstrated a horrible attitude.

I was scheduled to fly from Toronto to Atlanta on November 20, 2024, at 6:15 PM with flight DL2714, and from ATL to Melbourne FL with flight DL2435 at 10:39PM. I was boarding zone 8 and at the gate the Delta agent announced that the travelers can check the carry-on for free. I had a connecting flight in Atlanta, and I decided to keep my carry-on and went boarding. When approached the plane entrance, Delta male flight attendant told me that he won’t let me in the plane with carry-on. I tried to explain the reason I need my carry-on with me, but he called another person and that person laid a hand on me by pushing me away. I asked him to stop it and return to the gate to check my carry-on. After I checked my carry-on and returned to the plane the same male Delta flight attendant refused to let me in the plane and threaten me by calling security. I missed my two flights and was stressed. The Delta flight attendant was very rude and demonstrated a horrible attitude.

I believe the cleaning crew either at Rapid City airport or Minneapolis airport where the plane returned to simply found and kept my headphones. That is theft. I was specific about the appearance of the missing item (blue soft bag with noise cancelling headphones) and  the seat 6D. There is no way that the cleaning crew did not find it. The only other choice is if another passenger saw it and took it. I will not fly Delta again.

No seat assigned 2 days before Flight. No place for the carry-on and they over staffed with other people’s luggage. When I tried explaining to a team member called Sergio that I had to bring my luggage in as that's why I choose Delta, he was so rude and immediately threatened me saying he'll re-assign me to a different Flight. Then when I tried explaining I have a buissnes meeting I literally heard him copycat my words to a other team member saying "business meeting ahh". So rude. I'd never fly with them again. I'd take Spirit, Jetblue or Frontier before this experience any given day.

My fourth flight in a week and despite the various lengths and aircraft the service was top notch. This particular plane has got to be the most comfortable narrow body around. Of course 2-2 seating but other than that generous legroom and wide enough seats. The food was quite good(all on one tray) the IFE was wonderful and the flight attendant serving our cabin mostly alone was so kind and extremely efficient. Wi fi is so inconsistent on this route and we are warned in an email that it might not be available yet it’s works perfectly and is free.

The differences being no club access, no pillow or blanket and a reduced meal service. Despite all this it was a pleasant experience which, for me, has included the typical pleasant, efficient cabin crew.The breakfast (pictured) was totally adequate and IFE excellent. Really no complaints except a blanket and pillow would have been nice for an over four hour trip with a lay flat seat. By the way I keep hearing about free Delta Wi-Fi and haven’t experienced it once.

Their "accessible" procedure is long and complicated and then they don't follow through on what they promise. We recently flew from Orlando to Amsterdam and requested assistance on the flight - they ignored our requests multiple times and we had a horrendous experience on-board the flight because of it. They discriminated against disabilities and not interested in my voice regarding this. Their customer care supervisor Jacob Costillo has not taken my complaint seriously, palming me off with pathetic copy-and-paste responses, saying the matter is closed. I have forwarded my complaints for the U.S Department of Transportation and implore that other people think before booking a flight with Delta.

The comfort, the food, which was actually delicious for a change, the IFE, but most importantly the crew. Literally the entire cabin staff was genuinely gracious and efficient in every manner. I observed many of their interactions with passengers and each other and flawless is the word. I was happily compelled to tell as many as I could how impressed and grateful I was. I rarely complain and mostly expect things not to be up to par so this was a welcome surprise.Generally my Delta cabin crew experiences are good but this was perfect.

After receiving six delay notifications, I spoke to five different agents over the phone and interacted with two Customer Service (CS) agents onsite. The first onsite agent did nothing to help, but the second agent put us on standby for the 11:45 AM flight to San Diego, which was already full, so we didn't get on. Through online chat, an agent offered us 6,000 miles per person (for my wife and me) plus $50 each. I found this offer insulting and declined, not wanting to settle for something inadequate. The onsite agent gave us two $12 lunch coupons, which weren't enough for a decent meal at the airport. As notifications kept coming, our departure was rescheduled to 3:17 PM, with an arrival in San Diego at 6:30 PM. After one more call, a helpful agent automatically booked us on another flight to San Diego at 3:35 PM while keeping us on the original flight, ensuring we had a backup. We decided to wait for the 3:35 PM flight since our original one had significant mechanical issues. We eventually arrived in San Diego at 6:20 PM. We missed two meetings, a lunch with friends, and a planned ride to the hotel, forcing us to use public transportation and buy dinner, missing another planned dinner with friends. This was a funeral trip, making the delays emotionally draining. We experienced nearly a six-hour delay, and Delta didn’t handle this as they should have. After the trip, I filed a complaint as advised by the agents. Delta gave us 4,000 miles each, which was less than what was initially offered via chat, and offered $50 vouchers. Despite not agreeing to this compensation, they added the miles to our accounts. I requested a refund, citing a new DOT mandate that requires refunds for domestic flights delayed by three hours or more, which was ignored because our flight was three days before the mandate took effect. I reported this to the DOT online but have not received feedback yet. Delta’s service has deteriorated significantly.

Finally, when we boarded the plane and settled in, they announced that the flight had been canceled because one of the pilots hadn’t arrived. After standing in line for hours, until midnight, I finally had the chance to speak with the airport staff. I was informed that there were no available seats for the next two days. It took a great deal of persuasion and insistence before I was booked on a flight with a lower category ticket for the following day. I ended up waiting at the airport, sitting in a chair, for nearly 24 hours. They did not compensate me for the difference in ticket price, nor did they provide a hotel voucher or food voucher. Having traveled extensively with various airlines around the globe, I can confidently say that this has been the worst customer service experience I have ever encountered.

Upfront at premium price for a cup of coffee and a (modest) bag of cookies on a two hour flight on an early (7am) morning flight. Why is a breakfast not possible to serve? The most questionable was the lavatory, probably the most disgusting thing I have seen on a plane: dirty, old, and outworn. Comparisons would be here out of line, simply it was disgusting.

Excellent boarding process. Uneventful flight, including efficient service with a round of drinks and a little snack, actually far better than what meanwhile one gets from nearly all European “Full Service Airlines” when flying short- and medium haul.

We arrived at Orlando airport to face a melee to get bags tags (the machines would not respond to boarding passes and there was no-one on hand to help many frustrated customers). Customers were then faced with a huge slow moving queue to check bags in with a poor Delta employee sweating whilst dealing with already aggravated customers. Once arriving at the gate customers' experience was made worse by utter chaos: inaudible announcements (made via a tannoy system), customers stressed and on standby, travellers being hoarded onto the plane in a last minute panic (generated by the Delta staff themselves). Upon boarding the plane the experience only worsened - the Delta economy seats lean forward so that your back is put under immediate strain, there's less leg room than on short haul European Flights and the plane felt old and tired. The meals were luck laster for 1 of our party and 4 of our party were unable to have any meal at all: we have dietary restrictions which were booked in advanced and not delivered (meaning no meal for myself and 3 of my children for all 9 hours of our flight). Despite all of this and putting on a smile we were faced with obnoxious (probably overworked and tired) cabin staff who were rude, short, unhelpful and seemed in a huge rush to sit down for most of the flight. I asked a question of one air host who responded, "What!?" A "pardon" or "sorry I didn't hear you," would have been much warmer. To summarise we felt like herded cattle at best / cannon fodder at worst. We 100% regret flying with Delta - Virgin Atlantic are about 100000000000000 x better than this horrendous experience (for perspective we'd much rather have flown with Ryanair).
First class flight for 2.5hrs. No tvs and frozen salads. Delta plays dumb and wants you to jump through hoops to get any compensation on 3 tickets.

I was notified after arrival to the airport. Original delay was supposed to be 3 hours. Delta checked my bag all the way to the final destination. I was going to claim and check myself to avoid loss. But agreed due to the delay. Delta never got my luggage to the connecting flight. I ended up spending my entire vacation without luggage and got my bags a day before flying back. Delta gave me $30 airline credit for the delay and said that luggage issue isn't their problem. But connecting airline. 100% of the problem was caused by Delta. They didn't even bother to offer a different flight to make my connection. This cost me highly frustrating vacation and over $300 in additional expenses. Thanks Delta keep $30. This is the worst experience I have ever had with an airline.

I was lured by the promise of flying the A330Neo but on both the JFK to ATH and then back to JFK ended up on a 19 year old A330 that must have been acquired from a defunct Latin American airline. Why did I guess this? The inflight navigation was solely in Spanish, the aircraft had ashtrays in the lavatories, only one of which was functioning on the ATH-JFK segment. The lie flat seats were beat and, this was new to me, there were flying insects in my window, a few of which got out and wandered about. Really Delta? Cabin crew staff was efficient and pleasant. I ordered a "special" lamb dinner which I handed to my partner who ended up very very ill. We asked for the proverbial "barf bag" of which there were none so she was handed a large garbage bag. The purser was kind and promised to make a note to Headquarters ... its been a month and we don't expect any communication. Let me add that my non-special dinner was inedible but my meal from JFK was good. Lesson learned Delta!

The Delta rep was very kind and rescheduled my flights. I received a confirmation via email, checked in for my flight one day prior and even selected my seats. But upon arrival to the airport for my 1st flight to Rome, I was told that they could see my reservation, but the agent forgot the final step and my tickets had not been re-issued. I was forced to purchase a ticket to Rome at an exorbitant price, but was told to see a supervisor at Delta in Rome where they could re-issue my tickets for my remaining flight. I was assured in both Bari and Rome that the ticket I purchased would be refunded in full as the challenge was on their end. After speaking with a Delta rep upon my return they also agreed that a reimbursement is warranted. I've submitted my claim twice and have been denied. Every agent I speak with sees the mishap, and agrees but it is handled by a different department and you can not reach them by phone. Mistakes can happen, but I expected Delta to stand behind their reputation. Delta do better!

I have flown Delta for the last four trips and everything went smoothly. On this last trip, I needed wheelchair assistance getting from gate to another. There was always someone from Delta waiting for me as I departed the plane, and the employees were extremely helpful, cordial, and patient. On the return, I overslept and made it to the Delta Ticket Counter with 36 minutes to spare! The agents teased me and then got serious about finding me a wheelchair. I got to the check-in with plenty of time to spare, even after going through the TSA line. Also, Delta is one of the airlines who let you change your flight times or dates with no penalties.

Not only my airfare was more expensive than other airlines such as Alaska and Aeromexico, the service was just really so so. There are no meal provided to and from Los Angeles and the flights were right at meal time. I kept thinking what services they have provided that deserve higher airfare, but I don’t find any. Even other cheaper airline provides free WiFi on board as well. On top of that, they subject their passengers to a “tsa bag search” at the boarding gate, where they randomly selected passengers and forced them to a bag search. My friend who took another airlines told me they don’t see such search happening at their gates. And I wonder how “randomly” those passengers were selected. All were traveling alone, and minority. Not only the staff asked me to take my carry on baggage to check stations in a stern voice as if I’ve done something wrong, I had to open the bag for the staff to examine. I then have to take off my shoes and let them check my shoes and socks. All these happened at the gate at a slow speed while people kept passing by and watching. I passed the check of course but I’ll never take Delta again. Save some money and save the trouble. By the was, when I asked the flight attendant what drinks or food they have, she told me to check the menu. I mean, does that mean they have everything on the “menu”? They don’t even have almonds which is my usual option.

review_header: "when we switched to Delta it all fell apart"
review_text: Unfortunately when we switched to Delta it all fell apart. We were informed that they did not have enough available pilots to fly us to Atlanta so we were being re routed to Boston to acquire another pilot. We were assured this would cause only a minimal a delay, this was the first lie. When we arrived we had a very tight connection, and the notoriously awful TSA was in full form, screaming at everyone but actually doing nothing. We arrived at the gate just as the door was closing but she would not let us on and refused to rebook us. Delta offered hotel vouchers and directed everyone outside to wait for hotel shuttles. The joke was on us because the shuttles don't run after midnight!

A month before my flight I get an email saying that they had changed my first flight and due to this I would not be able to make it to my layover flight to New York so I canceled it and had to book a new flight with a different company, now they are saying that I never payed my original flight all the way back in 2020 and refuse to give me the credit even tho I have several conversation with representatives that clearly show I had paid and confirmed my flights.
They were all so friendly and kind. I sat in the wrong seat by mistake and they were so charming about figuring it out for me.

While the pilot nailed the landing on the RDU to ATL run, the fact that she did it with flaps that never closed completely after takeoff, which followed a faulty fueling that caused us to have a 1 hr delay. We could only fly at 2/3 normal speed and elevation due to the flaps which made us another hour late, and because the flaps were stuck they wouldn't open fully for landing, so we had to be diverted to an emergency, extra long runway.  They never let on to the passengers of course. But the attendants all took the rest of the day off due to stress issues after landing, and that was the flight crew for my connecting flight to ABQ. Which made that flight also delayed two hours, as we had to wait for a replacement flight crew to show up.  I'm not ever flying Delta again, that's for sure! It's either Delta as a whole, or Raleigh/Durham-Delta ground crews in particular, but just do a Google search. If it was possible to give zero stars for everything but the flight crew (who were superb) I would, but you can't submit the review with at least one star in each category. Flight crew got 4 out of 5 for lying to us about how dire our situation was. There's a way to give people truth without causing chaos. It's called training.

Unless you’re looking to sleep in the airport, be yelled at, be taken advantage of and lied to. The worst airline ever. My flight was at 9:30pm from JFK New York to Sky Harbor Phoenix and they caused a 12 hour delay. Absolutely no one was able to give an explanation. They did not accommodate us with meals or hotels. They showed up with little pillows that looked and smelt used. They were unable to accommodate the elderly with a wheelchair. Making her get us and get one herself. Thankfully the people on the flight, us, the customers were taking care of her needs. They were understandable for a 12 hour delay. Never have I been so disrespected when asking for help. The attendants were yelling at us telling us the same “this is all we know” which is nothing. The plane its self is a different story. Outdated and disgusting. Does not seem like they cleaned between flight with trash left in the seats. Don’t get me started on the bathrooms. I couldn’t decide if I needed to pee or throw up from how nasty it was. NEVER FLY DELTA. This review is making me leave a rating. Is I could pick 0 I would so consider my 1 as a 0.

2 luggages were delivered to me out of 3. Up to date the remaining luggage is yet to be delivered to me and no explanation has been given. Delta is claiming that the bag is with their partner (WestJet) in MSP and WestJet is saying the bag has been handed over to Delta Airlines. Both of them are not talking nor collaborating with each other. It seemed their partnership is “non-functioning nor working? Their collaboration efforts looks disjointed?” even though both are situated in the same airport. Several calls were made to both Delta and WestJet on daily basis without solution. When we landed in MSP on September 15, we were told someone has mistakenly taking my bag and left his or her own (which was the same colour , make like mine ). I was told that they will call the said passenger to return the luggage immediately and I will get it the following day. One expects the staff on duty to follow up with this situation but it seemed she lacked initiative or nor dedication? Maybe she requires training on how to handle such challenges, despite the fact that she claimed to have all information of the said passenger. It’s disturbing that both Delta Airlines and her partner are yet to provide feedback to me. The materials inside are wedding dresses that are needed very urgently.

Initially, I had to cancel my ticket due to a mistake made by their representative, who didn’t have complete knowledge while booking it for me. Despite this error being on their end, I was left to deal with the consequences. When I requested an extension for the eCredit of almost 1000 dollars, which I used to book my own ticket, Delta denied every single request without any flexibility. The lack of understanding and support from their customer service has been incredibly disappointing, especially after being a loyal customer. I cannot recommend Delta to anyone seeking fair treatment and decent customer service. There are plenty of other airlines that value their customers and handle issues more professionally.

review_header: “it should not be tolerated by Delta”
review_text: I was on DL 0694 on September 25, 2024. I have been flying only with Delta airlines first class for the last 20 years and have never encountered a problem as I did tonight, the flight attendant in first class Sadya decided to stop serving a drinks without reason. We were not belligerent. We were not loud. We were not disruptive. The only thing I can think of that we did wrong was I did not know how to open the bathroom door. For the past 20 years, I was 336 pounds and have never used a restroom on an airplane before, the fact that I did not know how to open the door was not surprising to me, but apparently it made her feel that she needed to cut off service to us. I have loved Delta for 20 years and her behavior is embarrassing and it should not be tolerated by Delta as to the standards that they keep for their flight attendants.

One of the female Delta staff members began by yelling at everyone impatiently on the intercom repeatedly. She was angry, and was not able to maintain any semblance of professionalism. She specifically picked me out of the line while waiting to board, and separated me from my friend I was traveling with. She proceeded to allow my friend to board and then when I stepped up behind her to board, this person screamed at me to get back in line and she refused to allow me to board. I waited in disbelief and then she sent me to the other agent who asked me what was going on, I said I didn't know but she won't let me board, at this time the agent yelled across the entire crowd, "Stop causing drama lady!" Instead of the agent scanning and letting me board she sent me back to the agent who refused to board me and threw me out of the line. I stood there observing her yelling at other customers, trying to separate kids from their families, another customer experiencing exactly what they just did to me but she was screaming. At this point my friend stared videoing the agents with her cell phone of all the bullying going on, the agent saw her and stomped over and forced her around the corner out of anyones view in the boarding cart and it was at this time that the agent grabbed my friends phone from her hand and erased all her video footage. She proceeded to yell at, tower over my friend, and repeatedly threaten her that we are not getting on the plane. My friend repeatedly told her that she was terrifying her! It continued and the agent came back to me and the threats continued that "they" are reviewing the video to determine if "they" are going to let me board. She then proceeded to gaslight me saying she wasn't the one not letting me board and that I may be not able to board. Why? I have no idea. After the entire plane was boarded, I was finally scanned and let on, the last to board, my friend was shaking and totally traumatized from the assault and abuse. After I got home I wrote a detailed complaint, letters to the board members in administration and received Zero response from anyone but they stated that they did an investigation and nothing happened, no one remembers me, they lied and said there was nothing on the video (which was over 30 minutes of dozens of incidences of abuses towards customers), refused to accept any responsibility. Delta absolutely covered up this ordeal with an entire gate being traumatized and abused by 2 of their employees and then my friend assaulted with her phone being grabbed from her hand and her videos being deleted.

But the departure gate was changed to B15 without any notification. I was consequently unaware of this change and missed my flight. The only notification was the departure screen which is barely readable as it is constantly changing. There were no PA announcements, no text messages, no phone calls, apparently no alerts to App holders, but I don’t fly frequently enough to justify it. My friend who helped me book the flight does, but he didn’t give me any warning either so I was unawares. At least they got me another flight, 4 hours later than my scheduled flight.

review_header: "they were not going to be responsible"
review_text: The value of the suitcase on the market is $180 dollars. When I arrived I immediately claimed at the counter, I showed them the suitcase and they only told me to do it online without receiving any help, they ignored me. Rest for 2 days after you arrive. and I returned to activities in the United States and tried to communicate again and it was impossible. Finally an advisor answered me and the damaged luggage claim page was not working either by cell phone or by a laptop computer. 7 days passed and when I was finally able to make the claim they told me that 7 days had already passed and that for that absurd reason and their platforms were not working they were not going to be responsible for my luggage. They gave me a 100 dollar voucher to travel with them. Who in their 5 senses would travel with that airline after they damage your luggage and then they don't want to pay you for the suitcase and you have to put your money to buy another one when they were the ones who damaged it? DELTA y su persona en una etapa del proceso rompió mi equipaje que iba ubicado en la bodega del avión mientras cursaba un vuelo Internacional con la aerolínea en mención. El valor de la maleta en el mercado es de $ 180 dólares. Cuándo llegué enseguida reclamé en el counter les mostré la maleta y sólo me indicaron que lo hiciera en línea sin recibir ayuda de ningún tipo, se desntendieron. Decanse los 2 dias luego de que llegue. y retorné actividades en Estados Unidos y volví a tratar de comunicarme y fue imposible. Finalmente me contsetó un Asesor y la página de reclamación de equipaje averiado no estaba funcioando ni por ceclular ni por un computador Laptop. pasaron 7 dias y cuando finalmente pude hacer la reclamación me cotestan que ya pasaron 7 días y que por ésa razón absurda y sus plataformas no funcionaban no iba a responder por mi equipaje. Me dieron un bono de 100 dolares para viajar con ellos. ¿Quién en sus 5 sentidos viajaría con ésa aerolinea despues de que estropean tu equipaje y luego no te quieren pagar por la maleta y debes tu poner de tu dinero para comprar otra cuando fueron ellos quién la dañaron?
Terrible service, employees don’t care and super frustrating that I will need to sue for such a small issue that they are unable to fix.

On 30th June, Delta cancelled our flight and couldn’t get us on another flight for 3 days. I have emailed them multiple times trying to get my expenses refunded and it’s been 2.5 months and I’m not even close to getting a resolution. Our boarding was delayed and when we got on the plane it was discovered a passenger with the same name as somebody on our flight, but who was meant to be flying on another airline, had made their way onto our flight (don’t even get me started on how much of a security risk that is, that’s a whole other issue!). As the flight to Johannesburg is 16 hours, the extra delay meant a crew member would’ve been over their hours if the flight took off (again, don’t even get me started on how you can schedule so that small delay can cause this). We sat on the plane for 3 hours before being told the flight was cancelled and to go to customer service in the airport to rebook our flight. Imagine hundreds of passengers at 1am with 3 customer service agents trying to get onto other flights. We were also on the phone to customer service at the same time as queuing. There were flights available with partner airlines but they wouldn’t put us on any of those, I assume because it would’ve been very expensive last minute. Eventually after hours of queuing and being on hold on the phone they said the next flight would be 3 days later. So now we are stuck in Atlanta for 3 days. I live in Cayman Islands and my sister lives in NYC. Even though my sister and I are not booked on the same ticket they expected us to share a room. I said that I wanted my own room and I was eventually given my own voucher. We got to the hotel after nearly 24 hours of no sleep only to be told that the hotel was full and that delta daily sends delayed passengers with no regard that the hotels are fully booked. We then had to walk with all out luggage to another hotel. When we got to the second hotel they said my sister had a voucher for 3 nights but mine was only for 1 night. So I was forced to share with my sister. What if she wasn’t with me? I would’ve had to pay out of pocket for a hotel room (which I wouldn’t be refunded for because delta is doing everything possible not to refund me). The hotel was also really far away, there was only fast food in the area so we had to Uber everywhere. Of course the airline won’t refund us for any of that. Not to mention that we had to entertain ourselves for the 3 days and I was completely unprepared for 100 degree weather as I was traveling to South African winter. This meant I had to buy new clothes. The cost of the delay is hundreds of dollars but they would only refund my sister $125 and they are delaying processing mine. Two and a half months later and I still don’t know how, when and how much my refund will be. I feel like delta is using constant delay tactics so they don’t have to pay me the refund. Also, absolutely no mention of any compensation for a 3 day delay which resulted in us missing a family event and we didn’t get to see our aunt who had been unwell and passed away shortly after. In all this the Delta staff have been completely unhelpful. The person who has been dealing with my refund keeps asking me for a tax number which we haven’t got in the Cayman Islands as we don’t have tax. I have told them 3 times that we don’t have it and they just keep telling me to ask my bank.

review_header: "not one offer of a drink or snacks"
review_text: Decent breakfast served immediately after take off by an efficient attendant. Following that there was no service at all. For over 4 hours there was not one offer of a drink or snacks. I guess if I had rung the call bell I could’ve got something but it was pretty surprising not to have a single walk through by the guy. When I went to the rest room he was snoozing on the jump seat. In addition no seat belt/ back check before landing. The guy in front of me had his seat reclined for touch down. So not just service, but safety issues. Not ok! Not an inexpensive ticket either.

A full meal was served by an efficient and friendly flight attendant. The entertainment, seat comfort, and service (including baggage delivery) were all excellent. Literally nothing to complain about. An unusual pleasant trip.

JAX depart time was suppose to be 7:10 AM and arrive in ATL at 8:23 AM. Depart time in ATL was suppose to be at 9:01 AM and arrive in YUL at 11:39 AM. Due delays in JAX, we only arrived in ATL at 8:45 AM instead of 8:23 AM. With this being said, I missed my connecting flight from ATL to YUL because of delays in JAX and we also got stuck in ATL tarmac for another 10 minutes before the aircraft got connected to the aerobridge. While running through the aerobridge to catch my connecting flight, I was also preparing my boarding pass on my phone and there it says, "we are sorry you missed your flight" and the Delta was offering an alternative flight with a layover for 12 hours. It asked me to accept the proposal which I did not hoping that I'd find another earlier flight. To my disappointment, all the flights they had for ATL to YUL was from 9:00 PM with arrival time of 11:49 PM. After rechecking my phone again, Delta rebooked me for the 9:00 PM flight with arrival time of 11:49 in YUL. I didn't have a choice in this situation so I had to sit all day and long hours (12 hours in total) at the airport. Airport was so crowded and hot and humid and food was expensive. I will never fly Delta again and never take Atlanta airport for layover or connecting airport. This was my worst travel experience ever.
I was forced to endure a 12-hour flight with no entertainment at all. The airline’s response was to offer me a $50 credit towards a future flight. What a joke!

review_header: “tried to call Delta but was left on hold”
review_text: When I picked up my carry-on that they forced me to check due to space, a wheel was completely missing. It was 3:30 AM my time and I could not find any Delta Reps for me to show it to in baggage claim. I had to struggle with the bag out of the airport, to the rental car, to the hotel and back again on the return trip. I had a busy schedule of college visits on only a few hours sleep. I tried to call Delta several times, but was left on hold for long periods. I was not able to get through to Delta until after 24 hours had passed, so they would not replace the luggage they broke. Delta asked me to fill out a baggage complaint with pictures and still denied to fix the baggage. It is not fair that they made it so difficult for me after they forced me to check my bag and then broke it. Who has time to sit on hold for at least 20 minutes, especially while traveling.

after calling delta regarding this issue the lady I spoke with was either not listening to me or didn't understand my situation. She kept telling me there was nothing on my account regarding a service animal, I know that, that is why I was calling because no one was reviewing my paperwork. instead she kept insisting my "comfort animal was not allowed on flights" only service animals. I have to repeat to multiple times, my service dog was not a EMA. Overall she was unhelpful and ignorant toward the end. I needed help with my service animal paperwork getting reviewed and instead she wanted to try to tell me the difference between an emotional support animal and service animal. Delta is the first airline I have had to deal with so much issues regarding my service dog. I have flown many domestic and international Arlines over the years and Delta has been by far the worst when it comes to dealing with service animals. I ended up having to go to the airport with my paperwork hoping they were able to add it to my reservation. After this experience I will not be flying Delta again as my service dog paperwork is still not on my account and I had to submit it again for my return flight.

Delta did nothing to get me on one of those flights. In addition, I have had to call the airline FIVE separate times to correct issues or make changes because their website wasn’t working. This has put me on hold for up to 2 hours trying to do something as simple as change a seat or ensure my pre-check number was added (an issues they never resolved). Choose any other airline and you will have a better experience.

review_header: "wont be flying with Delta ever again"
review_text: Crew member sees me, rolls his eyes, and after i ask him for a flight update due to storm he says “do i look like a weather station?” Then at check in, i have my hands full, watching my child, and we have 3 tickets. He took & scanned the tickets of people before me, but tells me “lets be self sufficient” and makes me scan the tickets myself, then turns to spouse behind me and says “you got a problem?” I cannot express how purposively this crew member was trying to make us start an altercation. He also did that fake “i appreciate you” statement with the most condescending tone, i did an audible mmmmmm back, and he started saying things behind my back, not loud enough that i could hear it, but loud enough to know he was being rude. It was awful to have a person use their job authority to be maliciously hostile knowing they will have no repercussions. we wont be flying with Delta ever again.

First my customer representative at the Airport did everything they could to ensure my bag made it to my destination over the course of my 48 hour flight delay. This delay was so long that I missed an important meeting at my destination. The most disappointing part is you have very highly paid executives and a CEO making 32million in one year. All of this is on the backs of customers like us trying to get ahead with what opportunities we have once we get to where we are going. Which I didn't.

She was just rude, inconsiderate, cold and unhelpful. We had a party of 6 travelers and when I pushed my sisters wheelchair to the desk to see her if we could possibly be seated together or near each other, she very rudely said there’s was nothing she could do. She just finished assigning all of the seats and did the best she could. When we boarded the plane 2 hours later, there were several completely empty rows. Clearly Iris didn’t want to be bothered with helping us. She should not be in customer service.

We booked with American Airlines and got out of there. We submitted a refund to Delta for the flight they cancelled and could not get us rebooked and they DENIED the claim! Delta Airlines is the Worst Airline in America! Don't Fly Delta!

They cancelled my flight which caused a major financial burden while stuck in expensive gloomy Seattle. I was told that my luggage was flown back to Atlanta. I get to Atlanta by way of a reputable airline and was referred to a small holding room where my luggage was told to be. The luggage holding room did not have my luggage and the employees are rude and unprofessional. No one can account for my luggage even though the airport is heavily surveillance?  I’ve written about 10 complaints dispersing them to Delta, DOT, Federal Aviation and Federal Department of Transportation. I am extremely angry, no follow-up or compensation along with no accountability for my luggage and valuables. I completed a claim and several complaints, with no follow-up.

One in particular kept making smart comments over the intercom repeatedly will on delta 1147 flight. From Chicago to Atlanta Ga. Repeatedly telling me to move my bags when they were out of the way 3 -4 times. I was already nervous & she made the worse of my life.

First flying from Rochester NY why did Delta have me flying backwards to JFK when I was traveling to the West Coast? My flight was booked, then canceled, then rebooked then canceled, then rebooked, only to cancel again, thus making me three days late for my vacation. I spoke with one of the flight crews regarding traveling into JFK and they said what ever you do, don't get stuck in JFK. I was really looking forward to getting away on vacation and Delta acted like they just don't care. Terrible customer service and not sure I want to fly anywhere for a while.

Approx 5 hours before take off, a text of cancellation due to weather. Although was to be my 1st flight, I'm not stupid. I did notice I was one of maybe 15 seats taken. They claim weather related. Ok. Fine. Weather was iffy at best. I booked a bus for as much money being last minute. Fast forward to Saturday eve ..... another text, we regret to inform you your flight from Lag-Syr is canceled. Definitely not worth their time to fly just a couple of people because the weather was fine. I was near Lag Saturday night and even during the rain, planes were taking off constantly. Another hit in the pocket for a last minute bus to Syr. I will stay grounded and forever stick with the bus (Flixbus) or Amtrak, both of whom got me to my destinations.

Cancelled our connecting flight while we are on the plane. Staff is absolutely no help and the compensation is not even good. Not only us, several flights cancelled with people sleeping outside their help desk for two days. An absolute disgusting and rude and unorganized airline don’t ever fly with them. Line for the help desk took 2 hours+.

I felt like an inconvenience and bother to him, rather than a valued customer. No beverage service on the flight because “not enough time.” On the positive side, they didn’t charge for head phones or carry on. Just disappointed overall, nonetheless.

The last time I flew on Delta was probably in May 2020, but this review thing would not let me choose that far back. I have an upcoming flight next week and need to change my return ticket to a different airport as there was a death in our family this week. I've been trying to get a hold of someone at Delta's customer service for many hours. I keep getting a wait time of over 2 1/2 hours to speak to a representative by phone. I can't remember my Delta.com password and attempted to change my password. It wasn't sending me the email to change the password and by the time it did, I was locked out of my account requiring me to provide verification of identity to get back in; however, it was suggested that I wait 24 hours to try again. That is absolutely ludicrous. Thankfully the funeral isn't for another two weeks; however, it is super frustrating that I have to wait that long to get back into my account and even then, it is not a guarantee. I'm super frustrated that I can't talk to a person on the phone for help. I tried via a chat and part way into the conversation with a real person, they weren't responding very quickly, even though I provided all the information they needed (confirmation number, flight information for what I want to change to, my name that is on the itinerary, etc.). I asked if they could call me instead, but then they told me to call them. I had been trying to do just that for a long time and it was getting me nowhere. I'm super overwhelmed and stressed out right now because of this situation and explained that it is due to a death in the family. They could have been way more helpful and caused a lot less stress and anxiety on my end in this delicate situation. This is the third family death for us this year. Why couldn't the CS representative just call me back? They have my number. Eventually that person set up the chat on a bot. At the time, I had no idea what that meant. The bot was not helpful at all as it kept saying it didn't understand what I was telling it, even though I gave it the same information as the live person on the chat. I generally don't have many issues with Delta, and it is my preferred airline to fly on. This is by far the worst experience with Delta that I've ever had. I'm now tempted to drive to the airport myself before my upcoming flight and talk to someone there in person. Why do airlines have to make their websites and logging into your account and/or password reset, etc. so difficult?

Who launches a faulty update at the peak of the summer travel season & then states that they bear no responsibility for the catastrophic repercussions of such? I spent a year & $40K planning the one & only large gesture birthday I will ever have the opportunity of giving my 85-year-old mother. Her dream was to experience an Alaskan Cruise with friends & family. I managed to put together a group of 11 people but could not have possibly anticipated that Delta would become not only the touchstone upon which this event depended but also the destroyer. This was my first & last cruise experience, and the entire travel experience was so deplorable I don’t ever want to leave my house again. I booked my mother and her 2 equally elderly sisters on a direct flight from Orlando to Seattle the evening before the cruise, just in case there were any delays, they should have had enough time to make the ship. On the morning of the 19th of July at 9am PST while walking my dog I learned of the issues with the “Global IT outage”. I ran home, checked the Delta flights & found them cancelled. There was NO notification of this change. I immediately tried calling, messaging & accessing Delta’s website. I sat at my kitchen table for 11 hours that day with 2 computers & 3 phones unable to reach anyone. I was on hold for 7 hours until the call dropped. Delta’s chat bot kept asking if I “was still there” and every time I responded “yes” it gave me a longer wait time for a representative than the previous estimate. I called my mother & her sisters and told them to get to the airport as quickly as possible, this was something they would have to solve in person at a Delta Counter. Technology was the problem; I could not help them from California via computer or phone. It was already afternoon in Florida. They arrived at the Orlando airport with their luggage at 3pm and stood in line for hours only to have the Delta agent turn them away with a flyer of useless information redirecting them to use Delta’s app or website. Neither functional, nor is it appropriate to expect 80 year old ladies to navigate a digital world. They returned to the Delta Counter but were told repeatedly that Delta could not rebook them on another flight and that they had to go to other counters and sort it themselves only to be told at both Southwest & Alaska that Delta had the responsibility of rebooking them. These ladies dragged their bags across the airport until 11pm that evening. In total they were turned away from the Delta counter 3 times & ultimately unable to arrive in Seattle in time to make the sailing. This is the most egregious failure to meet a Contract of Carriage I have ever experienced. When Frontier can go old school and pull out paper tickets in order to meet their contract of carriage but Delta chooses to strand & abandon ALL clients it is clear who is the better carrier. We arrived at the Seattle port Saturday morning to spend 2 hours waiting for Princess Cruise lines to agree to allow our ladies to board in Juneau as apparently this is a violation of some maritime law creating more fines & distress. If I haven’t been clear the entire point of this Holiday was to celebrate the person left stranded in Orlando, whom I disgracefully booked on Delta. My financial losses are such: Last minute one way flight to Juneau $ 2547.99 Unused Seattle Hotel $ 347.23 Last minute Juneau Hotel $

review_header: "intrusive check of my person and luggage"
review_text: The entertainment system was not working the whole flight. But the flight attendant Michael was very personable. Before the flight I was subjected to a very intrusive check of my person and luggage. I have flown hundreds of times on many airlines to and from many destinations and only on this route with this airline have I been treated like a suspect. This time I was asked strange questions at check in, like what are my hobbies? Where did I stay? Who did I see? , etc. The time a few years ago they took me in a room and went though all my luggage with a fine-tooth comb then went through it again at the gate! Almost missed my flight. This time, they didn't go though my checked bags but I was subjected to a thorough inspection of my carry on and had to remove my shoes (none of the other passengers had to do this). I became quite irate but the attendant there at the gate  remained calm and did tell me that they had detected a suspicious substance on my hand when they did that swab thing. Later, researching the substance I found it frequently is mistakenly confused with a component in hand lotion (glycerin). But I wonder why this has not happened to me on any other airline and, frankly, on any other Delta flight, though most of my flights on Delta have been domestic.

The problem is the complete lack of support during and afterwards. Under EU rules, the delay means they owe me 1200 euros under EU261. There is literally no way to get a human to handle this request, and the computer system is a black hole that keeps throwing my complaint away. The flight was fine, but the organization, and dependence on a computer system black box, makes for a terrible experience.

It was hot in the plane due to the issues. The issues were fixed. The legroom on the plane was terrible, I had to walk around on the plane so my legs could stretch out. Also, the turbulence was so strong, two food carts fell over. To top it off, a dog was walking down the aisle of the plane during the flight.
Additionally, our request light was on, and no flight attendant was seen at all. We left the flight without knowledge of the number of our baggage carousel.

They have partners like Latam and I flew by Latam. THEY DON'T TELL YOU THIS TRICK or robbery but when you fly with the partner, they will steal your miles blaming the partner company in my case is LATAM. They said to me that miles are based in the price that you pay AND NOT THE DISTANCE THAT GOOGLE EARTH PRECISELY TELL US. I really flew 12,326.24 MILES and they deposited into my account ONLY 4,855. Is missing 7,471.24 lots of miles stolen from me. All the other airlines works with distances which is what makes sense. But Delta is different they said that is based in what you paid for which doesn't make any sense in distance, an YES they found another way to rob you.

When we dropped her off to go back home, she was told that she could not fly for the next two days. The agent was very rude. No one let us know that the flight was overbooked. It is a two-hour drive to the airport, and she missed two days of work. I will never fly Delta again.

I found out via email upon waking up a few hours before the airport. There were no alternatives from/by Delta to get me to the wedding I planned to attend that day at destination. Both chat and phone agents were practically unreachable. Ultimately, I had to pay up a very significant amount and much more for a very last minute flight on another carrier out of my personal pocket. Delta provided zero compensation for this last minute cancellation.

A clear weather issue, some time they have no cabin crew or captains. They work like the really don't care what their passengers are going through. Simply don't have any words to express here. Good luck Delta - will see you guys filing bankruptcy soon if your service works like this.

I was bummed but understand it's related to the IT fiasco. What is not  related to the CrowdStrike problem is how Delta treated us! First, the gate agent announced the cancellation and then immediately left! Offered no help other than to say we should find a help desk to rebook. Stood in line for 3.5 hours only to have them tell me there are no fights for 4 days. When I asked to change my flight to 8/4, she told me no, they would only book within the week! I also couldn't get a hotel voucher because every hotel in the area is booked. Went to get my checked bag and after another hour in that line, we were all told that they would not be getting any more bags until 6:30am (this was now midnight) because they were too far behind with all the cancelled fights. After 5 more hours of waiting for them to get my bag, I was told they can't find it. They won't report it lost yet, they said they just can't find it and I need to wait longer! I can't believe they get away with treating customers like this. Delta used to be the only airline I trusted. I am shocked at their mishandling and complete lack of compassion. Oh wait, they did come through the line with water and animal crackers for us. Seriously Delta??? You should be ashamed!!!

I waited at my gate for 6 hours and they continuously delayed my flight and then cancelled it. I was then sent to the ticket desk where I was REFUSED a refund when I could not take the next flight out 2 days later. They were very rude and unhelpful and I have never in my 21 years of flying experienced anything of the sorts. I cannot believe the terrible customer service.

Horrible customer service in the LAX airport. Stayed in the line for 6 hours. Supervisor Omar even scared me with calling police regardless that i was with little baby stand in all day in the line because they had delayed and nobody could tell me if my flight is changed to other or no i just wanted to know what to do And left the desk telling us to go to the line again (6 hour line). Worst experience ever. Under his supervision when there were 100 people waiting were working only 3-4 desks however there were more then 10. Not giving any concrete answer to any question what to do when to come. Stayed in separate 4 lanes no any support solved the issue. Only one guy helped us after all day staying in different lanes before even they didn't know where who should stand

So waiting 4 hours in line meant nothing because I didn't scan their QR code since they didn't have any staff making anyone aware in line that there was a QR code that needed to be scanned. Worst customer service, all the employees were unhelpful and unempathetic, out of hotel vouchers and employees telling mothers in front of me that their children will have to sleep on the ground of the airport.

Never even took off. This is the 3rd time this year where there was no pilot. Flight got canceled and our bags were lost at the airport we never even left from. Delta is a joke and I’m cutting up my delta Amex card.

5 hrs prior to flight departure that plane had been delayed 30 minutes without an explanation. Our connecting flight was only 1 hr reducing it 30 minutes. We later landed late for our connecting flight resulting in a missed connection by multiple passengers. Airline offered a flight 18 hours later without any accommodations, coverage of meals, etc. Deltas only solution was a $50 voucher for each passenger for a future flight. Why would I fly with a company that can’t get it right the first several times? After talking with other passengers who had missed their connection, we found out this is a daily occurrence on this particular route as they and us had experienced the exact same thing on our outbound flight just didn’t miss our connection as we were waiting on a pilot.

We waited for everyone to leave the plane post landing to not hold up the line with getting our bags out with a sleeping toddler. The plane landed 10 mins early at 9:50am. After everything was clear, I started getting my 3 carryon bags ready while giving my sleeping toddler to my mother to hold. Immediately the flight attendant rolled her eyes and said, “are you done yet?” I paused after gathering my things and said “I had a sleeping child on my lap, I couldn’t move.” The flight attendant disrespectfully responded, “we have a time to follow.” I proceeded to take out all 3 carry on bags by myself as she stood there and watched. I felt greatly disrespected and unfortunately don’t feel safe flying Delta as they are not conducive to young families who are traveling. I’m disgusted and appalled, my toddler was upset and crying after all the commotion.

We were late for our flight and left in Montreal. Then a representative threatened to not put me on a flight at all. No one from Delta was even around to ask for help after an hour. An airport rep had to find a Delta employee. Online and phone support was useless. It wasn't until I was back in the US did they even want want to help. Don't fly Delta! They ruined a great trip.

The flight is over 10 hours. On the flight to Atlanta we were fed one very small meal at the start of the flight and then an inedible soggy, partially cooked pizza pocket towards the end of the flight. The flight left late and on arrival we spent an hour getting through security to transfer to our Nashville flight. We had one tiny bowl of pasta in over 13 hours. This was a day time flight and was sold as a full service flight, yet we were hardly fed. Delta should advise economy passengers to bring their own food.  The return flight was an overnight flight so the paucity of food did not affect us so much. But on this flight my husband's entertainment screen did not work, although one staff member did try to rectify this. The lady who checked us in in Nashville was slovenly and unkept. Her hair was all over the place and not brushed and her clothes were too small and not ironed. Generally, the flight staff were badly presented (sadly, the uniform does them no favours), rude and appeared to have no pride in their work. They just shoved the meals at passengers and gave the impression that we were an inconvenience. I have travelled on many airlines and have never seen such scruffy and grumpy flight attendants. In contrast, the gentleman who checked us in at Zurich Airport was professional, well presented, helpful and friendly.

Due to technical issues with flight, staff started deplaning people because at the time of boarding, Flight captain said that there was problem with tyre. 1 hour later, staff informed that we will switch to another plane. We took off at 10 when plan was supposed to leave at 7:21 PM. I lost my next connecting flight, so had to stay in Atlanta overnight. Airline gave option for meal and motel, so kind of them but they don't have wisdom to understand that many people travel for business or work. And for them, meal voucher, motel is not priority but Time is priority.  Next day flight again delayed from 9:16 am to 10 Am. Great. Then that Front desk staff asked me to get my Duffle bag tagged because there is no space in cabin. I explained to him, that this is not hand carry, a duffle bag, can fit under my seat as its soft and can fit in little space. First of all, he acted stubborn, yelled at me, closed the entry door and called security on me because I am not giving my bag to tag, even I explained that I am scared that I will get my bag damaged. As 2 months ago, They mishandled my hand carry , broke wheels and damaged my stuff inside. I had to literally drag that heavy hand carry.  Flight attendants never had problem with me to put that bag under seat. What was the point of all this fuss.

review_header: "disrespect of an employee of your company"
review_text: The plane landed in Atlanta early, but it took them about an hour to open the door. I was very worried because I didn't want to miss my connecting flight to Greenville, SC. ​​I saw a couple with a baby pass by my seat looking for the exit and I went after them. At that moment, one of the flight attendants arrives and yells at me loudly and in a disrespectful tone, "Ma'am! Where do you think you're going?" He took my suitcase from me, I explained the situation to him, but he continued to be furious and yelled at me to go to your seat and something else that I don't remember. I was in row 28, in row 26 there was a lady, who I believe works for the airline, because 80% of the time during the flight she was standing and talking and laughing with the flight attendants. When I passed my seat, the lady also in a contemptuous tone yelled at me "where do you think you're going, mommy!" and I replied, "I think you look prettier when you're quiet," and I continued to my seat. The lady in seat 26 and those in row 27 began to make fun of me for the situation. I didn't say anything. I'm not a person who fights, and I'm also a person over 67 years old. You can't imagine how bad I felt as a person, being the laughing stock of so many people, because of the disrespect of an employee of your company. I never want to fly again with your company, I can't understand what training your employees have, what's going on with human resources?

They offered a credit on a future flight (!?!). This has never happened to me in 30+ years of international travel. We had to get to our destination that day. In the taxi, I was able to book tickets on another airline, leaving from another airport. Needless to say it was expensive to do so. Plus, getting from the first airport to the second meant a taxi fare of almost $200 USD. We phoned and insisted on a refund rather than the credit. The agent we spoke to did provide the refund. Nevertheless, I will not book with Delta again.
We had some laughs and she gave us some great snacks. Airlines need good people like Linda. We were on flight 4991.

This was due to the absence of a pilot and an assistance team. They were unable to help or do anything about it but offer us a hotel to sleep in until tomorrow if they bump us on another flight. This is the worse airline ever.
However The seats are awful, my bottom is bruised and still numb - got off the plane 8 hours ago.

Cabin crew was very friendly. Clean nice trip. Excellent service and food. Worth the money! Arrived earlier than we scheduled. Cons: The endless walking to the gates. Old movies. The airport Delta staff in Boston’s check in on the 27th of March 2024. Checking in for JFK -> Greece. This male replying to our questions with “I don’t know” or pretending not to hear us (didn’t even respond to my hello). Although one of our luggages was underweight by 5 pounds, he wouldn’t give it back to us so we could put things from the 2nd suitcase which was 2 pounds overweight. It was standing right there next to him! I can’t he replied because I would have to weigh it again! I didn’t say a word. I regret it. I had to carry the suitcase away from the counter to stuff a jacket from it, in my back pack (to reduce those 2 pounds) cause I was blocking the line when no one was behind me waiting. I have never been spoken/treated to so rudely in my life and did not answer any of my questions on how to make my 100$ bill in change since he would not accept a 100$ bill. I hope more people make complaint’s about this fellow.

The online check-in was successful and I got a digital boarding pass. Upon arrival at the airport, I checked with a Delta staff at the counter and was told that my digital boarding pass was good enough and no additional check-in was needed. I went through security check and all gates successfully. However, when I lined up to board the plane, I was told that my boarding pass didn’t work and asked me to wait. I waited for a long time until the very end, because no staff was paying attention to passengers who needed to be cleared up. Finally, they checked their system and said I didn’t check in. I told them I have checked in online, otherwise I would not have a boarding pass. They showed a very impatient attitude and kept repeating that I didn’t check in. I didn’t want to argue and asked if they could check me in. They kept giving that bizarre attitude and a look that I didn’t know what I was doing. Shouldn’t they feel sorry for what their customers experienced? I was annoyed by their attitude and frustrated how messy Delta’s systems were. The staff was impatient and their arrogant attitude was unacceptable. I finally scanned my boarding pass and complained “stupid airline system”. Then they pulled me back and threatened me that if I didn’t apologize then they would take me off that plane and had me wait longer for the next flight. I was very angry but I did want to get back home. So, I apologized to them. Then they threatened me further that if take my attitude to the plane or they would take me off the plane. Wow, I don’t even have the right to be angry, given the way I was treated? Delta, your system is completely messed up. As a customer, I didn’t do anything wrong by checking in online but I was accused by the staff of not being responsible for checking in. Your messy system is not your customers’ fault. If your system is not capable of doing online check-ins, then don’t even ask your customers to do that. The staff abused their authority to threaten customers, forced customers to apologize and even took away customers’ right to be angry.  After I boarded the flight, the gentleman who sat next to me also complained how their seats were messed up and the horrible attitude their family received from Delta’s staff because they had a child who needed special care. I was not given a single smile but were treated with disrespect, impatience and arrogance. I cannot believe this is the level of service Delta.

It fit all of the size requirements. They didn’t explain what was going on and that I wouldn’t see my luggage again until my destination. (I had one layover.) They stuck a tag on it without my knowledge and took my suitcase without my permission.
But the food has gotten terrible. I sat in coach on the way to London, and business class on the way back. The food was the worst food I’ve ever eaten on a plane.

They delay and cancel flights for no valid reason with no refund. I’ve had many bad experiences with Delta specifically at the Houston airport and even the staff doesn’t know what they’re doing and DO NOT update passengers in a timely manner.

review_header: "long time before I fly Delta again"
review_text: We waited 2 hours for this.  Most connecting passengers missed there connections. It will be a long time before I fly Delta again. Not the first time I've been screwed by Delta. I'll fly American!
Our luggage was lost and severely damaged when it was eventually recovered and now they are refusing to make it right. I was given the runaround and eventually just blown off.

We actually made it to the gate after running through the airport with our 3 kids, one of which is a 7 week old infant and were told that they were closing the gate and that we could not get on. We were then stranded at Minneapolis Airport and subject to a $600 per day rental car rate with SIXT because of "supply and demand issues" with rental cars. There was not one single other available rental option in the airport. It was around 2am before we were able to find a decent hotel again due to "supply and demand issues". For the amount of money we paid with Delta for these flights and all of the travel that we've done in the past it is absolutely outrageous that we received the treatment that we did. Delta Airlines is not for the customers and their main focus is not to achieve customer satisfaction. I'd like to emphasize on the fact that they were un willing to offer us 5 minutes extra to board and that they left me and my family stranded with a 7 weeks old infant.

After having an awesome US trip with my son we were looking forward to getting home to Scotland. We arrived in SAN in plenty of time and boarded just 20 min later than scheduled but then sat in the plane on a taxi way for almost an hour with no explanation. Not a great start but then it got worse. On arrival in New York we then sat on the runway for another 2 hours which meant our flight back to the UK had gone. This is where the fun starts. It took over 2 hours to get through on the customer support line where they managed to arrange another flight (2 days later) but were unable to allocate a hotel room due to the late hour (now almost 2AM). The representative advised us to arrange our own accommodation and then claim the costs back by providing the receipts. (This turned out to be a bare faced lie). We finally found a Hotel and arrived at 5am. Unfortunately we now had another 2 days in the US but with our bags stuck in the airport , only the clothes we were wearing and no toiletries we had no option but to get out later that day (after some sleep) to buy essentials (keeping the receipts as advised by Delta of course). Come the day of travel we get to JFK and discover our bags are in Atlanta, 700 miles in the wrong direction on a different plane so when we eventually arrive in London at 2200 we still have no luggage so another overnight stay needed and another hotel bill. I was flying back home to Washington, D.C., from Austin, TX. Due to some issues, the first flight was delayed. There was no way that I would make my connection in Detroit. I was devastated as I needed to get home as soon as possible. I kept looking for other flights, but my missed connection was the night's last flight to IAD. I would have to wait until the morning for the next flight. Unexpectedly, a kind flight attendant approached me on the plane and said, “Hey, I noticed that you missed your connection to Dulles Airport, but I found this delayed flight heading to Reagan Airport. If you don’t mind changing airports, you can be in DC tonight instead of tomorrow morning. Is this something you would like to do?” I immediately said YES! I needed to get home right away, so arriving home 40 minutes after my original flight was much better than waiting until the morning. Upon arrival at Reagan National, I checked with Delta about my luggage. As expected, they were delayed. However, they assured me that my suitcases would be delivered the next day to my house, and they kept their word! What a relief! With everything going on, the last thing I needed was to go to the airport to retrieve my things. And I am so thankful for that. What this flight attendant doesn’t know (because I didn’t ask for a flight change or even mention my situation to anyone. This was just amazing customer service is that she helped me get home on time to be there the last night with my very special recently adopted cat. See, he was special because he was the sweetest cat I’ve ever met; he only wanted to be on my lap all the time and to be petted nonstop. He was blind, and he was my friend’s cat, who unexpectedly passed away in April this year, and I took in my sweet baby. He got very sick and was getting worse by the hour. He was waiting for me to get home. I got home at midnight, and he crossed the bridge Thursday afternoon. Thanks to this kind soul and her outstanding customer service, I was there for him, keeping him company during his last night. And for that, I will thank Delta Airlines forever. From the bottom of my broken heart.

The issue involves the behavior of a flight attendant as well as the conduct of the Minnesota ground staff and Delta supervisors. I was a passenger on flight 2987 from Philadelphia to Minnesota, with a connecting flight to Los Angeles (flight 748). Shortly after takeoff on flight 2987, my three-year-old daughter urgently needed to use the restroom. I explained that my daughter might have an accident in her seat, but the attendant insisted that we return to our seats, even when I asked if it would be acceptable for my daughter to have an accident. Once I identified that the supervisor was not handling the situation professionally, I asked to speak to his superior. As I headed up, the flight attendant and I exchanged words during the situation. However, as I was leaving, the flight attendant continued her uncontrolled unprofessional comments and proceeded to clap her hands four times in a confrontational manner, as if she wanted to fight, in front of other flight attendants and supervisors. This behavior went unaddressed. This experience was incredibly frustrating and distressing for both my daughter and me. I believe the treatment we received was unreasonable and lacked basic empathy, especially considering the needs of a small child. As I waited, the day shift manager arrived and, in a rude manner, ignored me to speak with the flight attendant and her supervisor down below at the plane.  After waiting for about 10 minutes, the manager returned, and I tried explained the entire situation to her but of course she interrupted me the whole time. Without listening to my story or understanding what happened, she informed me that I was banned from Delta flights for my conduct and could not reschedule a flight with Delta and use another airline. Her decision was based solely on the accounts of the flight attendant and the unprofessional in flight supervisor. Let me start by saying that the 24-hour cancellation window is ridiculously short and unforgiving. Life happens, plans change, and sometimes circumstances force you to alter your travel arrangements beyond this restrictive timeframe. However, Delta seems to lack any empathy or flexibility in this regard. Recently, I had to cancel a ticket I had purchased due to unforeseen circumstances. Imagine my dismay when I realized that I had to cancel within 24 hours of booking to be eligible for any refund whatsoever. This policy is not only inconvenient but also entirely unreasonable. It essentially forces travelers into a rushed decision-making process, leaving no room for any change of plans or emergencies that may arise shortly after booking. But the disappointment didn't end there. Upon canceling my ticket, I was shocked to discover that Delta imposed a hefty $99 cancellation fee. To add insult to injury, they offered me a measly $91 refund for a ticket that originally cost $200. It's simply outrageous that Delta sees fit to penalize their customers to such an extent for exercising their right to cancel within the designated timeframe. The $99 cancellation fee policy feels like a slap in the face to loyal customers who have already invested a significant amount of money in their travel plans. It's a clear case of Delta prioritizing profit over customer satisfaction and goodwill. Such predatory practices not only tarnish the airline's reputation but also erode trust and loyalty among passengers.

This flight was scheduled to leave at 1 PM from JFK to Buffalo. It pulled back from the gate. It headed toward the runway, but was turned around and returned to the gate. After waiting 50 minutes with no explanation whatsoever, passengers started getting antsy and asking questions. we were told that there was a piece of equipment mandated by the FAA, that had to be obtained before the plane could leave. We waited an additional 30 minutes. Ultimately, they received a small item that was inconspicuously delivered to a passenger. As it turns out, it was a seatbelt extender. When originally pulling away from the gate, they only had one on board. This particular passenger required a second one. That is what we waited an hour and a half for. It is understood that every person deserves dignity, it is ridiculous to have delayed 90 people a total of two hours, awaiting a seatbelt extender. The passenger requiring this should have been deboarded and placed on the next flight with the appropriate equipment. Additionally, what was most upsetting about this was the deceit. The seatbelt extender was. delivered to the passenger very secretly. The minute it was delivered, we were backed out of the jetway and in a queue of 12 planes to takeoff. Altogether, the delay was 2 to 2 1/2 hours. The flight was a 50 minute flight.
