For the departure flight I was given a seat from Ontario to SLC and to Austin Texas. However in my return flight there is no seat assigned either to SLC from Austin or SLC to Ontario. Then I have noticed the available seats have to be sold to passengers who wanted to upgrade, then the left overs will be assigned to a passenger like myself who got the last seat. What is going on in this airline just to profit is not fair. I have noticed there is no respect nor acknowledgement to the passengers booked for economy class. If you charge $533 for economy class Delta airlines should accommodate accordingly. You cannot just toss us to the last row because you have to make more money. Very disappointing. The person who is checking in to the aircraft whose name is Eve didn’t even want to assign me a seat. She kept giving me the run around telling me my name is in the board which wasn’t the whole time. I’m disgusted with this airline and will never book a flight with.

review_header: "impression is of a poorly run airline"
review_text: We had booked to fly from Atlanta to Dublin but ended up having our flight delayed 2+ hours. During the delay, the Delta desk agents would not answer any questions about the cause of the delay or how long the delay would be. The staff overall seemed to not know what was going on and even later stated that they "needed to go see what was going on" before they would be able to provide a departure time. Overall, the impression is of a poorly run airline, with staff that were unable or unwilling to answer any questions.

They refused to turn on the air conditioning while they made us wait for 40 minutes in the miserable cabin. Not only did they not turn on the air one of the flight attendants went onto the overhead speaker and yelled at us for asking. They have not offered water either. They also sold me a ticket in which it said I would be able to have a carry on. They ended up making me check it, they are making me go to the baggage claim to get it, and there was no compensation. This is a miserable airline and I would not recommend this to anyone.

review_header: "yet to receive a snack or beverage"
review_text: It was turbulent for 10 minutes after taking off, so the snack n beverage service was delayed and I understand. However, they started and got from first class to row 24 and stopped, no turbulence Then when they began again they started in first class again and stopped at front of main cabin. Now it’s 1:20 later and they are only at row 15! Not only slow on uptake, but very rude to serve some rows 2 or 3 times, while the rest of us are within anything Dinner hour and free is choice of 4 snacks or $12 or $10 purchase offerings. I get that weather delayed inbound

Mediocre at best. Seat etc was fine but so much was not. To start, some( not all) of the crew was grouchy or impersonal. A few were great. Second, at the gate free fast Wi-Fi was announced, neither was true. Once we crossed the coast line wi fi shut off for the rest of the trip.The crew insisted that was normal but considering on the same flight(reverse direction) same type aircraft we had full service, that just wasn’t true. One crew member quie2tly agreed and didn’t understand. In any case at least half the fee should be refunded (good luck to me.) The food was mediocre at best.In between the meal and snack only chips and cookies were available (10 1/2 hour trip) IFE was fine. I guess real complaint was a majority of crew who wanted to be anywhere else.

Because these are the old LATAM jets with 2-2-2 seating I was expecting a second rate trip. I was wrong. Seat was more comfortable than Delta Suites for sleeping. Crew was great. Warm and proactive service from start to finish. Skipped dinner 1130pm departure) so I  could sleep but breakfast 1 1/2 before landing was quite good. Didn’t watch anything but wi fi was great. Arrived early, everything was perfect.

review_header: "first class was good except the crew"
review_text: Their first class was good except the crew, never said hi or anything nice. They just grunted a lot to us. I know it is a hard job for them.

Our flight was not delayed, I got free access to the Delta Sky Club and I didn’t even have a membership. The economy seat was super comfortable, and we got seatback entertainment. They offered earplugs, and headphones to listen to the back entertainment. It works super well. There were so many options to choose from. They were passing out dinner. But I just got a cranberry cocktail And some cookies. We had the smoothest landing I have ever seen. If you haven’t flown Delta before, I recommend it on your next trip. The staff are super kind, on time, departure, and arrival, and it really feels like your first class in economy. The only thing that I recommend out for is the prices. For example, I flew around Christmas time, which is pretty expensive for Delta airlines. So if you want to fly, Delta, fly around February. That’s the best prices to fly with Delta but other than that, I highly recommen, was very satisfied.

Overnight flight, lie flat seat. Extremely comfortable flight made better by an attentive, friendly cabin crew. On time departure and early arrival. Entertainment was great. Literally nothing to complain about. Solid experience.

review_header: “Delta is refusing to engage with me”
review_text: The flight from Chicago to Detroit got delayed 3 hours, rendering my connecting flight impossible to catch. The only choice they gave me was to take a different flight at a different airport with a different airline. I recognised this new flight from when I was booking flights and it was significantly cheaper than my original. It was, after all, a much worse airline. So I wanted to be compensated for the price difference and the taxi fare to the different airport ($86). Delta is categorically refusing to engage with me on this because it was a "weather delay" and therefore "out of their control." Well it was not in my control either. I paid for a service, I did not receive it. Why should I pay for a service I did not receive? If I go to a steakhouse and order a $500 wagyu steak, but they tell me they're out of the wagyu and instead give me a cheap rubbery $10 steak, then insist on charging me the $500 of the wagyu, that would be grounds for a lawsuit. Why should this be any different?

review_header: "Questioning if I will fly Delta again"
review_text: That is now 6 hours delayed and still with a question mark as the luggage is outside the plane. I complained to them over messages and they lied to me that it was for bad weather and an hour later another airline departed to LA with no delays. Later I convinced the to tell me the “truth” that it was for maintenance issues. Regardless I believe Delta has serious problems with their existing management as last week my niece had the same problem. Their agents or people responding are very polite trying to compensate for the bad experience but the root of this problem is coming from their managers.

Food (roast beef salad) was quite good. Good service in first class. We unfortunately missed our return flight. We arrived at the counter 43 minutes before takeoff, 7 minutes before boarding and were told we were too late and couldn’t check in. The airport was empty. We are TSA pre-checked and priority with purchased first class tickets. There was absolutely no effort  by the counter agent to try to help us on to the flight. Just a shrug. She did try to help us book other flights, which would have been a red eye, losing first class seats and flying coach for a leg for one of us, and cost an extra $2000 per ticket on top of our already purchased first class seats. Thankfully we were able to see on our phone that we could fly first class on American to our destination with a far better schedule for only $1223 each first class. I have never experienced such an utter lack of effort on the part of an airline to get a customer on their flight. Super disappointed in Delta

Both inbound and outbound legs were on A220-100. This is an awesome aircraft very similar to the A220-300. The engines are very quiet and the seats wider than bigger single aisle planes and very comfortable. Overhead bins large enough to accommodate carry on bags. Bathrooms are very spacious more so than on larger B737 or A320s. No delay inbound to BOS; however the outbound flight to DFW was delayed by 2h 30m because of the winter storms. Delta through its mobile app and messaging kept us informed of each and every flight delay update. Although delayed we were glad to be home rather than being stranded in BOS. WiFi worked flawlessly on both flights. Cabin crews were very friendly offering snacks and water periodically throughout the flight. The DFW-BOS nonstop is a new route for Delta and I would definitely fly Delta again.

Wallet was stolen on a trip, and presented ticket and official ID. Was allowed in every airport lounge except Atlanta. Total lack of customer service, inconsistent practices and the workers looked as though they couldn’t care less. RUN. BAD AIRLINE

We arrived at 0530 for a flight to LAX for a cruise. They were so unequipped, the didn’t check the maintenance of their aircraft, chemicals used to de ice the wings and will not give you a refund. We boarded and de-boarded three different planes. The first one didn’t have de-icing for the wings, the second one sat on the tarmac for two hours and was taken to the hanger for maintenance and the final one didn’t have fuel and needed over 10000 gallons to be filled. My family tried to get off and they refused because they had shut the door. We missed our paid for cruise due to their lies, negligence, incompetent management and delay after delay after delay. Delta employees, including the pilot, told us we would make it in time for the cruise. We sat for over 9 hours, our cruise left at 3:30 and we touched down at 3:30. They gave us half of our ticket price, a hotel that was completely booked because of all the delays and the only reason they gave us the vouchers was because it was maintenance problems. If it is the weather causing delay they don't give you anything. We had to pay 400 dollars to fly out, rent a van for 130 for two days of use, buy our own hotel rooms because the one they gave us didn’t have any extra rooms. Today we fly out, scheduled to depart at 7 o'clock and the expected departure is 2300.

Delta's boarding process is chaotic, resembling a free-for-all for the last groups to board. Economy passengers were allowed to board after everyone else. The frustration arises when individuals unrelated to Business or First class board ahead of families. Consequently, families end up sitting apart from each other. I strongly discourage choosing their "Premium Economy," as it doesn't provide the promised better seating. Despite paying extra, we experienced no improvement during our two layovers on the return flight. Business class, First class, and other groups board first, rendering the premium upgrade ineffective. I will never use this airline again. The only positive aspect was the seats themselves. Including TVs would be beneficial as well, especially considering the chaotic situation they have created.

We couldn't take our flight and they emailed and said will issue a full credit back to my bank. But they lied and no refund ever happened. When we asked they ended up giving us an ecredit $400 short of our original payment! Be aware this company will not do what it promises.

I have a physical disability and was offered zero assistance with my bags while other passengers in the exact same position during pre boarding were all offered this help. Before I could ask for help the attendants literally turned their back on me. I was told I couldn’t have my small 3inch by 2 inch bag was too big to keep on my person and/or the seat in front of me and instead the attendant took it from me to place in a “safe place” of her own choosing. I feel this is entirely unprofessional and unnecessary. I fly constantly and have never had any of this happen before. I’ll be surprised if they actually have a wheelchair waiting for me as requested over 48 hours ago after this flight. I will never fly Delta ever again. The attendants are on a weird power trip that has absolutely zero to do with safety or protocol.
In Atlanta we were running to catch their flight to Amsterdam. Worst company ever.

I got tickets from San Diego to Shanghai and it turned to be worst experience ever. I wish I got economy of United or something. In two flights that I had with them they delayed them more than 5 times, that’s a record, not a good one though. My flight from San Diego to Seattle was delayed more than hour and so I got to the gate at Seattle for my Shanghai trip, 10 mins before flight and they didn’t let me in cause the gate was closed. They closed them 15 mins before flight so if they waited 5 mins for me and another travelers, we would’ve made it. They could see the first flight was delayed, the first flight was also delta but they didn’t wait even 5mins. The story gets better: They rescheduled my flight for tomorrow, they offered a 3 star hotel and only one voucher for a meal for 15$. I paid 8k on my ticket and that’s how they treated once I missed my flight due to their technical issues. The day after, I was at the airport for my second flight 3 hours before departure at 11:37am. Guess what? It got delayed! Once to 2pm, once gain to 3:16, and again to 4:20pm!!! All due to maintenance!! Right before boarding for 4:20, they delayed it again to 5:20pm because they didn’t have enough crew! To make it right, they sent out a 15$ meal voucher, how generous! Never fly with Delta! They don’t care about their customers at all.

Now they’re just some regular poor airline like every other poor airline and there’s nothing for platinum members anymore. It’s like they don’t care about anyone anymore only money just like everybody else.

review_header: "a lack of respect for the customers"
review_text: However, I encountered an unexpected time change that resulted in the loss of a day of work and pay. Moreover, my daughter, who was scheduled to pick me up from LAX, also had to call out of work on short notice to accommodate my arrival. This inconvenience not only impacted our schedules but also resulted in a full day of lost wages for both of us. While I understand that unforeseen circumstances can arise, what concerns me is the lack of explanation or communication regarding this time change. As a conscientious traveler, I believe it is essential to be informed of any alterations to the scheduled itinerary, especially when such changes can have a significant impact on personal and professional commitments. Just because the airline may have included it in fine print somewhere does not give them the right to change things without reason or explanation. The unexpected adjustment not only disrupted my carefully planned schedule but also led to an unplanned day off from work, incurring additional costs and inconveniences. Despite my attempts to call, I was put on hold for hours, and every time someone picked up, they transferred me to someone else without offering any explanation for deciding to switch my flight. This lack of communication not only created other inconveniences but also resulted in additional expenses. I believe this shows a lack of respect for the customers.

Delta didn’t give me any options just offered to refund me. Not even able to reach an actual person to talk to, only AI available. I am currently still stranded and Delta just send me a message saying that they had no alternative. I bought my ticket at delta website
Stuck in Seattle for hours. Reliability is key when traveling. I will avoid Delta Airlines and Seattle Airport in the future. Overall lame.

Every single one said it was ok. Ticket counter refused to take the dog and told me sorry while smiling in my face. They couldn't care less that I now need to cancel my ticket, find a hotel room during Christmas weekend, rent a car and find a shipper for a dog. Thanks Delta for all the Christmas joy.

review_header: "take some class on how to treat passengers"
review_text: Today however DL5219 departing LGA 11:49am to Indianapolis for the first time in forever I had gotten up to use the bathroom. I'm at seat 18 can't see if the doors are closed or not so I figured last call to run to use the bathroom it was only 3 rows back. I get the attendant walk over after I get in my seat giving me a speech about how I can't be up when the door is closed. I was humiliated that the whole back of the plane had to know I had to use the bathroom so bad after 2 large ice teas. She kept going about I should have pressed some button blah blah. She could have leaned in and be bit more polite. Her manners do not belong anywhere near ppl.I hope nobody else has to encounter her as she should probably take some class on how to treat passengers. This was the first time I encountered something like that. Hopefully they can correct this.

The next plane left 10 minutes early, and we watched it leave the terminal. When we rebooked, the agent wrote the wrong gate on our tickets. Luckily, we double checked the gate which was a ten minute walk. Thoroughly disgusted with Delta.

My 15 year old son who plays sports, is an A & B student, works Friday nights as a busboy, came to me asking where the gift box from Bath & Bodywork’s went being that he bought this as a gift for his girlfriend. Several of our items went missing (that could not be carried on) and when I filed a complaint with Delta, they stated they cannot do anything about it or investigate as this would be providing me preferential treatment. In the event you are traveling, do not check anything that might be attractive for one to steal. Delta had my luggage delivered within 12 hrs of the flight at 5:38AM where they left personal items on my front porch without a signature. They have to do better on protecting one’s personal items you pay to have delivered - at minimum, offer insurance if they’re going to allow for their associates to remove and steal items from your luggage. Super disappointed. A huge reminder on how not to treat customers…

This was a connecting flight to a flight headed towards PHX with 15 people now running late for a flight. The staff aboard the plane we were on assured us that the other plane knew we were coming and not to worry, and then took a leisurely time taking off making us even later. When we got to SEA we were instructed to run halfway through the airport to our gate, which we did, only to be told that the plane to PHX was departing early without us even when they knew that all 15 of us were on our way. Delta cares more about their punctual reputation than their actual passengers that THEY made late. Now my boyfriend is missing his grandfathers memorial because the next flight to Phoenix is not for another 12 hours and we are stuck in Seattle.

On Saturday, December 2, 2023, I arrived at the airport with only 30 minutes left before my flight was scheduled to depart. I express my most sincere apologies for my late check in and ask them if there is anything they could do to help me out. They were very attentive and instead of telling me you are late; they were fast to ask me and listen to my needs and the personal problem I was going through. They immediately started making phone calls to the point to receive the authorization to allow me to check in and make it to my flight. I want to share my gratitude and appreciation to Nadia and Manuel for going above and beyond their duties to help a customer. Employees like this should be rewarded for their actions. I am eternally grateful due to their actions; I was able to reach my destination on time and spent time with my family in a moment of need. -

The man assigned to the middle seat was moved to my seat. I had no room to move. After a couple hours I became dangerously overheated, began sweating profusely and nauseated. I got up to use the restroom and ended up fainting, falling backwards, injuring my head and neck. I couldn’t safely get up for 20 minutes or more. I was placed back in the same seat for the remaining 7 hours, unable to safely use the restroom. Delta denied responsibility. Stated initially I want on the flight despite hundreds of witnesses. Even the captain was informed. They then stated they had the the right to deny passengers their seats for any reason, even if it results in bodily injury. They also stated they checked the seating logs and determined there were other women on the flight seated in window seats, therefore it was not discriminatory. I was of similar size of the man that was given my seat. My injury required medical attention and therapy. Delta offered me a $100 flight coupon for my “inconvenience “. I was flying alone internationally, I am 60 years old. I am fearful to ever fly alone again.

review_header: "went over and beyond to help us"
review_text: Including everything else to make things go smoothly. Beyond Grateful, God bless you all that do customer service in and out each day! HAPPY HOLIDAYS AND a HAPPY NEW YEAR !
Never, ever again!

review_header: “my screen was not working at all”
review_text: Upon settling in, I noticed my screen was not working at all. My husband tried his and there was no sound as the headphone jack was damaged. We alerted the flight attendant and nothing happened. After 3 attempts one finally tried to reset mine, unsuccessfully. The flight was full so we had no option but to sit in our seats and be the only people on the flight that had no way to watch a movie or follow our route for 8 hours. So much for “Comfort Plus” and the high price we paid for the services we didn’t get. After our trip I tried to reach out to Delta Customer Service. It took 2 hours to reach a human only to be informed they no longer have a live person to talk with and the only route was online which got me nowhere with their “Chat”. I tried several times to file a complaint but my responses were not in the field of answers. I finally was able to file a complaint by not answering questions on the form and got an email from a human that I could now email back and try to describe our experience. Why would they think we’d ever fly with them again as there is the chance that the seats we are assigned could have non working monitors and electronics? What other equipment isn’t working on their aircraft?

We were told to go to the Delta help desk. There has been no one here for forty-five minutes. It is very frustrating! There is a line of people and not one worker trying to help, or get help. Come on Delta! Can’t you do better?

My seat was given to a man to fly comfortably and I was made to fly in his seat, without leg or armroom. A few hours into the flight I became severely overheated, began sweating profusely, and felt nauseated. I got up to use the restroom and ended up passing out cold in the middle aisle. I was only able to get safely up after 20 minutes. I was placed in the same seat without assistance to the restroom. I am a 60 year old women, it was a 9-hour flight, and I myself am not small. In the subsequent fall, I injured myself, requiring nearly 3 months to recover. Delta refused any responsibility or compensation. They would not even refund the cost of the flight. Their representatives first denied I was even on the plane despite a boarding pass and over 300 witnesses. They have also stated they did not discriminate because they had checked and other women were not denied their window seats on that flight. They stated they are able to move you from your seat for any reason, even if it results in injury to the passenger. They stated if I had purchased a first-class ticket perhaps this would not have occurred. Trying to deal with the second-largest airline in the world is impossible. They do not follow international regulations designed to protect passengers and they set up an impossible system when seeking compensation. shifting blame to their partnering airlines, despite being on a Delta flight, with Delta employees. I have had to speak with over 12 employees, supervisors, and others and received only stonewalling, the denial of responsibility, and a lack of any respect, follow-up or concern.
We had a flight diversion due to low visibility. I felt that the pilot made the right call to not land the plane on a dark foggy runway.

This bewildering policy was apparently due to the 'short-haul flight' rule. This sparked a heated debate, during which I felt an unprecedented level of disrespect as a paying customer. Every other airline I've flown with has offered this basic courtesy, often complimentary.  I am  disappointed and disheartened by Delta's disregard for passenger satisfaction. Their staff's dismissive attitude left me feeling belittled. Fly with Delta, and prepare to be overlooked and undervalued. I certainly won't be making that mistake again.

review_header: "I paid for that flight and felt attacked"
review_text: Plane stops, pilots comes on the intercom sorry for the delay, waiting for another plane to leave the gate. No worries. A young woman and her child get up to use the bathroom, they were seated right in front of me. They were allowed to, no problem. I figured, ok I guess that's acceptable. Get up to use the bathroom myself. The flight attendant aggressively demands I return to my seat immediately. This was not a polite nor friendly tone of voice I was greeted with. Where I take issue, is that even though I was standing two feet away from him, he announced this into the intercom to the whole plane. I asked him if he knew he was scolding me over the intercom and he said yes. I returned to my seat through the humiliating stares and laughs of the full plane. I returned after we were at the gate to use the restroom, and extended him the opportunity to apologize which he did not take. I feel that I have the right to privacy in the event a flight attendant needs to give me instructions, especially when Im standing two feet away from them. I had zero interaction with this young man until that moment and provoked him in no way, but felt he punitively used the intercom against me in that moment for no justifiable reason. I filed a formal complaint with Delta and their very tepid response was essentially "oh sorry about that." I paid for that flight and felt attacked

Multiple times I've been booted from a window seat in coach and "upgraded" to a middle seat in economy+ for a 5 hour red-eye booked flight where they were unable to reverse it. Ive had =baggage handlers go through my bags, lose my bags, break my luggage, and am currently sitting on the line with customer service for 2 hours still giving them my flight information after being routed to 4 different representatives. I could have spent less time driving across the country. Not much difference between Delta and Southwest these days, so might as well save a few bucks with another airline. Two hours sitting on hold and I decided to use this time to write my first ever review of a business. Side note: the level of DIY "self service" has also become ridiculous.

As always, the flight attendants can really make the difference. For this five hour trip, the seats were ok, the entertainment offerings were excellent, the food was decent ( especially using today’s lower standards) but the highlight was truly excellent attentive service by Bonnie, the lead flight attendant serving first class (16 seats) pretty much on her own. I’ve taken this flight often and sometimes see a rushed dinner service followed by a disappearing act until hours later. This wonderfully friendly and extremely efficient flight attendant was amazing and made a so so experience quite wonderful. She constantly checked on us leaving us wanting or needing nothing.

review_header: "Why would you separate a family with 2 kids?"
review_text: To make things worse, we were all assigned middle seats so other "single" passengers did not want to switch. Why would you separate a family with 2 kids? We fly out twice a year for vacations. No longer flying Frontier and Spirit. Adding Delta to that list.

Staff members were unhelpful and unprofessional of the delayed flight. Staff was very rude and even laughed at me while asking questions. I asked the  questions respectfully and I am baffled for the unprofessionalism. No one knew how to give direct answers on how to fix their mistake on my delayed flight. Rather received a mockery attitude and much uncertain answers. Save your money and go fly elsewhere please.

They gave me a ticket for May 24th. When I pointed out that it was their error and that they gave me the incorrect ticket, they refused to assist me. I was forced to purchase a fare adjustment to be placed back on the correct flight that I actually purchased. After several commissions through different channels, they have thus far refused to refund the fraudulent fare adjustment charge with no explanation or apology for their neglect and incompetence.

20 on the Nov.3rd 2023 when I bought the tickets, then was charged again for $1486.20 on the 5th. I called Delta after finally getting connected to someone who can speak English, I was told they can't refund me because they only have the ticket numbers I paid for and to call my bank. My bills are passed due now and I have late fees on my rent/phone etc. Will never fly Delta again. Especially after insinuating I was lying when I have my bank statement.
The person at the Delta counter (Kristie) was very helpful in rebooking us. She went above and beyond to get us the best rebook possible. Thank You Delta / Kristie.

However, this was the worst experience in over 35 years of flying. For 839$ (one way!) I got less space and comfort than on Hawaiian Airlines economy. The cabin was ice cold, no seat extension or anything, max 10°reclining possible. I took several pictures, some attaching. I expected an apology or refund, nada. Do not fly Delta.

I have always chosen Delta for its reputation for superior service and reliability, but my recent experience has made me reconsider that choice. To begin with, I was taken aback when, after upgrading to Comfort Class, I was relocated from an aisle seat to a middle seat without any prior notification or choice. Such a switch considerably reduced the comfort level I had anticipated with the upgrade. This was the first sign of my forthcoming ordeal. Upon addressing my concern at the airport, I was given a sheer run-around, being referred from one agent to another, with each passing the responsibility onto someone else. It felt as though my comfort and satisfaction as a customer were not valued in the slightest. My in-flight experience was no better. The flight attendants seemed disinterested and distant, making me feel more like a burden than a valued passenger. My simple request for an apple juice was met with confusion as I was handed a diet coke instead. This may seem like a trivial mistake, but it's indicative of the lack of attention to passenger needs. Moreover, after requesting headsets to perhaps distract myself from the accumulating frustrations, I had to repeat my request. Waiting an hour for such a basic amenity is unacceptable, especially when I could see other passengers receiving prompt service. I had hoped that my upgrade to Comfort Class would ensure a pleasant journey, but I found myself facing a series of disappointments and inconveniences. The lack of coordination, attention to detail, and basic courtesy have left a lasting negative impression. I urge Delta to look into these matters seriously. No passenger should feel as undervalued and disregarded as I did on Flight 800.

Kennedy, Brigit, Robin & Goldie made me feel comfortable and relaxed during my emergency flight to Idaho to see my dying sister. They checked on my well being throughout the flight and stopped by my seat to give me hugs. I'm so grateful for the crew.

This aircraft is comfortable with plenty of legroom; however, the overhead cabins are too small to hold a carry on bag with outside pocket. No delay and smooth flight to LGA. Connecting flight to DFW was on a A220-300. This is an awesome aircraft. If I could fly the A220-300 all the time I would do it. The engines are very quiet. The seats are wider than bigger single aisle planes and very comfortable. The overhead cabins are large enough to accommodate carryon bags. The bathrooms are spacious more so than on larger single aisle planes e.g. B737 and/or A320s. No delay on either leg and the cabin crews were very friendly offering snacks periodically. In flight WiFi worked flawlessly on A220 but was spotty on CRJ 900. I haven't flown DL in quite come time, but I definitely would fly this airline again.

review_header: "It was their system that was bad"
review_text: Air France cancelled my flight and rebooked me with Delta. Things seemed to be smooth as I could select my seat, 1D, and checked on Delta's website that the seat was reserved,  until Delta required me to check-in at the airport. I went to the Delta One section, the check-in agent was very nice and found my reservation, provided to me a boarding pass, only without a seat number. She made several attempts to request for one, but the system only allowed my seat to be assigned at the gate. Not only that, my boarding pass neither showed the class of service nor Sky Priority status, though she ensured me several times that I would be travelling in Delta One. The inconvenience began from there, with the security agent refused to allow me to use the Sky Priority line; not an issue as I was early. I did not get access to the Sky Club; not an issue either as I still could do it with my Amex Platinum card but chose to skip as the Sky Club was packed with a long waiting line. The gate agent finally assigned me a seat, exactly my seat 1D, but only until an hour before boarding. With US carriers having a reputation of dumping passengers for no reason, being through that process is not fun. It got a lot better on board, though not necessarily excellent. Cabin staff were very nice and accommodating. Food was just average in taste, and the whole meal was served on a single tray. I flew Delta One from JFK to Frankfurt a year earlier, and the meal was delicious and was properly served course after course. Not sure why there is such disparity on 2 very comparable routes. The semi-Delta One Suite was more spacious and comfortable than I thought, but it still lagged behind many leading products out there. Why do I still recommend the airline? Because I could see efforts from staff to help me. It was their system that was bad.

I was flying from San Diego to Detroit on Delta. The Delta representative in the boarding was very rude. She made sure to stop me as she said I have three items (backpack, carry-on and small 6x4” crossbody). I had to step out of the lane put my crossbody inside the backpack. I had to lose my flower bouquets (the one my daughter gave me for my birthday) because of my 6x4” crossbody. I’m not sure what was her problem with me, but it was obvious she is not treating everyone equal as three people in front of me, including my husband, had three items with them and she let them go to the plain without saying anything to them. I am very disappointed with Delta staff. Delta was my first stop to shop for flight it will not be anymore for sure. I am using my mileage on the Delta Amex then I will not care about it anymore. You lost a good customer Delta.

During the months of January and February in 2023, I embarked on a series of flights with Delta's partner airlines, which included LATAM, Aerolineas Argentinas, and Saudia. Regrettably, I failed to input my SkyMiles number when booking these flights. Consequently, I had to request mileage credit post-flight, a process that is typically straightforward. However, my experience with Delta proved to be far from hassle-free. Securing mileage credit from Delta proved to be an ordeal that required multiple requests and calls to customer service before any credit was recorded. It was not until September, a full seven months after my initial application, that I finally received mileage credit for the Saudia flights. Astonishingly, during a call with an agent in March, I was told my requests had been “archieved” and thus not acted upon. Then, when I called again in October, the agent advised that they had no record whatsoever that I had put in any request – this despite the fact that the agent in March had advised that my requests were safely in and I need not put them in again. It wasn't until October, following yet another customer service call, that I was granted the deserved credit for the Aerolineas Argentinas flights. However, the same agent informed me that she was unable to credit me for the LATAM flights, citing allegedly missing information in the documents I provided (boarding passes and receipts). In response, I diligently explained via email that all the requisite information was indeed included in the documents, but received no response. When I acquired a letter from LATAM confirming the presence of all necessary details and forwarded it to the agent with a request for confirmation of receipt, I was met with silence once more. Upon reaching out to Delta customer service to follow up, I was met with an abrupt response, being told that I "could not keep calling them," despite this being only my initial follow-up call, and that further contact would supposedly further delay the process. The agent then refused to provide me with any case number or confirmation number for my call – which goes against most customer service protocols. The culmination of these experiences has led me to the unfortunate realization that Delta's customer service falls far short of the expected standards, characterized by contradictory instructions, leading customers on wild goose chases to obtain information already provided, and gaslighting of customers. It appears that this deliberate "intentional friction" is designed with the expectation that customers will eventually abandon their pursuit of rightful mileage credit. Such service is incredibly disappointing for an airline that is purportedly renowned for its high level of customer service in the United States.

The beds were so small and tight that I nor my 2 friends got any sleep. We were so disappointed and really felt ripped off for spending 5 grand on this through princess ezair. You’re so busy trying to saved a buck that you cram in too many seats. It’s a joke to call this business class. Have to fly home November 3. Not looking forward to being up again all night.
Enjoyed meal and snacks provided. The inflight entertainment was good. The seats were very close and there is not much leg room.

And now after applying for reimbursements and being with them on Hold I got this email from Delta saying "I understand you received a $200 travel voucher (they didn't) from our Proactive Service Recovery team, as we understand this trip was not as pleasant as it should have been. The compensation provided is not meant to place a value on your experience; rather it is an attempt to make amends for your disappointment with our service. You mentioned you had to book a ticket on another airline. While we share your disappointment, we hope you understand we are unable to consider reimbursement for other airline tickets, unused hotels, car rentals, recreational tickets, lost wages/income, child/pet care, or loss of time in these instances. Accordingly, we are unable to honor your request. We realize this is a disappointment, and trust you understand our position".

Our Delta plane landed on time but had to wait for a gate. I missed my flight by 5 mins. A group of us watched from inside the airport while the plane just sat there. I thought they would wait to close the gate especially since we were going from one delta flight to another. I will avoid booking with Delta from now on and avoid layovers at Atlanta International.

I had a flight scheduled to depart at 4pm and arrive in Atlanta at 6:45 where I needed to connect to another flight that left at 7:10. That main flight delayed 3x and I had to change my connecting flight twice until finally for the 3rd time there were no more connecting flights. They offered me another flight the next day that would arrive too late for my purpose of travel. Thanks to delta I missed my cousins funeral.

1 hour into a 11 hour flight, my inflight entertainment stopped working. Despite the flight attendant attempting to restart it, it still didnt work. I was stuck there for close to 10 hours without any in flight entertainment. I filed a complaint, and only received a measly 10,000 points (monetary value of $100). I replied advising that this felt inadequate, and the response I received was that this was the maximum they offered for this kind of issue. Extremely disappointed, spent $2000 for terrible experience, and all they offer is $100 in return. Will never fly Delta again if I can avoid it.

review_header: "never fly with Delta Air Lines again"
review_text: The only functioning toilet door was very difficult to open and the toilet was cleaned only once during the entire 5hr flight. The reason why I know that is because I was sitting in an exit row close to the toilets. Secondly, one of the flight attendants was rather rude she has no customer service skills and it was evident that she really did not want to do her job. We will never fly with Delta Air Lines again.

Then we landed in Atlanta and our connecting flight was cancelled to Huntsville, AL. They of course blamed weather so they wouldn't have to be held accountable although a flight (DL1726) flew out of Atlanta to Huntsville an hour later. We were told at the ticket counter our next available flight would be 3 days later and if that wasn't "good enough" we would have to choose ground transportation and we would be reimbursed for the flight not taken and a rental car. We were given the runaround for over 8 weeks now and over 5 hours of our time for Delta to offer us $25 credit towards our cancelled flight (not money back) and now they won't even reimburse us our $275 rental car to drive through the night to get our child to NASA Space camp on a Sunday. Very Disappointed!

The agent today that we spoke to from the airport was not helpful and just told us to buy a new ticket which would be over $500. I have been forced to fly another airline separately from my family with great inconvenience. The agent who messed up my reservation on August 22nd should be reprimanded for her incompetence and negligence causing emotional and financial stress. Such agents shouldn't be allowed to work for Delta. Extremely poor service experience both then and today. Pity, I used to think Delta was one of the better airlines .

We bought flights months ago with miles and the company overbooked the flight. The flight was originally for 10:30 am and they decided to put us on the 7:30 am flight. When I called to fix the problem I was told their rates had gone up and they offered me the original flight but in the main cabin rather than comfort +. I was told I'll have to take the flight and ask for a refund. I was told the refund department will decide if we get a refund or not. I've never had this many problems with American Airlines.

review_header: "Delta has lost my business for good"
review_text: I thought that Delta's standards had improved over the years, but I had the worst airline experience on September 29th at LAX's terminal 3. I got to the airport early and I had my dog in his carrier. I got stopped by a female employee who told me that my dog was too big for his carrier. This is not the case, he is a chihuahua mix, and I have flown with my dog many times with no issues on much longer flights. She did not offer any solutions, just told me I could not fly with the carrier I had. I got in line to talk to customer service to figure out what my options were, and she then ushered me over again with a manager. The manager told me I could only fly with my dog if I purchased a different carrier from Delta. While the manager went to get the carrier, I waited for 45-50 minutes and almost ran out of time to check my bag. When the manager came back, she had a carrier the same size if not smaller than the one I walked in with. I was flustered and just wanted to get on my flight since I was running out of time, and they charged me $75 for a cramped Delta-branded carrier. I was stressed, my dog was stressed, and I had to literally run through the airport, jostling my poor dog, to make my flight in time (5 minutes later and I would have missed it.) It felt like a weird, gross scam and it was the most stressed out I've ever been dealing with an airline before. I fly extremely frequently (6-12 roundtrip flights a year via various airlines) but Delta has lost my business for good.

I was travelling with my family to Jamaica and we already had bad experience at JFK Airport. Thankfully, this airline was a polar opposite of the airport. The staff was very kind and the food was good. Thank you Delta.

review_header: "A horror of a night in an airplane"
review_text: com and paying for a 3rd additional suitcase, which forced us to get up early and to stand in line at terminal 2 at SFO airport, with the aggressive handling of a red suited male supervisor, making is repack our suitcases. After this stress we made it to near our departing gate for DL 916 to ATL right in time. We wanted to buy a sandwich and the departure screen showed on time for our flight. No sign of boarding, so we took our time. Suddenly the panel changed to last call, a practice I had seen in no other airport in the world. When notifying the harsh eyed lady at the Delta boarding gate, she only shrugged her shoulders and said this was the airport not the airline responsible for this wording. Guest feedback obviously is valued at Delta Airlines. Being a Skyteam frequent flyer with Air France Flying Blue, I wanted to connect to the wifi, but this was only allowed to Delta Skymiles members - or if I wanted to register with Delta Skymiles - an aberration if I am already a member with Flying Blue. Changing flight in Atlanta, we found ourselves in a packed plane and our seats being 50F and E, we could not even place our travelling backpacks in the overhead department, because two of these overheads were filled with the return flight staff equipment, so we had to squeeze these bags between our legs during 9 hours. On top of this Delta has one of the smallest leg space for its economy customers, as seen to this date. A horror of a night in an airplane and hardly will Delta see us ever book them again.

I have been loyal for over 40 years. In that time, I cannot count the number of times I said "I love my Delta Airlines". But lately, Delta has gone downhill. My latest flight international to Nice, FR, I took a chance on "Premium Select" class. A complete and utter waste of money. For the same price, I could have flown true business class with half a dozen other airlines - and gotten a full recline sleeper vs the garbage extra 1/2" seat. I'm talking $1800 more (one way) to fly on Delta. Never again will I fly Delta internationally. Domestically, Delta is a second rate airline - another half dozen budget airlines have better pricing and a better experience. I consider Delta now a "cattle car" carrier. And the latest snub on sky miles, I will do everything I can to not fly Delta anymore and promote those airlines who care. Sadly, the Delta employees continue to be the most courteous and professional. But Delta, the writing is on the wall, you will become a "has been" airline.

On time departure, early arrival. Comfortable seat for a 5 hour flight. Dinner was weird, A fairly robust main dish portion ( veggie lasagna) but that’s it. No app, no sales, no side veggie. Served on a tray with a pre wrapped cookie. Wow. Highlights were the entertainment system and exemplary service by the lone flight attendant brilliantly and tirelessly serving 20 people on his own. Talk about rising to the occasion! This guy deserves a raise!

Flight DL 1689 out of Seattle to Phoenix our connection was very short and had to literally run through the Seattle Airport, which is a nightmare in it self. I had asked a ticket for help in notifying the gate of this dilemma and received no help at all. I am 84 years old and had to run to the gate and when I got there my wife was trying to hold the gate and was told they couldn't do that, very unhelpful. I was last to board and the plane was packed like sardines and our seat was second to last row. To compound the situation, the person behind me was sick and kept sneezing on me between the seats. I could go on but from what I see from Delta, it will fall on deaf ears.

I paid extra for a comfort seat (about $100) after I'd made the initial booking. I made the booking through Orbitz. The ticket was for a Virgin Atlantic flight operated by Delta. Delta called me at 8:57 am, Aug 24, about 10 minutes before I was to leave for the airport. They asked if I would be willing to be re-routed through Boston because MCI-ATL was over-sold. I was offered $300 which was accepted. Comfort seats were not available on the MCI-Boston flight so I was put into the main cabin. I called Delta when I got to the airport to say I also wanted a refund on the comfort seat which was a separate charge on my CC. I was told my CC had already been credited. I called my CC company when I returned and they have no record of impending credits. As of 9/22, it's still not credited. When I got home, I called Delta again and was told they couldn't help me unless I had the MCI-BOS ticket number which I didn't keep and can't find. They said to call Orbitz. Orbit said they couldn't help because Delta called me directly and they didn't have the info. They emailed the flight info they had (MCI-ATL-BOS) which is attached. Orbitz said to contact Virgin Atlantic. Virgin Atlantic also said they couldn't help for the same reason although they forwarded the information I gave them to Delta. I still haven't received a response. Had I been in business class and agreed to be put in the main cabin, I would have credited the difference so why not the $100 I paid for a comfort seat which I'm sure Delta either sold to another passenger or upgraded someone. Everyone else already booked in the main cabin who agreed to switch would have been paid $300. I'm out an extra $100. I have no complaints about the flights themselves or any Delta staff.

We arrive at the airport and are waiting in the bag check line only to see on the screen that our flight was cancelled due to poor weather conditions. This was a surprise to us because we were not notified of this sudden cancellation until we got to the airport. Why not say something earlier or within the day so that we can plan accordingly? Our flights automatically got moved to Tuesday in the evening and we could stay here another day. We finally get to the front of the bag check line and we speak to the lady about the cancellation. Out of the 11 workers we spoke with during our time at the airport, she was one of the nice ones. We asked her if we could get any other flights tonight and she said there were none. She suggested we go to JFK and try but would not compensate us for travel to get there. Our flight was moved to Tuesday and it was Sunday evening. Where were we supposed to stay? They couldn't give us any hotel accommodations or nothing. They couldn't supply us with any solutions or offer to help or service us in any way which is poor customer service. We couldn't afford another night at a hotel so we actually ended up sleeping in the airport. They couldn't even supply blankets or nothing. We were just cold and freezing in the airport while we looked and googled for earlier flights, which are now double and triple the price. I'm talking $1,000 - $1,500 one way for a flight that was originally 300 or so. They couldnt even give us a refund for the flight. They just told us to call customer service. I had to wait 1-2 hours just to get a refund for that flight. So at this point we had to consider taking a bus until we finally found a flight with Delta the following day in the evening around 300. Fast forward to Monday September 11. We check in our bags go through everything and watching netflix by our gate until it was time to board. I think an hour or so before boarding I get an email saying that this flight is now cancelled. My friend and I check the screen and it still says the flight is on time. We went to the people at the gate who had to confirm whether or not the flight was cancelled. At this point we were getting even more frustrated because the same thing happened again. The customer service couldn't do anything for us. They moved our flight to Wednesday September 13. Again, no accommodation, no refund, nothing. The man acted like he did us a favor by giving us a food voucher for $32. What can $32 buy at an airport for 2 people? It was really frustrating because again we weren't notified until last minute of this cancellation. We decided to call and get another refund on the flight all while finding a bus that we could take to get home. We found 1 that was leaving at 10 pm and not too far from the airport. We purchased non refundable tickets, desperate to get home and thinking we would get there in time. We decided to get our bags that we checked and just take this bus. We headed to baggage claim and this was what really got me frustrated. We got there and our bags were not there! We had to wait 4 hours for our suitcases to come out. I asked countless workers where our bags were and we were either dismissed, ignored or not given a direct answer. Because baggage check took too long we missed the bus we were supposed to take and had to spend another night at the airport. We ended up taking a 6 am bus to finally get back home
I approached her when she first started her shift before she even logged on. She was so courteous and relieved my stress.

Agents were rude, they couldn't speak English properly, they were impatient and ultimately tried to rip me off by having me pay $99 in order to get a $242 credit (that would only have been good for 1 yr.) When I said that I wouldn't pay the $99 the guy said 'ok have a good day' and hung up. He also tried to string me along by saying 'we might be able to get your money back if you pay the $99' but he could not explain what missing information was needed in order to determine whether or not I'd get my money back. What a scam! Will never fly Delta again!!

review_header: "we should have booked with a better company"
review_text: We had to wait 8 hours at the airport. In Canada a credit or compensation must be made as stated by law. At the Delta counter they told the passengers to call Delta for the compensation. Numerous e-mails and calls were made to their customer service. Delta does not intend to conform with the law, which makes them a delinquent company. Now we have to deal with the Canadian transportation agency to get our compensation, which takes time. I don't recommend this airline to anyone and won't travel with them or any of their partners. I did not mind to book with a cheaper airline for a short flight, but we lost our time and energy in the process so we should have booked with a better company in the first place. Lesson learned! (Flight was in April 2022).

Now Delta says they will be reset to 0 every year! This is unacceptable, they are breaking their own promise. This is the 2nd time Delta has cheated me. In 2023 I was offered an Amex card and 40k miles. I spent the required $4,000 in three months, got the card, used it and instead of the 40k miles promised, I was given only 35k miles which now are going to be converted to annually reset MSD dollars! I protested, I sent them a screen shot of the offer, but I only got a run-around. This is in addition to the much higher requirements for redeeming miles than most all other airlines.

Then putting me on a connection flight to NYC. Once I get to NYC they then cancel it, making me get a hotel without a voucher! Spending extra money after I just came from vacation. Then the next day for the flight Delta employees want to come to work late (flight attendants) pushing our flight time further back. What happened professionalism in Delta. So frustrating!

My minor son and I (traveling alone) had to be up at 3am to airport on time. The flight Delta scheduled was not even flying that day. I had to be on the phone for over 30 minutes (while standing in the Prague airport with my child) desperately trying to get someone to change the flight to the correct one so we could make our way home to Boston. We ended up managing to sprint through the airport (mind you, this child also has a serious heart condition!) after having just 15 minutes to get to our gate. Since this trip, I have reached out to Delta to provide feedback, only to have them refuse to take responsibility for their mistake. Instead, they have blamed everyone else and straight out denied this even happened. I have phone records to prove my call took place. But they simply refuse to accept the blame. We will not be using Delta for our next European trip.

A few minutes later, I was boarding and had a comfort plus seat along with my husband. As I gave my boarding pass to get on, a huge siren went off and they told me to step back they needed to speak to me. I moved to the location they requested when a man working for Delta said in a pressured, loud and aggressive tone “There is a problem with your seat, the TV doesn’t work but we can move you to another seat with a working TV.” I hesitated because this all caught me off guard and said ok but show me the seat and it was a middle seat without the extra leg room. I said no and he said “Are you sure?” and I said I was traveling with my husband and if we can’t sit together we will just keep the seat with the broken tv in comfort plus. As it turns out that TV worked and Delta had been trying to give my seat to someone else for more money! About 15 years ago, I flew Delta and again coming back to the US from Athens, Greece I connected in Paris and they did a similar thing and asked me while I was seated in my seat to get up and they gave my seat that I had a ticket for and was already seated in to a man with the explanation that it was really his seat despite me having a paid ticket and boarding pass with that seat number. I had to stay in the airport for 5 hours waiting for another Delta plane. I never forgot that and it took 15 years for me to fly overseas with Delta again and now they did this. I never write reviews but want others to know as well as Delta that I will never fly with them again and will let everyone know about the scam they do, especially overseas to young women to take their seats for other passengers.

review_header: "Delta cannot be trusted for award travel"
review_text: Delta than cancelled and changed routings 3 times, resulting in loss of Korean Air Business Class ticket which both Delta and Korean Air refused to reissue, resulting in cancellation of my Korean Air Business Class trip and severe disruption to my annual vacation plans. Delta cannot be trusted for award travel - 1) Excess point requirements, 2) Very hard to get award travel, 3) When awarded, they will cancel and not reissue!

My husband and I had just landed in Paris on 16 August 2023 around 1000 and noticed that his bag did not make the flight. I spoke with Delta Customer Representative. She did an exceptional job walking us through the process and in return decreasing our anxiety. We appreciate her caring and professional attitude which ensured we received the best experience possible. on a scale of 1-10, she is a 20!

They did not help in any way when my sons orders got changed. I was absolutely appalled and am so glad there are many other airlines we can use found forward because no one in my family will ever fly with them again. I have 2 boys in the military and no airline has treated active duty military like Delta. Even Spirit Airlines was hassle free with last minute flight changes due to my son's orders being changed in the past. American Airlines, Southwest, Allegiant have all been super accommodating in making exceptions for active duty military. Shame on Delta for not supporting the military.
The staff is very polite and communicable. There were no delays, I even came to the destination in advance. Was glad to fly with them, strongly recommend!

From rude staff to airplanes constantly breaking, to the most disgusting terminal in every airport, Delta isn’t worth it. Don’t fly Delta unless you can burn 8+ hours on delays and enjoy being laughed at by the customer service personnel who are supposed to help you.

2 seats had sticky or broken seat back buttons. Very cramped seating. Worst of all, they were only serving snacks water and coffee from Florida to Atlanta to St. Louis. Nothing carbonated at all. This was the first flight of my life with no coke. Will never fly Delta again! Flight attendants were too casual. I did not belt at all and it went unnoticed until I belted in flight. Airplane mode not on also went unnoticed. Expected so much more from Delta.

Then we boarded the plane at 12:45am and the pilots could not reach their INTERNAL Delta ground control to take off - the pilot announced this on the airplane as we waited on the plane. At 2am Delta CANCELED the flight and we all had to find hotels and didn't get a flight to late the next day. I didn't even have time to cancel one of my excursions with a 24 hour notice. Getting any sort of refund is a NIGHTMARE.

review_header: "Don't trust the airline to update you"
review_text: My flight from Portland OR to Washington DC Dulles Airport originally had a layover in Seattle WA. Due to the first flight having a delay due to a light blinking for something that turned out to not be happening and them needing more fuel in order to be able to make the trip safely, I missed my connecting flight in Seattle WA. The flight arrived 5 minutes before the connecting flight was due to depart. I was unable to reach the gate in time, so I got in line for the customer service. I checked my texts, email and the delta app, but nothing showed up as having an alternate route. It took a while to get through the customer service line. When I reached the counter, I was informed that they had automatically booked me on a new flight even though I hadn't received any notification of this change. They printed my new ticket and said the new flight was due to depart in 15 minutes and was at the gate next to them. I walked over to the gate to find out that they had already closed the gate and weren't boarding the plane anymore. Therefore the tickets that customer service had given me were for a flight that had already finished boarding. So, I had to get back in line again. When I talked to the customer service representative, they told me that it was my fault for missing the second flight and because I had a basic ticket they couldn't help me with another flight option. That they could put me on a waiting list for an open seat going in the general direction. They said that I would just have to wait in the airport until a seat became available and they couldn't tell me when that might happen. I couldn't handle this news that I was stranded at the airport and had no idea when I might be getting another flight. I found a place to break down and cry and just before 11am my delta app notified me the info for the alternative flight that I had missed. This made me mad because this was two hours after I had needed it. So I collected myself and went back to customer service counter. The person who helped me didn't treat me like it was my fault for missing both flights and got me new boarding passes. This whole thing could have been avoided if I had gotten my notification about the reroute a lot sooner or if the customer service person had given me a ticket for a flight that hadn't closed there gates then say it wasn't their responsibility for the missed flight. Then on my last flight, the overhead space was a bit harder to reach then other planes and I am 4'11". When I had asked a flight attendant for help because I could reach they attendant told me she wasn't allowed to help me, which didn't bother me. But while I was struggling to pick up my bag high enough, the attendant told me that I was holding people up. A passenger ended up catching my bag as I was about to drop it and helping me the rest of the way.

Our flight was delayed by a 2 hour ground stop in Atlanta that caused us to miss our connection to Hartford on flight 1011. Despite a difficult situation beyond anyone's control, every Delta employee in the Savannah Airport, in the Atlanta airport, and in the air was courteous and professional in helping us and several hundred other stranded travelers get flights rebooked. We were able to get rebooked to flight 2069 for 7:05am the next morning and the airline gave us a complimentary hotel reservation and meal vouchers. I am sure that the airline did the same for several hundred people on this day and their commitment to customer service was refreshing and appreciated. thank you.

The first was over an hour late, the second 4 hours late, and the third landed in the wrong airport at midnight! I complained to Delta, of course. It took them a month to reply and offer me a laughable $25 voucher for future travel because it was due to factors outside of their control. I can believe that for one flight, but 3 out of 3 indicates a pattern of incompetence. Avoid Delta at all costs!

Our flight was delayed an hour.  We sat on the plane for one hour. They came on the intercom and said "we do not have pilots to fly and you must deplane. Once in the terminal again they came on the speaker and said that the flight was canceled due to bad weather (even though we all heard inside the plane that they didn't have pilots. They told us that they would not pay for lodging for us. All passengers including myself saw several planes land and let passengers off ... so if it was weather related planes could land but not take off?
Then told to deplane after sitting an hour to have to wait for another half hour til a new plane comes. If you have a chance to fly anywhere else other than Delta, I would suggest it.

My twin boys and I boarded at 3:41 Delta Flight 1043, which had us wait inside the plane in 80+ degrees (inside the aircraft) for over a 1 hour while the crew tried to fix the AC and mechanical issues the plane was experiencing. This caused a delay in our arrival, and our plans changed due to the fact that we missed our car rental and hotel arrival time. After we departed San Antonio, it was hard to relax and watch a movie as the aircraft was having issues with the monitors, and they kept turning on and off three to four more times until they rebooted the system. On our return flight scheduled for Monday, August 21, 2023, our flight was delayed four times before arriving at the airport at 1 PM. While we sat at the airport waiting from 1 PM to 6 PM our flight was delayed two to three more times. Finally, after waiting all afternoon/evening at the airport, at around 9-10 PM we received a message from Delta saying our flight was delayed until 9 AM the next morning August 22, 2023. The Delta attendant informed us that the delay was due to the fact that Delta could not find a Pilot and the replacement pilot they found earlier, had declined as well, so they were left with no pilot and no choice but to push the flight until the next day. The customer service representative helped us book a hotel and offered us an embarrassing and very offensive $15 voucher per person. We arrived at the hotel with no clothes to change into, no toothbrush, no toothpaste, no hairbrush, no pajamas, and no deodorant, with absolutely nothing but dirty clothes we had on from waiting all day at the airport. It was almost 11 PM at night and every store was closed at this time to try and purchase anything. My kids (two 11-year-old boys) were tired, bored, and very impatient. Also, because it was past 11 PM we were extremely tired, and due to most restaurants and stores being closed we were unable to use the food vouchers. We had to wait an additional 20 to 30 minutes for the hotel shuttle to finally pick us up from the airport and drop us off at the Sheraton Hotel. The next day our flight finally departed LAX and we were extremely disappointed to be placed in an old and dirty aircraft with smaller TVs than the normal ones (We booked 6 first-class seats), please see the attached pictures for reference. We also left our vehicle at the San Antonio, TX airport for when we arrived and we had to pay two extra days of car storage at the airport due to our delay, which we do not think is fair. As if that wasn't disappointing enough for Delta, we received an email on 08/22/2023 from Customer Care offering us a $100 Voucher for the horrible experience. Due to the fact that our flight was delayed over 4 hours and per the trip delayed coverage in Delta's guidelines, we are entitled to up to a $700 travel voucher per ticket (4 tickets) and reimbursement for items we paid for during this delay. Delta refuses to take accountability for their actions and only offer us $20 vouchers.

Our plane from Mexico City was diverted by a storm 20 minutes from Atlanta and landed in Savannah (presumably because of lack of fuel – this was not a great choice of airport, as it has no customs for an international arrival). As a result of this, we sat on the tarmac for 5.5 hours (beyond the legal limit of 4 hours), given nothing to eat but a small bag of chips and two glasses of water. It turns out there were three such planes stranded on the tarmac that afternoon, one with no food or water and no functioning bathroom. The incident made the local online news and TV and was described as "unprecedented". Eventually night fell, the pilots left and we were deplaned and processed through a makeshift customs office, then told to find our own accommodation as Delta had no vouchers, but were explicitly told to keep all receipts. Airport staff booked a hotel for me and three fellow passengers. If I had known I wouldn't be refunded I might have slept in the airport. The next morning we showed up at Savannah Airport at 9 for our 11:30 40-minute flight back to Atlanta. I was rebooked onto my Virgin ATL-LHR flight at 6:40 pm. But we didn't leave Savannah till 5:30 pm! First, we were told the plane needed cleaning, then, as time passed, that Delta were now obliged to rebook every single passenger, including their onward flights, by hand, using a defective printer, and they would call them each by name. Chaos ensued, and the flight kept being delayed by another hour. Half the passengers left and hired cars out of frustration. Of course I missed my Atlanta-London connection for the second time in 24 hours. I was luckily rebooked onto a 10 pm Delta flight to London (not in Premium, which I had booked on my original Virgin flight). We were emailed $400 in Delta vouchers, not as a measure of our inconvenience but as a token gesture of apology. I would simply have liked a clean measure of my inconvenience. When I submitted $250 of receipts to Delta for reimbursement, I spoke to a representative about how I would receive the payment and was told a cheque would be emailed to my UK address. Subsequently, Delta informed me that none of my expenses were eligible for reimbursement as bad weather had caused the disruption. This, however, takes no account of a) their duty of care to stranded passengers and b) the sheer incompetence of Delta staff the following day at Savannah airport which caused many people to miss their onward connections. I have tried texting and calling and have repeatedly been fobbed off and held in lines. Delta, I should say, issued a useful food voucher of $30 at Atlanta airport (this was around 8 or 9 pm, though, the first food we had been given all day) and I was then emailed a transport voucher of $35 (for what?) which wasn't actually in the email. On the phone to Delta this week, I was offered 5000 miles as a token to shut me up, which I refused. And in an email I was sent a conciliatory $90 voucher, again not actually accessible from the email. I won't let this drop. Virgin, by contrast, have been charming and helpful, and promised me some refund on my non-flown Premium leg.

I am absolutely disgusted with Delta Air Lines, they absolutely ruined the first day of vacation for my family and myself. They delayed our 5:30am flight 7 HOURS due to a mechanical issue. It ruined our entire first day of our vacation and we ended up having to book with a different airline last minute because Delta had nearly no other same day flight options except a red eye late night flight. We spent 5 hours in line trying to find other options, and probably over 10 hours by now on hold waiting to get customer service agents to pick up and help. We have spoken to 4 agents at least, and none have been willing to help or hold Delta accountable for the major inconvenience we had in our vacation due to their own doing. They cost us another 500 dollars each for the last minute flight change and only refunded us for the first half of the original trip. They are now refusing to cover the other flights we had to book even though the first customer service representative we talked with while at the airport during this mess told us they would, and have refused to provide any sort of voucher either. While we stood in line at our gate waiting to talk to the Delta attendant for help during all of this, they were giving out 1800 dollar vouchers for an overbooked flight and letting the volunteer passengers cut the line in front of us even though we had already been standing for an hour to rebook their flights. We didn't have a choice to be delayed due to Delta's maintenance issue and yet they are refusing to compensate us at all for any of our experience. It is totally negligent. The customer service reps told us they will do nothing for us and have refused to help any further.

On the way we had to overnight in St. Paul because we missed our connection, then took at 7am flight to Salt lake where we paid $770 to rent a car and drive 5 hours to get to Jackson. After multiple calls to CS and turn downs, I sent a FEDEX to the CEO requesting reimbursement for the additional car cost with receipts, nothing more, they didn't pay us the courtesy to respond. What kind of a CEO and airlines disses their clients like that - it's so disturbing.

Our travel agent booked our trip in February 2023 for our upcoming thirty eighth anniversary in August 2023. We arrived early at Atlanta on August 14, 2023. We did everything we were suppose to do, then went to our gate and sat waiting an hour and 15 minutes to board (Gate E15) When they called for Comfort Plus we excitedly got in line to board our flight D1970. When the agent scanned my passport and ticket it would not go through, the agent, who had a horrible attitude asked, where are you flying to?! I stated St. Lucia, she said they changed the flight to boarding gate E10 and the plane has already left. My husband and I were furious because nothing was announced, nor was our name called to let us know of the last minute change. My husband attempted to ask the Delta Rep when did the flight change? She rudely stated, I don't know sir. All I know is the flight gate was changed to E10, they were to depart at 9:45 am, but they departed earlier. My husband asked, what time did they depart? She stated at 9:43 sir. Please move out of the line. We missed our flight. We went to the Delta desk and the agent was no better. We advised her of what had happened and she said, I don't see that your flight was changed to another gate? She then kept looking and said, oh yeah, at the last minute they changed it, and you and your wife are listed as a no show. By this time we are heartbroken. We asked if there was another flight going out? She responded not today. We called our travel agent and she got a Delta Rep on the line for Delta Vacations and she was very unsympathetic. Our travel agent kept asking what could we do to fix this? The agent stated for us to go back to the Delta desk and see if they could book us on an other flight. We again advised we were told there were no more flights going out. We went back to the Delta help desk and the agent had the nerve to say: I don't know why they sent you back to me. They can see the same thing I can. She repeated that statement six times before saying there was nothing she could do. We called for a shuttle to return us back to our hotel, having to pay another $167 plus tax. Our travel agent was able to get us booked on the next day flight August 15, 2023 (this is our anniversary day). She got a Delta Rep on the line to see what compensation could be done and every agent we spoke to was adamant nothing could be done because it was our fault we missed the plane. We ended up losing a whole day (August 14,2023) at the resort, and had to spend more money for a hotel stay. To say the very least we are extremely disappointed in the way things were handled with Delta and will be using American Airlines or another airline moving forward.

to 8 years put on plane, but we weren’t allowed to board because the gate door was just being shut when we finally got through security. The door was still open, but the woman gate attendant wouldn’t let us board. Now we’re stuck in the Seattle airport with 5 little children, no luggage, no car seats. It boggles the mind that the woman at the gate would actually do this. We have no idea what we’re going to do now. Sleep in the airport, I guess, with no bedding or change of clothes.  I will never fly Delta again, and I will discourage everyone I know not to, as well.

review_header: "the last time I book with Delta"
review_text: I had delays on BOTH trips (on 8/3 and 8/13). On my first round I traveled a red eye so I slept for most of the flight, did not eat or drink anything. When I woke up I asked the flight attendant if I could have water as she was making her trash pick up rounds. It was approximately 25-30 minutes before our landing time so I told her 'no rush' since I knew she was making her rounds. She looked at me and said, 'we're about to land'. I am a frequent flyer and I have NEVER been made to feel uncomfortable for a cup of water. I responded with, 'you know what, it's fine. I don't need it.' Another flight attendant brought me a cup once she was done with her rounds. Seriously, that's all she needed to do. I made her job easy through the entire flight by knocking out and staying out of her way until I needed ONE cup of water 30 MINUTES before landing. This is the last time I book with Delta. I gave them an extra star because the other flight attendants were cool but if you're going to delay my flight AND treat me like I'm bothering you when I ask for water you won't see me in those planes again. Also, they promote on flight entertainment yet have no bluetooth option for people with earbuds and you don't offer earphones in order to use the entertainment option you claim to offer. It makes zero sense. I had to resort to playing games since I had no old school earphones that plug into YOUR device. I'm glad I wore comfortable shoes b/c they changed gates AT LEAST 5 times when I waited in Atlanta and twice when I waited in Minneapolis. Like come on guys, we're paying tons of money for a service and I flew the lowest level. I would have been PO'd if I paid for First or Business class!
