Despite the 7-hour flight duration, the second meal service was skipped entirely. No announcement or explanation was provided by the crew. I would appreciate an explanation and appropriate compensation.

The service was not provided in Dubai, both ways. I sent a complaint and the staff had the audacity to answer me that they checked with the staff and that my mom received assistance. Basically calling her a liar. She wrote back, stating the detail of her experience. I additionally required to check the CCTV to confirm what my mom experienced. The response I received was that they would basically only take in consideration the staff version of the story and give 15000 complimentary skywards miles as a “gesture of goodwill”. Emirates never acknowledged their mistake. And they have the audacity to give my mother miles, in case she wants to experience their pathetic service again. The audacity has no limit.

Baggage was lost / delayed for 5 days on arrival at MUC. Submitted claim for emergency essentials totalling €716.13, all receipts provided. Emirates agreed to pay €219 which I rejected and after numerous ongoing emails to them, no communication at all apart from from an auto reply stating it’s on review and I will be contacted in 14 days, over a year now and nothing and I will continue to take this further until full reimbursement of a legitimate claim is settled. Disgraceful service from Emirates, of which I was once a Gold member. Would not recommend Emirates Airlines to anyone anymore, worst service ever experienced!

I had almost no time to convince my manager at work and get emergency passport renewal. When I checked their fares, they were very high. Normally it should be around 1300 CAD in their Economy class one way but it shows 2400 CAD ( 4 seats left ) while checking their fares on their web site. While booking I got a call from my boss, after 10 minutes it shows the fare increased to 2700 CAD and shows only 2 seats left. I was worried and booked it. I cannot select seat due to last minute booking. When I reached airport the check in lady said only aisle seats available but the 3 seats next to me will be empty, if they assign someone there ask them to give you another seat. Not sure what this makes. I cannot sleep on those empty seats, just can stretch my legs. They did not assign anyone in those seats but Emirates air hostess and staff on flight keep looking at me strangely. When I checked the other seats I see other passengers have empty seats in Economy class next to my row and they were sleeping on them. I paid double the normal fare and it is not a last minute pleasure trip. I see more than 30 empty seats on the flight within the 4 rows front and behind my row in economy class. I was not assigned a seat in Dubai to Hyderabad flight but issued boarding pass in Toronto. Eventually they gave me Business class aisle seat, that flight is only 3.5 hours and I could not sleep in that short period. The food and drinks they offered in business class is same as in economy class. Their food is Indian cuisine which was ok to me. Shame on Emirates with this type of wrong news about availability of seats and impersistent seat allocation. Decided never travel on Emirates flights in future. Advise other travelers never fly on Emirates. Though food was good but all the free beers, vodka, or scotch whiskey is not worth the price you pay. Very bad experience.

Bad food, rude staff, awful airport and the worst service. They did not dispatch my luggage. I am waiting for it for days. Every day, they were calling me that your luggage will be delivered today and I had to stay at home. But they did not. The airport was the worst. Tap water was warm. There was not enough seats for people in front of gates. While Qatar Airways airport in Doha has separate spacious room with comfortable seats for ladies, there was not such a thing in Emirates airport. You had to pay for every single basic single. I never will fly with Emirates again.
Seat was comfortable. Entertainment system wasn’t that great and not many good movies. The food was disappointing bland and lacking flavour.

The A380 was old and not upgraded. The TV screen broke after 30 minutes flight. My wife called 2 times. 2 different annoyed crew responded "I'll come back to fix it". They never come back and no ICE system available during the entire flight. Worse, I ordered a $600 watch. The steward told me "I ll bring to you" 4 hours later, just before landing, he was taking pictures of passenger. I told him "What about my watch" He mumbled "sorry I have forgotten". I complained to his chief and of course cancelled my order. Return in their new Premium Economy class. Again a nightmare with no dedicated check in counter contrary to what they advertise, I have to wait 20 minutes. The flight was OK but at the level of other premium economy class. Emirates is expensive compared to other airlines but the huge price difference was once warranted by clean new aircrafts, Top entertainment, caring to passengers, and good service - but no more! I really prefer Etihad that flight out of nearby new Abu Dhabi airport. In comparison Dubai DXB looks now old.

Imagine seating aisle side and the push cart being ramp straight to your knee.  No apologies what so ever.  Similar things seem to happen to other passengers but the crew didn't seem to care that much. Aside from that, they just chug the food tray to you without even asking what meal you would like. I don't know what's their deal or if the  crew is having a bad moody day. But may I suggest not taking it out on the passengers who have earnestly paid for their flight.

I managed to sleep the entire flight with comfy bedding and lovely amenities kit. The return flight CGK-DXB was a lovely flight with amazing crew who came to check on me several times specially the business class supervisor who was from Uzbekistan. The meal service was also great and managed to sleep for few hours. After landing we were escorted to our bus to arrivals and in few minutes was out and my luggage were waiting for me et the belt and the chauffeur service was also excellent.

Premium Economy not available on this sector. Paid extra for bulk head seat. Good flight, meal, service etc. Due to Emirates status, used lounge in Amsterdam. It’s a contract lounge and is awful. Over crowded and just unpleasant. Total contrast in Dubai. Terminal A lounge is vast and very well appointed. Dubai to Auckland departing 13th June in Premium Economy. Seat 34J. I’m writing this because I had the best flight attendant and service I have ever had with Emirates including my experiences in Business. She went over and beyond and was totally charming. I wish I could remember her name, she was from Argentina. I actually spoke to the Cabin Manager about her. An absolute star. Again good food and I do find the seat very comfortable. Always manage a good sleep. I like Emirates and they are my long haul airline of choice.

05.2025. hecked in well, and then proceeded to board B777 - 300 where I found a Tired, Stressed or rather irritated crew member - my partner and i were seated on 47A/47B which she was shocked with that came with a loud question "are you staff?" My partner looking at me in wonder and bothered. We responded No we are not. She then demanded our boarding pass which indicated our seat numbers. She still looked puzzled like we were seated in a wrong place or on a wrong flight as she returned the passes to us. All our smiles and warmth were shuttered by this staff hardly taking off. We then got worried of if she will be the one attending to us and it turned out we were right to worry. As if that wasn't enough, time for our long waited meal came and  the crew to serve was the same. She tells us she only has Chicken for main  like there was no Menu that was issued prior to our meal - my partner doesn't eat chicken, mushrooms but not allergic and I don't fancy them either. We politely told her we want 2 beef. And she was like only chicken available. I repeated we want 2 beef as we don't eat chicken. Said since you don't want to eat chicken I can only give you the plate with a starter and Desert without the main. As I got shocked with how much I paid for our ticket with no discount or promotion. But we are being served like we are being done a favour. A huge thanks to her colleague who was so lively, sweet and professional. I guess she noticed how un happy we were.

Comfortable seat with good recline. Slept a good solid 7 hours. Food good, service not so good. Definitely had better crews in the past. Service was slow, dinner trays left for a long time. Had to alert a cabin attendant to take mine away. Dubai to Paris economy. Seat ok, service quite good and very good food. There is no other airline for me.

There were a few red faces when I came back and said that’s not the seat on my boarding pass – 1A. I was whisked away by the Purser amid a hail of apologies and the promise they would make up for it, and they certainly did. When it comes to typical flight times for an Airbus A380, at around 3 hours, the trip from Christchurch to Sydney is just a blip. Thanks to the great crew, I had the opportunity to enjoy the full first class experience. Dom Perignon was being poured within minutes of entering my suite and I was presented with the first-class menu. Before take-off I was given a set of PJ’s and fabric carry bag to take them home in. Then as the aircraft levelled out the meal service started with an enormous serving of caviar with the offer of more, followed by a melody of dishes that were to die for. After dinner, I accepted the bed turndown service. In addition to the luxurious padded seat, they attach a mattress along with a white sheet and a big fluffy pillow. Without ear plugs or a sleeping mask, I was asleep in less than 10 minutes and slept soundly for over an hour surrounded by the twinkling lights installed in the ceiling overhead as well as the floor. Tempted as I was to accept the invitation to try out the onboard shower, I felt that might be just a little too decadent for a 3-hour flight.  When I returned after changing from PJ’s back to my travel clothes the bed had returned to being a seat and my jacket and shoes were neatly arranged. We landed into Sydney 20min ahead of schedule and on a Friday night.

review_header: “they refused to made me a refund”
review_text: My trip was MIA-BOG. The people at the counter were very rude. I always use a small luggage as a personal item (under seat cabin bag), accepted at ALL airlines, but Emirates didn't accept it. When I told the counter agent that this baggage is accepted on all airlines as a personal item, he rudely told me that those were Emirates's rules and that in "someone else's home, the rules must be obey.” He also criticized me for traveling in economy class. Also, when I tried to buy in the app the extra baggage, I choose the extra baggage for the route MIA-BOG, but when I clicked "continue" the site changed the route to BOG-MIA. I noted the mistake when I receive the confirmation by email. Inmediatelly I called Emirates Customer Service but they refused to made me a refund. Now, I had to pay $100 at the counter and I lost the $130 that I paid in the app, because I don't need any extra bagagge for the route BOG-MIA. In addition to the unexpected expense, this experience ruined my trip.

It is often promoted as a top-tier airline, but my experience tells a different story. In economy class, the service is underwhelming at best. On this flight to Paris, I was nearly bumped to a later flight due to overbooking, and I had to insist firmly in order to be accommodated. The in-flight experience left much to be desired. The food was disappointing, the service was average, and the cabin felt overcrowded. I requested a glass of water which never arrived. I pressed the call button, but no one responded. Between Dubai and Paris, not once did the crew proactively offer water. As for business class – although I wasn’t flying in that cabin on this occasion, I have done so in the past – Emirates often charges a premium that is difficult to justify given the level of service compared to competitors. I also purchased a Wi-Fi session, which was advertised as high-speed internet. In reality, the download speed was just 2.82 Mbps and the upload speed only 1.78 Mbps – simply unacceptable. To add to the poor impression, the crew announced the wrong time upon arrival in Paris, a basic error that speaks to a lack of attention to detail. The cabin crew, for the most part, were unsmiling and disengaged. Overall, Emirates is no longer the exceptional airline it once was. In economy class, it feels more like a cattle car in the sky than a premium travel experience.

Despite several email and telephone calls Emirates have refused to refund what is a relatively small amount of money quoting ‘terms and conditions’, although their terms and conditions state that we are entitled to a refund. They used to be a good airline and we have flown with them fairly often. However we will not be using them again.

Catering was not the best this time: bland food and sides. We were served twice, it filled our stomach but that was it. Service provided by the staff was friendly and speedy despite a full plane. Seats were comfortable. We landed 30 min earlier in Amsterdam.

Had to use Emirates as backup because Cathay Pacific delayed our flight. Maybe because of that seat selection was not available for us. That one I do not blame this airline on. But: We got two seats way back at the end of 777. Behind me was a man in his 50s. At the altitude I reclined my seat (not all the way back) and was prepared to get some sleep in this 6 hr flight. Immidiately I feel tap on my shoulder and some arguing that I have to raise my seat. He was arguing that he could not eat with my seat reclined. I tried to explain that my seat does not affect his table position, but really I feel like he just wanted more space. He was really unpleasant to talk to, it felt like there was only his needs and everyone around should just obey to that. English is not my native languge, so I finished the argument with "ask the flight attendant", I was sure that she can explain everything better than me. The man catches flight attendant, explains that he want me to raise my seat. She does not ask any questions, just stands up near me and commands "raise your seat" and proceeds with taking back of my seat and tries to raise it with force. No questions asked. With flight attendant fully on his side I even did not even try to argue. It felt really dengerous to even talk back to these people. Food was given 2 hours (!) after take off. After food serving nobody did not even try to provide us with any sort of bevereges. Again, that is on 6 hrs flight. Is that even legal? We had to catch flight attendant to ask for any water-like substance. How dare you to ask me about upgrades to premium economy or business if you fail to provide any basic service for economy? Or does Emirates starts to provide basic service starting from business? It is logical to just use better airlines instead. It is a level lower than any low-cost airline in the Eastern Europe. I am a frequent flyer and did not expect something like that at the price that I paid. It is by far my worst flight expirience. My family and friends will never use Emirates ever again.
Flight attendants are friendly and polite. Seats are comfortable and can be reclined easily. The food is delicious. Flights departed on time.

Long-story short, our flight was cancelled after waiting on the plane for several hours, at 2 AM and under the rain, with two young children we had to find a hotel, catch a taxi and recheck everything out of the airport and then back in. Our luggage had been mishandled and all clothes wet. They wouldnt reimburse for costs incurred as they are counting dollars and cents at present. I wouldnt touch them again, they charge a very large sum of money and their after sale services are very poor

There was no time to get a drink. I was relieved to get my flight to Birmingham. I was hot and thirsty. Unfortunately, for a torturous 2 hours and 50 minutes, there wasn't a drop of liquid served, although I did ask for a glass of water, which never transpired. Apart from that, which, when you're tired and thirsty, seems a massive problem.

No PIR number was provided as the team at Manchester airport were very unorganised. All they asked me to do was fill out an online form, through GBS Enquiries which I did. I have been back and fourth and had multiple phone calls with the team but the complaint still has not been dealt with. The customer service has been extremely poor. I'm very disappointed with Emirates.

C to Dubai, then me and my group missed our flight to Dar. Emirates gave us a hotel booking and an alternative flight for the next day. But it is so weired we have never get any support into getting to the hotel. Its so sad that Emirates has started being a Zero Star Airline.

There were four of us (my husband, my two kids, and myself). We used points for three tickets and paid in full cash for the four ticket. We have business class one way. Not only was the cabin crew horrible from Miami to Dubai (they disappeared shortly into the flight and didn't resurface till the end of the flight. They left a table of snacks and wine and water by the bathroom), but they badly damaged my bag. My bag was just two weeks old and has tears and rips in it. The only way to file a complaint or notify them of your damage bag is to fill out an online complete form. It's the worst way of communication. They take weeks to get back to you and then will give you different excuses every time. They are the most unprofessional Employees I have ever worked with in my life. I feel like I was cheated and robbed from them. We spent over 450,000 points, and 7000 in cash in fees for one way tickets all to have horrible customer service, a damaged bag, and bad flight crew. Avoid this airline like the plague.
The cabin crew were admirable and friendly, the food was good and delicious. Highly recommended!

I was promised that I will get A Dubai Connect option in Dubai with my flight only to be told that I won’t. I have a layover of 20 hours and my husband is on the same journey with the shorter layover yet he received Dubai Connect. Never traveling with Emirates again.

Nearly every hour, we received announcements that the flight was being delayed by yet another hour or two. Such a delay, coupled with the treatment of passengers, is unacceptable. I am deeply disappointed with Emirates.

review_header: “Emirates refused to credit due to policy”
review_text: The larger issue I had was with FF miles. It was not allocated to my account when flights were booked. Eventually I found this out. Due to an ongoing software issue with Emirates website I was unable to log into my account. After multiple calls and emails they said they were "working on it". I was finally able to log in after 6 months, now points have expired. Emirates refused to credit these due to policy. Booking several flights (work and personal) shortly to Europe and USA but not with Emirates.

It has gone from being a luxury carrier to being more like a low cost airline. Flying in business class now feels like economy used to be. Here is how the quality has collapsed IMO You no longer get an amenities bag unless you are overnight. The quality of the wine in business class has been reduced from nice Loire, South African or Aussie quality wines, to cheap plonk. Makes no sense. The quality of the food is utterly disgusting. I'm not kidding here. Check the photo of the business class vegetarian meal that I uploaded with this review. Twice they have served me this POW camp slop in business class. Defies all expectations. No accompaniments, no chutney, or sauces. Just brown slop in white rice. What I don't understand is why they are so gung-ho on cost cutting while passenger numbers and revenue are at an all time high. They are cutting their own throats because carriers like Qatar are still offering really great quality service. In fact (and I never thought I would think this) Saudia business class beats Emirates on food quality. (Actually, if you look at the photo of my business class meal, everyone beats that). Emirates customer service is now more concerned with revenue retention than with fulfilling the ticket terms, and can be quite combative. I have noticed that changing a "Flex Plus" ticket, despite being fully changeable always attracts a fare change, even when the original class of ticket if still available to buy in Emirates.com. I had such a fight with them I refunded the entire Flex Plus ticket and rebought the travel in my new date at the lower price I don't know what happening, I have a real soft spot for Emirates. At one time they set the bar for quality, but that's not true anymore and it makes me really sad.

The flight was initially delayed and we only boarded at 2pm. We then sat in the aircraft until just before 5pm until they eventually told us to disembark. We then went to baggage collection where most of us waited at least 2 hours for our luggage to arrive. I then waited in a line for another 1 and a half hours to book a new ticket. When booking the new ticket I then informed them my previous flight I had booked the vegan option as I've been strictly vegan for 5 years. They couldn't promise me anything but they said they'd try put the request in as I couldn't adjust it on my app with the flight being canceled. On the flight there were zero vegan options and all I could eat after 20+ hours of travel stress was black tea and some fruit pieces. Furthermore, my skyrewards number never works and I have been unable to accumulate points every time I fly. In addition, I had to purchase my own wifi plan to let friends and family know I finally was safely on my way to Dubai. This has been the worst travel experience for me. Hungry, tired and severely inconvenienced.

I had already arrived from Colombo to Dubai on EK649 at least they were courteous and friendly. My connecting flight from Dubai to Glasgow was a nightmare. I had booked a diabetic meal and imagine I got the meal minus water. I needed to take my meds and numerous requests were ignored by very arrogant flight attendants specially one of them on this particular flight. After two and a half hours I received 1 cup of water . I was extremely thirsty and dehydrated and when I asked if I could have a bottle of water she curtly replied they do not have bottled water. She took off before I could ask for another cup of water. However passengers seated in front of me were served with water and juice . This didn't solve my problem as I just couldn't get a juice or water at that moment. After about another hour I kept buzzing for a flight attendant and no one came . When the 2nd meal was served I received a small bottle of water and by then I was feeling dehydrated. I'm 63 and not in the best of health . Is this fair? I have lodged a complaint with Emirates and I'm waiting for the response they say they will send me.  Unfortunately I have a return flight from Glasgow to Dubai and Dubai to Colombo and I feel violated and traumatized to think of what to expect . One thing for sure is I will never fly Emirates again. I'm just disgusted. That long walk from terminal to terminal and then taking a bus or the train is equally insane. I paid for Marhaba meet and greet service since I know with mobility issues I would miss the flight. Thankfully the Marhaba service lady was an Angel and so helpful something that the arrogant flight stewardess could learn. It doesn't cost anything to be nice. This was a long haul flight and I would have expected water to be provided in unlimited quantity. Shame on you Emirates. So much for your so called service you boast about. I'm done. I was going to see my 6 year old grandson after 5 years in Scotland and what should have been a happy journey was a nightmare. Unfortunately I have to go again via the same route on this heartless airline. Never again will I take that risk. I have flown Emirates prior and those short flights were so delightful. Not anymore .

Throughout the flight, it felt as though Economy passengers were treated as an afterthought. It took an excessive amount of time to receive any service, even something as simple as water, despite pressing the call button multiple times. On one occasion, I got up to stretch my legs and was approached by a flight attendant asking if I needed help. When I explained I was just trying to get some movement, I was told to return to my seat and wait for 10 minutes until service was completed. The tone and response felt dismissive and unnecessary. Another unsettling moment occurred when I pressed the service button. A flight attendant walked past me, nodded in acknowledgment, but didn’t stop. When she finally returned, she explained she had been “counting.” While I appreciate that tasks need to be completed, ignoring a passenger’s request and providing such a response felt dismissive and unprofessional. The final incident left me utterly shocked. While refilling my water bottle, another flight attendant accidentally spilled water all over my leg. Instead of a genuine apology or assistance, his response was, “I couldn’t see.” It’s difficult to understand how such carelessness and lack of attentiveness can happen on an airline that prides itself on excellence. As someone who has experienced the polished and attentive service in Business Class, the treatment in Economy was a glaring contrast. It felt as though Economy passengers were not afforded the basic courtesy or care expected from Emirates. While I understand there are differences in service levels between classes, this experience lacked the professionalism and warmth that should be standard across all cabins. I sincerely hope Emirates addresses these inconsistencies. Loyal customers, regardless of class, deserve better treatment and respect.

In comparison with other airlines I have enjoyed the Economy class more than the Business. I was lucky that no one was sitting next to me. The A380 passenger experience is awesome. Nice inflight crew. Decent catering. Unparalleled entertainment. Good comfort. When flying Economy Class, Emirates for me is my preferred choice.
I wasn't able to recline my seat on my final flight with Emirates. The airline is declining year over year. Never again Emirates.

EK 377 from BKK to DXB  was ok overall. However the standard of the 1st meal served from BKK was very disappointing. Whilst I appreciate this was a 0200 departure from BKK, something a little more substantial in terms of meal would have been appreciated. A little bag of caramel popcorn (as nice as it was) and a drink is simply unacceptable for the high price of the ticket paid. The french toast on the second meal service was soggy and more like a bread pudding, and the Pineapple and Papaya Compote did not taste either, and just looked like pureed fruit slapped onto the dish. Otherwise, no other comments, as the service was ok, and the flight into Dubai was on time. EK21 from DXB to MAN on time but main issue is around meals. Once the cabin crew came to serve breakfast, they already had ran out of the main Omelette dish stating 'everyone wanted this' - how can this always happen? This is very disappointing. Otherwise as from BKK, service ok - but nothing to write home about. Baggage reclaim at MAN was very slow - again reinforces the need to urgently close Terminal 1 ASAP and move to new terminal. I like Emirates - but they have a rival in Qatar Airways that I may consider the next time I fly to Thailand.

The check in process at Manchester was ok - but could be smoother (Self-Check In was ok, but could not print boarding pass). The experience at Manchester Airport however was very chaotic with boarding taking place from Gate 20 as the plane was on a Remote Stand and needed bus transfer to the aircraft. Poor communication between ground staff noted, and passengers were just choosing to board when they desired - not taking notice of staff. Flight delayed for one hour from Manchester - they need to close Terminal 1 ASAP as it is chaotic! The flights themselves were ok. Food was good, and the cabin crew appeared rather lacklustre and not very friendly on the MAN-DXB Sector. This was much improved from DXB - KUL Seats ok - but passengers pushing seats right back when eating is a concern.

Service was good but the second leg was somewhat ruined by two kids running up and down the aisle and showering the floor with pop corn. Yes this is the responsibility of the parents but aircrew should have said something. Overall staff were more consistent and visible than when flying business but polish was lacking, example when asking for a glass of the white Burgundy by name you had to show them the picture on the wine list. Yes it’s the little things but that’s what you fly first. Same goes for the quality of food which other than the caviar was ok but lacked the extra that you expect. Airport transfer to the airport in Singapore went well, however Emirates cancelled it for Munich which led to a long wait at the airport until they eventually sorted it by reimbursing the cost of a Taxi. This was a once in a lifetime treat and it failed to deliver. In business on the A380 the offer a good product let’s see how they do when they reconfigure the 777 but we won’t do first again.

I requested a refund for my return ticket from China to Tunis, dated December 29, 2022. Despite sending several emails, I have not received any response. Recently, I visited the Emirates Airlines office in Shanghai. The lady working there was very kind and promised to try contacting the Dubai office to process my refund. Indeed, I received an email (from a no-reply address) after 15 days stating that they had refunded me an amount of 100 Tunisian dinars, which is roughly $35. I sent another inquiry through their website (as no email address was available), filing a complaint on November 15, 2024. I explained that I paid more than 6,300 Tunisian dinars for two one-way tickets and one return ticket. Today, November 27, 2024, I received a system-generated email (from a no-reply address) stating the following: “After reviewing your ticket, we found that it has already been refunded, and no further refund is due. If you require further information or assistance regarding this refund, please visit the website to check our Help section, where you can find contact details for your local Emirates office or fill out a support request form.

Economy was pretty crammed and crew made little to no effort to go out of their way. No regular trolley service. No attention to detail. The most shocking thing was the airline’s refusal to board parents with young children first: in fact they actually sent one couple with a baby and toddler to the back of the line. In 50 years of flying I’ve never seen any airline do that, even the rubbish ones. I fly with Qatar and Singapore and there is no way Emirates are anywhere near their standard.

The extra room it added was well worth the additional expense, and top marks for both the seating and the customer service. On the DXB-AKL and DXB-GLA legs (GLA used because EDI not convenient; no extra cost), the economy product on the A380 was well worth it. Could do better: the B777 product is quite cramped by comparison (10-across, not recommended, but only on one shorter leg) and its IFE is tired, even before it is compared with the equivalent service on the A380. EK is working towards introducing A350s on the EDI sector and they can't come soon enough. Finally, the checkins at both EDI and AKL were very quick; opening "early" (four hours or so) does make life a lot easier.

As my girlfriend had indigestion problems in the morning, we asked for an extra waste bag just in case. The crew then told us we need her to get checked by a doctor at the plane's entrance to make sure she can fly, but instead they offboarded us without actually doing the professional medical checkup by the doctors that they called to the plane. We had then to get a certificate that she's clear to fly, which the doctor gave right away because her condition was absolutely fine. As a result, we wasted a work day each and had to pay the hotel at Dubai airport out of our pocket. I had never experienced this level of deceit, disrespect and mistreatment from any airline before. This is not the behavior I would expect from a respectable business. My girlfriend was fit to fly, as confirmed by the doctor literally 10 mins after we had been deplaned.  I'll never fly this airline again.

In Manchester they made us to wait more than 5 hours without providing proper infomration. After waiting 5 hours they asked to exit in Manchester airport. They arranged bus service and asked people to take a private taxi and submit for reimburse. We were waiting in queue for bus, but their staff came to us and asked us to take a cab and submit for reimburment as we had a 1 year old baby and it was raining. I showed them putting my destination price it is costing. They told yes it will be reimburse, you just need to submit a complaint. We raised a complaint and now they are not returing money. They are straight away declaing and they dont have proper call service or any other way to reach out to them. Now I am realizing they lied us to reduce the crowd. If something happens ever with anyone, please dont listen them else you will not get your money back. Better take a email confirmation or video recording as proof. Not sure if that even works to get the refund.

review_header: “level of service did not meet expectations”
review_text: The crew member seems not willing to assist me even on small issues and requests. I found this to be quite disappointing, as the level of service I received did not meet my expectations. I understand that cabin crew members have many responsibilities during a flight, but I believe that it's important for them to be approachable and willing to help passengers when possible. One aspect of the flight that I particularly enjoyed was the food. I found the meal options to be varied and flavorful, and the presentation was attractive and appealing.

Apart from the air hostess dropping a carton of orange juice on me, the air steward shouted aggressively for me to ‘SIT DOWN’ while I was in the toilet queue - while some were allowed to go through. There is a massive drop in the service standard. Compared to other airline's the service on Emirates is very poor, Better options out there.

The high-definition screens and user-friendly interface made for a very enjoyable viewing experience. The crew was attentive, professional, and genuinely friendly. The food on Emirates was excellent, exceeding my expectations.  Beverage options were abundant, with a fine selection of juices, soft drinks, wines, and other choices. One particular crew member stood out to me during this journey. Although she is relatively new to her role, her level of professionalism and service was outstanding. Her attention to detail, efficiency, and positive energy set her apart.  I look forward to flying with Emirates again, and I highly recommend this airline.

Has-Been" Many factors can influence one's satisfaction with an airline, e.g. cabin staff service, seat comfort, food, inflight entertainment, etc. But for me there's one primary factor that determines my satisfaction - on-time arrival. If the flight is 3 or 5 hour late, no food service and no inflight entertainment system would make up for it. When I fly somewhere, I have people waiting for me on the other side, or I have meetings to attend. And when the airline fails to arrive on time, as is nowadays usually the case with Emirates, no smile with "I'm sorry" from the air hostess makes up for it. Over the past few years, Emirates has had an amazing record of disappointing me in the punctuality aspect. Once a great airline, Emirates has been in decline over the past ten (or so) years. This, I suspect, started when they entered into an alliance with Qantas in 2013. Instead of helping the declining and money-losing Aussie carrier, Emirates Airlines has been contaminated by Qantas' monopoly attitude and public service mentality. As I am not seeing any prospects of improvement at Emirates, I will now have to change carriers. My advice to other passengers is: if inflight entertainment is your top priority - fly Emirates. If you want to arrive on time - don't.

The first leg of the trip we upgraded to premium economy, which was great. On the way home, we flew economy. We had requested gluten free food and were provided it on the way to Tanzania, but only 1/2 of us received it on the way home. At Dubai during our 5 hour layover, we attempted to speak to customer service, but the agent on site was not helpful. In fact, airline security was at the help desk and seemingly tried to prevent us from even speaking with the agent regarding upgrading and the issue with our food. After speaking with the help desk, we were advised we likely would not be receiving gluten free food on the 14 hour flight back to JFK despite the multi hour layover. Additionally, we were advised no additional premium economy seats were available for upgrade. While boarding, multiple other guests upgraded at the gate before us, so there were additional upgrades available, or at least so it seemed. We were not happy with our experience with this airline.

Also, Emirates has no clue how to organise passenger seating, with our underaged child separated from the rest of the family and placed in an aisle seat several rows away from us purely because another passenger had paid to have an aisle seat, and ground staff said they couldn't change the other passenger to the aisle seat our child was assigned. We had to depend on the kindness of the other passenger, who when told the situation by us, agreed to the swap as it was essentially for the same seat she had paid for. And we were not the only family this happened to, multiple families were separated from underage children. Finally, Emirates damaged one of our suitcases beyond repair or use, and it has taken them 9 months to process compensation. The compensation they have offered is ridiculous - $100 for a suitcase that cost $400 to purchase because product costs "depreciate". We are really unhappy with Emirates and will not be flying with them ever again.

Awful experience both ways LHR to Dubai on their A380. Rung up customer services 2 days before departure to get an idea of how full the flight was and was informed it was only 50% full. Called again a few hours before departure and again told the same. Got on the flight and it was full! I mean why would they need to lie? Then WIFI was not working so couldn't even use that. A new A380 plane and WIFI not working?  To top it off the plane was over an hour late departing. Then on return again plane late and again WIFI not working - but took my money as I paid for the full WIFI. And the flight again delayed! Been checking historical flights and for some reason all the Emirates flights to and from London over the last week or so have all been delayed for over an hour. Be careful, they encourage you to become a Sky Rewards Member and you can benefit from free WIFI! Why when it doesn't even work? And the complimentary WIFI is only for messaging, not for general Internet which is $16 for the full flight Dubai to London. Rubbish airline and missed 2 full days of work because of no WIFI. As someone who frequently travels on business I need to find an airline that I can do work on and has reliable WIFI long haul - Emirates is useless and doesn't work at all. Won't be using Emirates again. The air stewardess was awesome, very apologetic - I mean it's not her fault but she handled it very well.

I didn't have a great time, legroom wasn't great, and my recliner wasn't functioning. Hyderabad was a pain as there was a crowd at the Emirates gate. I can see that this airline is declining year over year. It is time to move onto another airline.

And we travelled home from Barcelona via Dubai to Perth on 777-200LR and A380 and service was the same. My overall experience with Emirates being my first time was great and I would recommend them for overseas travel. This was my first time travelling on the amazing A380 and it was great to fly on.

Many of them appeared really moody or even mean on all 4 flights. They always seemed annoyed and unimpressed when requesting their service for anything. I assume they're just taught to be lovely to business and first class customers and economy doesn't matter? It's just so odd. Are they extremely stressed or something? Even the cheapest airline staff has been much nicer to me every single time. I really wouldn't call myself a difficult customer - one time I asked if the staff could turn down the fan a few rows down mine because I couldn't reach and the air was making me freezing cold to which the cabin crew replied "Okay but I can't reach it so I have to ask the people in that row, next time just ask them yourself". What's that about? Then they also forgot to take my partners food tray and when they were coming around I told them about it and was met with "Oh... okay". Not a sorry or anything at all. I thought they would be trained to provide an overall better experience and interaction. Also I haven't pressed the button for staff service many times, but out of the times I have, they responded in only about 30% of the cases. Overall I'm absolutely disappointed with the cabin crew. Otherwise, the food was quite nice, the Internet was unreachable most of the time, plane relatively clean.

I was yelled by a flight attendant on my first flight just for waiting to use the restroom. I also had a bad time in Dubai during a layover. It was so cold inside the cabin, I never felt that cold in a plane before. I see that Emirates is declining in their service. It is time to move onto another airline.

Lounge in Barcelona busy, however a good selection of food and beverages, and most importantly a good shower. Business class very comfortable, good food and attentive service. I do like the bar area. A nice place to stretch one’s legs. 4 hour layover in Dubai, spent in lounge in Terminal c then Terminal b, which is the better lounge. Premium Economy to Auckland. Wonderful service, from a charming young lady on my aisle. I like that my status with Emirates is always acknowledged by the crew. A nice touch. Good food, and I found plenty to watch on the entertainment. Delayed by 1 hour in Dubai, so arrived an hour late into Auckland. Emirates is my airline of choice.

Travellers can only obtain VISAS through only one visa provider. We followed correct process for visa application and at the airport confirmed with departures that visa was valid. The unaccompanied child was permitted to board the Emirates flight, I still paid $100 additional for unaccompanied minor service. The entire time I checked with all stakeholders could this child travel unaccompanied to Dubai on her own. Every single time I was told yes. Emirates sold me the ticket, Emirates sold me the unaccompanied minor package but now are not accepting responsibility! Upon arrival in Dubai the minor was aggressively treated by immigration, detained for 24 hours and deported back home. The child was not permitted to cross the border to visit her grandmother residing in Dubai. Now the airline claims that the grandmother could have applied for a different visa at the Dubai airport. So they won't allow the child to leave with the grandmother but they will allow the grandmother to apply for another visa? Flawed policy. That is all these greedy airlines care about. The child was detained and while her physical needs were taken care of, she has been left psychologically traumatized. Received few meal vouchers while detained.

I tried to go back but was denied. I went straight to Emirates lost and found hoing to get some service as a premium customer. Instead i got send us an email. I held my ground and was fobbed off by being assured plane would be cleaned within four hours and they would send them on to me in Singapore my next stop. Guess what not found even though i gave them my exact seat and they could not care less. This is now a number of poor Emirates customer service experiences for me, so never again will I fly Emirates unless i have no other options.
Emirates food was amazing! The staff was very professional and helpful. I would fly again with them—I have no regrets about the money we spent.

review_header: “does not get any better than Emirates”
review_text: Premium Economy Auckland to Dubai. Really comfortable seat, good food and service. Had a good solid 8 1/2 hours sleep. Although the IFE is vast, I find the choice for me is limited. I’m just being picky I guess. The Business lounge in Terminal C is woeful. I will do a separate review. Dubai to Barcelona I used points to upgrade to Business. Fabulous. Very comfortable seat, charming service and good food. I love the bar area. I fly to Europe 2 to 3 times a year and always use Emirates. They slightly more expensive, but worth it.

The cabin manager Mohamed was very efficient but the lady serving my section was definitely not in her right mood. Meals were very disappointing, to say the least. Service from Mpohamed was exceptional!

We spent over an hour completing it. The Emirates lounge was very good and in fact that was the only proper meal we had. The male staff at the reception was very very helpful. In flight, it was an AWFUL experience. The staff could not cope with the full flight and dinner was served 2.5 hours after take off. Food was appalling!! Emirates catering leaves a lot to desire.

Their standards have clearly dropped while their prices have increased. I have been flying with them for 10 years and never did I get upgraded! I did not mind flying economy but now, the food is really bad, customer service is terrible. Not the best company out there anymore.

Plane was clean though seats were showing the age (old faded fabric). Took-off on time. IFE was ok nothing too impressive the way they advertise it. Emirates meal portion and quality is the best. I had the best beef lasagna. Dessert, bread, etc were also excellent. Generous with the drinks. Snack was served before landing, just a simple cheese sandwich. The crew on board wasn't too interactive. Only saw them during the meal services and that's about it.

On two of the four legs they ran out of food options. The meals were only served 2-3 hours into the flight. The worst happened on the last leg between DXB and JHB. We were seated between 4 drunk passengers (2 unrelated to the other 2) who’s behavior was shocking and filthy to say the least. The staff didn’t really handle the situation well and it seemed like they rather chose not to have any confrontation. Quite frankly, we were surprised those passengers were even allowed to board since they were already clearly drunk at the airport. In fact, 2 of them seemed to be somewhat drugged as well. The other two drunk passengers made the flight really uncomfortable for those around them, even indecently exposing themselves. We were just grateful that they did not become aggressive, posing a risk to smooth flight operations. The cabin supervisor’s judgement was poor and the cabin crew did nothing to rectify the situation, even after being alerted to the problem. In fact, they served 2 of them more alcohol which was absolutely the wrong thing to do. We have to say that we have never experienced such poor service and unprofessionalism before.  Emirates need to up their game. At the moment, Qatar Airways definitely have the upper hand.

On the return they surprised me on boarding with an upgrade to business class. Even though it was the middle seat, it didn’t bother me. They provided bulgari amenities kit and mattress and cover. After a delicious meal I had a 5 hrs sleep as it was an over night flight.

We highlighted it to the crew before takeoff and they sent a technician to check. The technician came, saw it from a distance and went back saying he’ll send someone else. The flight took off, no one came. Highlighted to the crew again - they said, “Our technician came but you refused to get up from your seat and let him check. And we can’t help you now”.  It was a 14 hour horrendous experience and deficiency in service, coupled with a lie and blaming it on us. It was physically painful with the armrest pushing on the shoulder for 14 hours and a mental agony at such service and behaviour by the crew.

review_header: "not welcome and passengers are a burden"
review_text: Unfortunately the facts are different. Attendants on 3 of the 4 legs a have flown with them look as they are very tired. Making eye contact, heads are turned away, being in the aisle for a short moment, I was literally pushed aside by a staff member walking up and down the aisle. Meal time was too short, 1 time I got my breakfast 30 minutes before landing, 5 minutes later they tried to collect my meal again. The meals itself were overall good and the food was enjoyable. Ground services in Amsterdam and Dubai were accurate and friendly. Overall I booked my next vacation in December and avoided this airline. The feeling I got from Emirates was that I am not welcome and passengers are a burden.

My carefully planned return trip from UK, with EMIRATES turned into a nightmare due to issues caused by their Dubai ground staff.  Upon checking in Manchester, I was issued a boarding pass for the MAN-DXB and DXB-SIN legs of my journey, with seats allocated according to my pre booking. However, upon reaching Dubai and during check-in, the counter staff took my boarding pass and issued a new one. Initially, I presumed new boarding pass was due to a soiled document and did not notice the seat change as there is no change in flight. To my disappointment, the new seat I was assigned turned out to be directly in front of the toilet onboard. I also sought assistance from cabin crew and online chat services before take-off, but unfortunately, no one helped me. I had specifically opted for an Economy Flex Plus ticket, solely to secure a seat reservation that would allow for a more comfortable journey. The proximity to the restroom doors, with their associated noise, significantly hindered my ability to rest or enjoy the flight services as intended. Furthermore, crew members accessing the overhead luggage bins above my seat at regular intervals further disrupted any chance of relaxation. Additionally, during the meal service, crew members did not lock the lavatory door, causing passengers to enter and exit while I was eating. This forced me to stop my meal. At the end of the journey, the crew sarcastically asked me about my flight experience, despite being well aware of the difficulties I had faced. Emirates' service in 2024 should be considered among the worst. Until today I have not received any reply on my compliant placed with Emirates and their customer service reminded me that it requires 60 days to send a reply. I must tell that compare to past, Emirates service quality are highly deteriorated and no one care of it there.
The air ticket is cheap. There's TV and wifi, there are also a gift for kids too. The services are very great. There are many delicious foods to eat too.

Due to the rains / flood in Dubai flights were getting canceled but Emirates never bothered to inform the passengers. I had to spend 6k (back and forth) on Uber coming from Pune to Mumbai to catch the flight. After I got to the gate they told me the flight was canceled. I was so furious. I asked them why I never got any text or email update and they blamed it on the passengers. So I asked her to verify my phone number. When I got to the airport I checked on the app about the flight details and till that time it showed on time. They never even bothered to change that. Now that I am asking for my refund they are not taking responsibility and returning my money.

The seats were wide, with plenty of legroom, and the food was quite good. Service was also fine. Shame they serve Prosecco and there is very limited choice on wines, but let's skip right past that. Obviously, I'd much rather fly business or first on Emirates, but this was better than the old business class on BA and worth paying to avoid economy.

Dirty Toilets, tissue all around the floor. The meal asked for at the time of booking and paying at least 25% more than other airlines, was not provided. A simple service for lukewarm water was not provided. In flight movies were nothing new or trendy. Overall a very poor performance.

We asked for a Bassinet for the baby a few times but didn't get one. The baby fell asleep and I was holding for about half an hour watering a bassinet still did not get one then I had to speak to one of the cabin crews with a firm tone to get one! They didn't even offer lunch to one of my daughters. When asked, the lady said oh do you want lunch? What do you mean? She is 11 years old and needs food to eat on board, doesn't she? They also didn't give us any baby food either. My boy was hungry and crying. The lady next to me with infants had to share one of her babies food with my boy. When I fed that food to my son, one cabin crew came with some baby food which we didn't ask for saying we ran out of what you asked for. Just terrible! We also noticed in general the cabin crews were unprofessional, careless and ignoring the passengers' requests. It was a terrible experience this time. Hope Emirates read these reviews and take serious actions to improve their services.

While I understand the circumstances surrounding the flight cancellation, the issue lies with the abysmal customer support I have encountered since then. Upon requesting a certificate for insurance purposes, I was informed that I would need to wait 30 days for processing, which I accepted as part of the procedures. However, upon receiving the certificate after the specified period, it was found to be incorrect for both myself and my travel companion. Subsequent attempts to rectify this error have been met with further delays and inefficiencies. Despite being advised to fill out another form for follow-up, it has now been two months since my initial request, and I am still awaiting the correct certificates. The lack of assistance and communication from customer support has been appalling, with promises to escalate the issue to the relevant department unfulfilled and no resolution in sight. As a loyal customer of Emirates, I am deeply dismayed by the subpar level of customer support and service provided in this instance. The unresolved issue with the certificates has also led to a delay in processing my insurance claim, further exacerbating the situation. It is truly disheartening to experience such incompetence and negligence. The disparity between the exceptional flight services and the inadequate customer support is not only disappointing but also unacceptable.

I was pleasantly surprised, however, by EK's economy product. While it is still economy and you can never 'go flat', I found Emirates' economy to be way better than United or Air Canada economy and, overall, offers solid hard and soft products. The seat is a decent size and has good legroom, again, compared to North American carriers. Catering was good with two full meals and a pizza or sandwich snack in between. Meal portions were good with plenty of variety. I was impressed by the 'engineering' of the economy meal tray with every conceivable space used to offer something. Every time I rang the call button, it was answered pleasantly. Washrooms were kept quite clean throughout both sectors. The ICE entertainment system offers tons of options. If paying out of my own pocket, I'd again chose EK economy.
The cabin was clean and well kept. The food was served on time and was appetizing. The IFE worked well and their library of content was well curated. Overall a good experience.

However, the link they provide does not lead to any option that allows for pre-purchasing luggage. Instead, the link leads to options for seat or class upgrades, food selection, or flight charges. In other words, Emirates takes extra effort to hide the option to buy extra kilograms prior to check-in. Today, I faced an extra charge of £380 because I was not given the option to purchase extra kilograms in advance. I tried searching but could not find the actual link to buy extra luggage. There are much better options to fly. Will not use your bad service next time.

Very rude flight attendants and crew. They only take care of higher levels, and other passengers, who are the majority of people in flight, are nothing to them. I was the gold member of this airline, and I stopped to fly with them. After 14 years, I tried to gain with minor hope for some changes, but it was worse than before. The crew's attitude on the ground and flights with economic passengers is unbelievable. It seems all of them are trained to deal with economy passengers like this. It is obviously not a chance for all of them to act like this with an insulting attitude.

They simply do not care about passengers. My sister had to cancel her leg of trip due to a diagnosed blood disorder that was serious enough she could not travel far from her home, fly, sit for long periods etc. While she undergoes series of tests to figure out cause and how to help her, Emirates would not let her cancel her one way, outbound flight. The flight does not leave for 7 months. They feel she can rest up and be healed by the date of departure.  She does have a flexible economy ticket to make the cancellation. They claim medical reasons are not approved reasons for cancellation of most of ticket value. Trying to change the name so i can save the trip and take a friend instead? Nope! Out of the question says Emirates.

Having flown the best (and worst) of discount airlines and everything in between, this was something else. Just the sense that you're the only one on board and that you call the shots. It was other-worldly. I drank dom perignon for 7 hours, ate a lot of caviar and chatted to some lovely relaxed staff (after all, they only had four passengers to attend to). The 'suite' was large, comfortable and opulent. Of course it was... Even though it was a 777 (not a 380), there was an absolute sense of luxury. Not sure if I'll ever try/fly first class again, but it was worth the points and a lot of fun.

Service was polite but disengaged, with little attempt by crew to interact with passengers. Seats were comfortable, with good legroom. I thought the IFE was excellent, with some quality new releases to choose from. The meals were large and generous - I am a Qatar Airways frequent flyer, and the Emirates meals are significantly larger than those on Qatar. However, the alcohol options are far smaller on Emirates, and on both flights I was only offered a drink once per flight. It's been nearly 20 years since I last flew Emirates and feel they have lost their shine; whilst I thought they were decent, I feel they lack the polish and refinement of Qatar.

Most importantly, 2 out of 2 times I flew with them, I was delayed for multiple hours. The first time it was just sitting on the plane with no AC for 2 hours, and the second was 3+ hours, due to some trivial problem with their cabin lights. That 2nd time I had a connecting flight to catch, and while on board they assured me it would be fine, and while I did make it to the gate while they were still boarding, they refused to board me due to having apparently unilaterally decided to rebook me to a flight 11 hours later, assuming I wouldn't make it. Turns out there were earlier flights, but they wouldn't book me to them due to not codesharing with those airlines. Not only was no compensation offered for this day-long delay, but when I finally booked a separate flight on my own, they wouldn't even refund me, and had me request it on my own online. Overall they just showed 0 willingness to help throughout the entire process, despite it being 100% their fault, for a delay caused by them and between flights both of which they operated. They made it as painful as it possibly could be, every step of the way. Oh, and the flights themselves were also bad - old-looking airplanes, terrible food, and relatively limited entertainment. Emirates might have earned a positive reputation due to their First Class experience, but for Economy flights, it's probably the worst airline I've ever flown.

First row in economy, so no one in front of me.  Service and meals were very good. Only 6 hours over night so decided not to sleep on this sector. Watched a couple of movies. The plane seemed on the older side, so movie selection not as good it seemed. Visited the lounge in Dubai due to my Emirates status, which was very good. Shower very welcome and good coffee. Flight to Auckland in Premium Economy a big step up from Economy. Seat very comfortable with loads of legroom, good recline and leg/foot rest. Slept for about 9 hours out of 15 hours. Service was friendly, professional and thorough buy a charming young British chap called Zak. Meals were delicious, hot towels etc. Entertainment was more extensive, although only watched 1 movie, as I wanted to sleep. Arrived half an hour early in Auckland. First off the plane and land side in less than 30 minutes.
..the rest are simply awful!

Shortly after that, Skywards locked my account, indicating it's due to "a routine review." However, after more than a few weeks, my account was still under "a routine review." That's when I started making a call to their customer service, but all they can do is sending an email to the internal team and told me to do the same, which I did ... but no response whatsoever from the internal team. Subsequent calls to the customer services and after hours of explaining, arguing, pleading yield the same outcome (or lack thereof.) The customer service agents were not willing to escalate the issue for us even though they knew that this issue has been going on way longer than their normal timeline. they did not try to help you in any way regardless of how bad the situation is. There was one one time after we pushed so hard to get to talk to their supervisor but even him would not try to help you anyway. Their entire customer service is there just to serve their internal team, not their customers. It has been almost three months now and my account is still under "a routine review". What supposes to be a dream trip has since becomes one of my worst nightmares. The customer service agents said the reward miles are valid for 3 years so nothing to be worried about, but how would it matter if my travel plan window is already passed - and at this rate who knows whether they will complete the "routine review" of my account within 3 years. All I want at this point is for the precious points I have been saving up all these years to go back to my Chase Ultimate Reward account and wake up from this nightmare.

I'm 2 days before first departure. I want to change the 3rd flight. My "Flex Plus" doesn't apply anymore since they will reissue all 2 flights and the first one is Business Saver. They want to charge me 900€ to upgrade the 1st one, then 300€ change fee. In other words, if "any" of your flights is saver, "none of them" are Plus anymore. I feel scammed.
Seat quality was average, food was also average, cabin crew were good. Ground services were slow. Flight was not bad but the layover at Dubai Airport was boring.

I love the food but the flight attendants on all my flights were unfriendly and rude. Many of them are acting like they are doing us a favor by serving us, even though that’s their job. On May 5, I flew from Tokyo to Dubai and most likely it was my last flight with the Emirates. Especially a flight attendant who was very unfriendly and also skipped our line while serving food. She was unfriendly with everyone.  She seems to be hating her job. Apart from the flight attendants, one other thing I am not happy about is the delays. In my experience, Emirates never departs and arrives on time, there is always a delay.

The crew had to write a report as she should have not been allowed boarding. My bag is completely soaked through, all contents of the bag is soaking. I spoke to the ground staff and they could offer no help what so ever or a report. Everything is ruined - I am furious, I’ve had no communication regarding my outbound flights that were cancelled due to the storms and now my luggage is ruined. I will never fly Emirates again.
Tasteless and overcooked. Not what it used to be when it was first launched.

Cabin crew reflect good training, collaborative. Food is standard like others, did not use IFE during flight. Connected in Dubai for less than 30 minutes and disembarked to bus then terminal and surprisingly my luggage arrived to terminal destination.

They have no contingency for rain and no interest in human care. They have provided no compensation for the impacted passengers. They claim that missing luggage was also due to the rain, they provide no help when things get tough and I will never be flying with them again. They also required me to fill out a medical form to board and they took zero notice of my one requirement (more drinking water than average) and, despite being able bodied, would not allow me to purchase the bulkhead seats after having spoken to me in person (a fit and healthy 35 year old with just a touch of hydrocephalus) due to the fact, and I’m quoting here I’m “disabled.”

FA good and attentive. Departure delayed by 30 minutes. Outdated seat you need to press button 100 times to go to flat. Food quality is average. Internet not working, I have to spend time trying and trying. Bathrooms are clean however it was at the back of the airplane, front bathroom kept for first class, and every time i went i found 3-4 waiting, Toothbrush not available.

The flight was delayed 4 times. We arrived 2.30 hours before departing time. After 1.30 hour wait and 2 very disorganized check-in counter change, the counter stopped taking in passenger. No explanation from the staff. We found out from a fellow passenger that the flight was not confirmed. I tried calling and contacting them online but both channels were too busy. We finally went to talk to the staff who couldn't confirm when we will be flying out. They told us that they could not confirm about our connecting flight in Dubai to Bangkok too. A two-to-three-days wait was probable. We finally had to cancel the flight and bought a new last-minute ticket from Qatar to get back home. We tried to get compensation on extra hotel charge and airfares but the airline is not taking any responsibility. Extremely poor management and definitely no sense of responsibility from the airline.

The services were top notch. We travelled by economy class but were treated nicely by the stewardess. The food was great and we were fed quite frequently. When coming back on 4th April, we had a bad experience due to mistake done by Air Canada since we had 2 layovers and one of the layover had to travel via Air Canada.

Not only did the person attending our aisle forgotten our drink requests once, but twice! One of which i also have to take the drink order myself. Not only that, the flight attendant didn’t apologise on both occasions which are of different time stamps, that’s a poor representative of the airline and i believe this is rather basic. Moreover and unfortunately, screen on the seat was blank and was requesting assistance to resolve it. Was reassured that it will be troubleshoot in 10-15 minutes. Guess what? Wasn’t resolve throughout the remaining of the flight. And also, i believe it’s basic to walk down the aisle once in awhile at your respective section to check-in with the guests to see everything is alright and needs immediate attention, but am noticing a pattern on both occasions, to and fro Dubai and Singapore. Seems like they only service during food and drinks, then hide back in the staff area.

The seat is comfortable, crew is friendly and professional. The aircraft is clean. However the catering is a little disappointing. For such an expensive ticket I was expecting far better to be honest.

Never fly Emirates again, do not recommend anyone to travel on Emirates - you will be left to dry. I checked onto EK421 with a 20 kg checked bag on 18th March from Perth Airport. Arrived at Dubai airport on the 19th morning, as of today after 3 days of being me hostage at Dubai airport - there's no information from Emirates airport staff on anything, no worry about my dietary needs, my medical needs, sorry about my personal & business plan). I am not allowed to access my essential needs & medication from checked-bag and they would not put me on to my next connecting flight. At Dubai Airport Emirates staff directed me and others to continuously watch out for the Gate number on the screen as the flight would be listed there (but they won't tell when), I and others kept waiting for hours for the flight to appear, they appear without gates, stay listed there and then gets canceled. Clearly Emirates are just listing ghost flights so they don't need to provide a hotel. I am now on airport for more than 36 hours, no hotel provided, no vegetarian food available, I now almost three days in the same pair of clothing, and my medication & other essentials are in a checked-in bag that Emirates staff don't even care and tell me anything on when it will be returned to me. Their pretext that this is due to rain is just made up, as of last few days Dubai has returned to normal, for sure essential airport services there shouldn't be hold up and the excuse of weather event is just hiding their lack of management ability.
6 hours delay. No communication. Unable ground staff and very rude. Lost baggage. I could spend hours making list of the problems. Will definitely change airline.

The situation is getting worse and day by day more flights are cancelled and more luggage lost. Emirates has lost it completely and the management of Emirates is not putting all what it takes to go back on track. After 11 years of flying Emirates as platinum member I am evaluating the possibility of moving to Qatar airways or even Etihad. Emirates has wonderful inflight service but the lack of professionalism of the ground staff is killing the company

Phone number sometimes worked and sometimes didn’t. Called 20 plus times. Headed to airport to speak to an agent in person while on the 4 hour call hold. Finally rebooked to New York but the original ticket was for Miami. Flight is at midnight and the airport wouldn’t let us through the gate so we are spending 6+ hours with no AC in hot conditions and my mum is elderly (70) and not in good health. Also told us that we had to pay our own fare to Miami from New York which cost an additional $800 which they said will not be refunded. Also we were told this at 10:30am when the flight was at 4pm today.

I would never recommend this airline. Cancelled flight home and literally left everyone to fend for themselves. Long delays and everyones been messed about. Absolutely diabolical for being such a massive company. Would give 0 stars if allowed. Definitely not travelling with them ever again

After 8 hours, when they let the passengers out of the plane, she didn’t get any assistance and had to walk a lot, as we know Dubai airport is huge. She lined up for 3 hours to get a new board pass, they gave her a boarding pass for 08:20am on 17/04/24, but it was already 22:10 17/04/24 when they give it to her. She didn’t eat for this whole time. Now they booked her in for on flight at 09:05 on 18/04/24, let’s see. The problem is not rescheduled the flight due the bad weather, the problem was the Emirates didn’t give any assistance to the passengers.

04.2024 which was late because of a technical issue and the crew doesn't want to work over shift. The said flight reached the next day without any inflight food (BOM-DXB) instead of the same day creating physical harassment, mental harassment and financial losses (hotel & further tour charges got cancelled). Despite having active transit visa your staff kept us waiting for three hours at DXB airport for issuing current transit. My Flight no. EK 0506 which has original time of departure 9.30am (DXB-BOM) has not yet departed (till 10 pm) because of bad weather conditions but flight EK 0502 which has original departure time of 13.00 pm has already reached BOM. How come? It seems EK 0506 is not important, (bad weather is applicable to all flights). This behaviour and approach of Emirates is totally not acceptable & hence we here by demand compensation.

Yes, we had booked economically, but then you can expect a fully functioning chair, right? Our flight to Bali took more than twenty hours in total. The quality of the chairs was nothing to write home about. We arrived at all destinations broken. I bought a new suitcase in Bali. This one also arrived “broken” at home in Amsterdam. One flight with Emirates was apparently too much for this beautiful suitcase. After some correspondence back and forth with Emirates, the conclusion was that they could not do anything for me and would not take responsibility. My conclusion is therefore to take a look at other companies where service may still be expected. In any case, I won't be booking Emirates again anytime soon. My next flight to Bali is with our KLM. Zowel op de heen- als op de terugvlucht zat ik of mijn reispartner op een kapotte stoel. Ja, we hadden economisch geboekt, maar dan mag je toch wel een volledig functionerende stoel verwachten? Onze vliegreis naar Bali duurde in totaal meer dan twintig uren. De kwaliteit van de stoelen was niet om naar huis te schrijven. Gebroken kwamen we op alle bestemmingen aan. Op Bali had ik een nieuwe koffer gekocht. Deze kwam ook “gebroken aan” thuis in Amsterdam. Één vlucht met Emirates was blijkbaar te veel voor deze mooie koffer. Na wat correspondentie heen en weer met Emirates was de conclusie dat ze niks voor mij konden betekenen en de verantwoordelijk niet op zich namen. Mijn conclusie is daarom ook om eens te kijken naar andere maatschappijen waar misschien nog wel service is te verwachten. In ieder geval zal ik Emirates niet meer zo snel boeken. Mijn volgende vlucht naar Bali is gewoon met onze KLM.

I have been traveling around for 4 decades. This airline is the worst I have traveled. From boarding desk staffs to aircrews, they are unfriendly, utterly rude and disrespectful. Pathetic all across the board.

I pay full price and more for a flex ticket, but I only get 3/4 of a seat as the obese person next to me far is overflowing into my chair.  When I insisted to be moved to another chair it took the staff 15 minutes for the cabin staff to even respond to my calls, they were too busy chatting at the crew area, I was watching them. I had to press the crew call button on and off over 20 times, that’s no exaggeration, before someone came to ask me what I wanted. After pointing out what was going on I was moved to the chair closest to the toilet, almost in the toilet, I could hear everything inside the bathroom. The seat they put me in sticks out into the aisle so every time the air hostess would walk past they would knock my chair, completely lacking awareness or care for the passengers. They really don’t care. it’s difficult to imagine a more incompetent bunch of cabin staff and management controlling an airline. It is 100% the last time I’ll ever consider flying Emirates. I didnt even have have space to even eat my meal so I couldn’t ask for my dinner I couldn’t rest without being leaned on and knocked constantly by the customer overflowing into my chair. This is absolutely unacceptable.
As it was a item of importance to me and I was very sad that it was left behind. Very disappointed with Emirates

the flight was from Riyadh to Islamabad via Dubai. Departure time from Riyadh was 4:25 PM on 9th of march and arrival time was 7:10 Pm on same date in dubai airport. the 2 hour stay and then departure from Dubai at 9:10 PM same date and arrival 1:30 AM 10th of march. We were handed over to Flydubai from emirates  which was strange bu Ok we did boarding and got notification that flight is delayed.. Total delay in Riyadh was 4 and half hours and reached very late to Dubai airport and the connecting flight were missed. We approach to emirates counter and they rudely refuse to provide us any service because we were having flydubai boarding passes and told us to deal with Flydubai. Long story short we were dealt with like animals for 18 hours in airport and depart to another airport which were around 700 KM away from our  ticketed airport and does not provide any transfortatin from that airport. The car were arranged by us which cost us around 250$. I will never recommend Emirates and flydubai to anyone.

The flight from Lisbon to Dubai was delayed by 3 hrs. Connecting flight to Phuket was missed due to that which of course can happen but there was zero handling of the situation in Dubai - it took 4,5 hours at the airport standing in lines to get a new boarding pass and a hotel voucher. Before that no information at all. After all this they take you to a hotel which is 30 minutes away from the airport without telling before which hotel and where it is - arriving at the hotel another long waiting session and then no one can say when the shuttle bus is going back to the airport - we don’t have that information, end of conversation! Zero information. Zero service. I booked seats on the flight in advance to be able to rest and in the email about the new flight it said the booked seat will remain for the new flight but that is not the case at all. So now instead of my paid window seat I’m sitting straight in the middle. All the service chat tells you is to file a complaint. Also I paid for a hotel in Phuket that I don’t get to use. This was by far the worst I’ve ever experienced by any airline. It’s such a joke, the way they treat people, their customers. Especially at the airport- no one cared at all for all of the travelers facing this situation. Everyone was treated with pure ignorance. Biggest mistreatment and miss organization ever! Don’t book this airline!

The captain kept us updated on turbulence and seatbelt reminder throughout flight. Cabin crew professional and available when needed, plenty of drinks available. Have flown Emirates since 2012 when flying to Europe never had a bad experience, always Economy but been fortunate to be offered upgrade x2. Gluten free meals the best.

My husband & I checked in online 48 hours before departure. Arrived at Venice Marco Polo Airport and took the online check-in line which was very short. The Emirates check-in was very good and answered our questions about our onward flight when arriving in Dubai further connection which was with Qantas to regional airport. We were surprised when given all three boarding passes for continuation to final destination with Qantas Chose aisle seats C/D as far back as possible. Flight was excellent with multilingual crew and co pilot Australian Captain from El Salvador. Always fly to & from to Europe with Emirates well looked after and the best gluten free meals. Arrived on time.

We were offered a long flight with one more transfer DXX-LJU - WAW no longer on Emirates and FlyDubai on budget airlines where the standard was far below expectations. Unfortunately, because of Emirates we also missed the next transfer and instead of 16 hours our journey lasted over 60 hours.
